problems.title: Erdős Problem 1191 — i
problems.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite Sidon set. Is it true that
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^{1/2}=0?$$

Here $x$ runs over $\mathbb{N}$ and the $\liminf$ is taken in `ℝ≥0∞`, so that it is $\infty$
rather than $0$ when the sequence tends to infinity.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1191.parts.i : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → IsSidon A →
    liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦ ENNReal.ofReal
      ((A ∩ .Icc 1 x).ncard / (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * log x ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))) atTop = 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1191 — ii
problems.statement:
Does there exist an infinite Sidon set $A$ such that
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^c>0$$
for some $c>0$?

A positive answer would also give a positive answer to Erdős Problem 39.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1191.parts.ii : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsSidon A ∧
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), 0 < liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦ ENNReal.ofReal
      ((A ∩ .Icc 1 x).ncard / (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * log x ^ c)) atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 161 — i
problems.statement:
Let $\alpha\in[0,1/2)$ and $n,t\geq 1$. Let $F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ be the smallest $m$ such that we can
$2$-colour the edges of the complete $t$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices such that if $X\subseteq
[n]$ with $\lvert X\rvert \geq m$ then there are at least $\alpha \binom{\lvert X\rvert}{t}$ many
$t$-subsets of $X$ of each colour. For fixed $n,t$ as we change $\alpha$ from $0$ to $1/2$ does
$F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ increase continuously or are there jumps? Only one jump?

Here growth is compared up to constant factors as $n\to\infty$. At $\alpha=0$,
each color must occur, following the source's Ramsey convention.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_161.parts.i :
    ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t →
      {p | p.1 ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (1 / 2) ∧ p.2 ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (1 / 2) ∧
        (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t p.1 : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
          (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t p.2 : ℝ))} =
        erdos_161.parts.i.answer t

problems.title: Erdős Problem 713 — i
problems.statement:
Is it true that, for every bipartite graph $G$, there exists some $\alpha\in [1,2)$ and $c>0$ such that $$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\sim cn^\alpha?$$

The condition that $G$ have at least two edges excludes degenerate forbidden graphs whose
extremal number is eventually zero, for which the displayed asymptotic with $c>0$ is impossible.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_713.parts.i :
    ∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), G.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∃ α c : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 ∧ 0 < c ∧
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => c * (n : ℝ) ^ α)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 713 — ii
problems.statement:
Must $\alpha$ be rational?

The same nondegeneracy condition on $G$ is used as in part (i). Rationality means that the real
number $\alpha$ lies in the image of the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{R}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_713.parts.ii :
    ∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), G.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∀ α c : ℝ, α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 → 0 < c →
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n G : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => c * (n : ℝ) ^ α) →
        α ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 593 (\$500)
problems.statement:
**Erdős Problem 593 (\$500)**: Characterize those finite 3-uniform hypergraphs which appear
in every 3-uniform hypergraph of chromatic number $> \aleph_0$.

The answer is the set of obligatory finite 3-uniform hypergraphs, represented here on the
labelled vertex sets `Fin n`.

Two-colorability (Property B) is a necessary condition, see
`erdos_593.variants.obligatory_implies_two_colorable`, but it is not sufficient: two triples
sharing a pair form a 2-colorable hypergraph that is not obligatory, see
`erdos_593.variants.common_pair_not_obligatory`. In the graph case ($r = 2$) the problem is
completely solved by Erdős–Galvin–Hajnal [EGH75]: the obligatory graphs are exactly the finite
bipartite graphs.

A resolution has been claimed by E. Li (arXiv:2606.24882, 2026); at the time of writing
erdosproblems.com still lists the problem as open.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_593 :
    {p : Σ n : ℕ, UniformHypergraph (Fin n) 3 | p.2.IsObligatory} = erdos_593.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 78
problems.statement:
Let $R(k)$ be the Ramsey number for $K_k$. Give a constructive proof that $R(k) > C^k$ for some
constant $C > 1$.

Equivalently, give an explicit construction of graphs on $n$ vertices which contain no clique
and no independent set of size $\geq c \log n$, for some constant $c > 0$.

We formalise "explicit" as: the adjacency relation of the graph on $n$ vertices is decided by a
single algorithm that runs in time polynomial in $n$ (see `explicitGraph`). This is the weakest
reasonable notion ("weakly explicit"); even this is open. The strongly explicit version, with time
polynomial in $\log n$, is `erdos_78.variants.strongly_explicit`.

This problem is #4 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_78 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ adj : List Bool × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, NoHomogeneousSet (explicitGraph adj n) ⌈c * log n⌉₊

problems.statement:
The diagonal-direction inverse question [Gr24, Problem 55; Au14, §1.3].

Let $p$ be an odd prime and suppose that $f : \mathbb{F}_p^n \times \mathbb{F}_p^n \to \mathbb{C}$
is a function bounded pointwise by 1. Suppose that
$\mathbb{E}_h \lVert \Delta_{(h,h)} f \rVert_{\square}^4 \geq \delta$.

Does $f$ correlate with a function of the form
$a(x)b(y)c(x-y)e_p(B(x,y))$, where $B$ is bilinear and
$e_p(t) = \exp(2\pi i t/p)$?

    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2), ∃ C : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ δ > 0, 0 < C δ) ∧
      ∀ (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) (n : ℕ)

      -- Edge case: avoid the trivial truth  $|f(0,0)| \leq 1$ if n = 0 (single point domain)
      (hn : 1 ≤ n)

      (f : 𝔽ₚⁿ × 𝔽ₚⁿ → ℂ)
      (hf : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ 1)

      -- Since f is 1-bounded, and since the box norm counts bounded configurations, the expectation
      -- of the box norm will never exceed 1. If $\delta > 1$, `h_bound` is vacuously false,
      -- rendering the entire implication trivially true.
      (hδ_le : δ ≤ 1)

      (h_bound : (1 / (p^n : ℝ)) * ∑ h : 𝔽ₚⁿ, boxNorm4 (multiplicativeDerivative (h, h) f) ≥ δ),
      ∃ (a b c : 𝔽ₚⁿ → ℂ) (B : 𝔽ₚⁿ →ₗ[ZMod p] 𝔽ₚⁿ →ₗ[ZMod p] ZMod p),

        -- Common assumption for inverse Gowers norm theorems, prevents trivial solutions by
        -- arbitrarily scaling one of the functions (and thus the correlation).
        (∀ x, ‖a x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x, ‖b x‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x, ‖c x‖ ≤ 1) ∧

        ‖(1 / (p^(2*n) : ℝ)) * ∑ x : 𝔽ₚⁿ, ∑ y : 𝔽ₚⁿ,
          f (x, y) * star (a x * b y * c (x - y) * ZMod.stdAddChar (B x y))‖ ≥ C δ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 963 — i
problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that in any set $A\subset \mathbb{R}$ of size $n$ there is a

$\sum_{b\in S}b$ are distinct for all $S\subseteq B$. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, is it true
that $f(n)\geq \lfloor \log_2 n\rfloor$?

This is the first part, a problem of Erdős [Er65, p. 188]. We read "estimate" as an asymptotic
equivalence $f(n)\sim$ `answer n`. The order of magnitude $\log n$ is easy (see
`erdos_963.variants.greedy` and the example $a_i=i$ in [Er65, p. 188]), so the question is the
constant.

    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_963.parts.i.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 963 — ii
problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that in any set $A\subset \mathbb{R}$ of size $n$ there is a
subset $B\subseteq A$ of size $\lvert B\rvert\geq k$ which is dissociated that is, the sums
$\sum_{b\in S}b$ are distinct for all $S\subseteq B$. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, is it true
that $f(n)\geq \lfloor \log_2 n\rfloor$?

This is the second part. Erdős [Er65, p. 188] asks whether the bound $\lfloor\log_3 n\rfloor$ can
be improved to $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. We state it for all $n\geq 1$, with
$\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ written as `Nat.log 2 n`.

As on the problem page, $A$ is any set of reals. [Er65] speaks of "given numbers" and uses the
example $a_i=i$. Allowing negative numbers makes the question harder. A dissociated set never
contains both $x$ and $-x$, and changing signs keeps a set dissociated. So the largest dissociated
subsets of $A$ and of $\{\lvert a\rvert : a\in A,\ a\neq 0\}$ have the same size, and the sets
$\{\pm a : a\in S\}$ (with $0$ added for odd $n$) show that $f(2m)=f(2m+1)$ is the least size of a
largest dissociated subset of a set of $m$ positive reals. Hence this statement asks for
$\lfloor\log_2 m\rfloor+1$ for $m$ positive reals. The question for positive reals with
$\lfloor\log_2\lvert A\rvert\rfloor$, one less, is `erdos_963.variants.positive`; it follows from
this statement.

problems.title: Pittel's stable-matching hyperbola threshold conjecture
problems.statement:
Pittel conjectures a threshold $p_*(n)$ for the rank pairs across stable matchings to trace
out a hyperbola. For all sufficiently large $n$, it lies between $\frac{9}{4}(\log n)^2/n$ and $1$.

The fixed reciprocal arc $(t,t^{-1})$ for $t \in [2/3,3/2]$ specifies the curve to cover in this
formulation. For each fixed $0<\delta<1$, compare probabilities at distance at least
$\delta\min(p_*(n),1-p_*(n))$ from the threshold. The relative margin keeps both comparison
ranges nonempty. On the upper range, the event holds with high probability uniformly at every
positive tolerance. On the lower range, it fails with high probability uniformly at one positive
tolerance for each $\delta$.
problems.lean:
theorem pittel_hyperbola_threshold :
    ∃ pStar : ℕ → Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1,
      let d (n : ℕ) := min (pStar n : ℝ) (1 - (pStar n : ℝ))
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, (9 / 4 : ℝ) * (Real.log n) ^ 2 / n < (pStar n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ δ ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1,
        (∀ ε > 0, Tendsto (fun n ↦
          ⨆ p : {p : unitInterval // (pStar n : ℝ) + δ * d n ≤ (p : ℝ)},
            marketLaw n p.1 (hyperbolaEvent n p.1 ε)ᶜ) atTop (𝓝 0)) ∧
        ∃ ε > 0, Tendsto (fun n ↦
          ⨆ p : {p : unitInterval // (p : ℝ) ≤ (pStar n : ℝ) - δ * d n},
            marketLaw n p.1 (hyperbolaEvent n p.1 ε)) atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1152
problems.statement:
For $n\geq 1$ fix some sequence of $n$ distinct numbers $x_{1n},\ldots,x_{nn}\in [-1,1]$. Let
$\epsilon=\epsilon(n)\to 0$.

Does there always exist a continuous function $f:[-1,1]\to \mathbb{R}$ such that if $p_n$ is a
sequence of polynomials, with degrees $\deg p_n<(1+\epsilon(n))n$, such that
$p_n(x_{kn})=f(x_{kn})$ for all $1\leq k\leq n$, then $p_n(x)\not\to f(x)$ for almost all
$x\in [-1,1]$?

This is Problem 2.42 in [Va99]. The $n$ nodes of the $n$-th row form the finite set `nodes n`.
We take $\epsilon(n)>0$. A smaller $\epsilon$ only shrinks the class of $p_n$, so this is
equivalent to allowing any real $\epsilon(n)\to 0$. We impose the degree bound only for
$n\geq 1$, since for $n=0$ the bound `natDegree < 0` can never hold. We read
"$p_n(x)\not\to f(x)$ for almost all $x$" as: for almost every $x$, the sequence $p_n(x)$ does
not converge to $f(x)$.

For $\deg p_n<n$ the interpolating polynomial is unique (the Lagrange polynomial). Erdős, Kroó
and Szabados [EKS89, pp. 232-233] give necessary and sufficient conditions on the nodes under
which, for every continuous $f$ and every fixed $\epsilon>0$, there are interpolating polynomials
of degree at most $\lfloor n(1+\epsilon)\rfloor$ approximating $f$ at the rate of the best
uniform approximation (in particular converging uniformly to $f$).

      ∀ ε : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ n, 0 < ε n) → Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) →
        ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) ∧
          ∀ p : ℕ → ℝ[X],
            (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ((p n).natDegree : ℝ) < (1 + ε n) * n) →
            (∀ n, ∀ x ∈ nodes n, (p n).eval x = f x) →
              ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1)),
                ¬ Tendsto (fun n => (p n).eval t) atTop (𝓝 (f t))

is a graph $H$ with $m$ edges such that in any $2$-colouring of the edges of $H$ there is a
monochromatic copy of $G$.

Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be the union of stars. More precisely, let
$F_1=\cup_{i\leq s}K_{1,n_i}$ and $F_2=\cup_{j\leq t}K_{1,m_j}$ with
$n_1\geq\cdots\geq n_s\geq1$ and $m_1\geq\cdots\geq m_t\geq1$. Prove that
$$\hat{R}(F_1,F_2)=\sum_{2\leq k\leq s+t}l_k$$
where
$$l_k=\max\{n_i+m_j-1:i+j=k\}.$$

The unions are vertex-disjoint, and $s,t\geq1$. Lean indices start at zero, so the condition
$i+j=k$ is represented by $(i+1)+(j+1)=k$.

    ∀ (s t : ℕ), 1 ≤ s → 1 ≤ t →
    ∀ (n : Fin s → ℕ) (m : Fin t → ℕ),
      Antitone n → Antitone m → (∀ i, 1 ≤ n i) → (∀ j, 1 ≤ m j) →
      sizeRamsey F(s, n) F(t, m) =
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (s + t),
          ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin s × Fin t)).filter
            (fun p ↦ (p.1.val + 1) + (p.2.val + 1) = k)).sup
              (fun p ↦ n p.1 + m p.2 - 1)

problems.title: Graceful Tree Conjecture (Ringel–Kotzig conjecture)
problems.statement:
Every tree admits a graceful labeling.

A graceful labeling of a tree $T$ with $m$ edges is an injective map $f : V \to \{0, \dots, m\}$
such that the multiset of absolute differences $|f(u) - f(v)|$ over edges $\{u,v\}$ of $T$
equals $\{1, \dots, m\}$.

theorem graceful_tree_conjecture {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (T : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel T.Adj] (hT : T.IsTree) :
    let m := T.edgeFinset.card
    ∃ f : V → ℕ,
      Function.Injective f ∧
      (∀ v, f v ≤ m) ∧
      T.edgeFinset.image (fun e =>
        e.lift ⟨fun u v => Int.natAbs ((f u : ℤ) - (f v : ℤ)),
                fun u v => by
                  show ((f u : ℤ) - f v).natAbs = ((f v : ℤ) - f u).natAbs
                  rw [← Int.natAbs_neg, neg_sub]⟩) = Finset.Icc 1 m

$n$ is prime (with a specific exception for $n^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{r}$)?

remains a conjecture.

    ∀ (n r : ℕ), n > 1 → r > 0 → n.gcd r = 1 →
      let R := Polynomial (ZMod n)
      let X : R := Polynomial.X
      let I : Ideal R := Ideal.span ({X^r - 1} : Set R)
      Ideal.Quotient.mk I ((X - 1)^n) = Ideal.Quotient.mk I (X^n - 1) →
      (n.Prime ∨ (n^2 : ZMod r) = 1)

vertices. If $\delta(G) \geq \frac{n + k(k-1)}{k+1}$, then for every longest cycle $C$ of $G$,
every path in $G - V(C)$ has at most $k-1$ vertices.

The bound on the number of vertices of a path is written as `+ 1 ≤ k` rather than `≤ k - 1`,
because subtraction on `ℕ` is truncated. The two forms agree for `k ≥ 1`.

A longest cycle is a cycle whose length is the circumference of `G`.

    ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj], IsKConnected G k →
      ((Fintype.card V : ℝ) + k * (k - 1)) / (k + 1) ≤ G.minDegree →
      ∀ (a : V) (C : G.Walk a a), C.IsCycle → C.length = G.circumference →
      ∀ (u v : offWalk C) (P : (G.induce (offWalk C)).Walk u v), P.IsPath →
        P.support.length + 1 ≤ k

problems.statement:
**The Bateman-Horn Conjecture**
Given a finite collection of distinct irreducible polynomials non-constant $f_1, f_2, \dots, f_k \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$
with positive leading coefficients that satisfy the Schinzel condition, the number
of positive integers $n \leq x$ for which all polynomials $f_i$ are simultaneously prime is
asymptotic to:
$$\frac{C}{D} \frac{x}{(\log x)^k}$$
where $D = \prod_i \deg(f_i)$ and $C$ is the Bateman-Horn constant given by the convergent
infinite product:
$$C = \prod_{p\in\mathbb{P}} (1 - 1/p)^{-k} (1 - \omega_p/p)$$
Here $\omega_p$ is the number of residue classes modulo $p$ for which at least one polynomial
vanishes. The product is only conditionally convergent: it is the limit as $N \to \infty$ of the
partial products over the primes $p < N$.

The Schinzel condition ensures that for each prime $p$, there exists some integer $n$
such that $p$ does not divide the product $f_1(n) f_2(n) \dotsb f_k(n)$, which guarantees the
infinite product converges to a positive value.
problems.lean:
theorem bateman_horn_conjecture
    (polys : Finset ℤ[X])
    (h_nonempty : polys.Nonempty)
    (h_irreducible : ∀ f ∈ polys, BunyakovskyCondition f)
    (h_compat : SchinzelCondition polys) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ Tendsto (BatemanHornPartialProduct polys) atTop (𝓝 C) ∧
      (fun x : ℝ => (CountSimultaneousPrimes polys x : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
        (fun x : ℝ => C / DegreesProduct polys * x / (Real.log x) ^ polys.card)

problems.title: Beaver Math Olympiad (BMO) — beaver math olympiad problem 1
problems.statement:
[BMO#1](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#1._1RB1RE_1LC0RA_0RD1LB_---1RC_1LF1RE_0LB0LE_(bbch))

Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$ and $(b_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be two sequences such that $(a_1, b_1) = (1, 2)$ and

$$(a_{n+1}, b_{n+1}) = \begin{cases}
(a_n-b_n, 4b_n+2) & \text{if }a_n \ge b_n \cr
(2a_n+1, b_n-a_n) & \text{if }a_n < b_n
\end{cases}$$

for all positive integers $n$. Does there exist a positive integer $i$ such that $a_i = b_i$?

The first 10 values of $(a_n, b_n)$ are $(1, 2), (3, 1), (2, 6), (5, 4), (1, 18), (3, 17),
(7, 14), (15, 7), (8, 30), (17, 22)$.

[BMO#1](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#1._1RB1RE_1LC0RA_0RD1LB_---1RC_1LF1RE_0LB0LE_(bbch)) is equivalent to asking whether the 6-state Turing machine
[`1RB1RE_1LC0RA_0RD1LB_---1RC_1LF1RE_0LB0LE`](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/1RB1RE_1LC0RA_0RD1LB_---1RC_1LF1RE_0LB0LE) halts or not.

There is presently no consensus on whether the machine halts or not, hence the problem is tagged
as a `question`.

The machine was discovered by [bbchallenge.org](https://bbchallenge.org) contributor Jason Yuen on
June 25th 2024.
problems.lean:
theorem beaver_math_olympiad_problem_1 :
    ∀ᵉ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (b : ℕ → ℕ)
    (a_ini : a 0 = 1)
    (a_rec : ∀ n, a (n + 1) = if b n ≤ a n then a n - b n else 2 * a n + 1)
    (b_ini : b 0 = 2)
    (b_rec : ∀ n, b (n + 1) = if b n ≤ a n then 4 * b n + 2 else b n - a n),
    ∃ i, a i = b i

problems.title: Beaver Math Olympiad (BMO) — beaver math olympiad problem 5
problems.statement:
[BMO#5](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#5._1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE_(bbch))

Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$ and $(b_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be two sequences such that $(a_1, b_1) = (0, 5)$ and

$$(a_{n+1}, b_{n+1}) = \begin{cases}
(a_n+1, b_n-f(a_n)) & \text{if } b_n \ge f(a_n) \cr
(a_n, 3b_n+a_n+5) & \text{if } b_n < f(a_n)
\end{cases}$$

where $f(x)=10\cdot 2^x-1$ for all non-negative integers $x$.

Does there exist a positive integer $i$ such that $b_i = f(a_i)-1$?

[BMO#5](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#5._1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE_(bbch)) is equivalent to asking whether the 6-state Turing machine
[`1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE`](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE) halts or not.

There is presently no consensus on whether the machine halts or not, hence the problem is tagged
as a `question`.

The machine was discovered by [bbchallenge.org](https://bbchallenge.org) contributor mxdys
on August 7th 2024.

The correspondence between the machine's halting problem and the below reformulation has been proven
in [Rocq](https://github.com/ccz181078/busycoq/blob/BB6/verify/1RB0LD_1LC0RA_1RA1LB_1LA1LE_1RF0LC_---0RE.v).
problems.lean:
theorem beaver_math_olympiad_problem_5 :
    ∀ (a b f : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ᵉ (hf : f = fun x ↦ 10 * 2 ^ x - 1)
    (a_ini : a 0 = 0) (b_ini : b 0 = 5)
    (a_rec : ∀ n, a (n + 1) = if f (a n) ≤ b n then a n + 1 else a n)
    (b_rec : ∀ n, b (n+1) = if f (a n) ≤ b n then b n - f (a n) else 3 * b n + a n + 5),
    ∃ i, b i = f (a i) - 1

problems.title: Beaver Math Olympiad (BMO) — beaver math olympiad problem 8
problems.statement:
[BMO#8](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#8._1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA_(bbch))

Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$ and $(b_n)_{n \ge 1}$ be two sequences such that $(a_1, b_1) = (10, 12)$ and

$$(a_{n+1}, b_{n+1}) = \begin{cases}
(a_n - \lfloor b_n/2 \rfloor - 3, 3 \lfloor (b_n+1)/2 \rfloor + 6) & \text{if } a_n > \lfloor b_n/2 \rfloor \cr
(3 a_n + 5, b_n - 2 a_n) & \text{if } a_n \le \lfloor b_n/2 \rfloor
\end{cases}$$

for all positive integers $n$.  Does there exist a positive integer $i$ such that
$a_i = \lfloor b_i/2 \rfloor + 1$?

[BMO#8](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#8._1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA_(bbch)) is equivalent to asking whether the 6-state Turing machine
[`1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA`](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/1RB0LD_0RC1RB_0RD0RA_1LE0RD_1LF---_0LA1LA) halts or not.

There is presently no consensus on whether the machine halts or not, hence the problem is tagged
as a `question`.
problems.lean:
theorem beaver_math_olympiad_problem_8 :
    ∀ᵉ (a : ℕ → ℤ) (b : ℕ → ℤ)
    (a_ini : a 0 = 10)
    (a_rec : ∀ n, a (n + 1) =
      if b n / 2 < a n then a n - b n / 2 - 3 else 3 * a n + 5)
    (b_ini : b 0 = 12)
    (b_rec : ∀ n, b (n + 1) =
      if b n / 2 < a n then 3 * ((b n + 1) / 2) + 6 else b n - 2 * a n),
    ∃ i, a i = b i / 2 + 1

problems.title: Chowla's Conjecture
problems.statement:
**Chowla's Conjecture** [Ch65, p. 96]: for every $k \ge 1$ and every injective shift tuple
`h : Fin k → ℕ`, the Cesàro average $\frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=1}^N \prod_{i < k} \lambda(n + h_i)$
tends to $0$ as $N \to \infty$. This linear-shift correlation is the special case
$f(x) = \prod_{i < k} (x + h_i)$ of Chowla's polynomial conjecture [Ch65]. The hypothesis `1 ≤ k`
excludes the empty product $1$, and injectivity excludes repeated factors $\lambda(n + h)^2 = 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem chowla_liouville_conjecture (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (h : Fin k → ℕ)
    (hh : Function.Injective h) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun N : ℕ ↦
        (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∏ i : Fin k, (ArithmeticFunction.liouville (n + h i) : ℝ)) /
          (N : ℝ))
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

problems.title: Cohen–Lenstra Heuristic (Imaginary Quadratic Case, $u = 0$)
problems.statement:
**Cohen–Lenstra Heuristic (Imaginary Quadratic Case, $u = 0$)** [CL84; Co93, §5.10]: given an
odd prime $p$ and finite abelian $p$-group $G$, the fraction of imaginary quadratic discriminants
$|D(d)| \le X$ whose $p$-Sylow class-group subgroup is isomorphic to $G$ tends to
`cohenLenstraWeight p 0 G`. (Wikipedia notes only the existence of the heuristics and their
$\approx 75.45\%$ real-quadratic prediction; this odd-$p$-part formula comes from [CL84] and
[Co93, §5.10].)
problems.lean:
theorem cohen_lenstra_imaginary_quadratic_p_sylow_conjecture (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] [Fintype G] (hG : IsPGroup p G) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun X : ℕ =>
        (((imagQuadRadicandsUpTo X).filter (HasQuadPSylowIso p G)).card : ℝ) /
          ((imagQuadRadicandsUpTo X).card : ℝ))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (cohenLenstraWeight p 0 G))

problems.title: Cohen–Lenstra Heuristic (Real Quadratic Case, $u = 1$)
problems.statement:
**Cohen–Lenstra Heuristic (Real Quadratic Case, $u = 1$)** [CL84; Co93, §5.10]: given an odd
prime $p$ and finite abelian $p$-group $G$, the fraction of real quadratic discriminants
$0 < D(d) \le X$ whose $p$-Sylow class-group subgroup is isomorphic to $G$ tends to
`cohenLenstraWeight p 1 G`. (Wikipedia notes only the existence of the heuristics and their
$\approx 75.45\%$ prediction; this odd-$p$-part formula comes from [CL84] and [Co93, §5.10].)
problems.lean:
theorem cohen_lenstra_real_quadratic_p_sylow_conjecture (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] [Fintype G] (hG : IsPGroup p G) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun X : ℕ =>
        (((realQuadRadicandsUpTo X).filter (HasQuadPSylowIso p G)).card : ℝ) /
          ((realQuadRadicandsUpTo X).card : ℝ))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (cohenLenstraWeight p 1 G))

problems.title: The $\frac 1 3$–$\frac 2 3$ conjecture
problems.statement:
Does every finite partially ordered set that is not totally ordered
contain two elements $x$ and $y$ such that the probability that
$x$ appears before $y$ in a random linear extension is between $\frac 1 3$ and $\frac 2 3$?

The set of all total order extensions is represented as order preserving
bijections $P$ of $1, ..., n$.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture_1_3_to_2_3 : ∀ (P : Type) [Finite P] [PartialOrder P]
    (not_total : ¬ Std.Total (α := P) (· ≤ ·)) (total_ext : Set <| OrderHom P ℕ)
    (total_ext_def : ∀ σ, σ ∈ total_ext ↔ Set.range σ = Set.Icc 1 (Nat.card P)),
    ∃ x y : P, ({σ ∈ total_ext | σ x < σ y}.ncard / total_ext.ncard : ℚ)
      ∈ Set.Icc (1/3) (2/3)

problems.title: Determinantal conjecture
problems.statement:
Does the determinant of the sum $A + B$ of two $n \times n$ normal
complex matrices $A$ and $B$ always lie in the convex hull
of the $n!$ points $\prod\_i (\lambda(A)\_i + \lambda(B)\_{\sigma(i)})$?
Here the numbers $\lambda(A)\_i$ and $\lambda(B)\_i$ are
the eigenvalues of $A$ and $B$, and $\sigma$ is an element of the symmetric
group $S\_n$.
problems.lean:
theorem determinantal_conjecture
    (n : Type) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (d1 d2 : n → ℂ) (U1 U2 : unitary (Matrix n n ℂ)) :
    (U1 * Matrix.diagonal d1 * star U1 + U2 * Matrix.diagonal d2 * star U2).det
      ∈ convexHull ℝ { ∏ i, (d1 i + d2 (σ i)) | σ : Equiv.Perm n }

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1002
problems.statement:
For any $0<\alpha<1$, let $f(\alpha,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{ \alpha k\})$. Does $f(\alpha,n)$ have an asymptotic distribution function?

In other words, is there a non-decreasing function $g$ such that $g(-\infty)=0$, $g(\infty)=1$,
and $\lim_{n\to \infty}\lvert \{ \alpha\in (0,1): f(\alpha,n)\leq c\}\rvert=g(c)$?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1002 :
    ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone g ∧
    Tendsto g atBot (𝓝 0) ∧
    Tendsto g atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
    letI f :=  fun (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) ↦
      (1 / log n) * ∑ k ∈ Icc (1 : ℕ) n, (1 / 2 - Int.fract (α * k))
    ∀ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (volume { α | α ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ f α n ≤ c }).toReal)
      atTop (𝓝 (g c))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1004
problems.statement:
For any fixed c > 0, if x is sufficiently large then there exists n ≤ x such that
the values of φ(n+k) are all distinct for 1 ≤ k ≤ (log x)^c.
This is an open problem.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1004 :
    ∀ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ n ≤ x,
      IsDistinctTotientRun n ⌊(Real.log (x : ℝ)) ^ c⌋₊

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1030
problems.statement:
Let $R(k,l)$ be the usual Ramsey number: the smallest $n$ such that if the edges of $K_n$ are
coloured red and blue then there exists either a red $K_k$ or a blue $K_l$.

Prove the existence of some $c>0$ such that
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}\frac{R(k+1,k)}{R(k,k)}> 1+c.$$

A problem of Erdős and Sós.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1030 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ L : ℝ,
      Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦
        (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey (k + 1) k : ℝ) /
          (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey k k : ℝ)) atTop (nhds L) ∧
      L > 1 + c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1035
problems.statement:
Is there a constant $c > 0$ such that every graph on $2^n$ vertices with minimum degree
$> (1-c) \cdot 2^n$ contains the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$?

This is Erdős's question [Er93, p. 345].

See also [576] for the extremal number of edges that guarantee a $Q_n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1035 :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 ^ n))) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      (∀ v, (G.degree v : ℝ) > (1 - c) * 2 ^ n) →
        (SimpleGraph.hypercube n).IsContained G

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1056
problems.statement:
Let $k ≥ 2$. Does there exist a prime $p$ and consecutive intervals $I_0,\dots,I_k$
such that $\prod\limits_{n{\in}I_i}n \equiv 1 \mod n$ for all $1 \le i \le k$?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1056 :
    ∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (boundaries : Fin (k + 1) → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono boundaries),
    AllModProdEqualsOne p boundaries

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1060 — i
problems.statement:
The conjecture is about the function $f(n)$ which counts the number of solutions to
$k\sigma(k)=n$, where $\sigma(k)$ is the sum of divisors of $k$. The first bound is that $f(n)$ grows slower
than any power of $n^(\frac{1}{\log\log n})$. The second bound is that $f(n)$ is at most a power of
$\log n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1060.parts.i :
    ∃ h : ℕ → ℝ,
      h =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ 1 / log (log n)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, #{k ≤ n | k * σ 1 k = n} ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ h n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1060 — ii
problems.statement: Part (ii) of Erdős Problem 1060: bound on the number of $k \le n$ with $k \sigma_1(k) = n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1060.parts.ii :
    ∃ (C : ℝ), (fun n ↦ (#{k ≤ n | k * σ 1 k = n} : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun n ↦ log n ^ C)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1070 — i
problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that, given any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, there exist $f(n)$ points
such that no two are distance $1$ apart. Estimate $f(n)$. In particular, is it true that
$f(n)\geq n/4$?

This is the first part, a problem of Erdős [Er87b, p. 171]. Since $f(n)=\Theta(n)$ is already
known, we ask for $\lim f(n)/n$. The limit exists by Fekete's lemma, since placing two
configurations far apart shows $f(a+b) \leq f(a)+f(b)$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1070.parts.i :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 erdos_1070.parts.i.answer)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1075
problems.statement:
Let $r\geq 3$. There exists $c_r>r^{-r}$ such that, for any $\epsilon>0$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large, the following holds. Any $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with at least
$(1+\epsilon)(n/r)^r$ many edges contains a subgraph on $m$ vertices with at least $c_rm^r$ edges,
where $m=m(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1075 :
    ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → ∃ c : ℝ, (r : ℝ)⁻¹ ^ r < c ∧
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ m : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto m atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)),
        H.IsUniform r → (1 + ε) * ((n : ℝ) / r) ^ r ≤ H.card →
          ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card = m n ∧
            c * (S.card : ℝ) ^ r ≤ (H.hypergraphInduce S).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 108
problems.statement:
For every r ≥ 4 and k ≥ 2 is there some finite f(k,r) such that every graph of chromatic number ≥ f(k,r)
contains a subgraph of girth ≥ r and chromatic number ≥ k?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_108 :
    ∀ r ≥ 4, ∀ k ≥ (2 : ℕ), ∃ (f : ℕ),
    ∀ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V) (_ : Nonempty V)
      (hchro : f ≤ SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber G),
    ∃ (H : G.Subgraph), (SimpleGraph.girth H.coe ≥ r) ∧
    (SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber H.coe ≥ k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 11
problems.statement: Is every large odd integer $n$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_11 :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Odd n → ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1100 — iii
problems.statement:
Let
$$g(k) = \max_{\omega(n)=k}\tau_\perp(n),$$
where $\omega(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$, and $n$ is restricted to
squarefree integers. Determine the growth of $g(k)$.

This is the third part. We read "determine the growth" as $g(k)=\Theta(\texttt{answer}\ k)$. Known
bounds are $(\sqrt2+o(1))^k<g(k)<(2-c)^k$ [Er81h, p. 173] (see
`erdos_1100.variants.erdos_simonovits`), and $g(k)\leq 3\cdot(3\cdot 2^{-2/3})^k$
[ErTe89, Theorem 1] (see `erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_g`). So $g$ is at most exponential,
the lower bound announced in [Er81h] would make it exponential, and already the base of the
exponential is open.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1100.parts.iii :
    (fun k : ℕ ↦ (g k : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_1100.parts.iii.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1110
problems.statement:
Let $p>q\geq 2$ be two coprime integers. We call $n$ representable if it is the sum of
integers of the form $p^kq^l$, none of which divide each other.

If $\{p,q\}\neq \{2,3\}$ then what can be said about the density of non-representable
numbers? Are there infinitely many coprime non-representable numbers, that is, an infinite
family of pairwise coprime non-representable integers?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1110 :
    ∀ (p q : ℕ), q < p → 2 ≤ q →
      Nat.Coprime p q → ¬(p = 3 ∧ q = 2) →
      ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧
        ∀ n ∈ A, ¬Representable p q n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1111
problems.statement:
If $G$ is a finite graph and $A,B$ are disjoint sets of vertices then we call $A,B$ anticomplete
if there are no edges between $A$ and $B$.

If $t,c\geq 1$ then there exists $d\geq 1$ such that if $\chi(G)\geq d$ and $\omega(G)<t$ then
there are anticomplete sets $A,B$ with $\chi(A)\geq \chi(B)\geq c$.

El-Zahar and Erdős [ElEr85] pose this as a question. Here $\chi(A)$ is the chromatic number of
the induced subgraph $G[A]$. Swapping $A$ and $B$, the conclusion says that both $\chi(A)$ and
$\chi(B)$ are at least $c$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1111 :
    ∀ t c : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → 1 ≤ c → ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧
      ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        (d : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → G.CliqueFree t →
          ∃ A B : Set V, Anticomplete G A B ∧
            (c : ℕ∞) ≤ (G.induce A).chromaticNumber ∧
            (c : ℕ∞) ≤ (G.induce B).chromaticNumber

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1132 — i
problems.statement:
For $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in [-1,1]$ let
$$l_k(x)=\frac{\prod_{i\neq k}(x-x_i)}{\prod_{i\neq k}(x_k-x_i)},$$
which are such that $l_k(x_k)=1$ and $l_k(x_i)=0$ for $i\neq k$.

Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots\in [-1,1]$ be an infinite sequence, and let
$$L_n(x) = \sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\lvert l_k(x)\rvert,$$
where each $l_k(x)$ is defined above with respect to $x_1,\ldots,x_n$.

Must there exist $x\in (-1,1)$ such that
$$L_n(x) >\frac{2}{\pi}\log n-O(1)$$
for infinitely many $n$?

This is the first part, asked in [Er67, p. 68] (see also [Va99, 2.43]); [Er61c, (4)] states it as
"quite possibly true". Both papers consider an arbitrary triangular array of nodes; as on the
problem page, we take the first $n$ terms of one sequence, a special case. The nodes are required
to be distinct, so that $l_k$ is defined. We let the constant $C$ in $O(1)$ depend on the sequence
and on $x$, the weakest reading. In [Er61c, (4)] it is an absolute constant.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1132.parts.i :
    ∀ x : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, x k ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) → Function.Injective x →
      ∃ t ∈ Set.Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1, ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1132 — ii
problems.statement:
For $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in [-1,1]$ let
$$l_k(x)=\frac{\prod_{i\neq k}(x-x_i)}{\prod_{i\neq k}(x_k-x_i)},$$
which are such that $l_k(x_k)=1$ and $l_k(x_i)=0$ for $i\neq k$.

Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots\in [-1,1]$ be an infinite sequence, and let
$$L_n(x) = \sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\lvert l_k(x)\rvert,$$
where each $l_k(x)$ is defined above with respect to $x_1,\ldots,x_n$.

Is it true that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{L_n(x)}{\log n}\geq \frac{2}{\pi}$$
for almost all $x\in (-1,1)$?

This is the second part, asked in [Er67, p. 68] ("Perhaps (7) holds for almost all $x_0$"), again
for triangular arrays. The nodes are required to be distinct. We write the $\limsup$ condition as:
for every $\varepsilon>0$, there are infinitely many $n$ with
$$L_n(x)\geq\left(\frac{2}{\pi}-\varepsilon\right)\log n.$$
This is equivalent, and avoids the junk value of a real `limsup` of an unbounded sequence.

The problem page says that a result of Bernstein [Be31] implies that the set of such $x$ is
everywhere dense. In [Er67, p. 68] Erdős derives this from his own unpublished bound (6), which
sharpens a result of Bernstein. It also follows from `erdos_1132.variants.tao` with
$\omega(n)=\log\log n$.

        ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
          (2 / Real.pi - ε) * Real.log n ≤ lebesgueFunction n x t

that
$$2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha + 1)_{\alpha < \gamma}^{r+1}$$
implies
$$\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha < \gamma}^r?$$

if $\kappa_\alpha$ is infinite.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1174, part (i)
problems.statement:
**Erdős Problem 1174, part (i)** [Va99, 7.91]. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal:
does there exist a graph $G$ with no $K_4$ such that every edge colouring of $G$
with countably many colours contains a monochromatic $K_3$?

For simplicity the colourings are given on all unordered pairs $\operatorname{Sym}_2(V)$;
only the values on the edges of $G$ matter, since a monochromatic triangle is witnessed by
edges alone.

Shelah proved that a graph with this property can consistently exist, so the
problem is not disprovable in ZFC; whether such a graph exists outright remains open.

    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
      ∀ c : Sym2 V → ℕ, ∃ x y z : V,

        c s(x, y) = c s(y, z) ∧ c s(y, z) = c s(x, z)

**Erdős Problem 1174, part (ii)** [Va99, 7.91]. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal:
does there exist a graph $G$ with no $K_{\aleph_1}$ (that is, every clique of $G$
is countable) such that every edge colouring of $G$ with countably many colours
contains a monochromatic $K_{\aleph_0}$ (an infinite clique all of whose edges
receive the same colour)?

For simplicity the colourings are given on all unordered pairs $\operatorname{Sym}_2(V)$;
only the values on the edges of $G$ matter.

Shelah proved that a graph with this property can consistently exist, so the
problem is not disprovable in ZFC; whether such a graph exists outright remains open.

    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (∀ S : Set V, G.IsClique S → #S ≤ ℵ₀) ∧

        ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x ≠ y → c s(x, y) = k

Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$. Is it true that there is a colouring of the
edges with $\aleph_1$ many colours such that, in any countable colouring of the vertices, there
exists a vertex colour containing all edge colours?

problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that in any $2$-colouring of the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there is
always a monochromatic family of at least $f(n)$ sets which is closed under taking unions and
intersections. Estimate $f(n)$.

Let $F(n)$ be defined similarly, except that we only require the family be closed under taking
unions. Estimate $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)\geq n^{\omega(n)}$ for some
$\omega(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$, and $F(n)<(1+o(1))^n$?

$f(n)=\Theta(\text{answer})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1189 — i
problems.statement:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

This is the first part of the questions of Erdős [Er80, p. 95]. We read "how many" as asking for
the asymptotics of $\log I(k)$, where $I(k)$ is the number of irreducible covering sets of size
$k$; this is the scale on which the number of minimal covering systems is known [BBMST24].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1189 — ii
problems.statement:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

size $k$. The answer is a pair (minimum, maximum), stated for each $k$ for which an irreducible
covering set of size $k$ exists.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 683
problems.statement:
Let $P(n, k)$ be the largest prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$.
There exists $c > 0$ such that $P(n, k) \ge \min(n - k + 1, k^{1 + c})$ for all $0 < k \le n/2$.

Erdős stated this for $1 \le k \le n$ with the bound $\min(n-k+1, k^{1+c})$ [Er79d]. The
minimum is needed even for $k \le n/2$: at $n = 2k$ every prime factor of $\binom{2k}{k}$ is at
most $2k$, so $P(n, k) \ge k^{1+c}$ fails for large $k$. The range $k \le n/2$ is natural
(cf. [#961](https://www.erdosproblems.com/961) and the
[discussion](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/683)).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_683 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 →
      (P n k : ℝ) ≥ min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) ((k : ℝ) ^ (1 + c))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 685 — i
problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ and let $n$ be large depending on $\epsilon$. Is it true that for all
$n^{\epsilon} < k \leq n^{1-\epsilon}$ the number of distinct prime divisors of $\binom{n}{k}$ is
$$(1+o(1))\, k \sum_{k < p < n} \frac{1}{p}?$$

The $o(1)$ is uniform in $k$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_685.parts.i :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ,
      (n : ℝ) ^ ε < (k : ℝ) → (k : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) →
        |(ω (n.choose k) : ℝ) - (k : ℝ) * primeRecipSum k n| ≤
          δ * ((k : ℝ) * primeRecipSum k n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 685 — ii
problems.statement:
Is it true that, for some constant $c > 0$, the number of distinct prime divisors of
$\binom{n}{k}$ is
$$(1+o(1))\, k \sum_{k < p < n} \frac{1}{p}$$
even for all $(\log n)^c \leq k \leq n^{1-\epsilon}$?

Here $\epsilon > 0$ is as in the first question, and the $o(1)$ is uniform in $k$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_685.parts.ii :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ,
      Real.log (n : ℝ) ^ c ≤ (k : ℝ) → (k : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - ε) →
        |(ω (n.choose k) : ℝ) - (k : ℝ) * primeRecipSum k n| ≤
          δ * ((k : ℝ) * primeRecipSum k n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 700 — i
problems.statement:
Let $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$ and let $P(n)$ be the largest prime
dividing $n$.

**(a)** Characterise those composite $n$ such that $f(n) = n/P(n)$.

Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78] note that $f(n) = n/P(n)$ when $n$ is a product of two primes
(`erdos_700.variants.prime_mul`), with $n = 30$ a further example. The characterisation itself is
open; we state it as the (unknown) set of all composite `n` with `f n = n / P n`.

This follows the largest-prime reading on erdosproblems.com. In [ErSz78, p. 98], the first prose
line below (7) reads: "where $P(n)$ is the greatest prime power which divides $n$."
The paper's reading is stated with $Q(n)$ in `erdos_700.variants.prime_power_divisor`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_700.parts.i :
    {n : ℕ | ¬ n.Prime ∧ 1 < n ∧ f n = n / P n} = erdos_700.parts.i.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 700 — iii
problems.statement:
Let $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$.

**(c)** Is it true that, for every composite $n$, $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$ for every $A > 0$?

Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78] prove the weaker bound $f(n) \le (1 + o(1)) n/\log n$ (the case $A = 1$).
Here $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$ is spelled out as: for every `A > 0` there is a constant `C`
(depending on `A`) with `f(n) ≤ C · n/(log n)^A` for every composite `n`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_700.parts.iii :
    (∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ n.Prime → 1 < n →
      (f n : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) / (Real.log n) ^ A)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 704 — ii
problems.statement:
Let $G_n$ be the unit distance graph in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with two vertices joined by an edge if
and only if the distance between them is $1$. Does
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\chi(G_n)^{1/n}$$
exist?

This generalises the Hadwiger–Nelson problem (Erdős Problem 508), the case $n = 2$. The
chromatic number is finite (see `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.cube_colouring`).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_704.parts.ii :
    ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((unitDistanceGraph n).chromaticNumber.toNat : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ)))
      atTop (𝓝 L)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 710
problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that in $(n,n+f(n))$ there exist distinct integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$
such that $k\mid a_k$ for all $1\leq k\leq n$. Obtain an asymptotic formula for $f(n)$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_710 : (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] erdos_710.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 711 — i
problems.statement:
Let $f(n,m)$ be minimal such that $(m,m+f(n,m))$ contains distinct integers
$a_1,\ldots,a_n$ with $k \mid a_k$ for $1 \leq k \leq n$. Prove that
$\max_m f(n,m) \leq n^{1+o(1)}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_711.parts.i : ∃ error : ℕ → ℝ,
    error =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ m, ∃ L,
      HasDivisibleDistinctTuple n m L ∧ (L : ℝ) ≤ Real.rpow n (1 + error n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 719
problems.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{ex}_r(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ be the maximum number of $r$-edges that can
be placed on $n$ vertices without forming a $K_{r+1}^r$ (the $r$-uniform complete graph on
$r+1$ vertices). Is every
$r$-hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices the union of at most $\mathrm{ex}_{r}(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ many copies
of $K_r^r$ and $K_{r+1}^r$, no two of which share a $K_r^r$?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_719 :
    ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r → ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
    H.IsUniform r → ∃ D : Finset (Finset (Fin n)),
      H.IsCompleteHypergraphDecomposition r D ∧
        D.card ≤ Hypergraph.cliqueExtremalNumber n r (r + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 726
problems.statement:
As $n\to \infty$ ranges over integers
$\sum_{p\leq n}1_{n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}}\frac{1}{p}\sim \frac{\log\log n}{2}$?

A conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75].

By $n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}$ we mean $n\equiv r\pmod{p}$ for some integer $r$ with $p/2<r<p$.
The remainder `n % p` is computed in `ℕ` before casting to `ℝ`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_726 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ ∑ p ∈ (range (n + 1)).filter
        (fun p : ℕ ↦ p.Prime ∧ (p : ℝ) / 2 < ((n % p : ℕ) : ℝ)),
      (1 : ℝ) / (p : ℝ))
    ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) / 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 727
problems.statement: Let $k ≥ 2$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ hold for infinitely many $n$?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_727 : ∀ k ≥ 2,
    Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | (Nat.factorial (n + k)) ^ 2 ∣ Nat.factorial (2 * n)}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 731
problems.statement:
Find some reasonable function $f(n)$ such that, for almost all integers $n$, the least integer
$m$ such that $m\nmid \binom{2n}{n}$ satisfies
$$m\sim f(n).$$

Here "almost all" means natural density $1$, and $m \sim f(n)$ means that for every
$\varepsilon>0$ the set of $n$ with $|m/f(n)-1|<\varepsilon$ has density $1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_731 : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    {n : ℕ | |(leastNonDivisor n : ℝ) / erdos_731.answer n - 1| < ε}.HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 734
problems.statement:
Find, for all large $n$, a non-trivial pairwise balanced block design $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq
\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that, for all $t$, there are $O(n^{1/2})$ many $i$ such that $\lvert
A_i\rvert=t$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_734 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), H.IsPairwiseBalancedDesign ∧
      (∀ e ∈ H, e.card < n) ∧ ∀ t : ℕ,
        ({e ∈ H | e.card = t}.card : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.sqrt n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 739
problems.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{m}$ be an infinite cardinal and $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\mathfrak{m}$.
Is it true that, for every infinite cardinal $\mathfrak{n}< \mathfrak{m}$, there exists a subgraph
of $G$ with chromatic number $\mathfrak{n}$?

A question of Galvin [Ga73]. Komjáth [Ko88b] proved it is consistent that
$2^{\aleph_0}=2^{\aleph_1}=2^{\aleph_2}=\aleph_3$ and that there exist graphs which fail this
property (with $\mathfrak{m}=\aleph_2$ and $\mathfrak{n}=\aleph_1$), so the statement below is
not provable in ZFC (if ZFC is consistent). Shelah [Sh90] proved that, assuming the axiom of
constructibility, the answer is yes with $\mathfrak{m}=\aleph_2$ and $\mathfrak{n}=\aleph_1$. It
remains open whether the answer is yes assuming the Generalized Continuum Hypothesis (see
`erdos_739.variants.gch`), so the statement is not known to be refutable either. Consistency
results about models of ZFC are not directly formalizable inside Lean's fixed model, so only the
question is recorded here.

The subgraph need not be induced (see `erdos_739.variants.induced`). The hypothesis that
$\mathfrak{m}$ is infinite follows from $\aleph_0 \le \mathfrak{n} < \mathfrak{m}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_739 :
    ∀ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : Cardinal.{u}),
      ℵ₀ ≤ n → n < G.chromaticCardinal →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, H.coe.chromaticCardinal = n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 757
problems.statement: What is the supremum of the set of admissible numbers?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_757 {A : Set ℝ} :
    erdos_757.answer = sSup {c | IsAdmissible c}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 768
problems.statement:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ be the set of $n$ such that for every prime $p \mid n$ there is
some $d \mid n$ with $d>1$ and $d \equiv 1 \pmod p$. Is there a constant $c>0$ such that,
for all large $N$,
$$\frac{\lvert A\cap[1,N]\rvert}{N}=
\exp\big(-(c+o(1))\sqrt{\log N}\log\log N\big)?$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_768 : ∃ c > 0, ∃ error : ℕ → ℝ,
    error =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧ ∀ᶠ N in atTop,
      erdos768Density N = Real.exp (-(c + error N) * erdos768Scale N)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 770 — iii
problems.statement:
Is it true that if `p` is the greatest prime such that `p - 1 ∣ n` and `p > n ^ ε`, then
`h n = p`?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 78 — strongly explicit
problems.statement:
The strongly explicit version of `erdos_78`: an explicit family of graphs on $n$ vertices with no
clique and no independent set of size $\geq c \log n$, where each adjacency query is answered in
time polynomial in $\log n$ (see `stronglyExplicitGraph`).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_78.variants.strongly_explicit :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ adj : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, NoHomogeneousSet (stronglyExplicitGraph adj n) ⌈c * log n⌉₊

problems.title: Erdős Problem 786 — i
problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ of density $> 1 - \epsilon$
such that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when
$r = s$?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_786.parts.i : ∀ ε > 0, ε ≤ 1 →
    ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (δ : ℝ), 0 ∉ A ∧ 1 - ε < δ ∧ A.HasDensity δ ∧ A.IsMulCardSet

problems.title: Erdős Problem 81
problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a chordal graph on $n$ vertices - that is, $G$ has no induced cycles of
length greater than $3$. Can the edges of $G$ be partitioned into $n^2/6+O(n)$ many cliques?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_81 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.IsChordal →
      ∃ P : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), G.IsCliqueEdgePartition P ∧
        (P.card : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 6 + C * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 852 — i
problems.statement:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $h(x)$ be maximal such that for
some $n < x$ the numbers $d_n, d_{n+1}, \ldots, d_{n+h(x)-1}$ are all distinct [Er85c]. Estimate
$h(x)$. In particular, is it true that
$$h(x) > (\log x)^c$$
for some constant $c > 0$?

The statement avoids defining $h$. Since $h(x)$ is the longest such run, $h(x) > y$ holds exactly
when some $n < x$ starts a run of $H > y$ distinct gaps. We state the question this way, with $x$
real. We read it as asking for one $c > 0$ such that the inequality holds for all large $x$.

The primes are indexed from $p_0 = 2$, as in `primeGap`. Shifting the index by one does not change
the question.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_852.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
      ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) < x ∧ ∃ H : ℕ, (Real.log x) ^ c < (H : ℝ) ∧ DistinctGapRun n H

problems.title: Erdős Problem 852 — ii
problems.statement:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $h(x)$ be maximal such that for
some $n < x$ the numbers $d_n, d_{n+1}, \ldots, d_{n+h(x)-1}$ are all distinct [Er85c]. Estimate
$h(x)$. In particular, is it true that
$$h(x) = o(\log x)?$$

The statement avoids defining $h$. It says that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large real $x$,
every run of $H$ distinct gaps $d_n, \ldots, d_{n+H-1}$ with $n < x$ satisfies
$H \leq \varepsilon \log x$. This is $h(x) \leq \varepsilon \log x$, because $h(x)$ is the longest
such run.

The indexing is as in `Erdos852.erdos_852.parts.i`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_852.parts.ii :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
      ∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) < x → ∀ H : ℕ, DistinctGapRun n H → (H : ℝ) ≤ ε * Real.log x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 854 — i
problems.statement:
Let $n_k$ denote the $k$th primorial, i.e. the product of the first $k$ primes.

If $1=a_1<a_2<\cdots <a_{\phi(n_k)}=n_k-1$ is the sequence of integers coprime to $n_k$, then
estimate the smallest even integer not of the form $a_{i+1}-a_i$. Are there
$$\gg \max_i (a_{i+1}-a_i)$$
many even integers of the form $a_{j+1}-a_j$?

This is the first part. A problem of Erdős [Er85c, p. 80], who writes "integer" instead of "even
integer"; all differences $a_{i+1}-a_i$ are even, so only even integers are meaningful. Here
"estimate" is read as $\Theta$. Erdős first thought that for large $k$ every even $t \leq
\max_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)$ is a gap, but [Ob1] reports computations of Lacampagne and Selfridge showing
this fails for $n_6 = 30030$ (OEIS A389839 and A048670 give $20$ and $22$).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_854.parts.i :
    (fun k ↦ (minEvenNonGap k : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_854.parts.i.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 854 — ii
problems.statement:
Let $n_k$ denote the $k$th primorial, i.e. the product of the first $k$ primes.

If $1=a_1<a_2<\cdots <a_{\phi(n_k)}=n_k-1$ is the sequence of integers coprime to $n_k$, then
estimate the smallest even integer not of the form $a_{i+1}-a_i$. Are there
$$\gg \max_i (a_{i+1}-a_i)$$
many even integers of the form $a_{j+1}-a_j$?

This is the second part. We read it as: there is an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that, for all
large $k$, the number of distinct gap values is at least $c$ times the largest gap.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_854.parts.ii :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (maxGap (kthPrimorial k) : ℝ) ≤ ((gapSet (kthPrimorial k)).card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 873
problems.statement:
Let $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and let $F(A,X,k)$ count the number of $i$
such that $[a_i,a_{i+1}, \dots ,a_{i+k−1}] < X$, where the left-hand side is the least common
multiple. Is it true that, for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists some $k$ such that
$F(A,X,k) < X^\epsilon$?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_873 : ∀ᵉ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ε > (0 : ℝ)), 0 < a 0 → StrictMono a →
    ∃ k, ∀ X > 0, F a X k < (X^ε).toEReal

problems.title: Erdős Problem 875
problems.statement:
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}\subset \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that the sets
$$S_r = \{ a_1+\cdots +a_r : a_1<\cdots<a_r\in A\}$$
are disjoint for distinct $r\geq 1$. How fast can such a sequence grow? How small can
$a_{n+1}-a_n$ be? In particular, for which $c$ is it possible that $a_{n+1}-a_n\leq n^{c}$?

A problem of Deshouillers and Erdős [Er98] (an infinite version of
[874](https://www.erdosproblems.com/874)). Such sets are sometimes called admissible. We state the
last question: the set of such $c$ is `erdos_875.answer`. The bound is required for all large $n$,
since otherwise the first few $n$ would constrain the answer. The first two questions are not
formalised separately. Erdős also writes that it is not completely trivial to find such a sequence
with $a_{n+1}/a_n\to 1$ (not formalised).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_875 :
    {c : ℝ | ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsAdmissible A ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (gap A n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ c} = erdos_875.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 878 — iv
problems.statement: Find an asymptotic formula for the number of $n<x$ such that $f(n)=F(n)$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_878.parts.iv :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦
      (((Finset.Ico 1 x).filter fun n ↦ f n = F n).card : ℝ))
      ~[atTop] erdos_878.parts.iv.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 878 — v
problems.statement: Find an asymptotic formula for $H(x)=\sum_{n<x}f(n)/n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_878.parts.v :
    H ~[atTop] erdos_878.parts.v.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 878 — vi
problems.statement: Is it true that $H(x)\ll x\log\log\log\log x$?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_878.parts.vi :
    H =O[atTop] fun x : ℕ ↦
        (x : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ))))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 881
problems.statement:
Let `A ⊂ ℕ` be an additive basis of order `k` which is minimal in the sense that
if `B ⊂ A` is any infinite set, then `A \ B` is not a basis of order `k`.

Must there exist an infinite `B ⊂ A` such that `A \ B`
is an additive basis of order `k + 1`?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_881 :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ),
      IsMinimalAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder k A →
        ∃ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ A ∧ B.Infinite ∧
          (A \ B).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder (k + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 883 — i
problems.statement:
For $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ let $G(A)$ be the graph with vertex set $A$, where two
integers are joined by an edge if they are coprime.

Is it true that if
$$|A| > \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + \lfloor n/3 \rfloor - \lfloor n/6 \rfloor$$
then $G(A)$ contains all odd cycles of length $\leq n/3 + 1$?

A problem of Erdős and Sárközy [ErSa97].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_883.parts.i :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n →
      n / 2 + n / 3 - n / 6 < A.card →
      ∀ l : ℕ, Odd l → 3 ≤ l → l ≤ n / 3 + 1 →
        l ∈ (coprimeGraph.induce (A : Set ℕ)).oddCycleLengths

problems.title: Erdős Problem 890 — a
problems.statement:
If $\omega_k(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ which are $>k$, then is it true
that, for every $k\geq 1$,
$$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega_k(n+i)\leq k?$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_890.parts.a :
    ∀ k ≥ 1, liminf (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ range k, (ω_gt k (n + i) : EReal))) atTop ≤ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 890
problems.statement:
Is it true that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\left(\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\right) \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1,$$
where $\omega$ counts the number of distinct prime factors without restriction?
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_890.parts.b :
    ∀ k ≥ 1, limsup (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ range k, (ω (n + i) : EReal)) *
      (log (log n) / log n)) atTop = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 91
problems.statement:
Suppose $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ has $\lvert A\rvert=n$ and minimises the number of distinct
distances between points in $A$. Prove that for large $n$ there are at least two
(and probably many) such $A$ which are non-similar.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_91 :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ¬ UniqueMinimizer n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 911
problems.statement:
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there is
a graph $H$ with $m$ edges that is Ramsey for $G$.

Is there a function $f$ such that $f(x)/x\to \infty$ as $x\to \infty$ such that, for all large $C$,
if $G$ is a graph with $n$ vertices and $e\geq Cn$ edges then
$$\hat{R}(G) > f(C) e?$$

Here $\hat{R}(G)$ is `sizeRamsey G G`, and $G$ has at least one vertex (for $n = 0$ the
inequality fails trivially).

problems.title: Main conjecture on fusible numbers
problems.statement:
If `x` is a fusible number and `y` is its successor, then the interval `[x + 1, y + 1)` can be
divided into intervals `[ℓₙ, ℓₙ₊₁)`, such that the fusible numbers in `[ℓₙ, ℓₙ₊₁)` are obtained by
fusing the `n + 1`st successor of `x` with a fusible number.
This formalization differs from Conjecture 7.1 in the paper in four ways:
(1) it is obtained from Conjecture 7.1 by plugging in `n + 1` into `n`, which simplifies the expressions
  and removes the need to assume `n ≥ 1`;
(2) the `n + 1`st successor `s^(n+1)(x)` is replaced by the explicit value `x + (2 - 1 / 2 ^ n) * m`;
(3) instead of defining `y` to be the successor of `x`, we assert that there is no fusible number
  strictly between `x` and `y`;
(4) instead of using `∃ z, IsFusible z ∧ q = s^(n+1)(x) ~ z` we use the value of `z` determined by the equality,
  namely `z = 2 * q - 1 - s^(n+1)(x)`, and it is easy to see `z ∈ [x + 1 - m / 2 ^ n, x + 1)` as required.
problems.lean:
theorem conj_7_1 (x y q : ℚ) (n : ℕ) (fus_x : IsFusible x) (fus_y : IsFusible y) (lt : x < y)
    (nmem_Ioo : ∀ z, IsFusible z → z ∉ Set.Ioo x y) :
    let m := y - x
    let ℓ (n : ℕ) := y + 1 - m / 2 ^ n
    IsFusible q → q ∈ Set.Ico (ℓ n) (ℓ (n + 1)) → IsFusible (2 * q - 1 - x - (2 - 1 / 2 ^ n) * m)

$v$ — each copy is obtained by adding $i \pmod{2n+1}$ to every vertex of the base copy.

      (∀ i v, f i v = f 0 v + i) ∧
      Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (T.map (f i)).edgeSet (T.map (f j)).edgeSet) ∧
      ⨆ i, T.map (f i) = (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n + 1)))

problems.title: Infinitude of Wall–Sun–Sun primes — infinite isWallSunSunPrime of disc eq
problems.statement:
Let $K$ be a real quadratic field of discriminant $D$ and let $\varepsilon$ be a fundamental unit
of $K$. Following [EJ10, Remark 2.2.8], an odd prime $p \nmid D$ is a Wall–Sun–Sun prime for $K$
if, in $\mathcal{O}_K$, $\varepsilon^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$ when
$\left(\tfrac{D}{p}\right) = 1$, and $\varepsilon^{2p+2} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$ when
$\left(\tfrac{D}{p}\right) = -1$. Both exponents are even, so the condition does not depend on the
choice of $\varepsilon$, and it is equivalent to asking the same congruence for every unit of $K$.
For $K = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ and $\varepsilon = \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}$ these are the classical
Wall–Sun–Sun primes other than $2$ and $5$ [EJ10, Proposition 2.2.6].

It is conjectured that for every fundamental discriminant $D \neq 1$ there are infinitely many
Wall–Sun–Sun primes with discriminant $D$ (Wikipedia; [EJ10, §4.1] gives the heuristic for
$\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$). It is stated here for $D > 0$ only. Wikipedia's sentence also covers
$D < 0$, but [EJ10] gives the definition above only for real quadratic fields, and its literal
extension to imaginary quadratic fields is degenerate: there every unit is a root of unity of
order dividing $4$ or $6$, and that order divides the relevant exponent $p - 1$ or $2p + 2$ for
every odd prime $p \nmid D$.
problems.lean:
theorem infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    [IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K] [IsTotallyReal K] {D : ℤ} (hD : discr K = D) :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Odd p ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ D ∧ ∀ ε : (𝓞 K)ˣ,
      (p : 𝓞 K) ^ 2 ∣ (ε : 𝓞 K) ^ (if J(D | p) = 1 then p - 1 else 2 * p + 2) - 1}.Infinite

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 133
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 133](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/):

For a simple connected graph $G$,
$\operatorname{path}(G) \ge \operatorname{rad}(G) +
(\mathrm{avg}_v\, l(v))^{cC_4(G)}$,
where $\operatorname{path}(G)$ is the path number of the graph (number of vertices of a largest induced path),
$\operatorname{rad}(G)$ is the radius (minimum eccentricity, as a natural number),
$\mathrm{avg}_v\, l(v) = l(G)$ is the average independence number of vertex
neighbourhoods, and $cC_4(G)$ is the $C_4$-free characteristic function
(1 if $G$ is $C_4$-free, not necessarily induced, and 0 otherwise).
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture133 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    let rad := G.radius.toNat
    let hasC4 := ∃ a b c d : α, a ≠ b ∧ a ≠ c ∧ a ≠ d ∧ b ≠ c ∧ b ≠ d ∧ c ≠ d ∧
      G.Adj a b ∧ G.Adj b c ∧ G.Adj c d ∧ G.Adj d a
    let cC4 : ℕ := if hasC4 then 0 else 1
    (rad : ℝ) + l G ^ cC4 ≤ (path G : ℝ)

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 96
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 96](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G` on at least two vertices,
`α(G) ≤ 1 + min_v distEven(v) · (max_v l(v) - 1)`
where `α(G) = G.indepNum` is the independence number,
`distEven(v)` is the number of vertices at even distance from `v`, and
`max_v l(v)` is the maximum independence number of a vertex neighbourhood.

We record the nontrivial-graph version: the literal source inequality fails on $K_1$,
where the independence number and even-distance count are both one, but the maximum
local independence number is zero, giving $1 ≤ 0$.

problems.title: *abc* conjecture
problems.statement: For every positive real number `ε`, there exist only finitely many triples `(a, b, c)` of coprime positive integers, with `a + b = c`, such that `c > rad(abc)^(1+ε)`

theorem abc (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    {(a, b, c) : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ 0 < c ∧ ({a, b, c} : Set ℕ).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧
    a + b = c ∧ (radical <| a * b * c : ℝ)^(1 + ε) < c}.Finite

problems.title: Resolution of singularities in positive characteristic.
problems.statement:
**Resolution of singularities in positive characteristic.**
Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p > 0$ and let $X$ be an integral scheme that is
separated and of finite type over $k$. Then there is an integral scheme $Y$ that is smooth over
$k$ together with a proper birational morphism $Y \to X$.

This is open from dimension four on; see [Hau2010]. Perfectness of $k$ is needed for the
conclusion as stated; see `exists_not_hasResolution_of_not_perfectField`.
problems.lean:

    [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral X]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [QuasiCompact sX] [IsSeparated sX] :
    Scheme.HasResolution sX

problems.title: Andrica's conjecture
problems.statement:
**Andrica's conjecture**
The inequality $\sqrt{p_{n+1}}-\sqrt{p_n} < 1$ holds for all $n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime number.

problems.title: Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots
problems.statement:
**Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots**, first half.
Let $a$ be an integer that is not a square number and not $−1$. Then the set $S(a)$
of primes $p$ such that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ has a positive asymptotic
density inside the set of primes. In particular, $S(a)$ is infinite.
problems.lean:
theorem artin_primitive_roots.parts.i (a : ℤ) (ha : ¬IsSquare a) (ha' : a ≠ -1) :
    ∃ x > 0, (S a).HasDensity x {p | p.Prime}

problems.title: Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots — ii
problems.statement:
**Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots**, second half.
Write $a = a_0 b^2$ where $a_0$ is squarefree. Under the conditions that $a$ is not a perfect
power and $a_0\not\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ (sequence A85397 in the OEIS), the density of the set
$S(a)$ of primes $p$ such that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ is independent of $a$ and
equals Artin's constant.
problems.lean:
theorem artin_primitive_roots.parts.ii
    (a a_0 b : ℤ) (ha : a = a_0 * b ^ 2)
    (ha' : ∀ n m, m ≠ 1 → a ≠ n ^ m) (ha_0 : Squarefree a_0)
    (ha_0' : ¬a_0 ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4]) :
    (S a).HasDensity ArtinConstant {p | p.Prime}

problems.title: Friedland's conjecture.
problems.statement:
**Friedland's conjecture.** In the critical range $m_3 \leq (m_1 - 1)(m_2 - 1)$, and away from the
formats $(3, 2p+1, 2p+1)$, the generic rank of a tensor of format $(m_1, m_2, m_3)$ is the value
$\lceil m_1m_2m_3 / (m_1 + m_2 + m_3 - 2) \rceil$ predicted by a dimension count
[Fri12, Conjecture 5.1]. The boundary $m_3 = (m_1-1)(m_2-1)$ is settled by
`isGenericRank_of_eq_critical` [Fri12, (5.11)]. It is known for $m_1 \leq 4$ and for $(n, n, n)$,
and has been verified numerically throughout the critical range for $m_3 \leq 20$
[BFZ24, Section 4.5].
problems.lean:
theorem isGenericRank_of_le_critical {m₁ m₂ m₃ : ℕ} (h₁ : 3 ≤ m₁) (h₁₂ : m₁ ≤ m₂) (h₂₃ : m₂ ≤ m₃)
    (h : m₃ ≤ (m₁ - 1) * (m₂ - 1)) (hexc : ∀ p : ℕ, (m₁, m₂, m₃) ≠ (3, 2 * p + 1, 2 * p + 1)) :
    IsGenericRank [m₁, m₂, m₃] (m₁ * m₂ * m₃ ⌈/⌉ (m₁ + m₂ + m₃ - 2))

problems.title: Open problem.
problems.statement:
**Open problem.** Determine the maximal rank of a complex $n \times n \times n$ tensor. No formula
is known: for $n = 1, 2, 3$ the values are `1`, `3` and `5`, while for $4 \leq n \leq 7$ only
the bounds in `isMaxRank_cube_bounds`, such as $7 \leq \operatorname{mrank}(4,4,4) \leq 10$,
are available [BFZ24, (4.25)-(4.28)].
problems.lean:
theorem isMaxRank_cube {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    IsMaxRank [n, n, n] (isMaxRank_cube.answer n)

problems.title: Unique Crystal Components
problems.statement:
If $n = ab$ is a crystal, then there are no other pairs of
positive integers $c, d > 1$, different from the couple $a, b$, such that $n = cd$ and
$B(c, d) ∈ ℕ$, i.e., the components of the crystals are unique.

problems.title: Pittel's second-moment conjecture for nearly balanced markets — second moment
problems.statement:
Pittel conjectures that if $d_n \ge 1$ and $d_n/n \to 0$, then the second moment of the number
$S_n$ of stable matchings is $O((\mathbb{E}[S_n])^2)$. The bound may depend on the sequence $d_n$.
problems.lean:
theorem second_moment (d : ℕ → ℕ) (hd : ∀ n, 1 ≤ d n)
    (hd_limit : Tendsto (fun n ↦ (d n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      secondMomentNumStableMatchings n (n + d n) ≤
        C * (expectedNumStableMatchings n (n + d n)) ^ 2

      secondMomentNumStableMatchings n (n + 1) ≤
        C * (expectedNumStableMatchings n (n + 1)) ^ 2

problems.title: Multiplicative persistence

after at most eleven iterations of the digit-product map.

The bound is sharp: $277777788888899$ has multiplicative persistence eleven.

*Reference:* [arXiv:2110.04263](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.04263)
problems.lean:
theorem multiplicative_persistence_conjecture :
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ k ≤ 11, (digitProduct^[k]) n < 10

problems.title: Conjecture 1.1 (Dean, 1988).
problems.statement:
**Conjecture 1.1 (Dean, 1988).** For every integer $k \geq 3$, every finite simple graph with
minimum degree at least $k$ contains a cycle whose length is divisible by $k$.

A cycle has length at least `3`, so the divisor is never `0` and the statement is not
satisfied for a trivial reason. `SimpleGraph.minDegree` is `0` on a graph with no vertices and
on a graph with no edges, so the hypothesis excludes both.
problems.lean:
theorem dean_conjecture :
    ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj], k ≤ G.minDegree →
        ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, k ∣ m

problems.title: Conjecture 4 (Alon-Tarsi, 1985), simple-graph specialization.
problems.statement:
**Conjecture 4 (Alon-Tarsi, 1985), simple-graph specialization.** Every bridgeless simple graph
has a list of cycles covering
every edge, with $\sum_{C} |E(C)| \leq \frac{7}{5}|E(G)|$.
problems.lean:
theorem alon_tarsi_short_cycle_cover :
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
      [DecidableRel G.Adj], G.IsBridgeless →
      ∃ C : Multiset (Cycle G), IsCycleCover G C ∧
        (totalLength C : ℚ) ≤ 7 / 5 * #G.edgeFinset

problems.title: Conjecture 1 (Fonollosa, 2026).
problems.statement:
**Conjecture 1 (Fonollosa, 2026).** For every $n \geq 2$ and every
$N < 2^n - 2^{\lfloor \log_2 n\rfloor}$, no set of $n$ residues mod $N$ is valid.

Equivalently the super-increasing set $\{2^k - 1 : 0 \leq k \leq n-1\}$ attains the least
valid modulus, which is `minModulus n`.

`0 < N` excludes `N = 0`, where `ZMod 0` is `ℤ` rather than a finite modulus and `{1, 2}` is
valid, which would make the statement false for a reason unrelated to the question.
problems.lean:
theorem min_modulus :
    ∀ n N : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → 0 < N → N < minModulus n →
      ∀ A : Finset (ZMod N), #A = n → ¬ IsValidMod A

problems.title: The Balister–Győri–Schelp conjecture
problems.statement:
The **Balister–Győri–Schelp conjecture** ([Conjecture 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.08630#page=6)):
for $s \ge 2$, every zero-sum list of $2^{s-1}$ nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^s$ is the
prescribed-difference profile of a perfect matching of $\mathbb{F}_2^s$.

The equivalence $e$ indexes the two endpoints of each pair and ensures that the pairs are disjoint
and exhaust the ambient vector space.
problems.lean:
theorem balister_gyori_schelp_conjecture (s : ℕ) (hs : 2 ≤ s)
    (v : Fin (2 ^ (s - 1)) → 𝔽₂ s)
    (hv_nonzero : ∀ i, v i ≠ 0)
    (hv_sum : ∑ i, v i = 0) :
    ∃ e : Fin (2 ^ (s - 1)) × Fin 2 ≃ 𝔽₂ s,
      ∀ i, e (i, 0) + e (i, 1) = v i

problems.title: Bass conjecture for commutative integral domains, in idempotent-matrix form.
problems.statement:
**Bass conjecture for commutative integral domains, in idempotent-matrix form.**

Let `A` be an idempotent matrix over `R[G]`. If the order of `g` is not invertible in `R`, then
the Hattori–Stallings trace of the projective module represented by `A` vanishes at the conjugacy
class of `g`. This includes every infinite-order `g`, whose `orderOf` is zero. This is
Conjecture 0.6 of [BLR08]. By Theorems 0.5 (ii) and 0.7 of [BLR08] it follows from the
Farrell–Jones conjecture with coefficients in every field of prime characteristic.
problems.lean:
theorem bass_conjecture_integral_domain {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] {G : Type*}
    [Group G] {n : Type*} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n (MonoidAlgebra R G))
    (hA : A * A = A) (g : G) (hg : ¬IsUnit (orderOf g : R)) :
    matrixHattoriStallingsTraceAt A g = 0

problems.title: Babai–Seress Conjecture (Conjecture 1.7)
problems.statement:
**Babai–Seress Conjecture (Conjecture 1.7)**: There exists an absolute constant $C$ such
that every finite simple non-abelian group $G$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{diam}(G) \leq (\log |G|)^C.$$

*Reference:* [L. Babai and Á. Seress, *On the diameter of permutation groups*,
European Journal of Combinatorics 13 (1992), Conjecture 1.7](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0195-6698(05)80029-0)

    ∃ C : ℕ,
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Fintype G] [IsSimpleGroup G],
    (∃ a b : G, a * b ≠ b * a) →
    (groupDiam G : ℝ) ≤ (Real.log (Fintype.card G : ℝ)) ^ C

*Reference:* [L. Babai and Á. Seress, *On the diameter of permutation groups*,

    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ,
    (groupDiam (alternatingGroup (Fin n)) : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ C

problems.title: Balanced prime conjecture — balanced primes
problems.statement:
Let $p_k$ be the $k$-th prime number.
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that $(p_n + p_{n+2}) / 2$ is prime?

theorem balanced_primes :
    {n : ℕ | Prime ((Nat.nth Prime n + Nat.nth Prime (n + 2)) / 2)}.Infinite

problems.statement:
Let $p_k$ be the $k$-th prime number.
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that
$p_n = \dfrac{\sum_{i = 1} ^ k p_{n - i} + p_{n + i}}{2*k}$?

theorem balanced_primes_order :
    ∀ k > 0, {n : ℕ | k ≤ n ∧ 2 * k * Nat.nth Prime n = ∑ i ∈ .Ioc 0 k,

problems.title: Beaver Math Olympiad (BMO) — beaver math olympiad problem 2 antihydra
problems.statement:
[BMO#2](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Beaver_Math_Olympiad#2._Hydra_and_Antihydra)

Antihydra is a sequence starting at 8, and iterating the function
$$H(n) = \left\lfloor \frac {3n}2 \right\rfloor.$$
The conjecture states that the cumulative number of odd values in this sequence
is never more than twice the cumulative number of even values. It is a relatively new open problem
with, so it might be solvable, although seems quite hard because of its Collatz-like flavor.
The underlying Collatz-like map has been studied independently in the past,
see doi:[10.1017/S0017089508004655](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0017089508004655) (Corollary 4).

It is equivalent to non-termination of the [`1RB1RA_0LC1LE_1LD1LC_1LA0LB_1LF1RE_---0RA`](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Antihydra) 6-state Turing machine (from all-0 tape). Note that the conjecture
that the machine does not halt is based on [a probabilistic argument](https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/Antihydra#Trajectory).

This machine and its mathematical reformulations were found by [bbchallenge.org](https://bbchallenge.org)
contributors mxdys and Rachel Hunter on June 28th 2024.
problems.lean:
theorem beaver_math_olympiad_problem_2_antihydra
    (a : ℕ → ℕ) (b : ℕ → ℤ)
    (a_ini : a 0 = 8)
    (a_rec : ∀ n, a (n + 1) = (3 * a n) / 2)
    (b_ini : b 0 = 0)
    (b_rec : ∀ n, b (n + 1) = if a n % 2 = 0 then b n + 2 else b n - 1) :
    ∀ n, b n ≥ 0

problems.title: The Beck–Fiala conjecture
problems.statement:
**The Beck–Fiala conjecture**

There exists a universal constant $C > 0$ such that every set system
$S_1, \dots, S_m \subseteq [n]$ of degree at most $t$ admits a colouring
$\chi \colon [n] \to \{-1, +1\}$ with
$\left|\sum_{j \in S_i} \chi(j)\right| \le C \sqrt{t}$ for every $i$.
problems.lean:
theorem beck_fiala_conjecture :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (n m t : ℕ) (S : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ j, (Finset.univ.filter fun i => j ∈ S i).card ≤ t) →
      ∃ χ : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ j, χ j = 1 ∨ χ j = -1) ∧
        ∀ i, |∑ j ∈ S i, χ j| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t

Ahlfors and Grunsky also conjectured in [AG37] that this upper bound is the precise value of the
