theorem landauConstant_exact_value :
    landauConstant = Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (5 / 6) / Real.Gamma (1 / 6)

problems.title: The Bollobás–Eldridge–Catlin conjecture (1978).
problems.statement:
**The Bollobás–Eldridge–Catlin conjecture (1978).**

If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are graphs on the same $n$ vertices with maximum degrees $\Delta_1$,
$\Delta_2$ satisfying $(\Delta_1 + 1)(\Delta_2 + 1) \le n + 1$, then $G_1$ and $G_2$ pack.
problems.lean:
theorem bollobas_eldridge_catlin_conjecture :
    ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G₁ G₂ : SimpleGraph V)
      [DecidableRel G₁.Adj] [DecidableRel G₂.Adj],
      (G₁.maxDegree + 1) * (G₂.maxDegree + 1) ≤ Fintype.card V + 1 → Packs G₁ G₂

problems.title: Brocard's Conjecture
problems.statement:
**Brocard's Conjecture**
For every `n ≥ 2`, between the squares of the `n`-th and `(n+1)`-th primes,
there are at least four prime numbers.

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Fractional Parts of Powers — problem 10 1
problems.statement:
Problem 10.1. Are there a transcendental number $\alpha$ and a positive real
number $\xi$ such that $\lVert \xi \alpha^n \rVert$ tends to~$0$ as~$n$ tends to infinity? [Har19]
(Trivial for $|\alpha| < 1$)
problems.lean:
theorem problem_10_1 :
    ∃ (α ξ : ℝ), 1 < |α| ∧ Transcendental ℚ α ∧ 0 < ξ ∧
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ distToNearestInt (ξ * α ^ n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Fractional Parts of Powers — problem 10 2
problems.statement:
Problem 10.2. To prove that $\lVert e^n \rVert$ does not tend to 0 as n tends to
infinity.
problems.lean:
theorem problem_10_2 :
    ¬ Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ distToNearestInt (Real.exp n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Fractional Parts of Powers — problem 10 3
problems.statement:
Problem 10.3. To prove that there exists a positive real number~$c$ such
that $\lVert e^n \rVert > e^{−cn}$, for every~$n \ge 1$. Posed by Mahler [Mah53].
problems.lean:
theorem problem_10_3 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Real.exp (-c * n) < distToNearestInt (Real.exp n)

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Fractional Parts of Powers — waldschmidt
problems.statement:
Waldschmidt [Wal03] conjectured that a stronger result holds, namely
that there exists a positive real number~$c$ such that $\lVert e^n \rVert > n^{-c}$ for
every~$n \ge 2$. This is supported by metrical results [Kok45].

Note: the bound $n^{-c}$ equals $1$ when $n = 1$ for all $c$, while the distance to the nearest
integer is always at most $1/2$, so the conjecture must start at $n \ge 2$.
problems.lean:
theorem waldschmidt :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → (n : ℝ) ^ (-c) < distToNearestInt (Real.exp n)

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Confined Powers of Non-Pisot Numbers
problems.statement:
Problem 10.7. Let $\varepsilon$ be a positive real number. Are there arbitrarily
large real numbers $\alpha$ such that $\alpha$ is not a Pisot number and all the
fractional parts $\{\alpha^n\}$, $n \ge 1$, are lying in an interval of length
$\varepsilon / \alpha$? [Bug12b]
problems.lean:
theorem problem_10_7 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ M : ℝ, ∃ α : ℝ, M < α ∧ ¬ IsPisot α ∧
      ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Int.fract (α ^ n) ∈ Set.Icc c (c + ε / α)

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: $p$-adic Littlewood Conjecture
problems.statement:
Problem 10.8 ($p$-adic Littlewood conjecture). For every real number $\xi$ and
every prime number $p$,
$$\inf_{q \ge 1} q \cdot \lVert q \xi \rVert \cdot |q|_p = 0,$$
where $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ denotes the distance to the nearest integer and
$|\cdot|_p$ denotes the $p$-adic absolute value. Posed by de Mathan and
Teulié [dMT04].
problems.lean:
theorem problem_10_8 (ξ : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    sInf {x : ℝ | ∃ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q ∧
      x = q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)} = 0

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Pisot orbits on the Cantor set
problems.statement:
Problem 10.61. Let $\alpha > 2$ be a Pisot number. For every $\xi \in C(\alpha)$ the
sequence $(\xi \alpha^n)_{n \ge 1}$ is not uniformly distributed modulo one.
problems.lean:
theorem problem_10_61 (α : ℝ) (hα : IsPisot α) (hα2 : 2 < α) :
    ∀ ξ ∈ pisotCantorSet α, ¬ IsEquidistributedModuloOne fun n : ℕ => ξ * α ^ (n + 1)

problems.title: Bunyakovsky conjecture
problems.statement:
**Bunyakovsky conjecture**
If a polynomial $f$ over integers satisfies both Schinzel and Bunyakovsky conditions,
there exist infinitely many natural numbers $m$ such that $f(m)$ is prime.

problems.title: The burning number conjecture
problems.statement:
**The burning number conjecture** (Bonato–Janssen–Roshanbin [BJR16]).

Every connected graph on `n` vertices can be burned in at most `⌈√n⌉` rounds: fires started at
one new vertex per round, each spreading to all neighbouring vertices every round, can burn
the whole graph in `⌈√n⌉` rounds.
problems.lean:
theorem burning_number_conjecture {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (hc : G.Connected) :
    burningNumber G ≤ ⌈Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V)⌉₊

problems.title: Complex Hadamard conjecture for fourth roots of unity
problems.statement:
**Complex Hadamard conjecture for fourth roots of unity** [Tu70, dLF11]: for every integer
$m \ge 1$, there exists a $2m \times 2m$ Butson-type Hadamard matrix $H(4, 2m)$ with entries in
$\{1, -1, i, -i\}$.

This quaternary conjecture comes from [Tu70, dLF11] (rather than the Wikipedia page above). By
Turyn's doubling construction [Tu70], an $H(4, 2m)$ matrix yields a real Hadamard matrix
$H(2, 4m)$, so this conjecture implies Hadamard's conjecture.
problems.lean:
theorem butson_hadamard_fourth_roots_conjecture (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) :
    ∃ M, IsButsonHadamard (n := 2 * m) 4 M

problems.title: Conjecture about cardinality of Lindelöf spaces — lindelof card
problems.statement:
Is there a Lindelöf Tychonoff space with singletons as Gδ sets with cardinality greater than
the continuum?

Note: the cited paper uses a blanket convention that all spaces are Tychonoff.
problems.lean:
theorem HasGδSingletons.lindelof_card :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X),
      T35Space X ∧ HasGδSingletons X ∧ LindelofSpace X ∧ 𝔠 < #X

problems.title: Casas-Alvero Conjecture
problems.statement:
The Casas-Alvero conjecture states that in characteristic zero, if a monic polynomial `P`
has the Casas-Alvero property, then `P = (X - α)ᵈ` for some `α`.
problems.lean:
theorem casas_alvero_conjecture (hP' : HasCasasAlveroProp P) :
    ∃ α : K, P = (X - C α) ^ P.natDegree

problems.title: Catalan's conjecture and related Diophantine equations
problems.statement:
For positive integers a, b, and c, there are only finitely many positive solutions (x, y, m, n) to the
equation $ax^n - by^m = c$ where $(m, n) \neq (2, 2)$ and $x, y > 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem pillais_conjecture (a b c : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) :
    { (x, y, m, n) : (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) |
      1 < x ∧ 1 < y ∧ 1 < m ∧ 1 < n ∧ (m, n) ≠ (2, 2) ∧
      a * x^n - b * y^m = c }.Finite

problems.title: The Catch-Up game and conjecture
problems.statement:
Let $T_N = \sum_{k=1}^{N} k = \frac{N(N+1)}{2}$.
If $T_N$ is even (equivalently $N \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ or $N \equiv 3 \pmod 4$),
then under optimal play the game `Catch-Up($\{1, \ldots, N\}$)` ends in a draw.
problems.lean:
theorem value_of_even_mul_succ_self_div_two
    (N : ℕ) (h_even : Even (N * (N + 1) / 2)) :
    value (.Icc 1 N) = .draw

problems.title: Černý Conjecture
problems.statement:
**Černý Conjecture**: Every synchronizing DFA with $n$ states admits a
synchronizing word of length at most $(n - 1)^2$.
problems.lean:
theorem cerny_conjecture :
    ∀ {α : Type*} {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] (M : DFA α σ) (hM : M.IsSynchronizing) ,
    ∃ w : List α, M.IsSynchronizingWord w ∧ w.length ≤ (Fintype.card σ - 1)^2

problems.title: Chebyshev's bias — rubinstein sarnak unconditional chebyshev bias
problems.statement:
Unconditional Rubinstein–Sarnak Chebyshev bias conjecture modulo $4$ (obtained by removing GRH
and the linear independence hypothesis LI from Rubinstein and Sarnak's conditional theorem): the
set of $n \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfying $\pi(n; 4, 3) > \pi(n; 4, 1)$ admits a logarithmic density
$\delta \in (1/2, 1)$.
problems.lean:
theorem rubinstein_sarnak_unconditional_chebyshev_bias :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, (1 : ℝ) / 2 < δ ∧ δ < 1 ∧ Set.HasLogDensity chebyshevModFourLeadSet δ

problems.title: Class number problem for real quadratic fields
problems.statement:
There are infinitely many real quadratic fields `ℚ(√d)` with class number one,
where `d > 1` is a squarefree integer.
problems.lean:
theorem class_number_problem :
    { d : ℤ | Squarefree d ∧ d > 1 ∧ IsClassNumberOne d }.Infinite

problems.title: Alaoglu–Erdős Prime-Ratio Conjecture
problems.statement:
**Alaoglu–Erdős Prime-Ratio Conjecture** [AE44]: whenever $m < n$ satisfy
`AreConsecutiveColossallyAbundant m n`, $n = p m$ for some prime $p$.
problems.lean:
theorem alaoglu_erdos_colossally_abundant_prime_ratio_conjecture (m n : ℕ)
    (h : AreConsecutiveColossallyAbundant m n) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n = p * m

problems.title: Alaoglu–Erdős Rational Prime-Powers Conjecture
problems.statement:
**Alaoglu–Erdős Rational Prime-Powers Conjecture** [AE44]: if $p \ne q$ are primes and
$x \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $p^x \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $q^x \in \mathbb{Q}$, then
$x \in \mathbb{Z}$.
problems.lean:
theorem alaoglu_erdos_prime_powers_rational_conjecture (p q : ℕ) (x : ℝ)
    (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q)
    (hr₁ : ∃ r₁ : ℚ, (p : ℝ) ^ x = r₁) (hr₂ : ∃ r₂ : ℚ, (q : ℝ) ^ x = r₂) :
    ∃ k : ℤ, x = k

problems.title: Congruent Number — Tunnell even converse

    2 * (C n).ncard = (D n).ncard → congruentNumber n

problems.title: Congruent Number — Tunnell odd converse
problems.statement: Tunnell's theorem (sufficient condition assuming BSD) for odd squarefree congruent numbers.

    2 * (A n).ncard = (B n).ncard → congruentNumber n

problems.title: Markel's $S_3$-conjecture
problems.statement:
**Markel's $S_3$-conjecture** (1973): any nontrivial finite ah-group is isomorphic to $S_3$.

The conjecture is open in general; it is known to be true for solvable groups.
problems.lean:
theorem conjClassSizes_iff_sym_three
    (G : Type) [Group G] [Fintype G] [Nontrivial G]
    (h : HasDistinctConjClassSizes (G := G)) :
    Nonempty (G ≃* Equiv.Perm (Fin 3))

problems.title: Conway's 99-graph problem
problems.statement:
Does there exist an undirected graph with 99 vertices, in which each two adjacent vertices have
exactly one common neighbor, and in which each two non-adjacent vertices have exactly two common
neighbors?
Equivalently, every edge should be part of a unique triangle and every non-adjacent pair should be
one of the two diagonals of a unique 4-cycle.
The first condition is equivalent to being locally linear.
problems.lean:
theorem conway99Graph : ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin 99),
    G.LocallyLinear ∧ NonEdgesAreDiagonals G

problems.title: Cramér's Conjecture
problems.statement:
**Cramér's Conjecture** [Cr36]: consecutive prime differences satisfy
$p_{n+1} - p_n = O((\log p_n)^2)$ as $n \to \infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem cramer_conjecture :
    (fun n : ℕ => (primeGap n : ℝ)) =O[Filter.atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ => (Real.log (Nat.nth Nat.Prime n)) ^ 2)

problems.title: Cunningham chains — Jones's conjecture — infinitely many firstKind chains
problems.statement:
Jones's conjecture (first kind): for every positive integer $k$, there are
infinitely many primes $p$ that start a first-kind Cunningham chain of
exactly length $k$.
problems.lean:
theorem infinitely_many_firstKind_chains (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) :
    Set.Infinite {p : ℕ | IsFirstKindChainOfLength p k}

problems.title: Cunningham chains — Jones's conjecture — infinitely many secondKind chains
problems.statement:
Jones's conjecture (second kind): for every positive integer $k$, there are
infinitely many primes $p$ that start a second-kind Cunningham chain of
exactly length $k$.
problems.lean:
theorem infinitely_many_secondKind_chains (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) :

problems.title: Density hypothesis for Riemann zeta zeros — density hypothesis zeta zeros
problems.statement:
Density Hypothesis: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $C > 0$ such that
$N(\sigma, T) \le C \, T^{2(1 - \sigma) + \varepsilon}$ for all $\frac{1}{2} \le \sigma \le 1$
and $T \ge 2$.
problems.lean:
theorem density_hypothesis_zeta_zeros (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ σ T : ℝ, 1 / 2 ≤ σ → σ ≤ 1 → 2 ≤ T →
      (zetaZeroCount σ T : ℝ) ≤ C * T ^ (2 * (1 - σ) + ε)

problems.title: Dickson's conjecture
problems.statement:
**Dickson's conjecture**
If a finite set of linear integer forms $f_i(n) = a_i n+b_i$ satisfies Schinzel condition,
there exist infinitely many natural numbers $m$ such that $f_i(m)$ are primes for all $i$.
problems.lean:
theorem dickson_conjecture (fs : Finset ℤ[X]) (hfs : ∀ f ∈ fs, f.degree = 1 ∧ BunyakovskyCondition f)
    (hfs' : SchinzelCondition fs) : Infinite {n : ℕ | ∀ f ∈ fs, (f.eval (n : ℤ)).natAbs.Prime}

problems.title: The generalized twin-prime conjecture
problems.statement:
**The generalized twin-prime conjecture**
For any positive integer $k$ there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 2k$ is prime.
problems.lean:
theorem generalized_twin_primes (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) :
    Infinite {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ (p + 2 * k).Prime}

problems.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line — distinct prop lt
problems.statement:
Is the proportion of distinct zeros of `L(s, χ)`, `χ` primitive, unconditionally larger than

theorem distinct_prop_lt (hχ : χ.IsPrimitive) : ∃ c > (3 - montgomeryTaylorConst⁻¹) / 2,
    ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧

problems.statement:

Almost all nontrivial zeros of `L(s, χ)`, `χ` primitive, are simple and on the critical

problems.title: Dirichlet divisor problem
problems.statement:
The Dirichlet divisor problem: is it true that $\Delta(x) = O(x^{1/4 + \varepsilon})$ for every
$\varepsilon > 0$? (Equivalently, is the infimum of admissible exponents equal to $1/4$?)
problems.lean:
theorem dirichlet_divisor_problem :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), divisorError =O[atTop] fun x => x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 4 + ε)

problems.title: Dubner's conjecture
problems.statement: Every even number greater than 4208 is the sum of two twin primes.
problems.lean:
theorem dubner_conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 4208 < n) (h : Even n) :
    ∃ p q : ℕ,
      IsTwinPrime p ∧
      IsTwinPrime q ∧

problems.title: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture
problems.statement:
The Elliott–Halberstam conjecture: for every $\theta < 1$ and $A > 0$ there exists a
constant $C > 0$ such that
$$\sum_{1 \le q \le x^{\theta}} E(x; q) \le \frac{C x}{\log^A x}$$
for all $x > 2$.
problems.lean:
theorem elliott_halberstam (θ : ℝ) (hθ : θ < 1) (A : ℝ) (hA : 0 < A) :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ x : ℕ, 2 < x →
      ∑ q ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊(x : ℝ) ^ θ⌋₊, E x q ≤ C * x / Real.log x ^ A

problems.title: Goldfeld's conjecture — goldfeld conjecture
problems.statement:
**Goldfeld's conjecture** ([Goldfeld1979], Conjecture B), in the form stated in the
introduction of [Smith2025]: when the quadratic twists $E^d$ of an elliptic curve $E$ over
$\mathbb{Q}$ are ordered by $|d|$, 50% of them have rank $0$ and 50% have rank $1$. See
`goldfeld_conjecture.variants.two_le` for the remaining case $2 \leq r$.

Goldfeld states the conjecture for the analytic rank of $E^d$, which the Birch and
Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture predicts is equal to the Mordell–Weil rank used here. Corollary 1.2
of [Smith2025] proves that the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for the quadratic twist
family of $E$ implies Goldfeld's conjecture for $E$.
problems.lean:
theorem goldfeld_conjecture (E : RatEllipticCurve) (r : ℕ) (hr : r = 0 ∨ r = 1) :
    atTop.Tendsto
      (fun H ↦ ({d ∈ twistIndexLE H | E.twistRank d = r}.ncard / (twistIndexLE H).ncard : ℝ))
      (𝓝 (1 / 2))

problems.title: Some conjectures about ranks of elliptic curves over ℚ — half rank zero and half rank one
problems.statement:
Conjecture by Goldfeld and Katz–Sarnak: if elliptic curves over ℚ are ordered by their
heights, then 50% of the curves have rank 0 and 50% have rank 1.
See p. 28 of https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~matyd/BSD2011/bsd2011-Bhargava.pdf.
problems.lean:
theorem half_rank_zero_and_half_rank_one (r : ℕ) (hr : r = 0 ∨ r = 1) :
    atTop.Tendsto
      (fun H ↦ ({E ∈ heightLE H | E.rank = r}.ncard / (heightLE H).ncard : ℝ)) (𝓝 (1 / 2))

problems.title: Some conjectures about ranks of elliptic curves over ℚ — rank height count asymptotic
problems.statement:
[PPVW2016] 8.2(b): for 1 ≤ r ≤ 20, the number of elliptic curves over ℚ with rank at least
`r` and naïve height at most `H` is asymptotically `H ^ ((21 - r) / 24 + o(1))`.
Note: ℰ_H in 8.2(b) should be ℰ_{≤H}, see the statement of Theorem 7.3.3.
When `r = 1`, the exponent is `20 / 24 = 5 / 6`, which agrees with the exponent in
`card_heightLE_div_pow_five_div_six_tensto` and is consistent with
`half_rank_zero_and_half_rank_one`.
The equality is asserted only for large `H`, matching the `o(1)` above: it cannot hold
at small `H`, because `heightLE H` is empty for `H ≤ 3` (`naiveHeight E ≤ 3` forces
`A = B = 0`, which both `Δ_ne_zero` and `reduced` exclude) and consists only of the two
rank-zero curves `y² = x³ ± x` for `4 ≤ H ≤ 26`, while the right hand side is
`Real.rpow` and hence strictly positive.
problems.lean:
theorem rank_height_count_asymptotic (r : ℕ) (h₁ : 1 ≤ r) (h₂ : r ≤ 20) :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, atTop.Tendsto f (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ H : ℕ in atTop,
        {E ∈ heightLE H | r ≤ E.rank}.ncard = (H : ℝ) ^ ((21 - r) / 24 + f H)

problems.title: Some conjectures about ranks of elliptic curves over ℚ — twentyone le rank height count asymptotic
problems.statement:
[PPVW2016] 8.2(c): the number of elliptic curves over ℚ with rank ≥ 21 and naïve height
at most `H` is asymptotically at most `H ^ o(1)`.
problems.lean:
theorem twentyone_le_rank_height_count_asymptotic :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, atTop.Tendsto f (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ H : ℕ, 1 < H → {E ∈ heightLE H | 21 ≤ E.rank}.ncard ≤ (H : ℝ) ^ f H

problems.title: Prime values and primitive divisors in elliptic divisibility sequences — einsiedler everest ward finite primes
problems.statement:
Einsiedler–Everest–Ward Conjecture (2001): every non-periodic (`∀ n ≠ 0, W n ≠ 0`) normalized
nonsingular elliptic divisibility sequence takes prime values $|W_n|$ at finitely many indices
$n \ge 1$. (Einsiedler–Everest–Ward, eq. (10), p. 5 also study sequences obtained by dividing out
bad-reduction factors, which need not satisfy the elliptic divisibility recurrence.)
problems.lean:
theorem einsiedler_everest_ward_finite_primes :
    ∀ W : ℤ → ℤ,
      IsNonsingularEDS W →
      (∀ n : ℤ, n ≠ 0 → W n ≠ 0) →
      {n : ℕ | 1 ≤ n ∧ (W n).natAbs.Prime}.Finite

**Equational Theories, Problem 8.1.** Does Equation 677 imply Equation 255 in every finite

problems.title: Equidistributed Sequences — isAccumulationPoint three halves pow
problems.statement: Find an accumulation point of the sequence `(3/2)^n` modulo `1`.

theorem isAccumulationPoint_three_halves_pow :

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1182 — i
problems.statement:

has

This is the first part: estimate $f(n)$. The problem is due to Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and
Schelp [BEFRS80] and appears in [Er78, p. 33]. We read "estimate" as the order of magnitude
`=Θ`. Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp [BEFRS80, Theorem 2] proved
$n^{3/2}(\log n)^{1/2}\ll f(n)\ll n^{5/3}(\log n)^{2/3}$ (`erdos_1182.variants.f_lower`,
`erdos_1182.variants.f_upper`).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1184
problems.statement:
Let $f(n,k)$ count the number of $1\leq i\leq k$ such that $P(n+i)>k$ (where $P(m)$ is the
largest prime divisor of $m$). Is it true that, if $\alpha>1$ is such that $n=k^{\alpha+o(1)}$,
then
$$f(n,k)=(1-\rho(\alpha)+o(1))k,$$
where $\rho$ is the Dickman function?

Erdős [Er76e, p. 272] writes that it seems certain that $f(n,k)=(1-c_\alpha+o(1))k$ for
$\log n=(\alpha+o(1))\log k$, where $U(k^\alpha,k)=(c_\alpha+o(1))k^\alpha$ and $U(x,k)$ counts the
$m\leq x$ with $P(m)\leq k$; so $c_\alpha=\rho(\alpha)$. He also reports that Ramachandra, Shorey
and Tijdeman proved $f(n,k)\geq k-\pi(k)$ for $n>\exp(c(\log k)^2)$.

We read $n=k^{\alpha+o(1)}$ as: $n=n(k)$ is any function of
$k$ with $\log n(k)/\log k\to\alpha$. The conclusion is $f(n(k),k)/k\to 1-\rho(\alpha)$. This is
equivalent to the uniform statement: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $\delta>0$ and $K$ such
that $\lvert f(n,k)/k-(1-\rho(\alpha))\rvert<\varepsilon$ whenever $k\ge K$ and
$\lvert\log n/\log k-\alpha\rvert<\delta$. The Dickman function is given by `IsDickman`, which
has exactly one solution on $[0,\infty)$, so the hypothesis `IsDickman ρ` is satisfiable and
determines $\rho(\alpha)$ for $\alpha>1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1184 :
    ∀ ρ : ℝ → ℝ, IsDickman ρ → ∀ α : ℝ, 1 < α → ∀ n : ℕ → ℕ,
      Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => Real.log (n k) / Real.log k) atTop (𝓝 α) →
        Tendsto (fun k : ℕ => (f (n k) k : ℝ) / k) atTop (𝓝 (1 - ρ α))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1221 — i
problems.statement:
Let $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ be points, ordered consecutively, around the circle (normalised to have
circumference $1$). Let
$$M_r(a)=\max_r \lvert a_{i+r}-a_i\rvert$$
and
$$m_r(a)=\min_r \lvert a_{i+r}-a_i\rvert,$$
where the indices are interpreted in a cyclic fashion and the distance is around the circle (in
other words, the maximum and minimum distance between $r$-consecutive points).

Let
$$\Lambda_r=\inf_a \limsup_n n M_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
$$\lambda_r = \sup_a \liminf_n nm_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
and
$$\mu_r=\inf_a \limsup_n \frac{M_r(a)}{m_r(a)},$$
where the outer $\inf/\sup$ is over all infinite sequences $a=(a_1,\ldots)$.

Is it true that $r(\Lambda_r-1)$, $r(1-\lambda_r)$, and $r(\mu_r-1)$ tend to infinity as
$r\to \infty$?

This is the first part, conjectured by de Bruijn and Erdős [dBEr49, §6]. We read $\Lambda_r$ and
$\lambda_r$ as in `bigLambda` and `smallLambda`, that is, as printed. The sequences are required
to have pairwise distinct points modulo $1$ (see `bigLambda`). Then $nM_r\geq r$ [dBEr49, §1],
so $r(\Lambda_r-1)\to\infty$ would hold trivially. Also $m_r\geq r\,m_1$, so the sequence
$a_k=\log_2(2k-1)$ of [dBEr49, §2] gives $\lambda_r\geq r/\log 4$, which exceeds $1$ for $r\geq2$,
so $r(1-\lambda_r)$ would be negative for $r\geq2$. The intended conjectures are about the
quantities normalised by $r$, so $r(\Lambda_r/r-1)=\Lambda_r-r$, and the first part asks whether
$\Lambda_r-r\to\infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1221.parts.i :
    ∀ K : ℝ, ∀ᶠ r : ℕ in atTop, ENNReal.ofReal ((r : ℝ) + K) < bigLambda r

where the indices are interpreted in a cyclic fashion and the distance is around the circle (in
other words, the maximum and minimum distance between $r$-consecutive points).

Let
$$\Lambda_r=\inf_a \limsup_n n M_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$
$$\lambda_r = \sup_a \liminf_n nm_r(a_1,\ldots,a_n),$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1221 — iii
problems.statement:

problems.title: Erdős Problem 382 — i
problems.statement:
Let $u \leq v$ be such that the largest prime dividing $\prod_{u \leq m \leq v} m$ appears with
exponent at least $2$. Is it true that $v - u = v^{o(1)}$?

We read this as: for every $\epsilon > 0$, every such pair with $v$ large enough satisfies
$v - u \leq v^{\epsilon}$. Cambie observed that this question reduces to old conjectures on gaps
between primes; for example, it follows from Cramér's conjecture. See also Erdős Problems 380 and
383.

    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ v : ℕ in atTop, ∀ u : ℕ, LargestPrimeRepeated u v →

problems.title: Erdős Problem 408 — i
problems.statement:
Let $\phi(n)$ be the Euler totient function and $\phi_k(n)$ be the iterated $\phi$ function, so
that $\phi_1(n)=\phi(n)$ and $\phi_k(n)=\phi(\phi_{k-1}(n))$. Let
$$f(n) = \min\{k : \phi_k(n)=1\}.$$
Does $f(n)/\log n$ have a distribution function?

We ask for a distribution function $F$ (non-decreasing, with $F(-\infty) = 0$ and
$F(+\infty) = 1$) such that, for every continuity point $c$ of $F$, the set
$\{n : f(n)/\log n \leq c\}$ has natural density $F(c)$. For $n \leq 1$ the quotient is $0$ in
Lean, which does not affect densities. Erdős, Granville, Pomerance and Spiro [EGPS90] proved
that the answer is yes, conditional on a form of the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_408.parts.i :
    ∃ F : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone F ∧ Tendsto F atBot (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto F atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      ∀ c : ℝ, ContinuousAt F c →
        {n : ℕ | (f n : ℝ) / Real.log n ≤ c}.HasDensity (F c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 408 — ii
problems.statement:
Is $f(n)/\log n$ almost always constant?

We read this as: is there a constant $\alpha$ such that, for every $\epsilon > 0$, the set of
$n$ with $|f(n)/\log n - \alpha| < \epsilon$ has natural density $1$? Erdős, Granville,
Pomerance and Spiro [EGPS90] proved that, conditional on a form of the Elliott–Halberstam
conjecture, $f(n)$ has normal order $\alpha \log n$ for some constant $\alpha > 0$, so that the
answer is yes under this hypothesis.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_408.parts.ii :
    ∃ α : ℝ, ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
      {n : ℕ | |(f n : ℝ) / Real.log n - α| < ε}.HasDensity 1

If $\tau(n)$ counts the number of divisors of $n$ then let
$$F(f,n)=\frac{\tau((n+\lfloor f(n)\rfloor)!)}{\tau(n!)}.$$

$$\lim_{n\to \infty}F((\log n)^C,n)=\infty$$

"For large $C$" means for all sufficiently large real $C$. Since $(\log n)^C$ increases with $C$

such $C$.

theorem erdos_420.parts.iii :

$K_n$ so that every $X\subseteq [n]$ with $\lvert X\rvert\geq m$ contains more than

for some constant $c_\alpha$ depending only on $\alpha$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 566
problems.statement:

Is it true that, if $H$ has $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, then $R(G,H) \ll m$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 579
problems.statement:
Let $\delta > 0$. If $n$ is sufficiently large and $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with no
$K_{2,2,2}$ (the octahedron) and at least $\delta n^2$ edges, must $G$ contain an independent
set of size $\gg_\delta n$?

This is a problem of Erdős, Hajnal, Sós, and Szemerédi [EHSS83]. It is **open**; they proved
the statement for $\delta > 1/8$ (see `erdos_579.variants.ehss_large_delta`), and the
difficulty is to push the edge-density threshold down to an arbitrary $\delta > 0$.

Here $K_{2,2,2}$ is the complete tripartite graph with all parts of size $2$, encoded as
`completeMultipartiteGraph (fun _ : Fin 3 => Fin 2)`; "contains no $K_{2,2,2}$" is expressed
via `SimpleGraph.Free`.

    ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), octahedron.Free G →
        δ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
          c * n ≤ (G.indepNum : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 596
problems.statement:
**Erdős Problem 596** (Erdős–Hajnal, [Er87]). For which finite graph pairs $(G_1, G_2)$ is it
true that

  (1) for every $n \geq 1$ there is a graph $H$ without a $G_1$ such that any
      $n$-colouring of $H$'s edges contains a monochromatic $G_2$, and yet
  (2) for every graph $H$ without a $G_1$ there is an $\aleph_0$-colouring of $H$'s edges
      with no monochromatic $G_2$?

Erdős and Hajnal originally conjectured that no such pair exists; but $(C_4, C_6)$
witnesses it (Nešetřil–Rödl + Erdős–Hajnal). The full question is to characterise the
class of all such pairs, recorded here as the unknown `erdos_596.answer`.

See Problem 595 for the specific case $(G_1, G_2) = (K_4, K_3)$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_596 :
    ∀ {U₁ U₂ : Type} [Finite U₁] [Finite U₂] (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂),
      IsErdosHajnalExceptional G₁ G₂ ↔ erdos_596.answer G₁ G₂

problems.title: Erdős Problem 602
problems.statement:
Does every almost-disjoint family of countably infinite sets whose pairwise
intersections all have size ≠ 1 have Property B?

Formally: let `α` be any type, let `(A_i)_{i ∈ I}` be a family of countably infinite subsets
of `α` such that for all `i ≠ j`, the intersection `A_i ∩ A_j` is finite and
`|A_i ∩ A_j| ≠ 1`. Does there exist a 2-colouring `f : α → Fin 2` such that no `A_i` is
monochromatic?

This is an open question about Property B for almost-disjoint families with a
forbidden intersection size of 1.

**Note:** This generalises the formulation in which the ground set is `ℕ`. Since every
countably infinite set is in bijection with `ℕ`, the two formulations are equivalent, but
working over an arbitrary ground type makes the statement apply immediately to, e.g.,
almost-disjoint families of countable subsets of an uncountable space.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_602 :
    ∀ {α : Type*} {I : Type*} (A : I → Set α),
      (∀ i, (A i).Countable ∧ (A i).Infinite) →
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).Finite) →
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Set.ncard (A i ∩ A j) ≠ 1) →
      HasPropertyB I A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 611 — i
problems.statement:
For a graph $G$ let $\tau(G)$ denote the minimal number of vertices that include at least one
from each maximal clique of $G$. Is it true that if all maximal cliques in $G$ have at least $cn$
vertices then $\tau(G) = o_c(n)$?

Here $n$ is the number of vertices, and $o_c(n)$ is uniform over all such graphs on $n$ vertices.
$\tau(G)$ is `SimpleGraph.cliqueTransversalNumber`, which (as in Erdős Problem 151) ignores
maximal cliques on one vertex; this makes no difference here, since for large $n$ every maximal
clique has at least $cn \geq 2$ vertices.

        (G.cliqueTransversalNumber : ℝ) ≤ ε * (n : ℝ)

$k_c(n) \geq n^{c'/\log\log n}$ for some $c' > 0$ (as reported on erdosproblems.com).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 910 — ii
problems.statement:
If $n\geq 2$ does every connected set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ contain more than $2^{\aleph_0}$ many
connected subsets?

Erdős [Er82e, p. 77] asks this for connected sets of dimension greater than one; [Er44, p. 446]
asks, for these sets, for $2^{\mathfrak{c}}$ connected subsets. The condition $n\geq 2$ alone
would make the answer trivially no: a segment in $\mathbb{R}^2$ has only $2^{\aleph_0}$ connected
subsets, its intervals. So we require `1 < smallInductiveDimension X`, which agrees with the
covering dimension for subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. As in `erdos_910.parts.i`, single points are not
counted as connected sets [Er44, p. 445].

Rudin's set $M$ [Ru58] has at most $2^{\aleph_0}$ connected subsets, since each one with more than
one point is $M$ minus a countable set. But $M$ lies in Rudin's continuum
$I=\bigcap_n\Gamma_n^*$, where each $\Gamma_n$ is a chain of $2$-cells whose links have diameter

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 21
problems.statement:
Suppose that $a_1, \dots, a_k$ are integers which do not satisfy Rado's condition: thus if
$\sum_{i \in I} a_i = 0$ then $I = \emptyset$. It then follows from Rado's theorem that the
equation $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$ is not partition regular. Write $c(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ for
the least number of colours required in order to colour $\mathbb{N}$ so that there is no
monochromatic solution to $a_1x_1 + \cdots + a_kx_k = 0$. Is $c(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ bounded in
terms of $k$ only?

This problem, which is known as Rado's boundedness conjecture, dates back to 1933 [Ra33]. It is
open for all $k \geq 4$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_21 : ∃ B : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ (k : ℕ) (a : Fin k → ℤ),
    ¬ RadoCondition a → minColours a ≤ B k

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 5
problems.statement:
Which finite groups have the smallest biggest product-free sets?

We formalise this as: determine the supremum of exponents $\alpha$ such that every nontrivial
finite group of order $n$ contains a product-free set of size $\geq c n^{\alpha}$ for some
absolute constant $c > 0$. (The trivial group is excluded since its only product-free subset
is empty.) Kedlaya [Ke97] showed that $\alpha = 11/14$ is admissible, and Green suggests this
exponent may well be sharp; the candidate extremal family is the Ree groups ${}^2G_2(q)$,
$q = 3^{2m+1}$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_5 :
    IsLUB {α : ℝ | ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Fintype G], Nontrivial G →
      ∃ S : Finset G, IsProductFree (S : Set G) ∧
        c * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ^ α ≤ (S.card : ℝ)}
      green_5.answer

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 50
problems.statement:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a set of density $\alpha > 0$. Does $10A$ contain a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - O(\log(1/\alpha))$?

More precisely: does there exist an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for all $n \geq 1$ and all
nonempty $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with density $\alpha > 0$, the sumset $10A$ contains a coset
of some subspace of dimension at least $n - C \log_2(1/\alpha)$?

The sumset $10A$ is defined as $\{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{10} : a_i \in A\}$, using the pointwise
scalar multiplication notation `10 • A` where `•` denotes the iterated addition of a set.

Note: We model $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ as `Fin n → ZMod 2`, which is an $n$-dimensional vector space
over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_50 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset (𝔽₂ n),
    A.Nonempty →
    let α : ℝ := A.dens
    ∃ (W : Submodule (ZMod 2) (𝔽₂ n)) (v : 𝔽₂ n),
      v +ᵥ (W : Set (𝔽₂ n)) ⊆ ↑(10 • A) ∧
      (n : ℝ) - C * Real.logb 2 (1 / α) ≤ Module.finrank (ZMod 2) W

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 51 — one half
problems.statement:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ has density $\alpha > 1/2 - C/\sqrt{n}$.
Does $A + A$ contain a subspace of co-dimension $O_C(1)$? [Sa11, Question 5.1]
problems.lean:
theorem green_51.one_half :
    ∀ (k : ℝ), 0 < k →
      ∃ (c : ℕ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
        ∀ (α : ℝ), α > (1/2 : ℝ) - k / sqrt (n : ℝ) → α ≤ 1 →
          n ≤ guaranteedMaxCosetDim n α + c

problems.statement:

Does $2A$ contain a coset of codimension $O_K(1)$?

theorem green_52 :

      S.card = K → A + (S : Set (𝔽₂ n)) = Set.univ →

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 59
problems.statement:
Is every $n \le N$ the sum of two integers, all of whose prime factors are at most
$N^\varepsilon$?

We read this as: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every sufficiently large $N$, every integer
$2 \le n \le N$ is $a + b$ with positive integers $a, b$ whose prime factors are all at most
$N^\varepsilon$. Positive summands exclude $n = 1$. [Gr24] quotes Erdős [Er82] for an
essentially equivalent conjecture, which is
[Erdős Problem 334](https://www.erdosproblems.com/334). [Gr24] also reports a remark of Wooley:
a positive answer for every $\varepsilon > 0$ would solve Vinogradov's least quadratic
non-residue problem for primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_59 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 N, ∃ a b : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧
      a + b = n ∧ IsSmooth ((N : ℝ) ^ ε) a ∧ IsSmooth ((N : ℝ) ^ ε) b

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 60
problems.statement:
Is there an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that, whenever $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is a set of squares
with $|A| ≥ 2$, the sumset $A + A$ satisfies $|A + A| ≥ |A|^{1 + c}$?
problems.lean:
theorem green_60 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
      ∀ (A : Finset ℕ),
        (∀ a ∈ A, IsSquare a) →
        2 ≤ A.card →
          ((A + A).card : ℝ) ≥ (A.card : ℝ) ^ (1 + c)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 61
problems.statement:
Suppose that $A + A$ contains the first $n$ squares. Is $|A| \geq n^{1 - o(1)}$?

It is known that necessarily $|A| \geq n^{2/3 - o(1)}$, whilst in the other direction there do
exist such $A$ with $|A| \ll_C n / \log^C n$ for any $C$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_61 :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 1 → ∀ (A : Finset ℕ),
        (Finset.Icc 1 n).image (· ^ 2) ⊆ A + A →
          (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - f n) ≤ A.card

problems.statement:
Let $p$ be a large prime, and let $A$ be the set of all primes less than $p$.
Is every $x \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$ congruent to some product $a_1 a_2$ where $a_1, a_2 \in A$?

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 68
problems.statement:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_p^2$ is a set meeting every line in at most 2 points. Is it true
that all except $o(p)$ points of $A$ lie on a cubic curve?

Such sets are called arcs. We read "cubic curve" as the zero set of a nonzero polynomial of total
degree at most $3$ in two variables over $\mathbb{F}_p$. This includes conics and lines, and unions
of these. The $o(p)$ is uniform in $A$: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every large prime $p$, every
arc $A$ has all but at most $\varepsilon p$ of its points on one such curve. Green asked a
projective form of this question in [Gr14, Section 4.4]. [Gr24] notes that the question is more
natural in projective space, and that the analogue over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with $q = p^2$ is false,
because of Hermitian quadrics.
problems.lean:
theorem green_68 :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ p₀ : ℕ, ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p₀ ≤ p →
      ∀ A : Finset (Fin 2 → ZMod p), MeetsLinesInAtMost 2 A →
        ∃ F : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) (ZMod p), F ≠ 0 ∧ F.totalDegree ≤ 3 ∧
          (numOffCurve F A : ℝ) ≤ ε * p

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 69
problems.statement:
Fix a number $k$. Let $A \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points, with no more than $k$ on
any line. Suppose that, for at least $\delta n^2$ pairs of points $(x, y) \in A \times A$, the
line $xy$ contains a third point of $A$. Is there some cubic curve containing at least $cn$
points of $A$, for some $c = c(k, \delta) > 0$?

We count ordered pairs of distinct points (`numPairsWithThird`), and a cubic curve is the zero set
of any nonzero real polynomial of degree at most $3$ (`OnCubic`), reducible ones included. The
constant $c$ depends only on $k$ and $\delta$. Small $n$ are harmless, since any $9$ points lie on
a cubic curve. [Gr24] notes that very little is known, except when $\delta = 1 - O(1/n)$, where the
statement follows from the main results of [GT13].
problems.lean:
theorem green_69 :
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ A : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), AtMostOnLine k A →
      δ * (#A : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ numPairsWithThird A → ∃ S ⊆ A, c * #A ≤ #S ∧ OnCubic S

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 70
problems.statement:
Fix integers $k, \ell$. Is it true that, given a set of $n \geq n_0(k, \ell)$ points in
$\mathbb{R}^2$, either some $k$ of them lie on a line, or some $\ell$ of them are 'mutually
visible', that is to say that line segment joining them contains no other point from the set?

This question was first raised by Kára, Pór and Wood [KPW05]. It is called the big-line-big-clique
conjecture [PoWo10, Conjecture 1]. We read "mutually visible" as "pairwise visible". The cases
$k \leq 3$ are trivial: a set with no three collinear points has all pairs visible. For the
cases $\ell \leq 5$, see `green_70.variants.five_visible`.
problems.lean:
theorem green_70 :
    ∀ k ℓ : ℕ, ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ),
      n₀ ≤ #P → HasCollinear k P ∨ HasMutuallyVisible ℓ P

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 75
problems.statement:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points. Does there exist a line $\ell$ through at
least two points of $X$ such that the numbers of points on either side of $\ell$ differ by at
most $100$?

This is a form of the Kupitz-Perles conjecture [Gr24]. We take $n \geq 2$, since a line through
two points of $X$ needs two points. If all points of $X$ are collinear, the line through them has
no points on either side.
problems.lean:
theorem green_75 :
    ∀ X : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), 2 ≤ #X → ∃ p ∈ X, ∃ q ∈ X, p ≠ q ∧ imbalance X p q ≤ 100

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 76
problems.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane. Can one select a set $A'$ of $n/2$ points, with the
property that any axis-parallel rectangle containing $1000$ points of $A$ contains at least one
point of $A'$?

We read "a set of $n/2$ points" as at most $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ points, and "containing $1000$
points" as containing at least $1000$ points. The points of $A'$ need not lie in $A$. If
$A' \subseteq A$ is required, then the answer is no; see `green_76.variants.subset`.
problems.lean:
theorem green_76 :
    ∀ A : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), ∃ A', #A' ≤ #A / 2 ∧ HitsRichRectangles 1000 A A'

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 85 — green 85
problems.statement:
Suppose that $A$ is an open subset of $[0, 1]^2$ with measure $\alpha$. Are there four points in
$A$ determining an axis-parallel rectangle with area $\gt c \alpha^2$?
problems.lean:
theorem green_85 :
  ∃ c > 0, ∀ A : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
    IsOpen A →
    A ⊆ Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1 →
    A.Nonempty →
    let α := (volume A).toReal
    ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂,
      {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 86
problems.statement:
Let $c > 0$. Let $A$ be a set of $n$ (distinct) integers. Does there exist $\theta$ such that
no interval of length $\frac{1}{n}$ in $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ contains more than $n^c$ of the
numbers $\theta a \pmod 1$, $a \in A$?

We read the question for every $c > 0$ and all $n \ge n_0(c)$. For small $n$ it can fail: for
$A = \{0, 1, 3\}$ and $3^c < 2$, three points with at most one in each interval of length
$1/3$ must be equally spaced, which is impossible. Intervals are half-open; for the question
over all $c > 0$ this does not matter, since a closed interval of length $1/n$ is covered by two
half-open ones. [Gr24] reports that the answer is yes for $c > 1/3$ [KRS00], and that
[Mo94, Problem 17 (4)] attributes the problem to Komlós and Ruzsa.
problems.lean:
theorem green_86 :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℤ, n₀ ≤ #A →
      ∃ θ : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, (numInInterval A θ t : ℝ) ≤ (#A : ℝ) ^ c

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 87 — asymptotic
problems.statement:
Is $p(k) = (C + o(1)) k^{-\delta} (\log k)^{-3/2}$ for some absolute constant $C$?

Green and Sawhney [GS26] proved $p(k) = (1 + o(1)) f(\{\log_2 k\}) k^{-\delta} (\log k)^{-3/2}$
for an explicit smooth, positive $f$ on $\mathbb{R} / \mathbb{Z}$ with
$\max f / \min f < 1 + 2 \cdot 10^{-7}$. The question is therefore equivalent to whether $f$ is
constant; they conjecture that it is not, so the expected answer is no, but this has not been
proved.
problems.lean:
theorem green_87.asymptotic :
    ∀ p : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, Tendsto (fun n ↦ i n k) atTop (𝓝 (p k))) →
      ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
        p ~[atTop] fun k : ℕ ↦ C * (k : ℝ) ^ (-δ) * (Real.log k) ^ (-(3 / 2 : ℝ))

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 87 — decreasing
problems.statement:
Let $p(k)$ be the limit, as $n \to \infty$, of the probability that a random permutation of
$[n]$ preserves some set of size $k$. Is $p(k)$ a decreasing function of $k$?

This is a conjecture of Peter Cameron (2010), see [BW15]. The statement is taken in the strict
sense, as in [BW15]: they verified $p(k) > p(k + 1)$ for $k < 30$, and the values computed

For every finite tree $T$ the class of $T$-free graphs (graphs with no induced subgraph

problems.title: First Hardy–Littlewood conjecture — first hardy littlewood conjecture
problems.statement:
Let $P = (m_1, \dots, m_k)$ be a tuple of distinct positive even integers. Let
$\pi_P(n)$ denote the number of primes $p\leq n$ such that $(p, p + m_1, \dots, p + m_k)$
forms an admissible prime constellation. Let $w(q; m_1, \dots, m_k)$ denote the
number of distinct residues of $0, m_1, \dots, m_k$ modulo $q$, and let
$$
  C_P = 2 ^ k\prod_{\substack{q\ \text{prime} \\ q\geq 3}}
    \frac{1 - \frac{w(q; m_1, \dots, m_k)}{q}}{\left(1 - \frac{1}{q}\right)^{k+1}}.
$$
Then
$$
  \pi_P(n)\sim C_P\int_2^n\frac{dt}{\log^{k+1}t}.
$$
problems.lean:
theorem first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) :
    FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m

and including $z$.
problems.lean:
theorem second_hardy_littlewood_conjecture {x y : ℕ} (hx : 2 ≤ x) (hy : 2 ≤ y) :
    SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor x y

problems.statement:
The Lander–Parkin–Selfridge conjecture: if the sum of $n$ positive integer $k$-th powers
equals the sum of $m$ positive integer $k$-th powers, with all values on the left distinct from
all values on the right, then $n + m \geq k$.

Formally, for positive integers $k, n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ and sequences
$x : \{0, \ldots, n-1\} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $y : \{0, \ldots, m-1\} \to \mathbb{N}$
with $x_i > 0$, $y_j > 0$, and $x_i \neq y_j$ for all $i, j$, if
$$\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i^k = \sum_{j=0}^{m-1} y_j^k,$$
then $k \leq n + m$.
problems.lean:
theorem lander_parkin_selfridge :
    ∀ (k n m : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (y : Fin m → ℕ),
      0 < n → 0 < m →
      (∀ i, 0 < x i) → (∀ j, 0 < y j) →
      (∀ i j, x i ≠ y j) →
      ∑ i, x i ^ k = ∑ j, y j ^ k →
      k ≤ n + m

problems.title: The Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture (1988).
problems.statement:
**The Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture (1988).**

If $n \ge 4k$ and $x_1, \dots, x_n$ are real numbers with $x_1 + \dots + x_n = 0$, then at least
$\binom{n-1}{k-1}$ of the $k$-element subsets $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ have
$\sum_{i \in S} x_i \ge 0$. (The bound is attained by $x = (n-1, -1, \dots, -1)$; the
condition $n \ge 4k$ cannot be weakened to $n \ge 3k + 1$ in general.)
problems.lean:
theorem manickam_miklos_singhi_conjecture :
    ∀ (n k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → 4 * k ≤ n → ∀ x : Fin n → ℝ, ∑ i, x i = 0 →
      (n - 1).choose (k - 1) ≤ nonnegSubsetCount n k x

with essentially the same density as in the positive integers, up to a factor of $2$.

[MathOverflow 434111](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/434111/are-prime-numbers-among-sums-of-prime-numbers-distributed-as-frac-n2-lnn).

[Me18] Meštrović, R., *Curious Conjectures on the Distribution of Primes
Among the Sums of the First `2n` Primes*, [arXiv:1804.04198](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.04198)
(2018).

    ((fun n : ℕ => (piRestricted n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) / (2 * Real.log n)))

problems.title: Colton's Conjecture (1999, Conjecture 2)
problems.statement:
**Colton's Conjecture (1999, Conjecture 2):** Infinitely many positive integers $n$ satisfy
both $n$ and $n + 1$ refactorable.
problems.lean:
theorem infinitely_many_consecutive_refactorable_pairs :
    {n : ℕ | n.IsRefactorable ∧ (n + 1).IsRefactorable}.Infinite

problems.title: Zelinsky's Conjecture (2002, Conjecture 32)
problems.statement:
**Zelinsky's Conjecture (2002, Conjecture 32):** Every arithmetic progression of positive
integers containing a refactorable number contains infinitely many; equivalently, for every modulus
$m \ge 1$ and refactorable $n_0$, some refactorable $n > n_0$ satisfies $n \equiv n_0 \pmod m$.
problems.lean:
theorem zelinsky_refactorable_progression_conjecture :
    ∀ m n₀ : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → n₀.IsRefactorable →
      ∃ n : ℕ, n₀ < n ∧ n.IsRefactorable ∧ n ≡ n₀ [MOD m]

problems.title: Moments of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line — moment isEquiv
problems.statement:
The asymptotic behaviour of the $k$th moment of the Riemann zeta function
is conjectured to be
$$
  \frac{1}{T}\int_0^T |\zeta(1/2 + it)|^{2k}dt \sim c_k \log(T)^{k^2},
$$
for some constant $c_k$.
problems.lean:
theorem moment_isEquiv (k : ℕ) : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
    moment k ~[atTop] fun T ↦ c * T.log ^ (k ^ 2)

problems.title: Moments of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line — moment isEquiv₃
problems.statement:
The constant in the asymptotic formula for the 3rd zeta moment is conjectured
to be $42a_3/9!$ [CG98].
problems.lean: theorem moment_isEquiv₃ : moment 3 ~[atTop] fun T ↦ 42 * arithmeticFactor 3 / 9 ! * T.log ^ 9

problems.title: Moments of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line — moment isEquiv₄
problems.statement:
The constant in the asymptotic formula for the 4th zeta moment is conjectured to
be $24024a_4/16!$ [CGo01].
problems.lean:
theorem moment_isEquiv₄ :
    moment 4 ~[atTop] fun T ↦ 24024 * arithmeticFactor 4 / 16 ! * T.log ^ 16

problems.title: Moments of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line — moment isEquivₖ
problems.statement:
The Keating–Snaith conjecture [KS00] for the $k$th moment of the Riemann zeta function,
provides the value of $c_k$ in the asymptotic formula [Co26, §3.4.5].
problems.lean:
theorem moment_isEquivₖ (k : ℕ) : moment k ~[atTop]
    fun T ↦ (arithmeticFactor k * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range k, (j ! : ℝ) / (j + k) !) *
      T.log ^ (k ^ 2)

problems.title: Particular values of the Riemann zeta function — irrational odd
problems.statement: $\zeta(2n + 1)$ is irrational for any $n\in\mathbb{N}^{+}$.
problems.lean:
theorem irrational_odd (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta (2 * n + 1) = x

problems.title: Rowland's GCD prime-generating recurrence — rowland generates all odd primes
problems.statement:
Rowland's conjecture (2008): every odd prime $p$ occurs as $d(n) = a(n) - a(n - 1)$ at some index
$n \ge 2$. The prime $2$ is excluded because $n$ and $a(n - 1)$ always have opposite parity, and
$n \ge 2$ excludes the artifact `rowlandDiff 1 = 7`.
problems.lean:
theorem rowland_generates_all_odd_primes {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hodd : Odd p) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n ∧ rowlandDiff n = p

problems.title: Rudin's conjecture.
problems.statement:
**Rudin's conjecture.** The maximal number of squares among the first $N$ terms of a non-trivial
arithmetic progression grows at most like $\sqrt{N}$:
$$Q(N) = O(\sqrt{N}).$$
problems.lean:
theorem rudins_conjecture :
    (fun N : ℕ => (Qmax N : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N : ℕ => Real.sqrt N

problems.title: Rudin's conjecture on squares in arithmetic progressions — rudins conjecture unique
problems.statement:
The strongest form of Rudin's conjecture also asserts *uniqueness*: for $N \ge 6$, any non-trivial
arithmetic progression attaining the maximum $Q(N)$ has common difference $24$. (Its initial term
is then forced by $\gcd(24, a) = 1$; the progression $24n + 1$ is the canonical representative.)
problems.lean:
theorem rudins_conjecture_unique (N : ℕ) (hN : 6 ≤ N) (q a : ℕ)
    (hqa : IsNontrivial q a) (hmax : Q N q a = Qmax N) : q = 24

problems.title: Rule 30 Prize, Problem 1 (non-periodicity).
problems.statement:
**Rule 30 Prize, Problem 1 (non-periodicity).** The center column of Rule 30 is not
eventually periodic: there is no positive period $p$ and threshold $N$ past which the column
repeats with period $p$.
problems.lean:
theorem centerColumn_not_eventually_periodic :
    ¬ ∃ p : ℕ, 0 < p ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ t : ℕ, N ≤ t → centerColumn (t + p) = centerColumn t

problems.title: Schanuel's Conjecture
problems.statement:
Given any set of $n$ complex numbers $\{z_1, ..., z_n\}$ that are linearly independent over
$\mathbb{Q}$, the field extension $\mathbb{Q}(z_1, ..., z_n, e^{z_1}, ..., e^{z_n})$
has transcendence degree at least $n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.
problems.lean:
theorem schanuel_conjecture (n : ℕ) (z : Fin n → ℂ) (h : LinearIndependent ℚ z) :
    n ≤ Algebra.trdeg ℚ (adjoin ℚ (Set.range z ∪ Set.range (cexp ∘ z)))

problems.title: Schinzel conjecture (H hypothesis)
problems.statement:
**Schinzel conjecture (H hypothesis)**
If a finite set of polynomials $f_i$ satisfies both Schinzel and Bunyakovsky conditions,
there exist infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that $f_i(n)$ are primes for all $i$.
problems.lean:
theorem schinzel_conjecture (fs : Finset ℤ[X]) (hfs : ∀ f ∈ fs, BunyakovskyCondition f)
    (hfs' : SchinzelCondition fs) : Infinite {n : ℕ | ∀ f ∈ fs, (f.eval (n : ℤ)).natAbs.Prime}

problems.title: Positivity conjecture.
problems.statement:
**Positivity conjecture.** Let $R$ be a regular local ring and let $M$, $N$ be finitely
generated $R$-modules such that $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length. If
$\dim M + \dim N = \dim R$, then $\chi(M, N) > 0$.

The hypothesis on dimensions forces $M$ and $N$ to be nonzero, since the dimension of the zero
module is $\bot$.
problems.lean:
theorem intersectionMultiplicity_pos (h : IsFiniteLength R (M ⊗[R] N))
    (hdim : Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N = ringKrullDim R) :
    0 < intersectionMultiplicity R M N

problems.title: Positivity conjecture
problems.statement:
**Positivity conjecture**, in the form stated on Wikipedia. Let $R$ be a regular local ring and
let $P$, $Q$ be prime ideals of $R$ such that $R/P \otimes_R R/Q$ has finite length. If
$\dim R/P + \dim R/Q = \dim R$, then $\chi(R/P, R/Q) > 0$.
problems.lean:
theorem intersectionMultiplicity_pos_quotient (P Q : Ideal R) [P.IsPrime] [Q.IsPrime]
    (h : IsFiniteLength R ((R ⧸ P) ⊗[R] (R ⧸ Q)))
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (R ⧸ P) + ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Q) = ringKrullDim R) :
    0 < intersectionMultiplicity R (R ⧸ P) (R ⧸ Q)

problems.title: Serre's uniformity question over $\mathbb{Q}$
problems.statement:
**Serre's uniformity question over $\mathbb{Q}$** [Ser72, Lem17]: is there a bound
$C$ such that every non-CM elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ has surjective mod-$p$
Galois representation for every prime $p > C$?
problems.lean:
theorem serre_uniformity :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic], E.j ∉ cmJInvariants →
      ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → C < p → HasFullTorsionAction E p

problems.title: Sierpiński's $5 / n$ Conjecture
problems.statement:
**Sierpiński's $5 / n$ Conjecture** [Si56]: Each integer $n \ge 2$ admits positive integers
$x, y, z \ge 1$ satisfying $5 / n = 1 / x + 1 / y + 1 / z$.
problems.lean:
theorem sierpinski_egyptian_fraction_conjecture {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    HasSierpinskiDecomposition n

problems.title: The extended Sierpiński problem.
problems.statement:
**The extended Sierpiński problem.** Is 271129 the second-smallest Sierpiński number?

Even if 78557 is confirmed as the smallest Sierpiński number, there could exist a composite
Sierpiński number $k$ with $78557 < k < 271129$. We formalize "second-smallest" as: the
least Sierpiński number $k$ such that there exists exactly one Sierpiński number below it.
problems.lean:
theorem extended_sierpinski_problem :
    IsLeast {k | k.IsSierpinskiNumber ∧
      ∃ k', k'.IsSierpinskiNumber ∧ k' < k} 271129

problems.title: Singmaster's conjecture
problems.statement:
Singmaster's conjecture: the number of times any number $t > 1$ appears in
Pascal's triangle is bounded.
problems.lean:
theorem singmaster: ∃ (C : ℕ), ∀ (t : ℕ), t > 1 →
    (Singmaster.solutions t).Finite ∧ (Singmaster.solutions t).ncard ≤ C

problems.title: Skewes's Number and Sign Changes of $\pi(x) - \operatorname{li}(x)$ — skewes number
problems.statement:
What is Skewes's number, the smallest integer $n \ge 2$ satisfying
$\pi(n) > \operatorname{li}(n)$? The bound $n \ge 2$ avoids the singularity of $\operatorname{li}$
at $1$ and $0 = \pi(0) = \operatorname{li}(0)$.

problems.title: The small Cohen-Macaulay modules conjecture.
problems.statement:
**The small Cohen-Macaulay modules conjecture.** If $R$ is a complete Noetherian local ring, then
there is a finitely generated $R$-module $M \ne 0$ such that some system of parameters of $R$ is
a regular sequence on $M$.

Hochster stated the conjecture for complete local domains [Ho17, Conjecture 2.1]. The two forms
are equivalent: for a minimal prime $P$ of $R$ with $\dim R/P = \dim R$, a small Cohen-Macaulay
module over the complete local domain $R/P$ is one over $R$. In the 2000s Hochster conjectured
the opposite, that some complete local domain has no small Cohen-Macaulay module
[Ho17, Conjecture 2.2], so this statement may well be false.
problems.lean:
theorem exists_isSmallCohenMacaulay [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] :
    ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module R M), IsSmallCohenMacaulay R M

problems.title: McDaniel's Theorem on Smith Numbers and the Smith Brothers Problem
problems.statement: Do infinitely many consecutive base-$10$ Smith-number pairs $(n, n + 1)$ (Smith brothers) exist?
problems.lean:
theorem infinite_smith_brothers :
    {n : ℕ | IsSmithNumber 10 n ∧ IsSmithNumber 10 (n + 1)}.Infinite

problems.title: Wichmann's conjecture on optimal rulers.
problems.statement:
**Wichmann's conjecture on optimal rulers.** Every optimal ruler of sufficiently large
length is a Wichmann ruler $W(r, s)$ (up to reflection, i.e. reversing the segment list).
Posed by Wichmann [Wi63]. The Wikipedia article records that no optimal ruler of length
$1, 13, 17, 23$ or $58$ is a Wichmann ruler, and that every other optimal length up to $213$ is
attained by one; non-Wichmann optimal rulers also occur alongside Wichmann ones at lengths
$9, 29, 50$ and $68$.
problems.lean:
theorem wichmann_conjecture :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ g : List ℕ, IsOptimal g → N < g.sum →
      ∃ r s : ℕ, g = wichmannGaps r s ∨ g = (wichmannGaps r s).reverse

problems.title: Spectral sets and weak tiling — isSpectral right of product of convexBody
problems.statement:
[KLM2023, Problem 7.2] For every positive dimension $n$, a convex body $A$ and a bounded,
measurable set $B$, must spectrality of $A \times B$ imply spectrality of $B$?
problems.lean:
theorem isSpectral_right_of_product_of_convexBody :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ), 0 < n → 0 < m →
      spectralProductImpliesRightSpectral n m

problems.title: Stern Primes — isSternPrime iff
problems.statement:
Does $\{2, 3, 17, 137, 227, 977, 1187, 1493\}$ exhaust all Stern primes? No ninth example appears
among the first $100{,}000$ primes (McCranie) or below $2 \times 10^{13}$ (Chaffin, `OEIS A042978`).
problems.lean:
theorem isSternPrime_iff :
    ∀ q : ℕ, IsSternPrime q ↔ q ∈ ({2, 3, 17, 137, 227, 977, 1187, 1493} : Set ℕ)

problems.title: Sum of three cubes
problems.statement:
An integer `n : ℤ` can be written as a sum of three cubes (of integers) if and only if
`n` is not `4` or `5` mod `9`.
problems.lean:
theorem isSumOfThreeCubes_iff_mod_9 :
    ∀ n : ℤ, IsSumOfThreeCubes n ↔ ¬(n ≡ 4 [ZMOD 9] ∨ n ≡ 5 [ZMOD 9])

problems.title: The symbol length problem
problems.statement:
**The symbol length problem** for complex rational function fields [Krashen2024, Problem 2.1.3.12
and §2.1.3.4]: determine, as a function of $m$, $n$ and the prime $p$, the symbol length of
$K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$, that is the least $k$ such that every class is a sum of at
most $k$ symbols, or $\infty$ if there is no such $k$. The answer `sl m n p : ℕ∞` is
characterised by: `k` is such a bound if and only if `sl m n p ≤ k`.
problems.lean:
theorem symbol_length_problem :
    ∀ m n p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ k : ℕ,
      k ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p n ↔ symbol_length_problem.answer m n p ≤ k

problems.title: Tarski's exponential function problem.
problems.statement:
**Tarski's exponential function problem.** Is the first-order theory of the real exponential
field $\mathbb{R}_{\exp} = (\mathbb{R}, +, \cdot, -, 0, 1, \le, \exp)$ decidable?
problems.lean:
theorem tarski_exponential_function_problem :
    (Language.orderedExpField.completeTheory ℝ).IsDecidable

problems.title: Thabit numbers and Thabit primes — exists thabit amicable exponent gt seven
problems.statement:
Does there exist an integer $n > 7$ for which $K_{n-1}$, $K_n$, and $9 \cdot 2^{2n - 1} - 1$ are
simultaneously prime, yielding an amicable pair via Thābit ibn Qurra's rule [Bo72, Gu04]? Only
$n = 2, 4, 7$ are currently known.
problems.lean:
theorem exists_thabit_amicable_exponent_gt_seven :
    ∃ n > 7, (thabitNumber (n - 1)).Prime ∧ (thabitNumber n).Prime ∧
      (9 * 2 ^ (2 * n - 1) - 1).Prime

problems.title: Toronto spaces — of t2 of torontoSpace
problems.statement: Any T2, Toronto space is discrete.
problems.lean:
theorem DiscreteTopology.of_t2_of_torontoSpace [T2Space X] [TorontoSpace X] :
    DiscreteTopology X

problems.title: The total colouring conjecture (Behzad 1965, Vizing 1968).
problems.statement:
**The total colouring conjecture (Behzad 1965, Vizing 1968).**

Every finite simple graph $G$ has a total colouring with at most $\Delta(G) + 2$ colours, i.e.
$\chi''(G) \le \Delta(G) + 2$, where $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree.
problems.lean:
theorem total_coloring_conjecture :
    ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G.totalChromaticNumber ≤ G.maxDegree + 2

problems.title: Open questions on transcendence of numbers — transcendental gamma one div
problems.statement: $\Gamma(1/n)$ for `n ≥ 2` is transcendental.
problems.lean: theorem transcendental_gamma_one_div (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : Transcendental ℚ (1 / n : ℝ).Gamma

problems.title: Tuza's conjecture
problems.statement:
Tuza's conjecture (1981): every finite graph $G$ satisfies $\tau(G) \le 2\nu(G)$,
where $\tau(G)$ is its triangle covering number and $\nu(G)$ is its triangle packing number.
The bound would be sharp, for example for $K_4$ and $K_5$.
problems.lean:
theorem tuza_conjecture {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    triangleCoverNumber G ≤ 2 * trianglePackingNumber G

problems.title: Union-closed sets conjecture
problems.statement:
For every finite union-closed family of sets, other than the family containing only the empty set,
there exists an element that belongs to at least half of the sets in the family.
problems.lean:
theorem union_closed
    [Nonempty n]
    (h_ne_singleton_empty : A ≠ {∅})
    (h_union_closed : IsUnionClosed A) :
    ∃ i : n, (1 / 2 : ℚ) * #A ≤ #{x ∈ A | i ∈ x}

problems.title: Unique Odd Untouchable Conjecture
problems.statement:
**Unique Odd Untouchable Conjecture:** Among odd integers, $5$ is the unique untouchable
value.
problems.lean:
theorem unique_odd_untouchable_conjecture {m : ℕ} (hodd : Odd m) :
    m.IsUntouchable ↔ m = 5

problems.title: VCₙ dimension of convex sets in ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ⁺¹, ℝⁿ⁺² — exists exponential bound hasAddVCNDimAtMost n of convex rn add one
problems.statement:
For every $n \ge 1$ there exists some $d$ such that every convex set in $\mathbb R^{n + 1}$ has
$\mathrm{VC}_n$ dimension at most $d$.

The bound can be taken to be $d = c^n$ for some constant $c \ge 2$ independent of $n$.
problems.lean:
lemma exists_exponential_bound_hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_of_convex_rn_add_one :
    ∃ c : ℕ, 2 ≤ c ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n),
      ∀ C : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ), Convex ℝ C → HasAddVCNDimAtMost C n (c ^ n)

problems.title: VCₙ dimension of convex sets in ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ⁺¹, ℝⁿ⁺² — hasAddVCNDimAtMost n two of convex rn add one
problems.statement:
Is it true that, for all $n$, every convex set in $\mathbb R^{n + 1}$ has
$\mathrm{VC}_n$ dimension at most 3?
problems.lean:
lemma hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_two_of_convex_rn_add_one :
    ∀ ⦃n : ℕ⦄, n ≠ 0 → ∀ ⦃C : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 1)))⦄,
      Convex ℝ C → HasAddVCNDimAtMost C n 3

problems.title: VCₙ dimension of convex sets in ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ⁺¹, ℝⁿ⁺² — hasAddVCNDimAtMost two two of convex r3
problems.statement: Every convex set in $\mathbb R^3$ has $\mathrm{VC}_2$ dimension at most 2.
problems.lean:
lemma hasAddVCNDimAtMost_two_two_of_convex_r3 {C : Set ℝ³} (hC : Convex ℝ C) :
    HasAddVCNDimAtMost C 2 2

problems.title: Vaught conjecture
problems.statement:
The Vaught conjecture states that for a countable language L and a complete L-Theory T
the number of countable models of T (up to isomorphism) is finite, $\aleph_0$ or $2^{\aleph_0}$.
problems.lean:
theorem vaught_conjecture {L : FirstOrder.Language} (hL : Countable L.Symbols)
                          {T : L.Theory} (hT : T.IsComplete) :
  numberOfCountableModels T ≤ Cardinal.aleph0 ∨ numberOfCountableModels T = Cardinal.continuum

problems.title: Vizing's conjecture (1968).
problems.statement:
**Vizing's conjecture (1968).**

For all finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, the domination number of the Cartesian (box)
product satisfies $\gamma(G \,\square\, H) \ge \gamma(G)\,\gamma(H)$.
problems.lean:
theorem vizing_conjecture :
    ∀ {α β : Type} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β),
      G.dominationNumber * H.dominationNumber ≤ (G □ H).dominationNumber

problems.title: Problem 4.2.
problems.statement:
**Problem 4.2.** Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a finite union of three or more
    intervals. If $\Omega$ weakly tiles its complement, must it also tile its complement
    properly?
problems.lean:
theorem problem_4_2 :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : 3 ≤ n) (Ω : Set ℝ)
      (_ : IsUnionOfNIntervals n Ω) (ν : Measure ℝ) (_ : IsWeakTilingMeasure Ω ν),
      ∃ T : Set ℝ, IsProperTiling Ω T

problems.title: Conjectures about Weakly First Countable spaces — cardinalMk le continuum of weaklyFirstCountable of countableSouslinNumber
problems.statement:
Problem 4 in [Ar2013]: If a Tychonoff weakly first-countable space has countable
Souslin number, then does its cardinality not exceed the continuum?
problems.lean:
theorem cardinalMk_le_continuum_of_weaklyFirstCountable_of_countableSouslinNumber :
    ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T35Space X →
      WeaklyFirstCountableTopology X → HasCountableSouslinNumber X → #X ≤ 𝔠

problems.title: Conjectures about Weakly First Countable spaces — existsWeaklyFirstCountableCompactBig
problems.statement:
Problem 2 in [Ar2013]: Give an example in ZFC of a weakly first-
countable compact Hausdorff space X such that $𝔠 < |X|$.

Note: [Ar2013] uses a blanket convention that all spaces are
Tychonoff and "compact" means compact Hausdorff.
problems.lean:
theorem existsWeaklyFirstCountableCompactBig :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X),
      WeaklyFirstCountableTopology X ∧ CompactSpace X ∧ T2Space X ∧
        𝔠 < #X

problems.title: Conjectures about Weakly First Countable spaces — existsWeaklyFirstCountableCompactNotFirstCountable
problems.statement:
Problem 3 in [Ar2013]: Give an example in ZFC of a weakly first-
countable compact Hausdorff space which is not first countable.

Note: [Ar2013] uses a blanket convention that all spaces are
Tychonoff and "compact" means compact Hausdorff.
problems.lean:
theorem existsWeaklyFirstCountableCompactNotFirstCountable :
    ∃ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X),
      WeaklyFirstCountableTopology X ∧ CompactSpace X ∧ T2Space X ∧
        ¬ FirstCountableTopology X

problems.title: Weighing matrix conjecture
problems.statement:
**Weighing matrix conjecture** (Wallis 1972; Geramita–Seberry [GS79]): for every positive integer
$m \ge 1$ and every weight $0 \le w \le 4m$, there exists a weighing matrix $W(4m, w)$ of order
$4m$ and weight $w$.

At $w = 4m$, this specializes to Hadamard's conjecture.
problems.lean:
theorem weighing_matrix_conjecture (m w : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hw : w ≤ 4 * m) :
    ∃ W, IsWeighingMatrix (n := 4 * m) w W

problems.title: Can a prime $p$ satisfy $2^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$ and $3^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$? — exists isWieferichPrime and isMirimanoffPrime
problems.statement:
Can a prime $p$ satisfy $2^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$ and $3^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$
simultaneously? That is, does there exist a prime $p$ that is both a Wieferich prime and a
Mirimanoff prime? Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems poses this question, citing
J. B. Dobson, [On Lerch's formula for the Fermat quotient](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3907v6).
Lenstra gave a heuristic argument against the existence of such a prime (see Dobson, Section 9).
problems.lean:
theorem exists_isWieferichPrime_and_isMirimanoffPrime :
    ∃ p : ℕ, IsWieferichPrime p ∧ IsMirimanoffPrime p

problems.title: Wieferich primes — infinite isWieferichPrimeBase
problems.statement:
For any given integer $a > 0$, are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that
$a^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$? The case $a = 1$ is trivial, since every prime qualifies
(`isWieferichPrimeBase_one_iff`). So is the case $a = 0$ under our definition
(`isWieferichPrimeBase_zero_iff`), which is why the source's restriction to $a > 0$ is dropped.
problems.lean:
theorem infinite_isWieferichPrimeBase :
    ∀ a : ℕ, {p : ℕ | IsWieferichPrimeBase a p}.Infinite

problems.title: Wilf's Conjecture
problems.statement:
**Wilf's Conjecture** [Wi78]: Every numerical semigroup $S \le \mathbb{N}$ obeys
$c(S) \le e(S) \cdot n(S)$.
problems.lean:
theorem wilf_numerical_semigroup_conjecture {S : AddSubmonoid ℕ} (hS : IsNumericalSemigroup S) :
    conductor S ≤ embeddingDim S * sporadicCount S

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 189
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 189](http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj189)
(status O):

For a simple connected graph `G`, if `max_v distEven(v) ≤ 1 + σ(G)`,
then `G` has a Hamiltonian path.

Here `distEven(v)` is the number of vertices at even distance from `v`, and
`σ(G)` is the **second-smallest degree** of `G`'s degree sequence (per
WOWII defEntry 65).
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture189 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected)
    (hσ : (Finset.univ.image (distEven G)).max' (by simp) ≤ 1 + secondSmallestDegree G) :
    ∃ a b : α, ∃ p : G.Walk a b, p.IsHamiltonian

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 199
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 199](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, if `tree(G) - 2 ≤ κ(G)`, then `G` has a Hamiltonian path.
The nontrivial vertex type encodes the source assumption $n > 1$.
Here `tree(G)` is the number of vertices in a largest induced tree and
`κ(G) = vertexConnectivity G` is the vertex connectivity of `G`.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture199 (G : SimpleGraph α) (h : G.Connected)
    (hκ : largestInducedTreeSize G - 2 ≤ vertexConnectivity G) :
    ∃ a b : α, ∃ p : G.Walk a b, p.IsHamiltonian

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 372
problems.statement:
WOWII Conjecture 372 on its positive-denominator domain. If $T$ is a tree with
more than two vertices and path cover number $p(T) \ge 2$, then
$\gamma_t(T) \ge \tau(T)/(p(T)-1)$, where $\gamma_t$ is the total domination
number and $\tau$ is the vertex cover number.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture372 (hT : T.IsTree) (hn : 2 < Fintype.card α)
    (hp : 2 ≤ T.pathCoverNumber) :
    (T.vertexCoverNum.toNat : ℝ) / ((T.pathCoverNumber : ℝ) - 1) ≤
      T.totalDominationNumber

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 40
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 40](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a nontrivial connected graph `G` the size `f(G)` of a largest induced forest
satisfies `f(G) ≥ ceil((p(G) + b(G) + 1)/2)` where `p(G)` is the path cover
number and `b(G)` is the largest induced bipartite subgraph size.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture40 (h_conn : G.Connected) (h_nontrivial : 1 < Fintype.card α) :
    ⌈(((pathCoverNumber G : ℝ) + b G + 1) / 2)⌉ ≤  G.largestInducedForestSize

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 61
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 61](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$, the size $f(G)$ of a largest induced forest
satisfies $f(G) \ge \mathrm{residue}(G) + \lceil \mathrm{diam}(G) / 3 \rceil$,
where $\mathrm{residue}(G)$ is the Havel-Hakimi residue and $\mathrm{diam}(G)$
is the diameter of $G$.

See: Favaron, Mahéo, Saclé (1991) for the residue; DeLaVina's Graffiti.pc for the conjecture.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture61 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    (residue G : ℝ) + ⌈(G.diam : ℝ) / 3⌉ ≤ (G.largestInducedForestSize : ℝ)

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 72
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 72](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`,
$\operatorname{tree}(G) ≥ ⌈\operatorname{ecc}_{\mathrm{avg}}(G) + \max_v \lambda(v)/3⌉$
where `tree(G)` is the number of vertices in a largest induced tree,
`ecc_avg(G)` is the average eccentricity of `G`, and
`max_v l(v) = max_v indepNeighborsCard G v` is the maximum over all vertices of
the independence number of the neighbourhood.

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 84
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 84](http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj84)
(status O):

For a simple connected graph `G` with positive minimum degree,
`tree(G) ≥ 2 · rad(G) / δ(G)`,
where `tree(G)` is the number of vertices in a largest induced subtree,
`rad(G)` is the radius, and `δ(G) = G.minDegree` is the minimum degree.

The hypothesis `0 < G.minDegree` follows from connectedness on a nontrivial
vertex set, but is stated explicitly so the theorem reads as a real-valued
inequality without `x / 0` corner cases.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture84 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (h : G.Connected) (hδ : 0 < G.minDegree) :
    2 * (G.radius.toNat : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) ≤ (largestInducedTreeSize G : ℝ)

problems.title: Zagier's conjecture
problems.statement:
**Zagier's conjecture**

The $\mathbb{Q}$-dimension of the vector space spanned by all multiple zeta values
of weight $n$ equals $d_n$, where $d_n$ is the Zagier dimension sequence
satisfying $d_0 = 1$, $d_1 = 0$, $d_2 = 1$, and $d_n = d_{n-2} + d_{n-3}$ for $n \geq 3$.
problems.lean:
theorem zagier_conjecture :
    ∀ n : ℕ, Module.finrank ℚ (mzvSpanOfWeight n) = zagierDim n

problems.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line — distinct prop lt
problems.statement:
Is the proportion of distinct zeros of `ζ` unconditionally larger than the Montgomery–Taylor
bound `(3 - c_MT⁻¹) / 2 = 0.8362…`?

Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, Bui and Heath-Brown [BH13] proved that the proportion of distinct
zeros is at least `0.84665`. They count the zeros with `0 < γ < T`, and the statement here counts
those with `T < γ ≤ 2T`.
problems.lean:
theorem distinct_prop_lt : ∃ c > (3 - montgomeryTaylorConst⁻¹) / 2, ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ,
    o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ T > 0, (c - o T) * N riemannZeta T (2 * T) ≤ Nd riemannZeta T (2 * T)

problems.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line — distinct prop one hundred
problems.statement: Almost all nontrivial zeros of `ζ` are simple.
problems.lean:
theorem distinct_prop_one_hundred : ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ T > 0, (1 - o T) * N riemannZeta T (2 * T) ≤ Nd riemannZeta T (2 * T)

problems.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line — simple prop lt
problems.statement:
Is the proportion of simple zeros of `ζ` on the critical line unconditionally larger than
the Montgomery–Taylor bound `2 - c_MT⁻¹ = 0.6725…`? [Cl26, §7.2] puts the ceiling of its
method at about `0.682`.

Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, Bui and Heath-Brown [BH13] proved that the proportion of simple
zeros is at least `19/27 = 0.7037…`. They count the zeros with `0 < γ < T`, and the statement here
counts those with `T < γ ≤ 2T`.
problems.lean:
theorem simple_prop_lt : ∃ c > 2 - montgomeryTaylorConst⁻¹, ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ,
    o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧
      ∀ T > 0, (c - o T) * N riemannZeta T (2 * T) ≤ Ns riemannZeta T (2 * T)

problems.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line — simple prop one hundred
problems.statement: Almost all nontrivial zeros of `ζ` are simple and on the critical line.
problems.lean:
theorem simple_prop_one_hundred : ∃ o : ℝ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ T > 0, (1 - o T) * N riemannZeta T (2 * T) ≤ Ns riemannZeta T (2 * T)

problems.statement:
**Infinitely many amicable numbers conjecture.**

Are there infinitely many pairs of amicable numbers?

While many amicable pairs are known, it remains open whether there are infinitely many.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amicable_numbers),
[erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)
problems.lean: theorem infinitely_many_amicable : type_of% Erdos830.erdos_830.parts.i

problems.title: Amicable numbers with opposite parity conjecture.
problems.statement:
**Amicable numbers with opposite parity conjecture.**
Do there exist amicable numbers $(a, b)$ where one is even and the other is odd?

All known amicable pairs are either both even or both odd. It is widely believed
that mixed-parity amicable pairs do not exist, but this remains open.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amicable_numbers)
problems.lean:
theorem opposite_parity_amicable :
    ∃ a b : ℕ, IsAmicable a b ∧ (Even a ↔ Odd b)

problems.title: Relatively prime amicable numbers conjecture.
problems.statement:
**Relatively prime amicable numbers conjecture.**
Do there exist amicable numbers $(a, b)$ with $\gcd(a, b) = 1$?

All known amicable pairs share a common factor. It is an open question
whether a pair of relatively prime amicable numbers can exist.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amicable_numbers)
problems.lean:
theorem relatively_prime_amicable :
    ∃ a b : ℕ, IsAmicable a b ∧ a ≠ b ∧ a.Coprime b

problems.title: Digit $2$ in base $3$ representation of $2^n$
problems.statement:
For $n > 8$, $2^n$ is not the sum of distinct powers of $3$. Expressed here in terms of the base $3$ digits of $2^n$.

This conjecture is equivalent to the non-halting of a $15$-state $2$-symbol Turing Machine.
The Turing Machine version is formalized in
[cryptids](https://github.com/google-deepmind/cryptids/blob/main/Cryptids/Semantics/ErdosTernary15.lean):
`ConjectureMachines.ErdosTernary15.halts_erdosTernary15_iff_exists_counterexample` proves that
this machine halts on the blank tape if and only if some $2^n$ with $n > 8$ has no digit $2$ in
base $3$. The repository also proves this for Tristan Stérin's $14$-state machine.

Source: *Hardness of Busy Beaver Value BB(15)*: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-72621-7_9
This is also https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12475.
problems.lean: theorem CollatzLike (n : ℕ) (hn : 8 < n) : 2 ∈ Nat.digits 3 (2^n)

problems.title: Same parity betrothed numbers conjecture.
problems.statement:
**Same parity betrothed numbers conjecture.**
Do there exist betrothed numbers $(m, n)$ where both have the same parity
(both even or both odd)?

All known betrothed pairs consist of one even and one odd number.

The requirement $m \neq n$ is part of the question: $\mathrm{IsBetrothed}\ n\ n$ says
$\sigma(n) = 2n + 1$, i.e. that $n$ is quasiperfect, which is the separate open problem
`QuasiperfectNumbers.exists_quasiperfect`.
problems.lean:
theorem same_parity_betrothed :
    ∃ m n : ℕ, m ≠ n ∧ IsBetrothed m n ∧ (Even m ↔ Even n)

problems.title: There is no complete disjoint NP pair
problems.statement:
**There is no complete disjoint NP pair** (Razborov [Ra94]; Pudlák's conjecture `DisjNP` [Pu17]).

No disjoint NP pair is complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions of pairs. This is the
strongest of the "incompleteness in the finite domain" conjectures: it implies that no
length-optimal propositional proof system exists [Ra94, KMT03], hence `NP ≠ coNP` and `P ≠ NP`.
Equivalently [Pu17], for every consistent polynomial-time axiomatized theory `T ⊇ S¹₂` some
disjoint NP pair is not provably disjoint in `T`.
problems.lean: theorem no_complete_disjoint_NP_pair : ¬∃ A B : DecisionProblem, IsCompleteNPPair A B

problems.title: There is no complete disjoint coNP pair
problems.statement:
**There is no complete disjoint coNP pair** (Pudlák's conjecture `DisjCoNP` [Pu17]).

No disjoint coNP pair is complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions of pairs. This
implies that `TFNP` has no complete problem and that `SAT` has no p-optimal proof system
[Pu17, Kh22].
problems.lean: theorem no_complete_disjoint_coNP_pair : ¬∃ A B : DecisionProblem, IsCompleteCoNPPair A B

problems.title: Some conjectures about ranks of elliptic curves over ℚ — exists rank ge thirtytwo
problems.statement:
Is there an elliptic curve over ℚ of rank at least 32?
The largest known rank of an elliptic curve over ℚ as of 2026 is at least 31 (and exactly
