problems.title: Erdős Problem 659
problems.statement:
Is there a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every subset of $4$ points determines at
least $3$ distances, yet the total number of distinct distances is $\ll \frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$?

There does exist such a set: a suitable truncation of the lattice
$\{(a,b\sqrt{2}): a,b\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ suffices. This construction appears to have been first
considered by Moree and Osburn \cite{MoOs06}, who proved that it has
 $\ll \frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ many distinct distances. This construction was independently found by
 [Lund and Sheffer](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/2014/07/16/point-sets-with-few-distinct-distances/),
 who further noted that this configuration contains no squares or equilateral triangles.

There are only six possible configurations of $4$ points which determine only $2$ distances
(first noted by Erdős and Fishburn [ErFi96]), and five of them contain either a square or an
equilateral triangle. The remaining configuration contains four points from a regular pentagon,
and Grayzel [Gr26] (using Gemini) has noted in the comments that this configuration can also be
ruled out, thus giving a complete solution to this problem.

Boris Alexeev provides a formalisation of the reduction, which is conditional on Bernays' theorem
(assumed as an axiom in the proof to obtain the $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ bound).
See the [formal proof](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/226d5fad7143dcebea2bbb5ec87f18a3a1dcea69/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos659.lean).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_659 : ∃ A : ℕ → Finset ℝ²,
   (∀ n, #(A n) = n ∧ ∀ S ⊆ A n, #S = 4 → 3 ≤ distinctDistances S) ∧
    (fun n ↦ distinctDistances (A n)) ≪ fun n ↦ n / sqrt (log n)

and let $A$ be the set of all naturals divisible by exactly one of $p_1, ..., p_k$ (with
multiplicity $1$). Then $A$ has density $> \frac{1}{e} - \epsilon$ and has the property
that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when $r = s$.

        S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
        (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
        (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 696
problems.statement:
Is it true that $H(n)/h(n)\to \infty$ for almost all $n$?

Formalised as: for every threshold $M$, the set of $n$ with $h(n) > 0$ and $H(n)/h(n) > M$
has natural density $1$. This is false: in fact, $H(n)/h(n) = 2 + o(1)$ for almost all $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_696 :
    ¬ ∀ M : ℝ,
      {n : ℕ | (h n : ℝ) > 0 ∧ (H n : ℝ) / (h n : ℝ) > M}.HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 793
problems.statement:
Let $F(n)$ be the maximum possible size of a subset $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, n\}$ such that
$a \nmid bc$ whenever $a, b, c \in A$ with $a \neq b$ and $a \neq c$. Is there a constant $c$ such
that
$$F(n) = \pi(n) + (c + o(1)) n^{2/3} (\log n)^{-2}?$$

A problem of Erdős [Er69, Er70b], who proved in [Er38] that
$F(n) = \pi(n) + O(n^{2/3} (\log n)^{-2})$. The answer is yes, with $c = 27/2$: this was proved by
GPT-5.6 Sol (prompted by Chojecki), refining the argument of [Er38]; see
`erdos_793.variants.constant`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_793 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((F n : ℝ) - Nat.primeCounting n) /
      ((n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3) / (log n) ^ 2)) atTop (𝓝 c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 868 — i
problems.statement:
Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, then
must $A$ contain a minimal additive basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] answered this in the negative.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_868.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      atTop.Tendsto (fun n => ncard_add_repr A 2 n) atTop → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 868 — ii
problems.statement:
Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) > \epsilon \log n$ for large $n$
and an arbitrary fixed $\epsilon > 0$, then must $A$ contain a minimal additive
basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] constructed a counterexample with $f(n) > c \log n$ for all large $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_868.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ᵉ (A : Set ℕ) (ε > 0), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ε * Real.log n < ncard_add_repr A 2 n) → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 884
problems.statement:
In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer to Erdős problem 884,
disproving it under the assumption of the *qualitative Hardy–Littlewood prime tuples
conjecture*, see Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.1 of
[Tao25](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf).

The qualitative conjecture states that for every admissible tuple $(h_1, \dotsc, h_k)$ of
integers, i.e. one which avoids at least one residue class modulo $p$ for every prime $p$,
there are infinitely many natural numbers $n$ such that $n + h_1, \dotsc, n + h_k$ are all
prime. Unlike the full Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, it does not give an asymptotic for the
number of such $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood
    (hHL : ∀ H : Finset ℤ, (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ h ∈ H, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ a + h) →
      {n : ℕ | ∀ h ∈ H, Prime ((n : ℤ) + h)}.Infinite) :
    ¬Erdos884Prop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 97 — three unit distance
problems.statement:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] have found a convex polygon on 20 points such that
every vertex has three vertices equidistant from it (and this distance is the same for all vertices).

[FiRe92] Fishburn, P. C. and Reeds, J. A., _Unit distances between vertices of a convex polygon_. Comput. Geom. (1992), 81-91.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance :
    ∃ A : Finset ℝ², A.Nonempty ∧ ConvexIndep A ∧ HasNUnitDistanceProperty 3 A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 97 — three unit distance cut min
problems.statement:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] also proved that the smallest $n$ for which there exists
a convex $n$-gon and a cut $\{A, B\}$ of its vertices such that $|\{b \in B : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$
for all $a \in A$, and $|\{a \in A : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$ for all $b \in B$, is $n = 20$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_97.variants.three_unit_distance_cut_min :
    sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ (V : Finset ℝ²) (A B : Finset ℝ²),
      n = V.card ∧ ConvexIndep V ∧ A.Nonempty ∧ B.Nonempty ∧ IsCut V A B ∧
      HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 B A ∧ HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 A B} = 20

problems.title: TAS Trees Conjecture: Trees with a single even-degree vertex.
problems.statement:
**TAS Trees Conjecture: Trees with a single even-degree vertex.**

Proven case of TAS Trees Conjecture: any tree containing exactly one vertex of even degree
possesses an orientation satisfying the Tournament Anti-Sidorenko inequality $t_{\vec{T}}(G) \le 2^{-e(T)}$.
problems.lean:
theorem tournament_anti_sidorenko_single_even_degree_tree {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (T : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel T.Adj] (hTree : T.IsTree)
    (hEven : (Finset.univ.filter (fun v => Even (T.degree v))).card = 1) :
    ∃ (D : Digraph V),
      D.IsOrientation T ∧
      ∀ {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] [Nonempty W]
        (G : Digraph W) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
        G.IsTournament →
        Digraph.homDensity D G ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ T.edgeFinset.card

problems.title: Resolution of singularities
problems.statement:
Resolution of singularities holds in dimension at most three over any perfect field. In
characteristic zero this is [Hir1964]. In positive characteristic, dimension at most two is
[Lip1978] and dimension three is due to Cossart and Piltant: [CP2008] and [CP2009] prove it for
quasi-projective varieties over a field that is differentially finite over a perfect subfield,
and [CP2019], Theorem 1.1, removes both restrictions, resolving every reduced separated
Noetherian quasi-excellent scheme of dimension at most three in any characteristic. That theorem
gives an everywhere regular source, which over a perfect field is the same as a smooth one. The
problem is open in positive characteristic from dimension four on.
problems.lean:
theorem resolution_of_singularities_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_three (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [PerfectField k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral X]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [QuasiCompact sX] [IsSeparated sX]
    (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 3) :
    Scheme.HasResolution sX

problems.title: Ringel's Conjecture and Kotzig's Conjecture for large $n$ — kotzig conjecture large
problems.statement:
For all sufficiently large $n$, the complete graph $K_{2n+1}$ decomposes into
$2n+1$ edge-disjoint copies of any tree $T$ with $n$ edges via cyclic shifts of a single
embedding.

The $2n+1$ copies are $f_0, f_1, \dots, f_{2n}$ where $f_i(v) = f_0(v) + i$ for all vertices
$v$ — that is, each copy is obtained by adding $i \pmod{2n+1}$ to every vertex of the
base copy. This is strictly stronger than `ringel_conjecture_large`.

Kotzig conjectured this holds for all $n$; see `Paper/KotzigConjecture.lean`. Montgomery,
Pokrovskiy, and Sudakov prove it for all sufficiently large $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem kotzig_conjecture_large :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] (T : SimpleGraph V),
      T.IsTree → T.edgeSet.ncard = n →
      ∃ f : Fin (2 * n + 1) → (V ↪ Fin (2 * n + 1)),
        (∀ i v, f i v = f 0 v + i) ∧
        Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (T.map (f i)).edgeSet (T.map (f j)).edgeSet) ∧
        ⨆ i, T.map (f i) = (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n + 1)))

problems.title: Ringel's Conjecture and Kotzig's Conjecture for large $n$ — ringel conjecture large
problems.statement:
For all sufficiently large $n$, the complete graph $K_{2n+1}$ decomposes into
$2n+1$ edge-disjoint copies of any tree $T$ with $n$ edges.

A "copy" of $T$ is the image $T.\text{map}(f_i)$ of $T$ under a vertex embedding
$f_i : V \hookrightarrow \text{Fin}(2n+1)$; the copies are pairwise edge-disjoint
and together cover every edge of $K_{2n+1}$.

This follows from `kotzig_conjecture_large`; see `Paper/RingelConjecture.lean` for the open form.
problems.lean:
theorem ringel_conjecture_large :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] (T : SimpleGraph V),
      T.IsTree → T.edgeSet.ncard = n →
      ∃ f : Fin (2 * n + 1) → (V ↪ Fin (2 * n + 1)),
        Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (T.map (f i)).edgeSet (T.map (f j)).edgeSet) ∧
        ⨆ i, T.map (f i) = (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n + 1)))

problems.title: TxGraffiti Conjecture 2: zero forcing versus independence (cubic graphs)
problems.statement:
TxGraffiti [Conjecture 2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17780):
for every connected graph $G$ with $\Delta(G) \le 3$ and $G \ne K_4$,
$$Z(G) \le \alpha(G) + 1.$$

This conjecture is **false**. Fischer gives a connected 24-vertex
counterexample with maximum degree $3$; see
[arXiv:2607.23664](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23664).
problems.lean:
theorem tx_graffiti_conjecture_2 :
    ¬ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
      [DecidableRel G.Adj] (_hConn : G.Connected)
      (_hDeg : G.maxDegree ≤ 3)
      (_hNotK4 : G = ⊤ → Fintype.card V ≠ 4),
      zeroForcingNumber G ≤ G.indepNum + 1

problems.title: Corollary 29 (Fradelizi-Manui-Meyer-Ndiaye, 2026).
problems.statement:
**Corollary 29 (Fradelizi-Manui-Meyer-Ndiaye, 2026).** For a planar convex body $K$ with a
centre of symmetry containing the origin and $p > 1$,
$$|K \oplus_p -K| \leq \left(\frac{2\Gamma(1+1/q)^2}{\Gamma(1+2/q)} + 2\right)|K|,$$
where $q$ is the Hölder conjugate of $p$.
problems.lean:
theorem volume_lpSum_le (K : Set ℝ²) (hK : Convex ℝ K) (hKc : IsCompact K)
    (hKi : (interior K).Nonempty) (hsym : HasCentreOfSymmetry K) (h0 : (0 : ℝ²) ∈ K)
    (p q : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) (hq : 1 / p + 1 / q = 1) :
    volume (lpSum p K (-K)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (rsConstant q) * volume K

problems.title: The Maxwell conjecture — counterexample morse
problems.statement:
The second half of **Theorem 1** of Arathoon–Ball–Kvalheim: after a small perturbation of the
charge strengths, the counterexample potential is a Morse function, i.e. it has finitely many
critical points, all of which are non-degenerate, and there are still at least $24$ of them.

*Reference:* [arXiv:2607.27197](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27197)
problems.lean:
theorem maxwell_conjecture.counterexample_morse :
    ∃ (q : Fin 5 → ℝ) (a : Fin 5 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)), Function.Injective a ∧
      (∀ j, 0 < q j) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ equilibria q a, HasNondegenerateHessianAt (potential q a) x) ∧
      (equilibria q a).Finite ∧ 24 ≤ (equilibria q a).encard

problems.title: Proposition 1
problems.statement:
**Proposition 1** of Arathoon–Ball–Kvalheim: iterating the construction, for every $m \geq 0$
there is a configuration of $3 + 2m$ positive point charges whose potential has a finite number
$k \geq 4 + 20m$ of critical points, all of which are non-degenerate. In particular the ratio
of critical points to charges is asymptotically at least $10$.

*Reference:* [arXiv:2607.27197](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27197)
problems.lean:
theorem maxwell_conjecture.iterated (m : ℕ) :
    ∃ (q : Fin (3 + 2 * m) → ℝ) (a : Fin (3 + 2 * m) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
      Function.Injective a ∧ (∀ j, 0 < q j) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ equilibria q a, HasNondegenerateHessianAt (potential q a) x) ∧
      (equilibria q a).Finite ∧ 4 + 20 * m ≤ (equilibria q a).encard

problems.title: Conjecture 1.4
problems.statement:
**Conjecture 1.4**: if $\mu$ is an atomless $T_p$-invariant Borel probability measure on
$\mathbb{T}$, then $T_{q^n}\mu$ converges weak-star to Lebesgue measure.
This paper disproves the conjecture.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture_1_4 :
    ¬ ∀ p q : ℕ, 2 <= p → 2 <= q → MultiplicativelyIndependent p q →
      ∀ μ : ProbabilityMeasure 𝕋,
        MeasureTheory.IsAtomLess μ.1 → MeasurePreserving (Tn p) μ μ →
        Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => μ.map (Tn_continuous (q ^ n)).aemeasurable) atTop
          (𝓝 UnitAddCircle.ProbabilityMeasure)

problems.title: Shitov's bound (2019)
problems.statement:
**Shitov's bound (2019)**: Every synchronizing DFA with $n$ states admits a synchronizing
word of length at most $\left(\frac{7}{48} + \frac{2 \cdot 15625}{1597536}\right) n^3 + o(n^3)$,
where the $o(n^3)$ term is uniform over all alphabets. This is the best known upper bound
towards the Černý conjecture.
problems.lean:
theorem shitov_upper_bound :
    ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun n : ℝ => n ^ 3) ∧
    ∀ {α : Type*} {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] (M : DFA α σ) (hM : M.IsSynchronizing) ,
    ∃ w : List α, M.IsSynchronizingWord w ∧
    (w.length : ℝ) ≤ (7 / 48 + 2 * 15625 / 1597536) * (Fintype.card σ : ℝ) ^ 3
      + f (Fintype.card σ : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1070 — ii
problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that, given any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, there exist $f(n)$ points
such that no two are distance $1$ apart. Estimate $f(n)$. In particular, is it true that
$f(n)\geq n/4$?

This is the second part, read as the inequality for every $n$. The answer is no: Dúcz and Varga
[DuVa26, Theorem 1] construct a finite unit distance graph $G$ in the plane with
$\alpha(G) < |V(G)|/4$. For its vertex set $X$, `f_le X` gives
$f(|X|) \leq \alpha(U_X) \leq \alpha(G) < |X|/4$, where $U_X$ is the unit distance graph on $X$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_1070.parts.ii : ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) / 4 ≤ (f n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1079
problems.statement:
Let $r\geq 4$. If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices with at least $\mathrm{ex}(n;K_r)$ edges then
must $G$ contain a vertex with degree $d\gg_r n$ whose neighbourhood contains at least
$\mathrm{ex}(d;K_{r-1})$ edges?

As Erdős [Er75] says 'if true this would be a nice generalisation of Turán's theorem'. This is
true (unless $G$ it itself the Turán graph), and was proved by Bollobás and Thomason [BoTh81].
Bondy [Bo83b] showed that if $G$ has $>\mathrm{ex}(n;K_r)$ edges then the corresponding vertex
can be chosen to be of maximum degree in $G$.

The number of edges in the neighbourhood of $v$ is the number of edges of $G$ both of whose
endpoints are adjacent to $v$. Graphs on a single vertex are excluded, since there every degree
is $0$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1079 : ∀ r : ℕ, 4 ≤ r → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
    ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), extremalNumber n (completeGraph (Fin r)) ≤ G.edgeSet.ncard →
      ∃ v : Fin n, c * n ≤ G.degree v ∧
        extremalNumber (G.degree v) (completeGraph (Fin (r - 1))) ≤
          {e ∈ G.edgeSet | ∀ x ∈ e, G.Adj v x}.ncard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1092 — f asymptotic 2
problems.statement:
Is it true that $f_2(n) \gg n$? Disproved by Rödl, who showed $f_r(n) = o(n)$ for all fixed
$r \geq 2$. A conjecture of Erdős, Hajnal, and Szemerédi.

This seems to be closely related to, but distinct from, [744](https://www.erdosproblems.com/744).

Tang notes in the comments that Rödl [Ro82] constructed, for any $\epsilon>0$ and $k$, a graph
with chromatic number $\geq k$ such that every graph on $m$ vertices is bipartite after deleting at
most $\epsilon m$ edges.
problems.lean:
theorem f_asymptotic_2 :
    ¬ ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ, IsAdmissible 2 g ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (g n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1092 — f asymptotic general
problems.statement:
More generally, is $f_r(n)\gg_r n$ for every $r \geq 2$? Disproved by Rödl, who showed
$f_r(n) = o(n)$ for all fixed $r \geq 2$.
problems.lean:
theorem f_asymptotic_general :
    ¬ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r → ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ, IsAdmissible r g ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (g n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1100 — i
problems.statement:
If $1=d_1<\cdots<d_{\tau(n)}=n$ are the divisors of $n$, then let $\tau_\perp(n)$ count the number
of $i$ for which $(d_i,d_{i+1})=1$.

Is it true that $\tau_\perp(n)/\omega(n)\to \infty$ for almost all $n$?

This is the first part, asked by Erdős and Hall [ErHa78, p. 483]. We read it as: for every $C$ the
set of $n$ with $\tau_\perp(n)\leq C\omega(n)$ has natural density $0$. This is equivalent to
$\tau_\perp(n)/\omega(n)\to\infty$ along a set of density $1$, and it avoids dividing by
$\omega(1)=0$.

The answer is yes. By [ErTe89, Corollary 2, p. 288], $\tau_\perp(n)\geq(\log n)^{\log 3-1+o(1)}$
for almost all $n$ (see `erdos_1100.variants.normal_order`), while $\omega(n)\sim\log\log n$ for
almost all $n$ (Hardy-Ramanujan).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1100.parts.i :
    ∀ C : ℝ, {n : ℕ | (tauPerp n : ℝ) ≤ C * (ω n : ℝ)}.HasDensity 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1100 — ii
problems.statement:
If $1=d_1<\cdots<d_{\tau(n)}=n$ are the divisors of $n$, then let $\tau_\perp(n)$ count the number
of $i$ for which $(d_i,d_{i+1})=1$.

Is it true that
$$\tau_\perp(n)< \exp((\log n)^{o(1)})$$
for all $n$?

This is the second part. Erdős and Hall [ErHa78, p. 483] say it would be reasonable to expect
that for every $\epsilon>0$ one has $\tau_\perp(n)<\exp((\log n)^{\epsilon})$; the problem page
asks it as a question. We read $o(1)$ as: for every $\epsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$.
This is equivalent to a bound for all $n$ with an exponent that tends to $0$. A bound for all $n$
with a fixed small $\epsilon$ fails: for example $\tau_\perp(30)=4>\exp((\log 30)^{0.1})$.

The answer is no. Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe89, Theorem 4, p. 289] proved
$\max_{n\leq x}\tau_\perp(n)\geq\exp\bigl(((\log 2)^2+o(1))\log x/(\log\log x)^2\bigr)$ (see
`erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_max`). This gives infinitely many $n$ with
$\tau_\perp(n)>\exp((\log n)^{1/2})$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1100.parts.ii :
    ¬ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (tauPerp n : ℝ) < Real.exp (Real.log n ^ ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1130 — ii
problems.statement:
For $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in [-1,1]$ let
$$l_k(x)=\frac{\prod_{i\neq k}(x-x_i)}{\prod_{i\neq k}(x_k-x_i)},$$
which are such that $l_k(x_k)=1$ and $l_k(x_i)=0$ for $i\neq k$.

Let $x_0=-1$ and $x_{n+1}=1$ and
$$\Upsilon(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\min_{0\leq i\leq n}\max_{x\in[x_i,x_{i+1}]}
\sum_k \lvert l_k(x)\rvert.$$
Describe which choice of $x_i$ maximise $\Upsilon(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$.

This is the second part. Erdős [Er47, p. 1172], [Er67, p. 66] conjectured that the maximisers are
the node sets of [erdosproblems.com/1129](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1129), characterised by
equal local maxima. This was proved by Kilgore [Ki77], [Ki78] and by de Boor and Pinkus [dBPi78]
for canonical node sets, with the smallest local maximum between consecutive nodes in place of
$\Upsilon$ (see [Ib16, Section 3.7]); this is `erdos_1130.variants.canonical`.

Here, as in the question, $\Upsilon$ includes the two outer gaps and the maximisers range over
all node sets in $[-1,1]$. A maximiser is then not unique in general, and it need not have all
$n+1$ local maxima $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_n$ equal: for $n=3$ the nodes $-s,0,s$ with
$0<s\le\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}$ all give $\Upsilon=\frac54$, the largest possible value, and for
$s=\frac12$ the four local maxima are $7,\frac54,\frac54,7$. The cited sources do not describe the
whole set of maximisers, so `erdos_1130.parts.ii.answer` is left as `sorry`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1130.parts.ii (n : ℕ) :
    {x : Fin n → ℝ | IsNodeSet x ∧ ∀ y : Fin n → ℝ, IsNodeSet y → upsilon y ≤ upsilon x} =
      erdos_1130.parts.ii.answer n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1164
problems.statement:
Let $R_n$ be the maximal integer such that almost every random walk from the origin in
$\mathbb{Z}^2$ visits every $x\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ with $\lVert x\rVert\leq R_n$ in at most $n$ steps.

Is it true that
$$\log R_n \asymp \sqrt{\log n}?$$

A problem of Erdős and Taylor, see [ErTa60, p. 153] and [Va99, 6.76]. This is true, as proved
independently by Révész [Re90] and Kesten, see [DPRZ04, Section 1.3], which reports that they
proved the following. The probability that the disc of radius $n$ is covered by time
$e^{t(\log n)^2}$ has $\liminf_{n\to\infty}$ at least $e^{-b/t}$ and $\limsup_{n\to\infty}$ at
most $e^{-a/t}$ for every $t>0$, where $0<a<b<\infty$ are constants. The exact limit is in
`erdos_1164.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni`.

We take the simple random walk (`IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps`). Read literally, $R_n$ would be $0$:
for every $n$ some walk misses a neighbour of the origin, and such walks have positive
probability. So $R_n=R_n(\omega)$ is the random variable `coveringRadius`, and
$\log R_n\asymp\sqrt{\log n}$ means tightness: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are constants
$c>0$ and $C$ such that $c\sqrt{\log n}\leq\log R_n\leq C\sqrt{\log n}$ with probability at least
$1-\varepsilon$ for all large $n$. This is the sense of the results above and of
`erdos_1164.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni`, which are about probabilities, not almost sure
bounds. [ErTa60, p. 153] asks an almost sure question about the time needed to cover the disc of
radius $n$; we follow the results in probability reported in [DPRZ04, Section 1.3].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1164 {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ} (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ c C : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      1 - ε ≤ (ℙ {ω | c * Real.sqrt (Real.log n) ≤ Real.log (coveringRadius X n ω) ∧
        Real.log (coveringRadius X n ω) ≤ C * Real.sqrt (Real.log n)}).toReal

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1165
problems.statement:
Given a random walk $s_0,s_1,\ldots$ in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, starting at the origin, let $f_n(x)$ count
the number of $0\leq k\leq n$ such that $s_k=x$.

Let
$$F(n)=\{ x: f_n(x) = \max_y f_n(y)\}$$
be the set of 'favourite values'. Find
$$\mathbb{P}(\lvert F(n)\rvert=r\textrm{ infinitely often})$$
for $r\geq 3$.

A problem of Erdős and Révész [Va99, 6.77]. We take the simple random walk, on any probability
space (`IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps`). Hao, Li, Okada and Zheng [HLOZ24, Theorem 1.1] showed that the
probability is $1$ for $r=3$ and $0$ for $r\geq 4$, see `erdos_1165.variants.hao_li_okada_zheng`.
The value of `erdos_1165.answer` for $r<3$ is not used.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1165 {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ} (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) (r : ℕ) (hr : 3 ≤ r) :
    ℙ {ω | ∃ᶠ n in atTop, (favouriteSites X n ω).encard = (r : ℕ∞)} = erdos_1165.answer r

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1166
problems.statement:
Given a random walk $s_0,s_1,\ldots$ in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, starting at the origin, let $f_k(x)$ count
the number of $0\leq l\leq k$ such that $s_l=x$.

Let
$$F(k)=\{ x: f_k(x) = \max_y f_k(y)\}$$
be the set of 'favourite values'. Is it true that
$$\left\lvert \bigcup_{k\leq n}F(k)\right\rvert \leq (\log n)^{O(1)}$$
almost surely, for all but finitely many $n$?

A problem of Erdős and Révész [Va99, 6.78]. The answer is yes. Almost surely there are at most
three favourite sites at all large times [HLOZ24, Theorem 1.1], see
`Erdos1165.erdos_1165.variants.hao_li_okada_zheng`, and the maximal local time is
$O((\log n)^2)$ [ErTa60, p. 162], see `erdos_1166.variants.erdos_taylor`. A favourite
site stays a favourite site for as long as the maximal local time does not change. So for each
value of the maximal local time, the sites that are favourite at some time while it has that value
are all favourite at the last such time, and there are at most three of them, up to finitely many
exceptions. This gives the bound $O((\log n)^2)$ stated on the problem page.

We take the simple random walk (`IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps`). We read $O(1)$ as a single exponent
`C` that works for almost every walk. The cardinality is `Set.encard`, so an infinite union would
not satisfy the bound.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1166 {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω] [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ} (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ᵐ ω, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ((⋃ k ≤ n, favouriteSites X k ω).encard : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.log n ^ C)

problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite $3$-uniform hypergraph, and let $F_G(\kappa)$ denote the collection of
$3$-uniform hypergraphs with chromatic number $\kappa$ not containing $G$. If
$F_G(\aleph_1)$ is non-empty, then it contains a hypergraph on at most
$2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$ vertices. Li [Li26, Corollary 1.4(1)] proved this.

          Cardinal.mk V ≤ (2 : Cardinal) ^ ((2 : Cardinal) ^ ℵ₀)

The assertion that two non-empty avoidance families $F_G(\aleph_1)$ and $F_H(\aleph_1)$
always have non-empty intersection is false. Li [Li26, Corollary 1.4(2)] gives a
counterexample using two triples sharing a pair and the loose seven-cycle.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1189 — iv
problems.statement:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

Are there infinitely many $n$ such that the divisors of $n$ (which are $>1$) form an irreducible
covering set?

This is the fourth part. Sun [Su07, Theorem 1.4(i) and Corollary 1.3] proved that the answer is
yes: see `erdos_1189.variants.sun`.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1198
problems.statement:
If $\mathbb{N}$ is $2$-coloured, must there exist an infinite set $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ such that
all expressions of the shape
$$\sum_{j=1}^{k}\prod_{i\in S_j}a_i,$$
for $k\geq 1$ and pairwise disjoint nonempty finite sets of indices $S_1,\ldots,S_k$ (excluding the
trivial expressions $a_i$, that is $k=1$ and $|S_1|=1$), have the same colour?

Erdős [Er80, p.104] wrote that "one would perhaps guess that the answer must be 'no' but no
counterexample is in sight". The case where every $S_j$ is a singleton is Hindman's theorem [Hi74].
The answer is no: a counterexample was given by Smith [Sm95].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1198 :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℕ → Fin 2, ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono a ∧ 0 < a 0 ∧ ∃ col : Fin 2,
      ∀ (k : ℕ) (S : Fin k → Finset ℕ), 0 < k → (∀ j, (S j).Nonempty) →
        Pairwise (fun j j' => Disjoint (S j) (S j')) → ¬ (k = 1 ∧ ∀ j, #(S j) = 1) →
        c (∑ j, ∏ i ∈ S j, a i) = col

problems.title: Erdős Problem 180
problems.statement:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite set of finite graphs then $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})$ is the maximum
number of edges a graph on $n$ vertices can have without containing any subgraphs from
$\mathcal{F}$. Note that it is trivial that $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})\leq \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ for
every $G\in\mathcal{F}$. Is it true that, for every $\mathcal{F}$, there exists $G\in\mathcal{F}$
such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\ll_{\mathcal{F}}\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})?$$

This is the Erdős–Simonovits compactness conjecture. The answer is no: OpenAI [OpenAI26] give a
family of connected bipartite graphs, none of them acyclic, for which no single member controls
the family extremal number. See `erdos_180.variants.counterexample`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_180 :
    ¬ ∀ family : Finset FiniteGraph,
      family.Nonempty → IsCyclicFamily family → IsCompactFamily family

Let $\{S_k\}$ be any sequence of sets in the complex plane, each of which has no finite
limit point. Then there exists a sequence $\{n_k\}$ of positive integers and a
transcendental entire function $f(z)$ such that $f^{(n_k)}(z) = 0$ if $z \in S_k$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 241 — upper bound white

$f(N) \leq ((2/0.574636066)^{1/3}+o(1))N^{1/3}$ (note that $(2/0.574636066)^{1/3}\approx 1.5155$).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 346
problems.statement:
Is it true that for every lacunary, strongly complete sequence `A` that is not complete whenever
infinitely many terms are removed from it, `lim A (n + 1) / A n = (1 + √5) / 2`?

The answer is no. A counterexample recorded at [erdosproblems.com/346] has all successive ratios
at least `6 / 5`, but has subsequences of successive ratios tending to two different limits,
`(1 + √5) / 2` and `(1 + √5) / 2 + 1 / 4`.

    Tendsto (fun n => A (n + 1) / (A n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 ((1 + √5) / 2))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 348
problems.statement:
For what values of $0 \leq m < n$ is there a complete sequence
$A = \{a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots\}$ of integers such that
 1. $A$ remains complete after removing any $m$ elements, but
 2. $A$ is not complete after removing any $n$ elements.

Completeness allows finitely many exceptions, and deletions remove indexed occurrences.

      (_ : ∀ s, s.card = m → IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (Function.updateFinset a s 0))
        (_ : ∀ t, t.card = n → ¬IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (Function.updateFinset a t 0)) } =
    erdos_348.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 481
problems.statement:
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_r\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{i}\frac{1}{a_i}>1$. For any
finite sequence of $n$ (not necessarily distinct) integers $A=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ let $T(A)$ denote
the sequence of length $rn$ given by
$$(a_ix_j+b_i)_{1\leq j\leq n, 1\leq i\leq r}.$$
Prove that, if $A_1=(1)$ and $A_{i+1}=T(A_i)$, then there must be some $A_k$ with repeated
elements.

given by Kolpakov and Talambutsa [KoTa22]. Essentially the same proof was found independently by
Barreto in the comment section.

If $T$ is a tree which is a bipartite graph with $k$ vertices in one class and $2k$ vertices
in the other class then
$$R(T)=4k-1.$$

This is false: Norin, Sun, and Zhao [NSZ16] have proved that if $T$ is the union of two stars on $k$
and $2k$ vertices, with an edge joining the centre of the two stars, then $R(T)\geq (4.2-o(1))k$,
and conjectured that $R(T)=(4.2+o(1))k$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 570

Let $k\geq 3$. Is it true that, if $m$ is sufficiently large, for any graph $H$ on $m$ edges
without isolated vertices,
$$R(C_k,H) \leq 2m+\left\lfloor\frac{k-1}{2}\right\rfloor?$$

for $k=3$ independently by Goddard and Kleitman [GoKl94] and Sidorenko [Si91]. This was proved
for $k=5$ by Jayawardene [Ja99]. Finally it was proved for all odd $k\geq 7$ by Cambie, Freschi,
Morawski, Petrova, and Pokrovskiy [CFMPP26].

This problem is #35 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

cycles in $G$. Assume $n>0$. Is it true that
$$\sum\frac{1}{a_i}\gg \log k?$$

the second question remains.

The bound is stated for all sufficiently large $k$: [GKS84, Theorem 4'] proves it for $k \geq b$,
where $b$ is a constant. The case of $k$ slightly larger than $1$ is a separate problem, studied
in [GPSV85].

problems.title: Erdős Problem 78 — li strongly explicit
problems.statement:
The construction of Li [Li23b] is strongly explicit: there are graphs on $n$ vertices with no
clique and no independent set of size $(\log n)^C$, for some constant $C > 0$, whose adjacency
queries are answered in time polynomial in $\log n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_78.variants.li_strongly_explicit :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ adj : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, NoHomogeneousSet (stronglyExplicitGraph adj n) ⌈(log n) ^ C⌉₊

problems.title: Erdős Problem 78 — little o sqrt
problems.statement:
Erdős also asked for an explicit construction of graphs on $n$ vertices whose largest clique and
independent set have size $o(n^{1/2})$. Such constructions are now known; see [Co15] for the
history.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_78.variants.little_o_sqrt :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ √(n : ℝ)) ∧
      ∃ adj : List Bool × ℕ × ℕ → Bool, IsPolyTime adj ∧
        ∀ᶠ n in atTop, NoHomogeneousSet (explicitGraph adj n) ⌈f n⌉₊

problems.title: Erdős Problem 78 — nonconstructive
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er47] gave a simple probabilistic, non-constructive proof that $R(k) > C^k$ for some
constant $C > 1$. In fact $R(k) > 2^{k/2}$ for all $k \geq 3$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_78.variants.nonconstructive :
    ∃ C > (1 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k in atTop, C ^ k < (SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 832
problems.statement:
Let $r\geq 3$ and $k$ be sufficiently large in terms of $r$. Is it true that every $r$-uniform
hypergraph with chromatic number $k$ has at least
$$\binom{(r-1)(k-1)+1}{r}$$
edges, with equality only for the complete graph on $(r-1)(k-1)+1$ vertices?

This was disproved by Alon [Al85]. The validity of this conjecture for $r=3$ remains open.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_832 :
    ¬ ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
      H.IsUniform r → H.HasHypergraphChromaticNumber k →
      ((r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1).choose r ≤ H.card ∧
      (H.card = ((r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1).choose r →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.card = (r - 1) * (k - 1) + 1 ∧ H = S.powersetCard r)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 834 — i
problems.statement:
Does there exist a $3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph in which every vertex has degree
$\geq 7$, where criticality means that the transversal number is $3$ and deleting any edge
reduces it to $2$?

In the first formulation, the transversal notion of criticality, Li [Li25] proves that a
$3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph must have a vertex of degree $\leq 6$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_834.parts.i :
    ¬ ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
    H.IsUniform 3 ∧ (H : Set (Finset (Fin n))).HasFiniteTransversal 3 ∧
      ¬ (H : Set (Finset (Fin n))).HasFiniteTransversal 2 ∧
      (∀ e ∈ H, (H.erase e : Set (Finset (Fin n))).HasFiniteTransversal 2) ∧
      ∀ v : Fin n, 7 ≤ H.hypergraphDegree v

problems.title: Erdős Problem 834 — ii
problems.statement:
Does there exist a $3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph with minimum degree at least $7$,
where criticality means that deleting any edge or vertex reduces chromatic number $3$ to $2$?

In the second formulation, the chromatic notion of criticality, Li [Li25] provides an
explicit $3$-critical $3$-uniform hypergraph on $9$ vertices with minimum degree $7$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_834.parts.ii :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
    H.IsUniform 3 ∧ H.HasHypergraphChromaticNumber 3 ∧
      (∀ e ∈ H, (H.erase e).HypergraphColorable 2) ∧
      (∀ v : Fin n, (H.filter (fun e ↦ v ∉ e)).HypergraphColorable 2) ∧
      ∀ v : Fin n, 7 ≤ H.hypergraphDegree v

problems.title: Erdős Problem 878 — iii all
problems.statement:
Is it true that, for all $x$, $\max_{n\le x}f(n)=\max_{n\le x}F(n)$?
Barreto noted that this is false at $x=210$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_878.parts.iii_all :
    ¬ ∀ x : ℕ, maxUpTo f x = maxUpTo F x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 88 — erdos mckay
problems.statement:
Erdős and McKay proved the statement of `erdos_88` with $\delta n^2$ replaced by
$\delta (\log n)^2$. Since $(\log n)^2 \leq n^2$, this weaker bound also follows from
`erdos_88`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_88.variants.erdos_mckay :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) < ε * Real.log n → (G.indepNum : ℝ) < ε * Real.log n →
        ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℝ) ≤ δ * Real.log n ^ 2 →
          ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).edgeSet.ncard = m

problems.title: Erdős Problem 88 — kwan sah sauermann sawhney
problems.statement:
Kwan, Sah, Sauermann, and Sawhney [KSSS22, Theorem 1.1] proved the following stronger statement.
Fix $C > 0$ and $\eta > 0$, and let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with no independent set or
clique of size $\geq C \log_2 n$, where $n$ is sufficiently large with respect to $C$ and $\eta$.
Then for every integer $0 \leq m \leq (1 - \eta) e(G)$ there is an induced subgraph of $G$ with
exactly $m$ edges.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_88.variants.kwan_sah_sauermann_sawhney :
    ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ η > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) < C * Real.logb 2 n → (G.indepNum : ℝ) < C * Real.logb 2 n →
        ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℝ) ≤ (1 - η) * G.edgeSet.ncard →
          ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).edgeSet.ncard = m

problems.title: Erdős Problem 883 — ii
problems.statement:
Is it true that, for every $\ell\geq 1$, if $n$ is sufficiently large and
$$|A| > \lfloor n/2\rfloor + \lfloor n/3\rfloor - \lfloor n/6\rfloor$$
then $G(A)$ must contain a complete $(1,\ell,\ell)$ tripartite graph on $2\ell+1$ vertices?

The second question was solved by Sárközy [Sa99], who proved this with
$\ell \gg \log n/\log\log n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_883.parts.ii :
    ∀ l : ℕ, 1 ≤ l → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A : Finset ℕ,
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n →
      n / 2 + n / 3 - n / 6 < A.card →
      (SimpleGraph.completeMultipartiteGraph (fun i : Fin 3 ↦ Fin (![1, l, l] i))).IsContained
        (coprimeGraph.induce (A : Set ℕ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 983 — i
problems.statement:
Let $n\geq 2$ and $\pi(n)<k\leq n$. Let $f(k,n)$ be the smallest integer $r$ such that in any
$A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ of size $\lvert A\rvert=k$ there exist primes $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ such
that $>r$ many $a\in A$ are only divisible by primes from $\{p_1,\ldots,p_r\}$.

Is it true that
$$2\pi(n^{1/2})-f(\pi(n)+1,n)\to \infty$$
as $n\to \infty$?

This is the first part. The primes may depend on $A$. Erdős and Straus conjectured this
[Er70b, p. 138 and p. 140].

The answer is no: Liam Price and GPT-5.5 Pro showed on the
[forum](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/983#post-6104) that
$f(\pi(n)+1,n)=2\pi(n^{1/2})+1$ for infinitely many $n$; see the
[explanation](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/983#post-6525) by Nat Sothanaphan.
Write $p_k$ for the $k$-th prime. By [Po79, Corollary after Theorem 2.2] there are infinitely
many $N$ with $p_{N-i}p_{N+i}<p_N^2$ for $1\leq i<N$. Take $n=p_N^2-1$, so
$\pi(n^{1/2})=N-1$. Let $A$ consist of the products of adjacent primes on the path
$p_{2N-1},p_1,p_{2N-2},p_2,\ldots,p_{N+1},p_{N-1},p_N$, its two endpoint primes, and the
other primes up to $n$. Then $\lvert A\rvert=\pi(n)+1$, and for any $r\leq 2N-2$ primes at
most $r$ elements of $A$ are divisible only by those primes, so $f(\pi(n)+1,n)\geq 2N-1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_983.parts.i :
    ¬ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦
      2 * (Nat.primeCounting (Nat.sqrt n) : ℤ) - (f (Nat.primeCounting n + 1) n : ℤ))
      atTop atTop

problems.title: Euclidean Ramsey configurations on a circle
problems.statement:
Every nonempty configuration of at most five distinct points on a circle is Euclidean
Ramsey: every finite colouring of a suitable Euclidean space has a monochromatic
copy with the same pairwise distances. Singletons and radius-zero circles are included.
problems.lean:
theorem at_most_five_circle_points_ramsey {s : ℕ} (a : Fin s → E (Fin 2))
    (hs : 0 < s) (hs5 : s ≤ 5) (ha : Function.Injective a)
    (hsphere : ∃ c : E (Fin 2), ∃ r : ℝ, ∀ i, dist (a i) c = r) :
    ∀ colors : ℕ, 2 ≤ colors → ∃ D : ℕ, 1 ≤ D ∧
      ∀ c : E (Fin D) → Fin colors, ∃ b : Fin s → E (Fin D),
        (∀ i j, dist (b i) (b j) = dist (a i) (a j)) ∧
          ∃ k : Fin colors, ∀ i, c (b i) = k

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 23
problems.statement:
Suppose that $\mathbb{N}$ is finitely coloured. Are there $x,y$ of the same colour such that $x^2 +
 y^2$ is a square?

Solved in [FrKlMo25].
problems.lean:
theorem green_23 :
    -- For every finite colouring of the natural numbers
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (c : ℕ → Fin k),
    -- there exist two numbers of the same colour whose squares sum to a square
    ∃ x y : ℕ,
      0 < x ∧ 0 < y ∧  -- Exclude trivial x^2 + 0^2 = x^2 solution
      c x = c y ∧      -- Same colour
      IsSquare (x^2 + y^2)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 49
problems.statement:
Suppose that $A \subset \mathbb{F}_2^n$ is a set with $|A + A| \leq K|A|$. Is it true that $A$
is covered by $K^{O(1)}$ translates of a subspace of size $\leq |A|$?

Solved by [GGM25], with at most $2K^{12}$ translates. The factor $2$ cannot be omitted: for
$A = \mathbb{F}_2^n \setminus \{0\}$ one has $K = 2^n / (2^n - 1)$, so $K^C \to 1$ as
$n \to \infty$, while every subspace of size at most $|A|$ is proper and two translates are needed.
problems.lean:
theorem green_49 :
    ∃ C > 0,
      ∀ n (A : Finset (𝔽₂ n)), A.Nonempty →
      ∀ K ≥ (1 : ℝ), (#(A + A) : ℝ) ≤ K * #A →
        ∃ (W : Submodule (ZMod 2) (𝔽₂ n)) (T : Finset (𝔽₂ n)),
          Nat.card W ≤ #A ∧
          (#T : ℝ) ≤ 2 * K ^ C ∧
          (A : Set (𝔽₂ n)) ⊆ T + W

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 85 — green 85 loose
problems.statement:
From [Gr24] "It is quite easy to show using Cauchy-Schwarz that there must be such a rectangle with
area $\gg \alpha^2 (\log 1/\alpha)^{-1}$."
problems.lean:
theorem green_85_loose :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ α in 𝓝[>] 0,
    ∀ A : Set (ℝ × ℝ),
    IsOpen A →
    A ⊆ Icc 0 1 ×ˢ Icc 0 1 →
    A.Nonempty →
    α = (volume A).toReal →
    ∃ x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂,
      {(x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₁, y₂)} ⊆ A ∧
      c * α ^ 2 * (Real.log (1/α))⁻¹ ≤ |x₁ - x₂| * |y₁ - y₂|

problems.title: Conjecture 20.76
problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group and assume that all abelian normal subgroups of $G$
have order at most $p^k$. Is it true that every abelian subgroup of $G$ has order at most
$p^{2k}$?

The answer is no. Muliarchyk's Proposition 6.1 gives a finite $2$-group of order
$2^{145}$ whose abelian normal subgroups have order at most $2^{42}$, but which
contains an elementary abelian subgroup of order $2^{85} > 2^{84}$.
problems.lean:
theorem kourovka_20_76 :
    ¬ (∀ᵉ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (hg : IsPGroup p G) (_ : Finite G) (k : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ H: Subgroup G, H.Normal ∧ IsMulCommutative H → Nat.card H ≤ p ^ k),
    (∀ H : Subgroup G, IsMulCommutative H → Nat.card H ≤ p ^ (2 * k)))

problems.title: Local uniformization after a finite extension.
problems.statement:
**Local uniformization after a finite extension.** Every valuation ring of a finitely generated
field extension $F \mid k$ that contains $k$ admits local uniformization over $k$ after a finite
extension $E$ of $F$, in any characteristic. This is the main theorem of [KK2009]. Compare
[Tem2013], where the extension of $F$ is purely inseparable but the ground field is extended too.
problems.lean:
theorem local_uniformization_after_finite_extension (k F : Type*) [Field k] [Field F]
    [Algebra k F] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k F] (𝒪 : ValuationSubring F)
    (hk : ∀ x : k, algebraMap k F x ∈ 𝒪) :
    ∃ (E : IntermediateField F (AlgebraicClosure F)) (_ : FiniteDimensional F E)
      (𝒪' : ValuationSubring E),
      𝒪'.comap (algebraMap F E) = 𝒪 ∧ 𝒪'.HasLocalUniformization k

problems.title: Mean value problem — mean value problem of real roots
problems.statement:
The following tighter bound depending on the degree $d$ of the polynomial $p$ has been shown by
Tischler. Let $z$ be a complex number such that the normalised polynomial $p(X + z) - p(z)$ has
only real roots, i.e. every $x$ with $p(x) = p(z)$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Im} x = \operatorname{Im} z$. Then there is a critical point $c$ of $p$ such that
$|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(z)|$.
problems.lean:
lemma mean_value_problem_of_real_roots (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree) (z : ℂ)
    (h : ∀ x : ℂ, p.eval x = p.eval z → x.im = z.im) (K : ℝ) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1)/ p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval z‖

problems.title: Mean value problem — mean value problem of roots same norm
problems.statement:
The following tighter bound depending on the degree $d$ of the polynomial $p$ has been shown by
Tischler. Let $z$ be a complex number such that all nonzero roots of the normalised polynomial
$p(X + z) - p(z)$ have the same norm, i.e. all $x \ne z$ with $p(x) = p(z)$ have the same
distance to $z$. Then there is a critical point $c$ of $p$ such that
$|p(z) - p(c)|/|z-c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(z)|$.
problems.lean:
lemma mean_value_problem_of_roots_same_norm (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree) (z : ℂ)
    (h : ∀ x y : ℂ, p.eval x = p.eval z → p.eval y = p.eval z → x ≠ z → y ≠ z →
      ‖x - z‖ = ‖y - z‖) (K : ℝ) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1)/ p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval z‖

problems.title: Partitions $n = x + y$ with $x^2 + xy + y^2$ prime — conjecture 4
problems.statement:
Conjecture:
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sum_{p < N, \, p \equiv 1 \pmod 3} x(p)^2}{\sum_{p < N, \, p \equiv 1 \pmod 3} y(p)^2} = \frac{52}{9},$$
where for a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, $x(p) > y(p) > 0$ are the unique positive integers such
that $p = x(p)^2 + x(p)y(p) + y(p)^2$.
- _Zhi-Wei Sun_

Disproved by Hecke's (1920) equidistribution theorem for Hecke Grossencharacters of
$\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$, which yields the true limit
$$\frac{\int_0^{\pi/6} (\cos\theta - \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\sin\theta)^2\,d\theta}{\int_0^{\pi/6} \frac{4}{3}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta} = \frac{2\pi}{2\pi - 3\sqrt{3}} \approx 5.780124 \neq \frac{52}{9}.$$
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture_4 :
    ¬ Filter.atTop.Tendsto
      (fun N : ℕ =>
        (∑ p ∈ (Finset.range N).filter (fun p => p.Prime ∧ p % 3 = 1), ((xp p : ℝ) ^ 2)) /
        (∑ p ∈ (Finset.range N).filter (fun p => p.Prime ∧ p % 3 = 1), ((yp p : ℝ) ^ 2)))
      (nhds (52 / 9 : ℝ))

problems.title: Central factorial numbers: $((2n)!!)^2$
problems.statement:
Let $\zeta$ be a primitive $(2n+1)$-th root of unity. Then the permanent of the
$2n \times 2n$ matrix $[m(j,k)]_{j,k=1..2n}$ is $a(n)/(2n+1) = ((2n)!!)^2/(2n+1)$,
where $m(j,k)$ is $1$ or $(1+\zeta^{j-k})/(1-\zeta^{j-k})$ according as $j = k$ or not.
- Zhi-Wei Sun, Jun 26 2022

Proved by [SSX22], Theorem 1.3(ii): for odd $m > 1$ and $\zeta$ a primitive $m$-th root of
unity, the permanent of $[c_{j,k}]_{1 \le j,k \le m-1}$ is $((m-1)!!)^2/m$. Take $m = 2n+1$;
translating both matrix indices by one leaves $j - k$ unchanged. For $n = 0$ the matrix is
empty and both sides are $1$.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) :
    let N : ℕ := 2 * n
    let K : ℕ := N + 1
    ∀ (ζ : ℂ), IsPrimitiveRoot ζ K →
      Matrix.permanent (fun (j k : Fin N) =>
        if j = k then
          (1 : ℂ)
        else
          let pow : ℤ := (j : ℤ) - (k : ℤ)
          (1 + ζ ^ pow) / (1 - ζ ^ pow)
      ) = (a n : ℂ) / (K : ℂ)

problems.title: Parities of partition numbers — odd bound
problems.statement:
The odd half of Theorem 1 of Ono–Swaminathan, with its effective bound: for square-free `D > 1`
with `D ≡ 23 (mod 24)` there is an `m` coprime to `6` with `m ≤ 12 h(-D) + 2` such that
`p((D m² + 1) / 24)` is odd, where `h(-D)` is the class number of `ℚ(√-D)`. Here `ℚ(√-D)` is
`AdjoinRoot (X ^ 2 + D)`, a number field since `X ^ 2 + D` is irreducible over `ℚ` for `D > 0`.
problems.lean:
theorem ono_swaminathan.odd_bound (D : ℕ) (hD : 1 < D) (hsq : Squarefree D) (h23 : D % 24 = 23) :
    haveI : Fact (Irreducible (X ^ 2 + C (D : ℚ))) :=
      ⟨irreducible_X_sq_add_C_of_pos (Nat.cast_pos.2 (by lia))⟩
    ∃ m : ℕ, m.Coprime 6 ∧
      m ≤ 12 * NumberField.classNumber (AdjoinRoot (X ^ 2 + C (D : ℚ))) + 2 ∧
      Odd (partitionNumber ((D * m ^ 2 + 1) / 24))

problems.title: The Sato–Tate conjecture
problems.statement:
**The Sato–Tate conjecture**: for a non-CM elliptic curve $E$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ and
$-1 \le a \le b \le 1$, the proportion of primes $p < N$ whose normalized coefficient
belongs to $[a,b]$ tends to
$$
\frac{2}{\pi}\int_a^b \sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx
$$
as $N \to \infty$.

The finitely many primes where the supplied equation fails to have integral
coefficients and nonsingular reduction do not affect this limit.

Established through the work of Clozel–Harris–Taylor [CHT08], Taylor [Tay08],
Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor [HST10], and
Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor [BGHT11].
problems.lean:
theorem satoTate_conjecture
    (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic] (hCM : ¬ HasCM E)
    (a b : ℝ) (ha : -1 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hb : b ≤ 1) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun N : ℕ ↦
        (primeCountInInterval E a b N : ℝ) /
          ((Nat.primesBelow N).card : ℝ))
      Filter.atTop
      (nhds (satoTateMeasure a b))

problems.title: Serre's multiplicity conjectures — intersectionMultiplicity pos of unramified
problems.statement:
Serre proved the positivity conjecture when $R$ is of mixed characteristic and unramified, that
is, when the characteristic $p$ of the residue field is not in the square of the maximal ideal
of $R$ [Se00]. The hypothesis $p \notin \mathfrak m^2$ excludes $p = 0$ and the equal
characteristic case, where $p = 0$ in $R$.
problems.lean:
theorem intersectionMultiplicity_pos_of_unramified (p : ℕ) [CharP (ResidueField R) p]
    (hp : (p : R) ∉ maximalIdeal R ^ 2) (h : IsFiniteLength R (M ⊗[R] N))
    (hdim : Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N = ringKrullDim R) :
    0 < intersectionMultiplicity R M N

problems.title: ShelahSpencerZeroOneLaw
problems.statement:
If $0 < \alpha < 1$ is irrational, then for every first-order sentence $\varphi$ in the
language of graphs, the probability that $G(n, n^{-\alpha})$ satisfies $\varphi$ tends to either
zero or one as $n \to \infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem zeroOne_irrational
   (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α ∧ α < 1) (hirr : Irrational α) (φ : Language.graph.Sentence) :
   Tendsto (fun n =>
     sparseRandomGraph n α hα.1
       {G | @Language.Sentence.Realize Language.graph (Fin n) G.structure φ}) atTop (𝓝 0) ∨
   Tendsto (fun n =>
     sparseRandomGraph n α hα.1
       {G | @Language.Sentence.Realize Language.graph (Fin n) G.structure φ}) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: ShelahSpencerZeroOneLaw
problems.statement:
If $0 < \alpha < 1$ is rational, then there is a first-order sentence $\varphi$ in the
language of graphs whose probability in $G(n, n^{-\alpha})$ does not converge as
$n \to \infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem zeroOne_rational
   (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α ∧ α < 1) (hrat : ¬Irrational α) :
   ∃ φ : Language.graph.Sentence,
   ∀ b : ENNReal,
   ¬ Tendsto (fun n =>
     sparseRandomGraph n α hα.1
       {G | @Language.Sentence.Realize Language.graph (Fin n) G.structure φ}) atTop (𝓝 b)

problems.title: Sidorenko's conjecture (1993)
problems.statement:
**Case: `H = K_{a,b}` is a complete bipartite graph (Sidorenko 1993, graphon version).**

Every complete bipartite graph $K_{a,b}$ satisfies Sidorenko's inequality for all graphons on $[0, 1]$.
problems.lean:
theorem sidorenko_completeBipartiteGraph_graphon {A B : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B]
    [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq B] (W : LimitObjects.Graphon) :
    (graphonEdgeDensity W) ^ (completeBipartiteGraph A B).edgeFinset.card ≤
      graphonHomDensity (completeBipartiteGraph A B) W

problems.title: TAS Trees Conjecture: The $(2,3,4)$-spider tree (Solved case).
problems.statement:
**TAS Trees Conjecture: The $(2,3,4)$-spider tree (Solved case).**

The $(2,3,4)$-spider tree satisfies the Tournament Anti-Sidorenko Trees Conjecture.

*Reference:*
* [ArXiv 2605.14138](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14138)
problems.lean:
theorem tournament_anti_sidorenko_spider234 {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (T : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel T.Adj] (hSpider : IsSpider234 T) :
    ∃ (D : Digraph V),
      D.IsOrientation T ∧
      ∀ {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] [Nonempty W]
        (G : Digraph W) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
        G.IsTournament →
        Digraph.homDensity D G ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ T.edgeFinset.card

problems.title: Voronovskaja-type Formula for the Bezier Variant of the Bernstein Operators
problems.statement:
Classical Voronovskaja theorem (α = 1).

For functions $f$ that are $C^2$ on $[0,1]$, the limit:
$$
n\bigl( B_n f(x) - f(x) \bigr)
\;\longrightarrow\;
\frac{1}{2}\, x(1 - x)\, f''(x)
$$
problems.lean:
theorem voronovskaja_theorem.bernstein_operators
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ I)
    (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 f I) :
    let f'' : ℝ := iteratedDerivWithin 2 f I x
    Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) => (n : ℝ) * (bezierBernstein n 1 f x - f x))
    atTop
    (𝓝 ((1 / 2) * x * (1 - x) * f''))

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 24
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 24](http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj24)
(status F, disproved):

For every finite simple connected graph `G`,
`b(G) ≥ λ(G) + ⌈(min_v dist_even(v)) / 3⌉`
where `b(G)` is the size of a largest induced bipartite subgraph,
`λ(G) := max_v l(v)` is the maximum over all vertices of the independence
number of the open neighbourhood of `v`, and `dist_even(v)` is the number of
vertices at even distance from `v`.

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 33
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 33](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$,
$\operatorname{path}(G) \ge \lceil 2 \operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(M, V) \rceil$,
where $\operatorname{path}(G)$ is the number of vertices of a largest induced path of $G$,
$M$ is the set of maximum-degree vertices, and
$\operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(M, V)$ is the average of all nonzero distances
$\operatorname{dist}\_G(m, v)$ with $m \in M$ and $v \in V$.

The conjecture is false: the source records an October 2005 counterexample with
$\operatorname{path}(G) = 7$ and $\operatorname{dist}\_{\operatorname{avg}}(M, V) = 3.56$.

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 5
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 5](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, `Ls(G)` is bounded below by the maximal size
of a sphere of radius `radius(G)` around the centres of `G`.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture5 (G : SimpleGraph V) (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    letI centers := { v : V | G.eccent v = G.radius }
    letI r_nat := G.radius.toNat
    letI sphere_verts (v : V) : Set V := { w | G.dist v w = r_nat }
    letI sphere_size (v : V) : ℝ := ↑(Finset.univ.filter (fun w => w ∈ sphere_verts v)).card
    letI max_sphere_size := sSup (sphere_size '' centers)
    max_sphere_size ≤ Ls G

problems.title: Agoh-Giuga conjecture — isStrongGiuga iff
problems.statement:
Giuga showed that a number `n` is strong Giuga if and only if it is
Carmichael and `∑_{p|n} 1/p - 1/n ∈ ℕ` (i.e., if and only if it is Carmichael
and weak Giuga).
Ref: G. Giuga, _Su una presumibile proprieta caratteristica dei numeri primi_
problems.lean:
theorem isStrongGiuga_iff {a : ℕ} (ha : a.Composite) :
    IsStrongGiuga a ↔ IsCarmichael a ∧ ∃ n : ℕ, ∑ p ∈ a.primeFactors, (1 / p : ℚ) - 1 / a = n

problems.title: Agoh-Giuga conjecture — isWeakGiuga iff sum primeFactors
problems.statement:
A composite number $n$ is weak Giuga if and only if
$$
\sum_{p\mid n} \frac{1}{p} - \frac{1}{n} \in\mathbb{N}.
$$
problems.lean:
theorem isWeakGiuga_iff_sum_primeFactors {n : ℕ} (hn : n.Composite) :
    IsWeakGiuga n ↔ ∃ m : ℕ, ∑ p ∈ n.primeFactors, (1 / p : ℚ) - 1 / n = m

**Hironaka's theorem.** Every integral scheme that is separated and of finite type over a field
of characteristic zero admits a resolution of singularities. This is the main theorem of
[Hir1964]; see [Kol2007], Theorem 36, for a statement in the generality used here.

problems.title: The Alon–Saks–Seymour conjecture — disproved.
problems.statement:
**The Alon–Saks–Seymour conjecture — disproved.**

It was conjectured (Alon, Saks and Seymour, c. 1991, see [Ka91]) that every graph whose edge
set is partitioned into $k$ complete bipartite subgraphs is $(k+1)$-colourable, i.e.
$\chi(G) \le \operatorname{bp}(G) + 1$ — the natural generalisation of the Graham–Pollak
theorem, which is the case $G = K_n$.

This is **false**: Huang and Sudakov [HS12] constructed graphs with
$\chi(G) \ge c \operatorname{bp}(G)^{6/5}$.
problems.lean:
theorem alon_saks_seymour_conjecture : ¬
    ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.chromaticNumber ≤ bicliquePartitionNumber G + 1

problems.title: Alspach's conjecture (1981), proved by Bryant, Horsley and Pettersson (2014).
problems.statement:
**Alspach's conjecture (1981), proved by Bryant, Horsley and Pettersson (2014).**

Let $n$ be odd and let $m_1, \dots, m_t$ be integers with $3 \le m_i \le n$ and
$m_1 + \dots + m_t = \binom{n}{2}$. Then the complete graph $K_n$ decomposes into cycles of
lengths $m_1, \dots, m_t$. (These conditions are clearly necessary: $K_n$ has all degrees even
only for odd $n$, and its edges must be split exactly among the cycles.)
problems.lean:
theorem alspach_conjecture :
    ∀ (n : ℕ), Odd n → ∀ m : Multiset ℕ, (∀ x ∈ m, 3 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ n) → m.sum = n.choose 2 →
      ∃ C : Multiset (Cycle (completeGraph (Fin n))),
        IsCycleDecomposition (completeGraph (Fin n)) C ∧ lengths C = m

$\lfloor (m+1)n/2 \rfloor$ for $m,n \geq 3$ [BFZ24, (4.22)].

problems.statement:
For $n \neq 3$ the generic rank of an $n \times n \times n$ tensor is
$\lceil n^3 / (3n - 2) \rceil$ [Fri12, (5.8)].

The generic rank of a $4 \times m \times m$ tensor is $\lceil 4m^2 / (2m + 2) \rceil$

[AOP09]; see [BFZ24, Section 4.5].

    IsGenericRank [4, m, m] (4 * m ^ 2 ⌈/⌉ (2 * m + 2))

problems.title: Generic and maximal rank of 3-tensors — isGenericRank of eq critical
problems.statement:
The generic rank at the critical boundary is $(m_1-1)(m_2-1)+1$
[Fri12, Corollary 6.4(2)]. By `critical_ceilDiv`, this is the dimension-count value in
`isGenericRank_of_le_critical`.

problems.statement:

$\min(m_3, m_1m_2)$ [Fri12, (5.1)].

    IsGenericRank [m₁, m₂, m₃] (min m₃ (m₁ * m₂))

problems.statement:
The generic rank of a $3 \times 2p \times 2p$ tensor is $\lceil 12p^2 / (4p + 1) \rceil$, the
value $r_0$ predicted by a dimension count [Fri12, (5.3)]. The hypothesis $2 \leq p$ is the
ordering $3 \leq 2p$ of the format.

theorem isGenericRank_three_even {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) :
    IsGenericRank [3, 2 * p, 2 * p] (12 * p ^ 2 ⌈/⌉ (4 * p + 1))

problems.title: Generic and maximal rank of 3-tensors — isGenericRank three odd
problems.statement:
The generic rank of a $3 \times (2p+1) \times (2p+1)$ tensor is
$\lceil 3(2p+1)^2 / (4p + 3) \rceil + 1$, one more than the value $r_0$ predicted by a dimension
count [Fri12, (5.4)]. These are the only formats in the critical range known to exceed $r_0$. The

problems.title: Conjecture 1.6 (Even case).
problems.statement:
**Conjecture 1.6 (Even case).**
For a nonempty isolate-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices,
if $D$ is even, then $(D + 2)^2 \cdot i(G) \leq (D^2 + 4) \cdot n$.

Proved by Cho, Kim, Kim and Oum ([arxiv/2202.09594](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.09594),
Corollary 1.3).
problems.lean:
theorem independentDominationEven (hIso : 0 < G.minDegree) (hEven : Even G.maxDegree) :
    let D := G.maxDegree
    let i := G.indepDominationNumber
    let n := Fintype.card V
    (D + 2)^2 * i ≤ (D^2 + 4) * n

problems.title: Conjecture 1.6 (Odd case).
problems.statement:
**Conjecture 1.6 (Odd case).**
For a nonempty isolate-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices,
if $D$ is odd, then $(D + 1)(D + 3) \cdot i(G) \leq (D^2 + 3) \cdot n$.

Proved by Cho, Kim, Kim and Oum ([arxiv/2202.09594](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.09594),
Corollary 1.3).
problems.lean:
theorem independentDominationOdd (hIso : 0 < G.minDegree) (hOdd : Odd G.maxDegree) :
    let D := G.maxDegree
    let i := G.indepDominationNumber
    let n := Fintype.card V
    (D + 1) * (D + 3) * i ≤ (D^2 + 3) * n

problems.title: TxGraffiti Conjecture 1: independence, annihilation, and residue
problems.statement:
TxGraffiti [Conjecture 1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17780):
for every nontrivial connected graph $G$ with $\Delta(G) \ge 2$,
$$\alpha(G) \ge \frac{a(G) + R(G)}{\Delta(G)}.$$

This conjecture is **true**.

**Proof sketch.** Substitute the Caro–Wei lower bound $\alpha \ge W$ for $\alpha$
and reduce to $a \le (\Delta - 1) \alpha$. The case $\Delta = 2$ is trivial
($a = \alpha$). For $\Delta \ge 4$ an AM–HM argument with $m \le (n - a)\Delta$
yields a quadratic whose discriminant is negative. For $\Delta = 3$ the
annihilation number has a closed form in the degree counts $(n_1, n_2, n_3)$ and
$a \le 2W$ is verified in three regimes. See
[arXiv:2606.29553](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29553).
problems.lean:
theorem tx_graffiti_conjecture_1 (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (_hConn : G.Connected)
    (_hDeg : 2 ≤ G.maxDegree) :
    (G.annihilationNumber + residue G : ℝ) / G.maxDegree ≤ G.indepNum

problems.title: Bounded Burnside problem
problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a finitely generated group, and assume there exists $n$ such that for every $g$ in $G$,
$g^n = 1$. Must $G$ be finite?

The answer is negative. Novikov and Adian proved that for every odd $n > 4381$ there exist
infinite, finitely generated groups of exponent $n$ [NA68]; Adian later reduced this to odd
$n > 665$ [Ad79]. The even case is harder: Ivanov proved $B(m, n)$ infinite for $m > 1$ and
even $n \ge 2^{48}$ divisible by $2^9$ [Iv94], and Lysënok improved this to $m > 1$ and
$n \ge 8000$ [Ly96]. Any such group, for example the free Burnside group $B(2, 667)$,
refutes the statement below.

Note this concerns only the universally quantified question stated here, which a single
counterexample closes. The classification of which free Burnside groups $B(m, n)$ are finite
remains open, with $B(2, 5)$ the best known open case.
problems.lean:
theorem bounded_burnside_problem :
    ¬ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (fin_gen : Group.FG G)
      (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 0) (bounded : ∀ g : G, g^n = 1), Finite G

problems.title: Decidability of reachability for branching vector addition systems
problems.statement:
The reachability problem for branching vector addition systems is decidable.

That is, the predicate taking a dimension `d`, a branching vector addition system `b` of
dimension `d` and a target vector `t ∈ ℤ^d`, and returning whether `t` is reachable in `b`, is
a computable predicate. Note that the dimension is part of the input: a single algorithm must
work for all dimensions.

As of August 2026, the solution is quite recently announced and is not
yet peer-reviewed.
problems.lean:

    ComputablePred fun p : Σ d : ℕ, Bvas d × (Fin d → ℤ) => p.2.1.Reachable p.2.2

problems.statement:

real numbers $\xi$ for which $(\{\xi r_n\})_{n \ge 1}$ is *not* dense modulo one has

    (hsub : Tendsto (fun n => r (n + 1) / r n) atTop (nhds 1)) :
    dimH {ξ : ℝ | ¬ Dense (Set.range fun n => (↑(ξ * r n) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))} = 0

problems.statement:
**Furstenberg's theorem** [Fur67] (the $\times 2, \times 3$ case). For every irrational
number $\xi$, the two-parameter family $(\{\xi \, 2^m 3^n\})_{m, n \ge 1}$ is dense modulo
one.

problems.statement:
The **Pollington–de Mathan theorem** [Pol79][Mat80]. For every lacunary sequence
$(m_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of positive integers, the set of real numbers $\xi$ for which
$(\{\xi m_n\})_{n \ge 1}$ is *not* dense modulo one has full Hausdorff dimension.
problems.lean:
theorem pollington_de_mathan (m : ℕ → ℕ) (hm : ∀ n, 0 < m n) (hlac : IsLacunary m) :
    dimH {ξ : ℝ | ¬ Dense (Set.range fun n => (↑(ξ * m n) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))} = 1

problems.title: Adamczewski–Faverjon
problems.statement:
**Adamczewski–Faverjon** [AF20, Conjecture A.3], proved there from Part (i) of Theorem 1.1.
Let $b_1, \dots, b_r$ be multiplicatively independent positive integers, and for every $i$ let
$\xi_i$ be a real number that is automatic in base $b_i$. Then $\xi_1, \dots, \xi_r$ are
algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, unless one of them is rational.

Two points of fidelity. The hypothesis is the *joint* multiplicative independence of
$b_1, \dots, b_r$ that [AF20] defines on p. 3 (no nonzero integer tuple $(n_i)$ has
$\prod_i b_i^{n_i} = 1$), not the weaker pairwise condition; it is what the proof feeds to
Part (i) of Theorem 1.1, via the multiplicative independence of $1/b_1, \dots, 1/b_r$.
Automaticity is the broad notion that the proof of Conjecture A.3 uses: the base-$b_i$ digits
of $\xi_i$ are $k$-automatic for some $k \ge 2$, which need not be $b_i$.
problems.lean:
theorem adamczewski_faverjon {r : ℕ} (b : Fin r → ℕ) (hb : ∀ i, 2 ≤ b i)
    (hind : Nat.MultiplicativelyIndependentFamily b)
    (ξ : Fin r → ℝ) (hauto : ∀ i, IsBroadlyAutomaticInBase (b i) (ξ i))
    (hirr : ∀ i, Irrational (ξ i)) :
    AlgebraicIndependent ℚ ξ

problems.title: Alaoglu–Erdős Conjectures on Colossally Abundant Numbers — alaoglu erdos prime or semiprime ratio
problems.statement:
Unconditional prime-or-squarefree-semiprime ratio theorem [AE44, p. 455]: if $m < n$ satisfy
`AreConsecutiveAlaogluErdosColossallyAbundant m n`, then $n / m$ is either prime or a product of two
distinct primes (proved via the six exponentials theorem [La66, Ra68]). Varying $\varepsilon > 0$
yields the same set of integers under `IsAlaogluErdosColossallyAbundant` as under [AE44, p. 448]'s
greatest-maximizer convention, so both give the same consecutive pairs; some one-sided strict
tie-breaker is needed, since a four-way tie $n, np, nq, npq$ with primes $p < q$ under two-sided
non-strict `IsColossallyAbundant` would include consecutive terms $np, nq$ of ratio $q / p$.
problems.lean:
theorem alaoglu_erdos_prime_or_semiprime_ratio (m n : ℕ)
    (h : AreConsecutiveAlaogluErdosColossallyAbundant m n) :
    (∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n = p * m) ∨
      ∃ p q : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p ≠ q ∧ n = p * q * m

problems.statement:

$n > 1$ simultaneously maximize $\sigma_1(n) / n^{1+\varepsilon}$ [AE44, EN75].

      (σ 1 k : ℝ) / (k : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε) ≤ (σ 1 n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + ε)} ≤ 4

problems.title: Equidistributed Sequences — isEquidistributedModuloOne transcendental three halves pow
problems.statement:
It is not true that for every transcendental number `x` the sequence `x * (3 / 2) ^ n` is
equidistributed modulo `1`. The sequence `(3 / 2) ^ n` is lacunary, so by the theorem of
Pollington [Pol79] and de Mathan [Mat80] the set of real numbers `x` for which `x * (3 / 2) ^ n`
is not even dense modulo `1` has Hausdorff dimension `1`. This set is uncountable, so it contains
transcendental numbers. Alternatively, an elementary nested-interval construction (see issue
#5003) gives a Cantor set of `x` with `Int.fract (x * (3 / 2) ^ (8 * j)) ∈ [0, 1 / 10]` for all
`j`, which already rules out equidistribution for uncountably many, hence some transcendental,
`x`. By Koksma's metric theorem (Kuipers–Niederreiter, Chapter 1, Section 4), the sequence
`x * (3 / 2) ^ n` is equidistributed modulo `1` for almost all `x`.
problems.lean:
theorem isEquidistributedModuloOne_transcendental_three_halves_pow :
    ¬ ∀ x : ℝ, Transcendental ℚ x →
      IsEquidistributedModuloOne (fun n ↦ x * (3 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1005
problems.statement:
Let $\frac{a_1}{b_1}, \frac{a_2}{b_2}, \ldots$ be the Farey fractions of order $n \geq 4$. Let
$f(n)$ be the largest integer such that if $1 \leq k < l \leq k + f(n)$ then $\frac{a_k}{b_k}$ and
$\frac{a_l}{b_l}$ are similarly ordered, in other words $(a_k - a_l)(b_k - b_l) \geq 0$. Estimate
$f(n)$: in particular, is there a constant $c > 0$ such that $f(n) = (c + o(1)) n$ for all
large $n$?

Mayer [Ma42] proved that $f(n) \to \infty$ and Erdős [Er43] that $f(n) \gg n$. Van Doorn [vD25b]
proved $(1/12 - o(1)) n \le f(n) \le n / 4 + O(1)$ and conjectured that $f(n) = (1/4 + o(1)) n$,
which was proved by Cipollini and GPT-5.5; see `erdos_1005.variants.constant`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1005 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (f n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 c)

set on $f(n)$ vertices. Estimate $f(n)$.

theorem erdos_1024 :
    (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.linearIndependenceNumber n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
    erdos_1024.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1042 — i
problems.statement:
Let $F\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a closed set of transfinite diameter $1$ which is not contained in
any closed disc of radius $1$.

If $f(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(z-z_i)\in\mathbb{C}[x]$ with all $z_i\in F$ then can
$$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert < 1\}$$
have $n$ connected components?

A problem of Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58, p. 139, Problem 6], who proved that if $F$ is the
disc of radius $1$ then this set can have $n$ connected components (for example $f(z)=z^n+1$).

As in the answer of Ghosh and Ramachandran [GhRa24] to their Question 1.2, we read "can"
existentially: there is such an $F$ for which $n$ components occur for infinitely many $n$.
[GhRa24] answer this question in the affirmative; the classical example $F=[-2,2]$
[GhRa24, Example 2.7] already gives $n$ components for every $n\ge 1$, see
`erdos_1042.variants.chebyshev_segment`. The universal reading, for every such $F$, is
`erdos_1042.variants.universal`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1042.parts.i :
    ∃ F : Set ℂ, IsClosed F ∧ transfiniteDiameter F = 1 ∧
      (∀ c : ℂ, ¬ F ⊆ Metric.closedBall c 1) ∧
      ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ f : ℂ[X], MonicWithRootsIn F n f ∧ numComponents f = n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1042 — ii
problems.statement:
If the transfinite diameter of $F$ is $<1$ then must this set only have at most $(1-c)n$
connected components, where $c>0$ depends only on $F$ (or just the transfinite diameter of $F$)?

This is the second question of [EHP58, p. 139, Problem 6], which asks for $n$ large. It was solved
by Ghosh and Ramachandran [GhRa24, Theorem 2.1(a)], who proved that, if $d$ is the transfinite
diameter of $F$ and $0<d<1$, then the set has at most $(1-c)n$ connected components for some
$c>0$ depending on $F$. Precisely, they prove $\limsup_n C_n(F)/n<1$, where $C_n(F)$ is the
maximal number of components over all admissible $f$ of degree $n$; this is the statement below.
The answer is yes, in this form.

[GhRa24] assume throughout that $F$ is compact of positive capacity, so we assume $0<d$; a closed
$F$ with $d<1$ is bounded, hence compact. The condition "$n$ large" is needed: for $n=1$ the set
$\{\lvert z-z_1\rvert<1\}$ has one component, which is more than $(1-c)n$. The parenthetical
"or just the transfinite diameter of $F$" is not formalised: [GhRa24] only remark that their
quantities $M(K)$ and $m(K)$ are not determined by the capacity.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1042.parts.ii :
    ∀ F : Set ℂ, IsClosed F → 0 < transfiniteDiameter F → transfiniteDiameter F < 1 →
      ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ f : ℂ[X], MonicWithRootsIn F n f →
        (numComponents f : ℝ) ≤ (1 - c) * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1069
problems.statement:
Given any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the number of $k$-rich lines (lines which contain
$\geq k$ of the points) is, provided $k\leq n^{1/2}$,
$$\ll \frac{n^2}{k^3}.$$

Erdős [Er87b] describes this as a conjecture of himself, Croft, and Purdy. It was proved by
Szemerédi and Trotter [SzTr83]. We take $k \geq 2$, since for $k \leq 1$ there are infinitely
many $k$-rich lines.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1069 :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (n k : ℕ) (s : Finset ℝ²), s.card = n → 2 ≤ k →
      (k : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt n →
        ((richLines s k).ncard : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / (k : ℝ) ^ 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1081
problems.statement:
Let $A(x)$ count the number of $n\leq x$ which are the sum of two squarefull numbers (a number
$m$ is squarefull if $p\mid m$ implies $p^2\mid m$). Is it true that
$$A(x) \sim c \frac{x}{\sqrt{\log x}}$$
for some $c>0$?

Odoni [Od81] proved this is false.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1081 :
    ¬ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
      (fun x : ℝ ↦ (A x : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun x ↦ c * x / Real.sqrt (Real.log x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1106 — i
problems.statement:
Let $p(n)$ be the partition number of $n$ and $F(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of
$\prod_{i= 1} ^ {n} p(n)$, then $F(n)$ tends to infinity when $n$ tends to infinity.

The answer is yes: Schinzel and Wirsing [ScWi87] proved $F(n) \gg \log n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1106.parts.i :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ #(∏ i ∈ Icc 1 n, partitionNumber i).primeFactors) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1115
problems.statement:
Let $f(z)$ be an entire function of finite order, and let $\Gamma$ be a rectifiable path on which
$f(z)\to \infty$. Let $\ell(r)$ be the length of $\Gamma$ in the disc $\lvert z\rvert<r$.

Find a path for which $\ell(r)$ grows as slowly as possible, and estimate $\ell(r)$ in terms of
$M(r)=\max_{\lvert z\rvert=r}\lvert f(z)\rvert$.

In particular, can such a path $\Gamma$ be found for which $\ell(r)\ll r$?

This is Problem 2.41 of [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős; see also [HaLi18, Problem 2.41].
The answer is no: Gol'dberg and Eremenko [GoEr79] proved that for every $\rho\in[0,\infty]$ there
is an entire function $f$ of order $\rho$ such that, for any asymptotic curve $\Gamma$ on which
$f\to\infty$, the length of $\Gamma$ in $\lvert z\rvert\leq r$ is not $O(r)$ (see also [HaLi18,
Updates 2.7 and 2.41]). The length in $\lvert z\rvert\leq r$ is at most the length in
$\lvert z\rvert<2r$, so $\ell(r)=O(r)$ for the open disc used here would make the length in the
closed disc $O(r)$ too.

We formalise the last question only: the first part asks for a best possible path and an estimate
in terms of $M(r)$ and has no precise claim to state, so it is not formalised. Reading choices:
$f$ is non-constant (a constant has no path on which $f\to\infty$, which would make the statement
trivially true); finite order is `Erdos516.OfFiniteOrder`; $\Gamma$ is given by its arc length
parametrisation `γ` (every rectifiable path on which $f\to\infty$ has infinite length and can be
reparametrised by arc length, without changing the curve traversed or the length in any disc);
$\ell(r)\ll r$ means $\ell(r)\le Cr$ for some $C$ and all large $r$.

[HaLi18, Problem 2.41] also report that Hayman [Ha60b] (and Piranian) showed that if
$\log M(r)=O((\log r)^2)$, one can take for $\Gamma$ a ray from the origin, so that $\ell(r)=r$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1115 :
    ¬ ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, Erdos516.OfFiniteOrder f → (¬ ∃ a : ℂ, ∀ z, f z = a) →
      ∃ γ : ℝ → ℂ, IsAsymptoticPath f γ ∧
        ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ r : ℝ in atTop, lengthInDisc γ r ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1119
problems.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{m}$ be an infinite cardinal with $\aleph_0 < \mathfrak{m} < \mathfrak{c} =
2^{\aleph_0}$. Let $\{f_\alpha\}$ be a family of entire functions such that, for every
$z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$, there are at most $\mathfrak{m}$ distinct values of $f_\alpha(z_0)$.
Must $\{f_\alpha\}$ have cardinality at most $\mathfrak{m}$?

This is Problem 2.46 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős. The question is
**independent of ZFC**: the headline statement is neither provable nor refutable from the
usual axioms of set theory, so its `sorry` cannot be filled either way.

The answer is yes if $\mathfrak{m}^+ < \mathfrak{c}$ (see
`erdos_1119.variants.easy_case`), so the question reduces to the case
$\mathfrak{m}^+ = \mathfrak{c}$, where it is undecidable: Kumar and Shelah [KuSh17]
produced a model of $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_2$ in which the answer is yes (with
$\mathfrak{m} = \aleph_1$), while Schilhan and Weinert [ScWe24] produced a different
model of $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_2$ in which the answer is no.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1119 :
    ∀ (m : Cardinal.{0}), ℵ₀ < m → m < 𝔠 →
    ∀ F : Set (ℂ → ℂ), (∀ f ∈ F, Differentiable ℂ f) →
      (∀ z₀ : ℂ, #{y : ℂ | ∃ f ∈ F, f z₀ = y} ≤ m) →
      #F ≤ m

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1130 — i
problems.statement:
For $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in [-1,1]$ let
$$l_k(x)=\frac{\prod_{i\neq k}(x-x_i)}{\prod_{i\neq k}(x_k-x_i)},$$
which are such that $l_k(x_k)=1$ and $l_k(x_i)=0$ for $i\neq k$.

Let $x_0=-1$ and $x_{n+1}=1$ and
$$\Upsilon(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\min_{0\leq i\leq n}\max_{x\in[x_i,x_{i+1}]}
\sum_k \lvert l_k(x)\rvert.$$
Is it true that
$$\Upsilon(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\ll \log n?$$

This is the first part, a question of Erdős [Er67, p. 66], who could prove only
$\Upsilon<\sqrt n$ [Er47, Theorem 2]. We read $\ll$ as: there is an absolute constant $C$ with
$\Upsilon(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\le C\log n$ for all $n\ge 2$ and all nodes
$-1\le x_1<\cdots<x_n\le 1$. The answer is yes: $\Upsilon(x)$ is at most the minimal Lebesgue
constant (`erdos_1130.variants.erdos_inequality`, from [Ki77], [Ki78] and [dBPi78]), and the
Chebyshev nodes show that this is $<\frac2\pi\log n+O(1)$ [Er61c, p. 236].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1130.parts.i :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ), 2 ≤ n → IsNodeSet x →
      upsilon x ≤ C * Real.log n
