problems.title: Erdős Problem 118
problems.statement:
**Erdős Problem 118** (problem of Erdős and Hajnal). Let $\alpha$ be such that
$\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$. For every $n \ge 3$, must $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$?

The original question is asked for cardinals, ordinals, and order types; we state the
ordinal version, which is the standard reading: ordinals $\alpha$ with
$\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ are called *partition ordinals*.

The answer is **no**, shown independently by Schipperus [Sc99, Sc10] and Darby [Da99].
Larson [La00] gave the concrete counterexample $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$, for which
$\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ holds yet $\alpha \not\to (\alpha, 5)^2$. See Chapter 2.9 of
[HST10] for further background.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_118 :
    ¬ ∀ α : Ordinal.{0}, OrdinalRamsey α α 3 →
      ∀ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n → OrdinalRamsey α α n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1182 — ii
problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that there is a connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $f(n)$ edges
such that
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Let $F(n)$ be maximal such that every connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $\leq F(n)$ edges
has
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Estimate $f(n)$ and $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)/n\to \infty$?

This is the second part: estimate $F(n)$. As an order of magnitude, `=Θ`, this is known:
$F(n)=\Theta(n)$, by $F(n)\ge n-1$ (`erdos_1182.variants.F_ge_pred`, from Chvátal's theorem
[Ch77]) and the linear upper bounds of `erdos_1182.variants.brandt` and
`erdos_1182.variants.nikiforov_rousseau`. The finer question of the asymptotic behaviour of
$F(n)/n$ is open, see `erdos_1182.variants.brandt_expects`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1182.parts.ii :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (F n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] erdos_1182.parts.ii.answer

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1182 — iii
problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that there is a connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $f(n)$ edges
such that
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Let $F(n)$ be maximal such that every connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $\leq F(n)$ edges
has
$$R(K_3,G)= 2n-1.$$
Estimate $f(n)$ and $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)/n\to \infty$?

This is the third part, asked in [BEFRS80, Section 5] and in [Er78, pp. 33-34], where Erdős says
it seems certain. The answer is no: Brandt [Br96] proved $F(n)\le 84n$ (as recorded on the problem
page, see `erdos_1182.variants.brandt`), and [NiRo09, Theorem 5.1] implies $F(n)<50n$ for large
$n$ (see `erdos_1182.variants.nikiforov_rousseau`).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1182.parts.iii :
    ¬ Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (F n : ℝ) / n) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1207
problems.statement:
Let $P_d(n)$ be such that in any set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ there exist at least $P_d(n)$ many points which do not contain an isosceles triangle. Estimate $P_d(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $$P_2(n)<n^{1-c}$$ for some constant $c>0$?

Lee, Pohoata, and Zhu [LPZ26] proved the stated planar bound. Their isosceles-free subsets
also exclude degenerate triangles of equally spaced collinear points.

theorem erdos_1207 :

problems.title: Erdős Problem 186
problems.statement:
Let $F(N)$ be the maximal size of $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ which is 'non-averaging', so that
no $n\in A$ is the arithmetic mean of at least two elements in $A$. What is the order of growth
of $F(N)$?

It is known that $N^{1/4}\ll F(N) \ll N^{1/4+o(1)}$: the lower bound is due to Bosznay [Bo89] and
the upper bound to Pham and Zakharov [PhZa24, Theorem 1]. So $\log F(N)/\log N\to 1/4$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_186 :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ Real.log (F N) / Real.log N) atTop (𝓝 (1 / 4))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 198
problems.statement:
Let $V$ be a vector space over the rationals and let $k$ be a fixed
positive integer. Then there is a set $X_k \subseteq V$ such that $X_k$ meets
every infinite arithmetic progression in $V$ but $X_k$ intersects every
$k$-element arithmetic progression in at most two points.

At the end of [Ba75] the author claims that by "slightly modifying the method of [his proof]", one
can prove this.
problems.lean:
lemma baumgartner_strong (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℚ V] (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ X : Set V,
      (∀ Y, Y.IsAPOfLength ⊤ → (X ∩ Y).Nonempty) ∧
      (∀ Y, IsAPOfLength Y k → (X ∩ Y).ncard ≤ 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 207
problems.statement:
For any $g\geq 2$, if $n$ is sufficiently large and $\equiv 1,3\pmod{6}$ then there exists a
3-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices such that

- every pair of vertices is contained in exactly one edge (i.e. the graph is a Steiner triple
system) and

- for any $2\leq j\leq g$ any collection of $j$ edges contains at least $j+3$ vertices.

Proved by Kwan, Sah, Sawhney, and Simkin [KSSS22b].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_207 :
    ∀ g : ℕ, 2 ≤ g → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    n % 6 = 1 ∨ n % 6 = 3 → ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)),
      H.IsBlockDesign 2 3 ∧ ∀ E ⊆ H,
        2 ≤ E.card → E.card ≤ g → E.card + 3 ≤ (E.biUnion id).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 228
problems.statement:
Does there exist, for all large $n$, a polynomial $P$ of degree $n$, with coefficients $\pm1$, such
that $$\sqrt n \ll |P(z)| \ll \sqrt n$$ for all $|z|=1$, with the implied constants independent of
$z$ and $n$?

The answer is yes, proved by Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba [BBMST19].

[BBMST19] Balister, P. and Bollob\'{A}s, B. and Morris, R. and Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., _Flat Littlewood Polynomials Exist_. arXiv:1907.09464 (2019).

theorem erdos_228 :
    ∃ (c₁ : ℝ) (c₂ : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ p : Polynomial ℂ, p.degree = n ∧
    (∀ i ≤ n, p.coeff i = 1 ∨ p.coeff i = -1) ∧
    ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ = 1 →
    ( √n < c₁ * ‖p.eval z‖ ∧ ‖p.eval z‖ < c₂ * √n )

problems.title: Erdős Problem 239
problems.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to \{-1,1\}$ be a multiplicative function. Is it true that
$$ \lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n\leq N}f(n)$$ always exists?

The answer is yes, as proved by Wirsing [Wi67], and generalised by Halász [Ha68].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_239 :
    ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ,
    (∀ n ≥ 1, f n = 1 ∨ f n = -1) ∧
    (∀ m n, m.Coprime n → f (m * n) = f m * f n) ∧
    f 1 = 1 →
    ∃ L, Tendsto (fun N ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) / N) atTop (𝓝 L)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 245
problems.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A + A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} \geq 3?
$$

The answer is yes, proved by Freiman [Fr73].

[Fr73] Fre\u{\i}man, G. A., _Foundations of a structural theory of set addition_. (1973), vii+108.

      atTop.Tendsto (fun N ↦ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : ℝ) / N) (𝓝 0) →
      3 ≤ atTop.limsup
        fun N : ℝ ↦ ((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊ |>.ncard : EReal)
          / (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard

problems.statement:
Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)>1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 294
problems.statement:
Let $N\geq 1$ and let $t(N)$ be the least integer $t$ such that there is no solution to
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$$
with $t=n_1<\cdots <n_k\leq N$. Estimate $t(N)$.

Solved by Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24, Theorem 1.6] (up to $(\log\log N)^{O(1)}$), who proved that
$$\frac{N}{(\log N)(\log\log N)^3(\log\log\log N)^{O(1)}}\ll t(N) \ll \frac{N}{\log N}.$$
The unspecified $O(1)$ exponent is the real number `K`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_294 :
    (∃ K : ℝ, (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) / (Real.log N * Real.log (Real.log N) ^ 3 *
        Real.log (Real.log (Real.log N)) ^ K)) ≪ (fun N : ℕ => (t N : ℝ))) ∧
    ((fun N : ℕ => (t N : ℝ)) ≪ (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) / Real.log N))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 297
problems.statement:
Let $N\geq 1$. How many $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ are there such that
$\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}=1$?

Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24] proved that the count is $2^{(0.91\cdots+o(1))N}$, where $0.91\cdots$ is
an explicit number defined as the solution to a certain integral equation; independently the same
asymptotic was proved by Conlon, Fox, He, Mubayi, Pham, Suk, and Verstraëte [CFHMPSV24]. We
formalise the question as asking for the exponential growth rate
$\lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\log_2 \#\{A\}$. The first conjunct is the existence and
uniqueness of $\lambda^*$, which [LiSa24] state with the theorem.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_297 : (∃! l : ℝ, massIntegral l = 1) ∧
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => Real.logb 2 (count 1 N) / N) atTop (𝓝 erdos_297.answer)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 384
problems.statement:
If $1<k<n-1$ then $\binom{n}{k}$ is divisible by a prime $p\leq n/2$ (except
$\binom{7}{3}=\binom{7}{4}=5\cdot 7$).

A conjecture of Erdős and Selfridge [ErGr80]. Proved by Ecklund [Ec69], who made the stronger
conjecture that whenever $n>k^2$ the binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$ is divisible by a prime
$p<n/k$. Discussed in problem B31 and B33 of Guy's collection [Gu04]. Stronger forms of this
conjecture are [1094](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1094) and
[1095](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1095).

Ecklund's theorem is stated for $n \geq 2k$ with the single exception $\binom{7}{3}$; by the
symmetry $\binom{n}{k} = \binom{n}{n-k}$ this is the form above, where $\binom{7}{4}$ is the
second exception. The prime bound is $p \leq n/2$ (that is, $2p \leq n$); see
`erdos_384.variants.strict` for the strict inequality.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_384 (n k : ℕ) (hk : 1 < k) (hkn : k < n - 1) (h₃ : (n, k) ≠ (7, 3))
    (h₄ : (n, k) ≠ (7, 4)) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ n.choose k ∧ 2 * p ≤ n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 402
problems.statement:
Prove that, for any finite set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$, there exist $a, b\in A$ such
that

$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_402 (A : Finset ℕ) (h₁ : 0 ∉ A) (h₂ : A.Nonempty) : ∃ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A),
    a.gcd b ≤ (a / A.card : ℚ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 405
problems.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. Is it true that the equation $(p-1)!+a^{p-1}=p^k$ has only finitely many
solutions?

Originally proposed by Erdős and Graham [ErGr80].
Brindza and Erdős [BrEr91] proved that there are finitely many such solutions.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 413 — ii
problems.statement:
Does there exist some $\epsilon > 0$ such that there are infinitely many
$\epsilon$-barriers for $\omega$? Lau [La26, Theorem 1.3] gives a positive answer.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_413.parts.ii :
    (∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), { n | IsBarrier (fun n => ε * ω n) n }.Infinite)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 436 — i
problems.statement:
If $p$ is a prime and $k, m \geq 2$, let $r(k, m, p)$ be the minimal $r$ such that
$r, r + 1, \ldots, r + m - 1$ are all $k$th power residues modulo $p$, and let
$\Lambda(k, m) = \limsup_{p \to \infty} r(k, m, p)$. Is $\Lambda(k, 2)$ finite for all $k$?

A question of Lehmer and Lehmer [LeLe62]. Hildebrand [Hi91] proved that $\Lambda(k, 2)$ is finite
for all $k \geq 2$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_436.parts.i : ∀ k ≥ 2, Λ k 2 < ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 447 — i
problems.statement:
How large can a union-free collection $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ be? By union-free we mean
there are no solutions to $A\cup B=C$ with distinct $A,B,C\in \mathcal{F}$. Must
$\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert =o(2^n)$?

In [Er65b] Erdős reported that the estimate $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert=o(2^n)$ was proved in
unpublished work by Sárközy and Szemerédi.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_447.parts.i :
    (fun n : ℕ => (maxUnionFree n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (2 : ℝ) ^ n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 499
problems.statement:
The conjecture of van der Waerden, which states that the permanent of a doubly stochastic matrix is
at least $n^{-n} n!$.

Proved by Gyires [Gy80], Egorychev [Eg81], and Falikman [Fa81].

[Gy80] Gyires, B., The common source of several inequalities concerning doubly stochastic matrices. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1980), 291-304.
[Eg81] Egorychev, G. P., The solution of the van der Waerden problem for permanents. Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR (1981), 1041-1044.
[Fa81] Falikman, D. I., Proof of the van der Waerden conjecture on the permanent of a doubly stochastic matrix. Mat. Zametki (1981), 931-938, 957.
problems.lean:
lemma vanDerWaerden (n : ℕ) (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hM : M ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ (Fin n)) :
    n ^ (- n : ℤ) * n ! ≤ M.permanent

problems.title: Borsuk's conjecture, small dimensions
problems.statement:
**Borsuk's conjecture, small dimensions**: `Borsuk.BorsukConjecture n` holds for
$n \leq 3$. Elementary for $n \leq 1$, proved by Borsuk [Bo33] for $n = 2$ and by
Eggleston [Eg55] for $n = 3$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_505.small_dim (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 3) : BorsukConjecture n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 578
problems.statement:
If $G$ is a random graph on $2^d$ vertices, including each edge with probability $1/2$, then $G$
almost surely contains a copy of $Q_d$ (the $d$-dimensional hypercube with $2^d$ vertices and
$d2^{d-1}$ many edges).

A conjecture of Erdős and Bollobás. Solved by Riordan [Ri00], who in fact proved this with any
edge-probability $>1/4$.

Here almost surely means that the probability tends to $1$ as $d\to\infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_578 :
    Tendsto (fun d : ℕ =>
      binomialRandom (Fin d → Bool) ⟨1 / 2, by norm_num⟩
        {G | (hypercube d).IsContained G}) atTop (nhds 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 588 — grunbaum
problems.statement:
Grünbaum [Gr76] proved that for $k \geq 4$,
$$f_k(n) \gg_k n^{1 + \frac{1}{k-2}}.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_588.variants.grunbaum :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ≤ k → ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 2)) ≤ (numLinesWithPointsMax k n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 588 — grunbaum order
problems.statement:
Erdős speculated that Grünbaum's bound $n^{1 + \frac{1}{k-2}}$ may be the correct order of
magnitude of $f_k(n)$ for $k \geq 4$. This is false: by
`Erdos588.erdos_588.variants.solymosi_stojakovic` [SoSt13], for every $k \geq 4$ we have
$f_k(n) \neq O(n^{1 + \frac{1}{k-2}})$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_588.variants.grunbaum_order :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ≤ k →
      ¬ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numLinesWithPointsMax k n : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 2)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 588 — karteszi
problems.statement:
Kárteszi [Ka63] proved that for $k \geq 4$,
$$f_k(n) \gg_k n \log n,$$
resolving a conjecture of Erdős that $f_k(n)/n \to \infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_588.variants.karteszi :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ≤ k → ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ) ≤ (numLinesWithPointsMax k n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 588 — solymosi stojakovic
problems.statement:
Solymosi and Stojaković [SoSt13] proved that for $k \geq 4$,
$$f_k(n) \gg_k n^{2 - O_k(1/\sqrt{\log n})}.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_588.variants.solymosi_stojakovic :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ≤ k → ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - C / Real.sqrt (Real.log (n : ℝ))) ≤
        (numLinesWithPointsMax k n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 588 — sylvester
problems.statement:
Sylvester showed (see [BGS74]) that
$$f_3(n) = \frac{n^2}{6} + O(n).$$

The upper bound $f_3(n) \leq n(n-1)/6$ is `Erdos588.erdos_588.variants.trivial_upper` with
$k = 3$. The lower bound comes from a construction on a cubic curve.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_588.variants.sylvester :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numLinesWithPointsMax 3 n : ℝ) - (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 6) =O[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 588 — three lower
problems.statement:
Burr, Grünbaum, and Sloane [BGS74] and Füredi and Palásti [FuPa84] gave constructions which
show that
$$f_3(n) \geq \left(\frac{1}{6} + o(1)\right) n^2.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_588.variants.three_lower :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 / 6 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ (numLinesWithPointsMax 3 n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 588 — three not isLittleO
problems.statement:
The restriction to $k \geq 4$ in `Erdos588.erdos_588` is necessary: $f_3(n)$ is not $o(n^2)$.
This follows from `Erdos588.erdos_588.variants.sylvester`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_588.variants.three_not_isLittleO :
    ¬ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numLinesWithPointsMax 3 n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 6 — decreasing
problems.statement:
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n > d_{n+1} > \dots > d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_6.variants.decreasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) > primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 6 — increasing
problems.statement:
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < \dots < d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_6.variants.increasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) < primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 651 — erdos 651
problems.statement:
Let $f_k(n)$ denote the smallest integer such that any $f_k(n)$ points in general position in
$\mathbb{R}^k$ contain $n$ which determine a convex polyhedron. Is it true that
$$
  f_k(n) > (1+c_k)^n
$$
for some constant $c_k>0$?

A problem of Erdős [Er97e]. We read "determine a convex polyhedron" as "are in convex position",
and the inequality as holding, with some $c_k > 0$, for all sufficiently large $n$. We ask the
question for every dimension $k \geq 3$. The planar case $k = 2$ is the Erdős-Klein-Szekeres
problem (see `erdos_651.variants.planar`).

The answer is no. Pohoata and Zakharov [PoZa22, Theorem 1.1] proved that $f_3(n) \leq 2^{o(n)}$,
and this implies $f_k(n) \leq 2^{o(n)}$ for every $k \geq 3$, see
`erdos_651.variants.pohoata_zakharov`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_651 :
    ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (1 + c) ^ n < (f k n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 651 — nonempty cardSet
problems.statement:
For $k \geq 2$ and every $n$ there is an integer $N$ such that any $N$ points in general
position in $\mathbb{R}^k$ contain $n$ points in convex position. So $f_k(n)$ is well defined.

This is the higher-dimensional Erdős-Szekeres theorem. For $n \leq k + 1$ one can take $N = n$.
For larger $n$ it follows from Ramsey's theorem, which gives $f_k(n) \leq R_{k+2}(k+3, n)$, see
[PoZa22, Section 1].
problems.lean: theorem nonempty_cardSet {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (n : ℕ) : (cardSet k n).Nonempty

problems.title: Erdős Problem 652
problems.statement:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and let
$R(x_i)=\#\{ \lvert x_j-x_i\rvert : j\neq i\}$, where the points are ordered such that
$$R(x_1)\leq \cdots \leq R(x_n).$$
Let $\alpha_k$ be minimal such that, for all large enough $n$, there exists a set of $n$ points
with $R(x_k)<\alpha_kn^{1/2}$. Is it true that $\alpha_k\to \infty$ as $k\to \infty$?

Mathialagan [Ma21] proved that given a set $P$ of $k$ points and a set $Q$ of $n$ points,
with $2\leq k\leq n^{1/3}$, there exists a point in $P$ which determines
$\gg (kn)^{1/2}$ distances to points in $Q$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_652 : Tendsto alpha atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 656
problems.statement:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ be a set with positive upper density. Must there exist an infinite set
$B\subseteq A$ and integer $t$ such that
$$\{b_1+b_2: b_1\neq b_2\in B\}+t\subseteq A?$$

Erdős [Er75b] posed this as a candidate for a density version of Hindman's theorem. This is true,
and was proved by Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson [KMRR24, Theorem 1.2 (i)], even for sets of
positive upper Banach density and with $t \geq 0$.

The inclusion says that every $b_1+b_2+t$ is an element of `A`, as an integer.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_656 :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, 0 < A.upperDensity →
      ∃ B ⊆ A, B.Infinite ∧ ∃ t : ℤ, ∀ b₁ ∈ B, ∀ b₂ ∈ B, b₁ ≠ b₂ →
        ∃ a ∈ A, (a : ℤ) = b₁ + b₂ + t

problems.title: Erdős Problem 697
problems.statement:
For each $m$ and $\alpha$, the density of the set of integers which are divisible by
some $d \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$ with $1 < d < \exp (m ^ \alpha)$ exists.
problems.lean:
theorem density_exists (m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) : ∃ δ, HasDensity
    {n : ℕ | ∃ d, d ≡ 1 [MOD m] ∧ (d : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ioo 1 (exp (m ^ α)) ∧ d ∣ n} δ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 697 — i
problems.statement:
Let $\beta = \frac{1}{\log 2}$. Then $lim_{m\rightarrow\infty} \delta (m, \alpha) = 0$ if
$\alpha < \beta$. This is proved in [Ha92].
problems.lean: theorem erdos_697.parts.i {α : ℝ} (hα : α < 1 / log (2 : ℝ)) : Tendsto (δ · α) atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 697 — ii
problems.statement:
$lim_{m\rightarrow\infty} \delta (m, \alpha) = 1$ if $\beta < \alpha$.
This is proved in [Ha92].
problems.lean: theorem erdos_697.parts.ii {α : ℝ} (hα : 1 / log (2 : ℝ) < α) : Tendsto (δ · α) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 716
problems.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of all $3$-uniform hypergraphs with $6$ vertices and $3$ $3$-edges.
Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}_3(n,\mathcal{F})=o(n^2)?$$

The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa and Szemerédi [RuSz78] (this is known as the Ruzsa-Szemerédi
problem).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_716 :
    (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.configurationExtremalNumber n 3 6 3 : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 722
problems.statement:
Let $k>r$ and $n$ be sufficiently large in terms of $k$ and $r$. Does there always exist a block
$r-(n,k,1)$ design (or Steiner system with parameters $(n,k,r)$), provided the trivial necessary
divisibility conditions $\binom{k-i}{r-i}\mid \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ are satisfied for every $0\leq i<r$?
That is, can one find a family of $\binom{n}{r}\binom{k}{r}^{-1}$ many subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
all of size $k$, such that any $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ of size $r$ is contained in exactly one
set in the family?

This was proved by Keevash [Ke14] for all $(r,k)$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_722 :
    ∀ r k : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → r < k → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    (∀ i < r, (k - i).choose (r - i) ∣ (n - i).choose (r - i)) →
      ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), H.IsBlockDesign r k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 732 — ii
problems.statement:
Is there some constant $c>0$ such that for all large $n$ there are at least
$\exp(c n^{1/2}\log n)$ block-compatible sequences?

Alon has proved there are at least $2^{(\frac{1}{2}+o(1))n^{1/2}\log n}$ many sequences
which are block-compatible for $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_732.parts.ii :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    Real.exp (c * Real.sqrt n * Real.log n) ≤ (Hypergraph.blockSizeProfiles n).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 751 — i
problems.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\chi(G)=4$. If $m_1<m_2<\cdots$ are the lengths of the
cycles in $G$ then can $\min(m_{i+1}-m_i)$ be arbitrarily large?

The answer is no: Bondy and Vince [BoVi98] proved that every graph with minimum degree at least $3$
has two cycles whose lengths differ by at most $2$, and hence the same is true for every graph with
chromatic number $4$.

`erdos_751.variants.finite` below carries the Lean proof. It assumes a finite vertex type,
where this quantifies over any `V : Type`, and the two are joined by de Bruijn-Erdős: a graph
that is not $3$-colourable has a finite subgraph that is not $3$-colourable, and cycles of that
subgraph are cycles of the whole. Mathlib does not have de Bruijn-Erdős, so that step is not
formalised here.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_751.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = 4 ∧
      ∀ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, ∀ m' ∈ G.cycleLengths, m < m' → m + k ≤ m'

problems.title: Erdős Problem 756
problems.statement:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points. Can there be $\gg n$ many distinct distances
each of which occurs for more than $n$ many pairs from $A$?

The answer is yes: Bhowmick [Bh24] constructs a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that
$\lfloor\frac{n}{4}\rfloor$ distances occur at least $n+1$ times.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_756 :
    (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (maxRichDistances n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 771
problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that, for every $m\geq 1$, there exists some
$S\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $\lvert S\rvert=f(n)$ such that $m\neq \sum_{a\in A}a$ for all
$A\subseteq S$.

Is it true that
$$f(n) = \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)\frac{n}{\log n}?$$

The answer is yes: the lower bound is due to Erdős and Graham and the upper bound to Alon and
Freiman [AlFr88].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_771 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) / (2 * Real.log n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 79
problems.statement:
We say $G$ is Ramsey size linear if $R(G,H)\ll m$ for all graphs $H$ with $m$ edges and
no isolated vertices.

Are there infinitely many graphs $G$ which are not Ramsey size linear but such that all of
its proper subgraphs are?

Asked by Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp [EFRS93]. $K_4$ was long the only known example.
Wigderson [Wi24] proved that there are infinitely many such graphs.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_79 :
    ∀ (N : ℕ), ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : N ≤ n) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      ¬ G.IsRamseySizeLinear ∧
      ∀ H : G.Subgraph, H < ⊤ → H.coe.IsRamseySizeLinear

problems.title: Erdős Problem 790 — ii
problems.statement:
In particular, is it true that $l(n)n^{-1/2}\to\infty$? The lower bound in [CKS75,
Theorem (1.1)] gives a positive answer.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_790.parts.ii :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (l n : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (n : ℝ)) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 80 — i
problems.statement:
Let $c>0$ and let $f_c(n)$ be the maximal $m$ such that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and
at least $cn^2$ edges, where each edge is contained in at least one triangle, must contain a
book of size $m$, that is, an edge shared by at least $m$ different triangles. Estimate
$f_c(n)$. In particular, is it true that $f_c(n)>n^\epsilon$ for some $\epsilon>0$?

The answer is no. Fox and Loh [FoLo12] proved that $f_c(n) \leq n^{O(1/\log\log n)}$ for every
fixed $c < 1/4$, so no $\epsilon > 0$ works for, say, $c = 1/8$. For $c > 1/4$ the situation is
different: $f_c(n) \geq n/6$, see [erdosproblems.com/80](https://www.erdosproblems.com/80).

The bound $c < 1/2$ is what makes the hypothesis satisfiable: a simple graph on $n$ vertices
has at most $n(n-1)/2$ edges, so no graph has $cn^2$ of them once $c \geq 1/2$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_80.parts.i :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → c < 1 / 2 →
      ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) ^ ε < f c n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 800
problems.statement:
If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices which has no two adjacent vertices of degree $\geq 3$ then
$$R(G)\ll n,$$
where the implied constant is absolute.

A problem of Burr and Erdős. Solved in the affirmative by Alon [Al94].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_800 :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      Fintype.card V = n →
      (∀ u v, G.Adj u v → ¬(3 ≤ G.degree u ∧ 3 ≤ G.degree v)) →
      (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey G : ℝ) ≤ C * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 833
problems.statement:
Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for all $r\geq 2$, in any $r$-uniform
hypergraph with chromatic number $3$ there is a vertex contained in at least $(1+c)^r$ many edges?

This was solved by Erdős and Lovász [ErLo75], who proved in particular that there is a vertex
contained in at least $\frac{2^{r-1}}{4r}$ many edges.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_833 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
      H.IsUniform r → H.HasHypergraphChromaticNumber 3 →
        ∃ v : Fin n, (1 + c) ^ r ≤ (H.hypergraphDegree v : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 882
problems.statement:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that in the set
$$\left\{ \sum_{a\in S} a : \emptyset\neq S\subseteq A\right\}$$
no two distinct elements divide each other?

A problem of Erdős and Sárközy. The answer is $(1+o(1))\log_2 n$: the lower bound
$\lvert A\rvert > \log_2 n - 1$ is achieved by the construction of Erdős, Lev, Rauzy, Sándor
and Sárközy [ELRSS99] (see `erdos_882.variants.lower_bound`), while
[Erdős Problem 1](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1) gives
$\lvert A\rvert \leq \log_2 n + \tfrac{1}{2}\log_2\log n + O(1)$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_882 :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (maxAntichainCard n : ℝ) / Real.logb 2 n)
      Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 903
problems.statement:
Let $n=p^2+p+1$ for some prime power $p$, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_t\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a
block design (so that every pair $x,y\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ is contained in exactly one $A_i$). Is it
true that if $t>n$ then $t\geq n+p$?

This is true, and was proved by Erdős, Fowler, Sós, and Wilson [EFSW85].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_903 :
    ∀ p : ℕ, IsPrimePow p →
    ∀ H : Finset (Finset (Fin (p ^ 2 + p + 1))),
      H.IsPairwiseBalancedDesign → p ^ 2 + p + 1 < H.card →
        p ^ 2 + p + 1 + p ≤ H.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 917 — i
problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 4$ and $f_k(n)$ be the largest number of edges in a graph on $n$ vertices which has
chromatic number $k$ and is critical (i.e. deleting any edge reduces the chromatic number).

Is it true that
$$f_k(n) \gg_k n^2?$$

This is the first part. It was proved by Toft [To70]. We read $\gg_k$ as: for each $k$ there is
$c > 0$ with $f_k(n) \geq cn^2$ for all large $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_917.parts.i :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ≤ k → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ (f k n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 917 — iii
problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 4$ and $f_k(n)$ be the largest number of edges in a graph on $n$ vertices which has
chromatic number $k$ and is critical (i.e. deleting any edge reduces the chromatic number).

More generally, is it true that, for $k\geq 6$,
$$f_k(n) \sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\lfloor k/3\rfloor}\right)n^2?$$

This is the third part. It has a negative answer: the constructions in
`erdos_917.variants.lower_construction` disprove it for $k \not\equiv 0 \pmod 3$
(see `erdos_917.variants.not_asymptotic`).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_917.parts.iii :
    ¬ ∀ k : ℕ, 6 ≤ k → (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f k n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] conjecturedValue k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 961 — sylvester schur
problems.statement:
Sylvester and Schur [Er34] proved that every set of $k$ consecutive integers greater than $k$
contains an integer divisible by a prime greater than $k$, i.e. not $(k+1)$-smooth.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_961.sylvester_schur (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) : Erdos961Prop k k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 980
problems.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ and $n_k(p)$ denote the least $k$th power nonresidue of $p$. Is it true that
$$\sum_{p<x} n_k(p)\sim c_k \frac{x}{\log x}$$
for some constant $c_k>0$?

Erdős [Er65b] asked this; it is true, and was proved by Elliott [El67b]. As in [El67b], the sum
is over the primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod k$ (for each of which a $k$th power nonresidue exists).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_980 (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), residueSum k ~[atTop] fun x ↦ c * x / Real.log x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 985
problems.statement:
Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q \leq p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?

The answer is yes. Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet $L$-functions, the
least prime primitive root modulo $p$ is less than $\sqrt{p} - 2$ for every prime $p > 2791$
[MTT16, Theorem 1]. A finite computation covers the odd primes $p \leq 2791$. The Generalized
Riemann Hypothesis is proved [Al26].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_985 : ∀ᵉ (p : ℕ) (hp_prime : p.Prime) (hp_nontrivial : p ≠ 2),
    ∃ q, q.Prime ∧ q < p ∧ orderOf (q : ZMod p) = p - 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 994
problems.statement:
Let $E\subseteq (0,1)$ be a meaurable subset with Lebesgue measure $\lambda(E)$. Is it true that,
for almost all $\alpha$,
$$\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}1_{\{k\alpha \}\in E}=\lambda(E)$$
for all $E$?

This is a conjecture of Khintchine [Kh23] (with the exceptional null set of $\alpha$ allowed to
depend on $E$). It is false, and was disproved by Marstrand [Ma70].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_994 :
    ¬ ∀ E ⊆ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, MeasurableSet E →
      ∀ᵐ α : ℝ, Tendsto (visitAverage E α) atTop (nhds (volume E).toReal)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 999
problems.statement:
For any function $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ the property that, for almost all
$\alpha$
$$\left\lvert \alpha-\frac{p}{q}\right\rvert < \frac{f(q)}{q}$$
has infinitely many solutions with $(p,q)=1$, is equivalent to
$$\sum_{q\geq 1}\phi(q)\frac{f(q)}{q}=\infty.$$

The Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture. It is easy to prove that the latter follows from the former.
Erdős proved this in the special case when $f(q)q$ is bounded. The full conjecture was proved by
Koukoulopoulos and Maynard [KoMa20].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_999 : ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ q, 0 ≤ f q) →
    ((∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) ↔
      ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q)

problems.title: Eswarathasan–Levine conjectures on harmonic numerators — eswarathasan levine three elements subset
problems.statement:
Eswarathasan–Levine inclusion theorem (1991): every prime $p \ge 5$ satisfies
$\{p - 1, p^2 - p, p^2 - 1\} \subseteq J_p$ (using Wolstenholme's theorem at $p - 1$; cf.
`WolstenholmePrime.wolstenholme_theorem` and `WolstenholmePrime.wolstenholme_harmonic`).
problems.lean:
theorem eswarathasan_levine_three_elements_subset {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) :
    ({p - 1, p ^ 2 - p, p ^ 2 - 1} : Set ℕ) ⊆ harmonicNumDivisibleSet p

The inequality $p_{n+1}-p_n < (\log p_n)^2-\log p_n$ holds for all $n>4$.
A consequence of Firuzbakht's conjecture.

problems.title: Gauss circle problem — exact form floor
problems.statement:
The value of $N(r)$ can be expressed as
$$
  N(r) = 1 + 4\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\left(\left\lfloor\frac{r^2}{4i+1}\right\rfloor -
    \left\lfloor\frac{r^2}{4i + 3}\right\rfloor\right).
$$

    N r = 1 + 4 * ∑' (i : ℕ), (⌊r ^ 2 / (4 * i + 1)⌋ - ⌊r ^ 2 / (4 * i + 3)⌋)

problems.title: Gerstenhaber's theorem
problems.statement:
**Gerstenhaber's theorem** [Ger61]: if $A$ and $B$ are commuting $n \times n$
matrices over a field $K$, then the unital $K$-algebra $K[A, B]$ they generate
has dimension at most $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem finrank_adjoin_pair_le (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) (hAB : Commute A B) :
    Module.finrank K (Algebra.adjoin K {A, B}) ≤ n

problems.title: Gourevitch's series identity
problems.statement:
The Gourevitch series identity:
The following identity holds:
$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1 + 14 n + 76 n^2 + 168 n^3}{2^{20 n}} \binom{2n}{n}^7 = \frac{32}{\pi^3}.$
This was originally conjectured in [G2003] by Guillera and proven in [A2025] by Au.
problems.lean:
theorem gourevitch_series_identity :
    ∑' n : ℕ, ((1 + 14 * n + 76 * n ^ 2 + 168 * n ^ 3) / (2 ^ (20 * n)) : ℝ)
      * Nat.centralBinom n ^ 7 = 32 / (Real.pi ^ 3)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 1
problems.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of $n$ positive integers. Does $A$ contain a sum-free set
of size at least $\frac n 3 + Ω(n)$, where $Ω(n) → ∞$ as $n → ∞$?

Bedert [Be25] proved that every set of $n$ integers contains a sum-free subset of size at least
$\frac n 3 + c \log\log n$ for some absolute constant $c > 0$, so the answer is yes.

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 14 — green 14 polynomial
problems.statement:
Is $W(k, r)$ a polynomial in $r$, for fixed $k$?

We formulate this as asking if $W(k, r)$ has polynomial growth in $r$.
The answer is no, already for $k = 4$. Every red $k$-term progression with $k \ge 3$ contains a
red $3$-term progression, so `mixedMonoAPGuaranteeSet k r ⊆ mixedMonoAPGuaranteeSet 3 r`, and
both sets are nonempty by van der Waerden's theorem, so $W(3, r) \le W(k, r)$. Polynomial
growth for one $k \ge 4$ would therefore force polynomial growth for $k = 3$, contradicting
`green_14_polynomial_k_eq_3` [Gr21, p.3].
problems.lean:
theorem green_14_polynomial :
    ¬ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∃ d : ℕ, (fun r => (W k r : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun r => (r : ℝ) ^ d

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 27 — lower
problems.statement:
Propose a better lower bound along primes.

Cao and Yuan [CY26, Theorem 1.1] prove $m(p) \gg \log p \log \log p$. This beats `lowerBest`,
since $\sqrt{\log \log \log p} / \log \log \log \log p = o(\log \log p)$.

Xinjie He [He26, Theorem 1.2] and Hou and Yang [HY26, Theorem 1.1] prove the stronger bound
$m(p) \gg (\log p / \log \log p)^2$. He's proof is formalised in Lean, see
`green_27.variants.lower_he26_hy26`. Together with `green_27.variants.upper_be23`, this lower bound
gives $m(p) = (\log p)^{2 + o(1)}$. The exact order of $m(p)$ remains open.
problems.lean:
theorem green_27.lower :
    (lowerBest =o[primesAtTop] green_27.lower.answer) ∧ (green_27.lower.answer =O[primesAtTop] m)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 3
problems.statement:
Suppose that $A \subset [0,1]$ is open and has measure greater than $\frac{1}{3}$. Is there a
solution to $xy = z$ with $x, y, z \in A$?

The answer is yes. [FGY26] prove that an open product-free subset of $(0,1)$ has measure strictly
less than $\frac{1}{3}$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_3 :
    ∀ A : Set ℝ,
      IsOpen A → A ⊆ Icc 0 1 → volume A > 1/3 →
        ∃ x y z, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ A ∧ z ∈ A ∧ x * y = z

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 38 — lower
problems.statement:
Can we improve the lower bound? The answer sequence must be eventually nonnegative, since
`=O` compares norms.

Yes. Itty, Rosin, Carstensen and Reichman [IRCR26] found a valid set of size $134753$ in
$\mathbb{F}_7^{10}$ (an independent set in the tenth strong power of $C_7$). Taking products
gives valid sets of size $134753^{\lfloor n/10 \rfloor}$ in $\mathbb{F}_7^n$, see
`green_38.variants.lower_itty_rosin_carstensen_reichman`, so the growth rate is at least
$134753^{1/10} > 3.258020 > C_1$ (note $134753 > 367^2 = 134689$). Gao [Ga26] and then Buys,
Polak and Zuiddam [BPZ26] improved the rate further, to $3.258789\ldots$ and $3.2588\ldots$
respectively; the latter is formalised in Lean. The exact growth rate remains open.
problems.lean:
theorem green_38.lower :
    (∀ᶠ n in atTop, 0 ≤ green_38.lower.answer n) ∧ green_38.lower.answer ≤ᶠ[atTop]
      LargestAdmissibleCardinality ∧
    ∃ c > C₁, (fun n ↦ c ^ n) =O[atTop] green_38.lower.answer

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 54 — green 54
problems.statement:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ be a balanced compact set (that is, $\lambda K \subseteq K$
whenever $|\lambda| \leq 1$) and suppose that the normalised Gaussian measure
$\gamma_\infty(K) \geq 0.99$. Does the sumset $10K = K + \cdots + K$ ($10$ times) contain a compact
convex set $C$ with $\gamma_\infty(C) \geq 0.01$?

The answer is yes: Hua, Song and Tudose proved that if $\gamma_n(A) > 5/6$ then $3(A + A + A)$
contains a symmetric convex body $C$ with $\gamma_n(C) \geq 1/4$, uniformly in $n$.
problems.lean:

    ∀ K : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact K → Balanced ℝ K → (0.99 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤
    gaussianMeasureInf K → ∃ C : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ (10 : ℕ) • K ∧
    (0.01 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ gaussianMeasureInf C

theorem green_82_upper_bound :
    ∃ C > 0, ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ A : Finset ℤ, A.card = n ∧
      ({θ : ℝ | θ ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ ∑ a ∈ A, cos (2 * π * a * θ) = 0} : Set ℝ).ncard ≤
      (⌊C * (n * Real.log n) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)⌋₊ : ℕ∞)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 84
problems.statement:
Is there a function $f : \{1, \dots, N\} \to \{-1, 1\}$ with $|\hat{f}(\theta)| \geq c\sqrt{N}$
for all $\theta$?

We read this as: is there an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that such an $f$ exists for all
sufficiently large $N$? It cannot hold for all $N$: for $N = 2$,
$\hat f(\theta) = e(\theta)(f(1) + f(2)e(\theta))$ vanishes for some $\theta$. The answer is yes
[BBMST20], see `green_84.variants.bbmst`.
problems.lean:
theorem green_84 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, IsSignOn N f ∧
      ∀ θ : ℝ, c * √N ≤ ‖fourierSum N f θ‖

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 9 — green 9 i
problems.statement:
Problem 9 (i): is $r_3(N) \ll N(\log N)^{-10}$?

Solved in [BlSi20].
problems.lean:
theorem green_9_i :
    (fun (N : ℕ) ↦ (r 3 N : ℝ)) ≪ fun (N : ℕ) ↦ (N : ℝ) * (Real.log N) ^ (-10 : ℝ)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 91
problems.statement:
Take a random graph $G(n, \frac{1}{2})$. Is there almost surely a bipartition of $G$ into two sets
of $n/2$ vertices with the property that $99\%$ of vertices have more neighbours on their own side
than on the other?

We read "almost surely" as "with probability tending to $1$ as $n \to \infty$", and "$99\%$ of
vertices" as at least $\frac{99}{100} n$ vertices. A bisection is the partition into a set `s` with
$\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ elements and its complement; for odd $n$ the parts have sizes differing by
one, as in [FKNSS22]. [Gr24] writes that the question "was apparently asked by Füredi in 1988".
The answer is yes
[FKNSS22, Theorem 1.1], see `green_91.variants.fknss`.
problems.lean:
theorem green_91 :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ prob n fun G ↦
      ∃ s : Finset (Fin n), s.card = n / 2 ∧ (99 / 100 : ℝ) * n ≤ numFriendly G s)
      atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Gromov's Polynomial Growth Theorem
problems.statement:
**Gromov's Polynomial Growth Theorem** : A finitely generated group has
    polynomial growth if and only if it is virtually nilpotent.
problems.lean:
theorem GromovPolynomialGrowthTheorem [Group.FG G] :
    HasPolynomialGrowth G ↔ Group.IsVirtuallyNilpotent G

problems.title: Hajós' conjecture (1961) — disproved.
problems.statement:
**Hajós' conjecture (1961) — disproved.**

Hajós conjectured that every graph with chromatic number at least $k$ contains a subdivision of
$K_k$ (a strengthening of Hadwiger's conjecture). This is **false**: Catlin [Ca79] gave
counterexamples for every $k \ge 7$, and Erdős and Fajtlowicz [EF81] showed that almost all
graphs are counterexamples.
problems.lean:
theorem hajos_conjecture : ¬
    ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ),
      (k : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → ContainsSubdivision (completeGraph (Fin k)) G

problems.title: The Hall ratio conjecture (Harris 2019) — disproved.
problems.statement:
**The Hall ratio conjecture (Harris 2019) — disproved.**

Harris conjectured that the fractional chromatic number is bounded by a constant multiple of the
Hall ratio: there is a constant $C$ with $\chi_f(G) \le C\,\rho(G)$ for every graph $G$. This
is **false**: Dvořák, Ossona de Mendez and Wu [DOW20] and, independently, Blumenthal, Lidický,
Martin, Norin, Pfender and Volec [BLMNPV22] constructed graphs with $\chi_f / \rho$
arbitrarily large.
problems.lean:
theorem hall_ratio_conjecture : ¬
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.fractionalChromaticNumber ≤ C * hallRatio G

problems.title: First Hardy–Littlewood conjecture — not first and secondHardyLittlewoodConjecture
problems.statement:
Richards [Ri74] showed that only one of the two Hardy-Littlewood conjectures can be true.

[Ri74] Richards, Ian (1974). _On the Incompatibility of Two Conjectures Concerning Primes_. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 80: 419–438.
problems.lean:
theorem not_first_and_secondHardyLittlewoodConjecture :
    (∀ {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ), FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m) →
      ¬(∀ {x y : ℕ} (hx : 2 ≤ x) (hy : 2 ≤ y), SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor x y)

problems.title: The Hasse--Weil conjecture for elliptic curves — exists hasAnalyticContinuation rat
problems.statement:
The **Hasse--Weil conjecture** over $\mathbb{Q}$: the $L$-series of an elliptic curve over
$\mathbb{Q}$ has an analytic continuation to $\mathbb{C}$. This follows from the modularity
theorem, see [Wikipedia].
problems.lean:
theorem exists_hasAnalyticContinuation_rat (E : WeierstrassCurve ℚ) [E.IsElliptic] :
    ∃ L, HasAnalyticContinuation E L

problems.title: Hedetniemi's conjecture (1966) — disproved.
problems.statement:
**Hedetniemi's conjecture (1966) — disproved.**

For all finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, the chromatic number of the tensor product was
conjectured to satisfy $\chi(G \times H) = \min\{\chi(G), \chi(H)\}$.

This is **false**: Shitov [Sh19] constructed finite graphs $G$, $H$ with
$\chi(G \times H) < \min\{\chi(G), \chi(H)\}$. The inequality $\le$ always holds
(`chromaticNumber_tensorProd_le_min`); it is the reverse inequality that fails.
problems.lean:
theorem hedetniemi_conjecture : ¬
    ∀ {α β : Type} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β),
      (tensorProd G H).chromaticNumber = min G.chromaticNumber H.chromaticNumber

problems.title: Evens–Venkov
problems.statement:
**Evens–Venkov.** For a finite group $G$ and a field $k$, the cohomology ring
$H^*(G, k) = \mathrm{Ext}^*_{k[G]}(k, k)$ of the group algebra $k[G]$ is a finitely generated
$k$-algebra.
problems.lean:
theorem cohomologyRing_finiteType_monoidAlgebra (G : Type u) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    Algebra.FiniteType k (cohomologyRing k (MonoidAlgebra k G))

problems.title: Friedlander–Suslin
problems.statement:
**Friedlander–Suslin.** If $A$ is a finite-dimensional cocommutative Hopf algebra over a
field $k$, that is, the group algebra of a finite group scheme over $k$, then $H^*(A, k)$ is a
finitely generated $k$-algebra.
problems.lean:
theorem cohomologyRing_finiteType_of_isCocomm [Coalgebra.IsCocomm k A] :
    Algebra.FiniteType k (cohomologyRing k A)

problems.title: Friedlander–Suslin
problems.statement:
**Friedlander–Suslin.** If $A$ is a finite-dimensional cocommutative Hopf algebra over a
field $k$ and $M$ is a finite-dimensional $A$-module, then $H^*(A, M)$ is a finitely generated
module over $H^*(A, k)$.
problems.lean:
theorem cohomology_finite_of_isCocomm [Coalgebra.IsCocomm k A] (M : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    [FiniteDimensional k M] : Module.Finite (cohomologyRing k A) (cohomology k A M)

problems.title: Residual finiteness of hyperbolic groups — hyperbolic exists finiteIndex ne top
problems.statement:
Does every nontrivial hyperbolic group have a proper subgroup of finite index?

This is Problem (H1)(b) in [BMS]. The trivial group has no proper subgroup, so we assume that
$G$ is nontrivial.

No. By [KaWi00] (see `hyperbolic_residuallyFinite_iff_exists_finiteIndex_ne_top`), this problem
is equivalent to `hyperbolic_residuallyFinite`, which was disproved in [OAI26a].
problems.lean:
theorem hyperbolic_exists_finiteIndex_ne_top :
    ¬ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.IsHyperbolic G] [Nontrivial G],
      ∃ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ ∧ H.FiniteIndex

problems.title: Residual finiteness of hyperbolic groups — hyperbolic residuallyFinite
problems.statement:
Is every hyperbolic group residually finite?

This is Problem (H1)(a) in [BMS] and Q 1.15 in [Be04].

No. This was disproved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26a], which constructs
a torsion-free hyperbolic group that is not residually finite. The
[Lean proof](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/lean/OAI/GroupTheory/Hyperbolic/Main.lean#L7)
of [OAI26a] defines hyperbolicity by uniformly thin geodesic triangles in a Cayley graph. That
definition is equivalent to `Group.IsHyperbolic`, but the equivalence is not part of the Lean
proof.
problems.lean:
theorem hyperbolic_residuallyFinite :
    ¬ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.IsHyperbolic G], Group.ResiduallyFinite G

problems.title: Residual finiteness of hyperbolic groups — hyperbolic residuallyFinite iff exists finiteIndex ne top
problems.statement:
Every hyperbolic group is residually finite if and only if every nontrivial hyperbolic group has a
proper subgroup of finite index.

This is the theorem of [KaWi00] that Problems (H1)(a) and (H1)(b) are equivalent.
problems.lean:
theorem hyperbolic_residuallyFinite_iff_exists_finiteIndex_ne_top :
    (∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.IsHyperbolic G], Group.ResiduallyFinite G) ↔
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.IsHyperbolic G] [Nontrivial G],
        ∃ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ ∧ H.FiniteIndex

problems.title: Hyperperfect numbers — two hyperperfect characterization
problems.statement:
Not every $2$-hyperperfect integer has the form $3^m(3^{m+1} - 2)$ with $m \ge 1$ and $3^{m+1} - 2$
prime: Alexander Violette (June 2026, [OEIS A007593](https://oeis.org/A007593)) found the
four-prime-factor $2$-hyperperfect counterexample
$n = 3^{16} \cdot 129140227 \cdot 256572153302107 \cdot 225205396855537107298933866373$.
problems.lean:
theorem two_hyperperfect_characterization :
    ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, IsHyperperfect 2 n →
      ∃ m ≥ 1, (3 ^ (m + 1) - 2).Prime ∧ n = 3 ^ m * (3 ^ (m + 1) - 2)

problems.title: Inscribed square problem — exists inscribed rectangle
problems.statement: It is known that every Jordan curve admits at least one inscribed rectangle.
problems.lean:
theorem exists_inscribed_rectangle (γ : Circle → ℝ²) (hγ : IsEmbedding γ) :
    ∃ t₁ t₂ t₃ t₄ r, IsRectangle (γ t₁) (γ t₂) (γ t₃) (γ t₄) r

problems.title: Inscribed square problem — exists inscribed rectangle of smooth
problems.statement:
It is known that every *smooth* Jordan curve admits inscribed rectangles of all aspect ratios.
Here a smooth Jordan curve is a smooth embedding of the circle into the plane, i.e. a smooth
simple closed curve with nowhere vanishing velocity.
problems.lean:
theorem exists_inscribed_rectangle_of_smooth (γ : Circle → ℝ²)
    (hγ : IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 1) (𝓡 2) ∞ γ) (r : ℝ) (hr : r > 0) :
    ∃ t₁ t₂ t₃ t₄, IsRectangle (γ t₁) (γ t₂) (γ t₃) (γ t₄) r

problems.title: Inscribed square problem — exists inscribed square of C2
problems.statement:
It is also known that every $C^2$ Jordan curve admits an inscribed square.
Here a $C^2$ Jordan curve is a $C^2$ embedding of the circle into the plane, i.e. a $C^2$
simple closed curve with nowhere vanishing velocity.
problems.lean:
theorem exists_inscribed_square_of_C2 (γ : Circle → ℝ²)
    (hγ : IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 1) (𝓡 2) 2 γ) :
    ∃ t₁ t₂ t₃ t₄, IsRectangle (γ t₁) (γ t₂) (γ t₃) (γ t₄) 1

problems.title: Jacobson Conjecture — jacobson conjecture of right noetherian
problems.statement:
Originally, on page 200 of [Ja1956], Jacobson asked if the Jacobson conjecture holds for all right
Noetherian rings. However in [He1965] Herstein constructs a right Noetherian ring for which the
Jacobson conjecture does not hold.
problems.lean:
theorem jacobson_conjecture_of_right_noetherian :
    ¬ ∀ (R : Type) [Ring R] [IsRightNoetherianRing R], JacobsonConjectureFor R

problems.title: Kakeya problem — kakeya finite
problems.statement:
The finite field Kakeya conjecture asserts that any Kakeya set in `𝔽_qⁿ` has size at
least `c_n · qⁿ` for some constant `c_n` depending only on `n`.
This was first proved by Dvir [Dv08]. The best known bound to date, due to Bukh and Chao [BuCh21],
establishes that any Kakeya set in `𝔽_qⁿ` has size at least `qⁿ / (2 - 1/q)^(n - 1)`.
The dimension is positive, as in `kakeya_set_conjecture`; for `n = 0` the empty set is a Kakeya
set and the bound would read `1 ≤ 0`.

[Dv08] Dvir, Z., _On the size of Kakeya sets in finite fields_. Journal of the American Mathematical Society 22 (2009), no. 4, 1093–1097.
[BuCh21] Bukh, B. and Chao, T.-W., _Sharp density bounds on the finite field Kakeya problem_. Discrete Analysis 26 (2021), 9 pp.
problems.lean:
theorem kakeya_finite {F : Type*} [Field F] [Fintype F] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (K : Finset (Fin n → F)) (hK : IsKakeyaFinite K) :
    card F ^ n / (2 - 1 / card F : ℚ) ^ (n - 1) ≤ K.card

problems.title: Kaplansky's Conjectures — i
problems.statement: If $P$ is the Promislow group, then the group ring $\mathbb{F}_p[P]$ has a non-trivial unit.
problems.lean:
theorem UnitConjecture.counterexamples.i (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] :
    ∃ (u : (MonoidAlgebra (ZMod p) PromislowGroup)ˣ), ¬IsTrivialUnit u.val

problems.title: Kaplansky's Conjectures — ii
problems.statement: If $P$ is the Promislow group, then the group ring $\mathbb{C}[P]$ has a non-trivial unit.
problems.lean:
theorem UnitConjecture.counterexamples.ii :
    ∃ (u : (MonoidAlgebra ℂ PromislowGroup)ˣ), ¬IsTrivialUnit u.val

problems.title: Kaplansky's direct finiteness conjecture
problems.statement:
**Kaplansky's direct finiteness conjecture** asserts that for every field $K$ and every group
$G$, the group algebra $K[G]$ is directly finite: $ab = 1$ implies $ba = 1$.

It is false. An internal OpenAI model found a finite field $K$ of characteristic two, a finitely
generated group $G$ and $a, b \in K[G]$ with $ab = 1$ and $ba \neq 1$ in September 2026
[OAI26c]; see `direct_finiteness_conjecture.variants.char_two` and OpenAI's Lean proof.
problems.lean:
theorem direct_finiteness_conjecture :
    ¬ ∀ (K : Type) [Field K] (G : Type) [Group G],
      IsDedekindFiniteMonoid (MonoidAlgebra K G)

problems.title: Keith numbers — klazar luca keith counting bound
problems.statement:
Klazar–Luca counting bound (2007, Theorem 1.2): there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for every
integer $x \ge 2$, the number of base-$10$ Keith integers at most $x$ satisfies
$$\#\{N \le x : N \text{ is a Keith number}\} \le \frac{C x}{\sqrt{\log x}}.$$
problems.lean:
theorem klazar_luca_keith_counting_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x : ℕ, 2 ≤ x →
      ({N : ℕ | N ≤ x ∧ IsKeithNumber N}.ncard : ℝ) ≤
        C * ((x : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log (x : ℝ)))

problems.title: Köthe conjecture — amitsur conjecture
problems.statement:
The **Amitsur Conjecture**: If `J` is a nil ideal in `R`, then `J[x]` is a nil ideal of the polynomial ring `R[x]`.
This is known to be false, see Agata Smoktunowicz, _Polynomial rings over nil rings need not be nil_.
problems.lean:
theorem amitsur_conjecture : ¬ ∀ (R : Type) [Ring R] (J : TwoSidedIdeal R), IsNil J →
    IsNil (TwoSidedIdeal.map (Polynomial.C) J)

problems.title: Conjecture 19.25
problems.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be finite groups of the same order with
$\sum_{g \in G} \phi(|g|) = \sum_{h \in H} \phi(|h|)$,
where $\phi$ is the Euler totient function. Suppose that $G$ is simple. Is
$H$ necessarily simple?

The answer is negative by [vDJMM26, Theorem 4.1]. The groups
$G = \operatorname{PSU}(3,3)$ and $H = C_6 \times S_4 \times (C_7 \rtimes C_6)$
both have order $6048$ and totient sum $23984$, but only $G$ is simple.
In the semidirect product, a generator of $C_6$ acts on $C_7$ by multiplication
by $3$ modulo $7$.
problems.lean:
theorem kourovka_19_25 :
    ¬ ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H] [Fintype G] [Fintype H],
       Fintype.card G = Fintype.card H →
       ∑ g : G, φ (orderOf g) = ∑ h : H, φ (orderOf h) →
       IsSimpleGroup G → IsSimpleGroup H

problems.title: Conjecture 8.8 — kourovka 8 8a
problems.statement:
Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely-generated group $G$ containing an
element $a$ such that every element of $G$ is conjugate to a power of $a$?

Here a power of $a$ means $a^n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Answered affirmatively by V. S. Guba, Math. USSR-Izv. 29 (1986), 233–277.
problems.lean:
theorem kourovka_8_8a :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), ¬ IsCyclic G ∧ Group.FG G ∧
      ∃ a : G, ∀ g : G, ∃ n : ℤ, IsConj g (a ^ n)

problems.title: Conjectures about Latin Squares — growthRateZn
problems.statement:
Conjecture 6.9 in [Wa2011]:
$$
\lim_{\substack{n \to \infty \\ n \text{ odd}}} \frac{1}{n} \log(z_n / n!) = -1
$$
Note that $z_n = 0$ for even $n$ (see `z_even`), so the limit must be restricted to odd $n$; here
we parametrise odd $n$ as $2k + 1$.

This is true: the limit exists and equals $-1$. It follows from the asymptotic
$z_n = (e^{-1/2} + o(1)) \, n!^2 / n^{n-1}$ for odd $n$ of [EMM19, Theorem 1.2] and Stirling's
formula; the introduction of [EMM19] notes that the theorem confirms this conjecture.
problems.lean:
theorem growthRateZn :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun k => (1 : ℝ) / (2 * k + 1) *
      Real.log (z (2 * k + 1) / (2 * k + 1).factorial)) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (-1))

problems.title: Conjectures about Latin Squares — maxTransversalsBound
problems.statement:
Theorem 7.2 in [Wa2011]:
For all $n \geq 5$,
$$
15^{n/5} \leq T(n) \leq c^n \sqrt{n} \cdot n!
$$
where $c = \sqrt{\frac{3 - \sqrt{3}}{6}} \cdot e^{\sqrt{3}/6}$
problems.lean:
theorem maxTransversalsBound :
    let c := Real.sqrt ((3 - Real.sqrt 3) / 6) * Real.exp (Real.sqrt 3 / 6)
    ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 5 →
      (T n : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc ((15 : ℝ) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 5)) (c ^ n * Real.sqrt n * n.factorial)

problems.title: Conjectures about Latin Squares — numTransversalsZn
problems.statement:
Conjecture 6.7 in [Wa2011]:
There exist real constants $0 < c_1 < c_2 < 1$ such that
$$
c_1^n n! \leq z_n \leq c_2^n n!
$$
for all odd $n \geq 3$.

This is true. By [EMM19, Theorem 1.2], $z_n = (e^{-1/2} + o(1)) \, n!^2 / n^{n-1}$ for odd $n$
(the paper's $s_n$ equals $n! \, z_n$), which proves Vardi's conjecture [EMM19, Conjecture 1.1]:
the bounds hold for all large odd $n$ with any $0 < c_1 < 1/e < c_2 < 1$. The finitely many
remaining odd $n \geq 3$ are covered by $0 < z_n < n!$, after decreasing $c_1$ and increasing $c_2$.
problems.lean:
theorem numTransversalsZn :
      ∃ᵉ (c₁ > (0 : ℝ)) (c₂ < (1 : ℝ)) (_ : c₁ < c₂),
      ∀ n ≥ 3, Odd n →
        (z n : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc (c₁ ^ n * n.factorial) (c₂ ^ n * n.factorial)

problems.title: Conjectures about Latin Squares — oddOrderLeq9LatinSquareTransversal
problems.statement: The conjecture is known to be true for $n \leq 9$.
problems.lean:
theorem oddOrderLeq9LatinSquareTransversal :
    ∀ n ≤ 9, Odd n → ∀ (L : LatinSquare n), ∃ σ, IsTransversal L σ

problems.title: Legendre's conjecture — ferreira large n
problems.statement: Ferreira proved that the conjecture is true for sufficiently large n.
problems.lean:
theorem legendre_conjecture.ferreira_large_n :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ p ∈ Set.Ioo (n ^ 2) ((n + 1) ^ 2), Nat.Prime p

problems.title: Leinster Groups — abelian is leinster iff cyclic perfect
problems.statement:
An abelian group is a Leinster group if and only if it is cyclic with order equal
to a perfect number.

Reference: Leinster, Tom (2001). "Perfect numbers and groups". Theorem 2.1.
problems.lean:
theorem abelian_is_leinster_iff_cyclic_perfect (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] [Fintype G] :
    IsLeinster G ↔ IsCyclic G ∧ Nat.Perfect (Fintype.card G)

problems.title: Leinster Groups — dihedral is leinster iff odd perfect
problems.statement:
The dihedral group `DihedralGroup n` (of order `2n`) is a Leinster group if and only if `n` is
an odd perfect number. This gives a one-to-one correspondence between dihedral Leinster groups
and odd perfect numbers.

In particular, the existence of odd perfect numbers is equivalent to the existence of
dihedral Leinster groups.

Reference: Leinster, Tom (2001). "Perfect numbers and groups".
problems.lean:
theorem dihedral_is_leinster_iff_odd_perfect (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] :
    IsLeinster (DihedralGroup n) ↔ Nat.Perfect n ∧ Odd n

problems.title: Leinster Groups — exists nonabelian leinster group
problems.statement:
Non-abelian Leinster groups exist.

For example, `S₃ × C₅` (order 30) and `A₅ × C₁₅₁₂₈` are Leinster groups.

Reference: Leinster, Tom (2001). "Perfect numbers and groups".
problems.lean:
theorem exists_nonabelian_leinster_group :
    ∃ G : Type, ∃ (_ : Group G) (_ : Fintype G),
      IsLeinster G ∧ ¬ ∀ (a b : G), a * b = b * a

problems.title: Zariski's local uniformization theorem.
problems.statement:
**Zariski's local uniformization theorem.** Every valuation ring of a finitely generated field
extension $F \mid k$ that contains a field $k$ of characteristic zero admits local uniformization
over $k$. This is the main theorem of [Zar1940].
problems.lean:
theorem local_uniformization_of_charZero (k F : Type*) [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType k F] [CharZero k] (𝒪 : ValuationSubring F)
    (hk : ∀ x : k, algebraMap k F x ∈ 𝒪) :
    𝒪.HasLocalUniformization k

problems.title: Local uniformization
problems.statement:
Local uniformization holds in transcendence degree at most three over any field. In
characteristic zero this is [Zar1940]. In positive characteristic, surfaces are [Abh1956];
threefolds over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p > 5$ are [Abh1966],
simplified in [Cut2009]; and the remaining characteristics $2, 3, 5$ are [CP2008] and [CP2009],
for quasi-projective threefolds over a field $k$ with $[k : k^p] < \infty$. It follows in the
generality stated here from [CP2019], Theorem 1.1, which resolves the singularities of every
reduced separated Noetherian quasi-excellent scheme of dimension at most three in any
characteristic: the centre of $\mathcal{O}$ on a resolution of a proper model of $F \mid k$ is a
regular point.
problems.lean:
theorem local_uniformization_of_trdeg_le_three (k F : Type*) [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType k F] (𝒪 : ValuationSubring F)
    (hk : ∀ x : k, algebraMap k F x ∈ 𝒪) (hF : Algebra.trdeg k F ≤ 3) :
    𝒪.HasLocalUniformization k

problems.title: Mathoverflow 235893 — mathoverflow 260589
problems.statement:
There exists a connected bijection ℝ → ℝ^2 where the inverse is not connected,
proven in [mathoverflow/260589](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/260589) by user
[Gro-Tsen](https://mathoverflow.net/users/17064/gro-tsen).
problems.lean:
theorem mathoverflow_260589 :

problems.title: MathOverflow 508539

where $E$ denotes the edge boundary (the number of edges between $A$ and its complement), and
$V$ denotes the inner vertex boundary (the number of points in $A$ having a neighbor outside $A$).

zero the cardinality hypothesis allows the whole cube, whose boundaries are empty.

Simon Colton conjectures that the number of refactorable numbers less than $x$ is at least
$\frac{x}{2\log x}$. This is an asymptotic claim, so we state it for sufficiently large $x$.

In this form it is a theorem: Zelinsky [Ze02, Theorem 7] proved that for every $k$ the number of
refactorable numbers $\le n$ exceeds $k \pi(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and
$\pi(n) \sim n / \log n$. It also follows from Spiro's asymptotic [Sp85], by which the count is
$\frac{x}{\sqrt{\log x}} (\log \log x)^{-1 + o(1)}$. See `colton_conjecture` for the
pointwise conjecture that remains open.

problems.statement:
$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sum_{p < N, \, p \equiv 1 \pmod 3} x(p)}{\sum_{p < N, \, p \equiv 1 \pmod 3} y(p)} = 1 + \sqrt{3},$$
where for a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, $x(p) > y(p) > 0$ are the unique positive integers such
that $p = x(p)^2 + x(p)y(p) + y(p)^2$.

      fun x => x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6)

problems.title: Asymptotic density of powerful numbers — asymptotic erdos szekeres
problems.statement:
Erdős and Szekeres [ES35] proved that the number of powerful integers up to $x$ satisfies
$$Q(x) = \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} x^{1/2} + O(x^{1/3}).$$
In particular $Q(x) \sim \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} \sqrt{x}$.
problems.lean:
theorem asymptotic_erdos_szekeres :
    (fun x : ℝ => (Q x : ℝ) - A * x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2)) =O[atTop]
      fun x => x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)

problems.title: Asymptotic density of powerful numbers — error term improvement
problems.statement:
Can the exponent $1/6$ in the error term of the Bateman–Grosswald asymptotic be improved
unconditionally? That is, is there $\delta > 0$ such that
$$Q(x) = \frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)} x^{1/2} + \frac{\zeta(2/3)}{\zeta(2)} x^{1/3} +
O(x^{1/6 - \delta})?$$
The answer is yes. Liu proved the exponent $121/860 + \varepsilon$ assuming the Riemann
Hypothesis [SA26, §1], and the Riemann Hypothesis is proved [Al26].
problems.lean:
theorem error_term_improvement :
    ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ),
      (fun x : ℝ => (Q x : ℝ) - A * x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2) - B * x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3)) =O[atTop]
        fun x => x ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 6 - δ)

problems.title: Lagarias' Criterion
problems.statement:
**Lagarias' Criterion**. A refinement of Robin's criterion: the Riemann Hypothesis
is equivalent to
$$
  \sigma(n) < H_n + e^{H_n}\log H_n
$$
for all $n \geq 2$, where $H_n = 1 + 1/2 + \cdots + 1/n$ is the $n$th harmonic number.

Note that [Co26] states this for all $n \geq 1$, but at $n = 1$ both sides equal $1$; Lagarias'
original formulation is the non-strict inequality for all $n \geq 1$, with equality only at
$n = 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem lagarias_criterion : RiemannHypothesis ↔
    ∀ n > 1, σ 1 n < harmonic n + exp (harmonic n) * log (harmonic n)

problems.title: RiemannHypothesis
problems.statement: The statement that Lagarias' criterion holds.
problems.lean:
theorem lagarias_criterion_rhs {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 < n) :
    σ 1 n < harmonic n + exp (harmonic n) * log (harmonic n)

problems.title: Robin's Criterion
problems.statement:
**Robin's Criterion**. The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to
$$
  \sigma(n) < e ^ {\gamma} n\log\log n
$$
for all $n > 5040$, where $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant and $\sigma(n)$ is
the sum of divisors.
problems.lean:
theorem robin_criterion :
    RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∀ n > 5040, σ 1 n < (exp eulerMascheroniConstant) * n * log (log n)

problems.title: RiemannHypothesis
problems.statement: The statement that Robin's criterion holds.
problems.lean:
theorem robin_criterion_rhs {n : ℕ} (hn : n > 5040) :
    σ 1 n < exp eulerMascheroniConstant * n * log (log n)

problems.title: Weil's Positivity Criterion
problems.statement:
**Weil's Positivity Criterion**. The Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to the non-positivity of
Weil factor sums on the convolution of test functions. In [Co26] this is expressed as
$$
  \sum_v W_v(g\star g^*) \leq 0
$$
for all compactly-supported smooth functions $g : \mathbb{R}_+^{\times} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that
the Mellin transform of $g$ vanishes at $\pm i / 2$, where $g^*(x) := \bar{g}(x^{-1})$ and $W_v$
are the multiplicative Weil factors defined in [Co26]. We formalise this as the corresponding
additive statement (via $x = e^u$), since convolution in mathlib is additive, and restrict to
real-valued test functions $g$, which suffices for the equivalence.
problems.lean:
theorem weil_positivity_criterion :
    RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∀ g : C_c(ℝ, ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ∞ g → IsTestFunction g →
      weilArchimedean (g ⋆ fun x ↦ g (-x)) +
        ∑' p : Nat.Primes, weilNonArchimedean p (g ⋆ fun x ↦ g (-x)) ≤ 0

problems.title: RiemannHypothesis
problems.statement: The statement that the Weil criterion holds.
problems.lean:
theorem weil_positivity_criterion_rhs {g : C_c(ℝ, ℝ)} (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g)
    (h : IsTestFunction g) :
    weilArchimedean (g ⋆ fun x ↦ g (-x)) +
      ∑' p : Nat.Primes, weilNonArchimedean p (g ⋆ fun x ↦ g (-x)) ≤ 0

problems.title: Vanishing
problems.statement:
**Vanishing.** Let $R$ be a regular local ring and let $M$, $N$ be finitely generated
$R$-modules such that $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length. If $\dim M + \dim N < \dim R$, then
$\chi(M, N) = 0$. Conjectured by Serre and proved by Roberts [Ro85] and, independently, by
Gillet and Soulé [GS87].

    (hdim : Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N < ringKrullDim R) :
    intersectionMultiplicity R M N = 0

problems.statement:
**Non-negativity.** Let $R$ be a regular local ring and let $M$, $N$ be finitely generated
$R$-modules such that $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length. Then $\chi(M, N) \ge 0$.
Conjectured by Serre and proved by Gabber in 1995 [Ro98].
problems.lean:

    0 ≤ intersectionMultiplicity R M N

problems.lean:

    (hdim : Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N = ringKrullDim R) :

problems.title: Dimension inequality.
problems.statement:
**Dimension inequality.** Let $R$ be a regular local ring and let $M$, $N$ be finitely generated
$R$-modules such that $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length. Then
$\dim M + \dim N \le \dim R$. Proved by Serre for every regular local ring [Se00].

    Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N ≤ ringKrullDim R

problems.title: Sidorenko's conjecture for graphons (1993).
problems.statement:
**Sidorenko's conjecture for graphons (1993).**

For every finite bipartite simple graph $H$ and every graphon $W$ on $[0, 1]$ with Lebesgue measure:
$t(H, W) \ge t(K_2, W)^{e(H)}$, where $t(K_2, W) = p(W)$ is the edge density of $W$,
and $t(H, W)$ is the graphon homomorphism density of $H$ in $W$.

This is false. The finite counterexample of [OAI26a] (see `sidorenko_conjecture`) also refutes
the graphon form: the step graphon of the finite host graph has the same homomorphism
densities and the same edge density as the host. This reduction is not part of the linked Lean
proof of the finite form.
problems.lean:
theorem sidorenko_conjecture_graphon :
    ¬ ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (H : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel H.Adj],
      H.IsBipartite →
      ∀ (W : Graphon),
        (graphonEdgeDensity W) ^ H.edgeFinset.card ≤ graphonHomDensity H W

problems.title: Case: `H = C_{2k}` is an even cycle (Sidorenko 1993, graphon version).
problems.statement:
**Case: `H = C_{2k}` is an even cycle (Sidorenko 1993, graphon version).**

Every even cycle $C_{2k}$ satisfies Sidorenko's inequality for all graphons on $[0, 1]$.
problems.lean:
theorem sidorenko_even_cycle_graphon (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k)
    (W : LimitObjects.Graphon) :
    (graphonEdgeDensity W) ^ (cycleGraph (2 * k)).edgeFinset.card ≤
      graphonHomDensity (cycleGraph (2 * k)) W

problems.statement:

    (W : LimitObjects.Graphon) :
    (graphonEdgeDensity W) ^ H.edgeFinset.card ≤ graphonHomDensity H W

problems.title: Six standard deviations suffice
problems.statement:
**Six standard deviations suffice** (Spencer, 1985)

For every $n$ and every family of $n$ subsets $S_1, \dots, S_n$ of $\{1, \dots, n\}$,
there is a colouring $\chi : \{1, \dots, n\} \to \{-1, +1\}$ such that
$\left|\sum_{j \in S_i} \chi(j)\right| \le 6\sqrt{n}$ for every $i$.
problems.lean:
theorem six_standard_deviations :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Fin n → Finset (Fin n)),
      ∃ χ : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ j, χ j = 1 ∨ χ j = -1) ∧
        ∀ i, |∑ j ∈ S i, χ j| ≤ 6 * Real.sqrt n

      (∃ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n ∧ (n : ℝ) < Real.exp (72795134 / 100000) ∧

problems.title: There are infinitely many Steiner systems with $t = 4$.
problems.statement:
**There are infinitely many Steiner systems with $t = 4$.**

Keevash (2014) proved that for any fixed $t$ and $k$, a Steiner system $S(t, k, n)$
exists for all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying the necessary divisibility conditions.
Since there are infinitely many such admissible $n$, this implies infinitely many
$S(4, k, n)$ systems exist (for any fixed $k > 4$). The proof is nonconstructive.

Explicit examples include $S(4, 5, 11)$ (the unique system, related to the Mathieu
group $M_{11}$) and $S(4, 7, 23)$ (related to the Mathieu group $M_{23}$).

Only nontrivial systems with $4 < k < n$ are counted: for every $n$ the single block
$\{1, \dots, n\}$ is an $S(4, n, n)$, and all $4$-subsets of an $n$-set form an $S(4, 4, n)$.
problems.lean:
theorem infinitely_many_steiner_t4 :
    {s : Σ k n : ℕ, S(4, k, n) | 4 < s.1 ∧ s.1 < s.2.1}.Infinite

problems.title: There are infinitely many Steiner systems with $t = 5$.
problems.statement:
**There are infinitely many Steiner systems with $t = 5$.**

Keevash (2014) proved that for any fixed $t$ and $k$, a Steiner system $S(t, k, n)$
exists for all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying the necessary divisibility conditions.
This settles the long-standing open problem of whether infinitely many $S(5, k, n)$
systems exist. The proof is nonconstructive.

Only two explicit examples are known: $S(5, 6, 12)$ and $S(5, 8, 24)$, both Witt
designs related to the Mathieu groups $M_{12}$ and $M_{24}$ respectively.

Only nontrivial systems with $5 < k < n$ are counted, for the same reason as in
`infinitely_many_steiner_t4`.
No Steiner system with $t \geq 6$ has been explicitly constructed, though Keevash's
result guarantees their existence nonconstructively as well.
problems.lean:
theorem infinitely_many_steiner_t5 :
    {s : Σ k n : ℕ, S(5, k, n) | 5 < s.1 ∧ s.1 < s.2.1}.Infinite

problems.title: The Tu-Deng conjecture.
problems.statement:
**The Tu-Deng conjecture.** For $k \ge 2$ and a nonzero residue $t$ modulo $2^k - 1$, there
are at most $2^{k-1}$ pairs of residues $(a, b)$ with $a + b = t$ whose binary weights
(of their representatives in $0, \dots, 2^k - 2$) sum to at most $k - 1$.

Proved in [LLX26] and independently in [Cu26]; see also the Lean development [Lean26].
problems.lean:
theorem tu_deng_conjecture (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (t : ZMod (2 ^ k - 1)) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    {p : ZMod (2 ^ k - 1) × ZMod (2 ^ k - 1) |
        p.1 + p.2 = t ∧ binaryWeight p.1.val + binaryWeight p.2.val ≤ k - 1}.ncard
      ≤ 2 ^ (k - 1)

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 13
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 13](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, the size `b(G)` of a largest induced bipartite subgraph
satisfies `b(G) ≥ diam(G) + max_{v ∈ V} l(v) - 1`, where `diam(G)` is the diameter
of `G` and `l(v) = indepNeighborsCard G v` is the independence number of the
neighbourhood of `v`.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture13 (G : SimpleGraph α) (h : G.Connected) :
    letI maxL := (Finset.univ.image (fun v => indepNeighborsCard G v)).max' (by simp)
    (G.diam : ℝ) + (maxL : ℝ) - 1 ≤ b G

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 16
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 16](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, the size `b(G)` of a largest induced bipartite subgraph
satisfies `b(G) ≥ 2 * (rad(G) - 1) + max_{v ∈ V} l(v)`, where `rad(G)` is the radius
of `G` (the minimum eccentricity) and `l(v) = indepNeighborsCard G v` is the independence
number of the neighbourhood of `v`.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture16 (G : SimpleGraph α) (h : G.Connected) :
    letI maxL := (Finset.univ.image (fun v => indepNeighborsCard G v)).max' (by simp)
    letI r := G.radius.toNat
    2 * ((r : ℝ) - 1) + (maxL : ℝ) ≤ b G

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 17
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 17](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, the size `b(G)` of a largest induced bipartite subgraph
satisfies `b(G) ≥ α(G) + ⌈diam(G) / 3⌉`, where `α(G)` is the independence number of `G`
and `diam(G)` is the diameter of `G`.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture17 (G : SimpleGraph α) (h : G.Connected) :
    (G.indepNum : ℝ) + ⌈(G.diam : ℝ) / 3⌉ ≤ b G

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 18
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 18](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$, the size $b(G)$ of a largest induced bipartite
subgraph satisfies
$b(G) \ge \alpha(G) + \lceil \sqrt{\mathrm{dist}_{\max}(M)} \rceil$,
where $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number, $M$ is the set of maximum-degree
vertices, and $\mathrm{dist}_{\max}(M) = \max\{\mathrm{dist}_G(u,v) \mid u, v \in M\}$
is the maximum distance between two maximum-degree vertices (DeLaVina's
`dist_max(M)`). Proven by Benny John (Feb. 2006), generalizing Schindl's proof
of conjecture 17.

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 23
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 23](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, `b(G) ≥ ⌊α(G) + dist_avg(M) / 2⌋`, where `b(G)` is
the size of a largest induced bipartite subgraph, `α(G)` is the independence number,
`M` is the set of maximum-degree vertices, and `dist_avg(M)` is the average distance
between distinct vertices of `M`.

This conjecture is false; there is a counterexample with `b(G) = 19`, `α(G) = 15`,
and `dist_avg(M) = 10`.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture23 :
  ¬ ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected),
    let M : Set α := {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}
    ⌊(G.indepNum : ℝ) + distAvgSet G M / 2⌋ ≤ (b G : ℝ)

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 25
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 25](http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj25)
(status F, disproved):

For every finite simple connected graph $G$,
$b(G) ≥ 2⌈(1 + \min_v \operatorname{dist}_{\mathrm{even}}(v))/3⌉$,
where $b(G)$ is the size of a largest induced bipartite subgraph and
$\operatorname{dist}_{\mathrm{even}}(v)$ counts the vertices at even distance from $v$.

The nontrivial vertex type excludes graphs with fewer than two vertices.
The source gives the same counterexample as for Conjecture 24.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture25 :
    ¬ ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α],
      ∀ (G : SimpleGraph α) (_ : G.Connected),
        let minDistEven := (Finset.univ.image (distEven G)).min' (by simp)
        2 * ⌈(1 + (minDistEven : ℝ)) / 3⌉ ≤ (b G : ℝ)

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 3
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 3](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a connected simple graph `G`, the number of leaves in a maximum spanning
tree satisfies `Ls(G) ≥ G.indepDominationNumber * MaxTemp(G)`, where `G.indepDominationNumber` is the independent
domination number and `MaxTemp(G)` is `max_v deg(v)/(n(G) - deg(v))`.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture3 {G : SimpleGraph α} [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nontrivial α] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    G.indepDominationNumber * MaxTemp G ≤ Ls G

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 4
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 4](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

If `G` is a connected graph then the maximum number of leaves over all spanning
trees satisfies `Ls(G) ≥ NG(G) - 1` where `NG(G)` is the minimal neighbourhood
size of a non-edge of `G`.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture4 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] [Nontrivial α] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    NG G - 1 ≤ Ls G

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 6
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 6](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a connected graph `G` we have
`Ls(G) ≥ 1 + n(G) - m(G) - a(G)` where `a(G)` is defined via independent sets.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture6 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    1 + (Fintype.card α : ℝ) - matchingNumber G - α(G) ≤ Ls G

problems.title: Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 91
problems.statement:
WOWII [Conjecture 91](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
(disproved, 2026):

For a simple connected graph `G`,
`b(G) ≤ 1 + f(G) · ⌈avg_v l(v)⌉ / 2`
where `b(G)` is the largest induced bipartite subgraph size,
`f(G) = largestInducedForestSize G` is the largest induced forest size, and
`avg_v l(v) = l G` is the average independence number of the neighbourhoods.

Disproved by an 11-vertex counterexample (Max Talwar, 2026; graph6
`JBza_CB?wF_`) with `b(G) = 8`, `f(G) = 6` and `l G = 2`, violating
`8 ≤ 1 + 6·⌈2⌉/2 = 7`.
problems.lean:
theorem conjecture91 :
    ¬ ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α],
      ∀ (G : SimpleGraph α) (_ : G.Connected),
        b G ≤ 1 + (G.largestInducedForestSize : ℝ) * ⌈l G⌉ / 2
