problems.title: Erdős Problem 1129
problems.statement:
For $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in [-1,1]$ let
$$l_k(x)=\frac{\prod_{i\neq k}(x-x_i)}{\prod_{i\neq k}(x_k-x_i)},$$
which are such that $l_k(x_k)=1$ and $l_k(x_i)=0$ for $i\neq k$.

Describe which choice of $x_i$ minimise
$$\Lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\max_{x\in [-1,1]} \sum_k \lvert l_k(x)\rvert.$$

A problem of Bernstein [Be31] and Erdős [Er47, p. 1171], [Er67, p. 66]. They conjectured that
the minimisers are characterised by equioscillation of the Lebesgue function. This was proved by
Kilgore [Ki77], [Ki78] and by de Boor and Pinkus [dBPi78] for canonical node sets, that is, node
sets with $x_1=-1$ and $x_n=1$ (see [Ib16, Section 3.7] and [RaVa15, Proposition 2.8]); this is
`erdos_1129.variants.canonical`.

Here the minimisers range over all node sets in $[-1,1]$, as in the question. For $n\ge 3$ there
are uncountably many of them [RaVa15, Theorem 2.5] (`erdos_1129.variants.free_nodes_not_unique`):
suitable affine images of the canonical minimiser inside $[-1,1]$ are minimisers too. All of them
are described in the Lean formalisation [Ren26], which erdosproblems.com lists for this problem:
for $n\ge 2$ a node set minimises $\Lambda$ if and only if its local maxima between consecutive
nodes are all equal and both $\sum_k\lvert l_k(-1)\rvert$ and $\sum_k\lvert l_k(1)\rvert$ are at
most that common value, and for $n=1$ every node set minimises $\Lambda$. For $n=4$ all minimisers
are also given in [RaVa15, Theorem 5.2].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1129 (n : ℕ) :
    {x : Fin n → ℝ | IsMinimiser x} = erdos_1129.answer n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 360
problems.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that $\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$ can be partitioned into $f(n)$ classes so that
$n$ cannot be expressed as a sum of distinct elements from the same class. How fast does $f(n)$
grow?

A problem of Erdős and Graham [ErGr80]. Conlon, Fox, and Pham [CFP21, Theorem 1.5] determined
the order of growth of $f(n)$ up to a multiplicative constant, proving
$$f(n) \asymp \frac{n^{1/3}(n/\phi(n))}{(\log n)^{1/3}(\log\log n)^{2/3}}.$$
Here $\phi$ is Euler's totient function, and the statement is asymptotic ($n \to \infty$).

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 100 — i
problems.statement:
Is every group well-approximated by finite groups? There are really two questions here, namely
is every group sofic? and is every group hyperlinear? This is the first one: is every group sofic?

We use the characterisation of soficity in [Pe08, Theorem 3.5], see `IsSofic`. It only involves
finite subsets, so a group is sofic if all its finitely generated subgroups are. These are
countable, so it is enough to quantify over groups in `Type`.

[Gr24] lists this as open. The answer is no: OpenAI announced in 2026 that the unit group of the
binary Leavitt algebra is not sofic [Op26], and Fournier-Facio [FF26, Theorem 1.3] gives a
finitely presented torsion-free non-sofic group, using a criterion from [Op26]. Kun and Thom
[KT26] give further non-sofic groups. These results are in 2026 preprints.
problems.lean: theorem green_100.parts.i : ¬ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsSofic G

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 100 — ii
problems.statement:
Is every group well-approximated by finite groups? There are really two questions here, namely
is every group sofic? and is every group hyperlinear? This is the second one: is every group
hyperlinear?

We use the characterisation of hyperlinearity in [Pe08, Theorem 3.6], see `IsHyperlinear`, with
the normalised Hilbert–Schmidt norm. [Gr24] gives a precise form of this question with the
operator norm instead, see `green_100.variants.operator_norm`. As for `green_100.parts.i`, it is
enough to quantify over groups in `Type`.

[Gr24] lists this as open. The answer is no: Liu [Li26, Theorem 1.1] constructs a countable group,
a wreath product, that is not hyperlinear. This is a 2026 preprint.
problems.lean: theorem green_100.parts.ii : ¬ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsHyperlinear G

numbers is positive", and they first establish that the density exists at all: "It is clear that

problems.title: Erdős Problem 848
problems.statement:
Is the maximum size of a set $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never squarefree
(for all $a, b ∈ A$) achieved by taking those $n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}$?

This asks whether `Erdos848 N` holds for all $N$ (formulated using `A ⊆ Finset.range N`).

This was solved for all sufficiently large $N$ by Sawhney in this note. In fact, Sawhney proves
something slightly stronger, that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that if
$\lvert A\rvert \geq (\frac{1}{25}-c)N$ and $N$ is large then $A$ is contained in either
$\{ n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ or $\{n\equiv 18\pmod{25}\}$.

        n ^ 2 + n.choose 2 < H.edgeSet.ncard → cycleGraph 4 ⊑ H

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1013 — graver yackel
problems.statement:
Graver and Yackel [GrYa68] proved
$$h_3(k)\gg \frac{\log k}{\log\log k}k^2.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1013.variants.graver_yackel :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      c * (Real.log k / Real.log (Real.log k)) * k ^ 2 ≤ (h3 k : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1013 — lower
problems.statement:
The upper bound $f(n) \leq (2+o(1))(n/\log n)^{1/2}$ of Davies and Illingworth [DaIl22] for the
function $f$ of [1104] gives
$$\left(\frac{1}{2}-o(1)\right)k^2\log k\leq h_3(k).$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1013.variants.lower :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 / 2 - ε) * k ^ 2 * Real.log k ≤ (h3 k : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1013 — upper
problems.statement:
The lower bound $f(n) \geq (1-o(1))(n/\log n)^{1/2}$ for the function $f$ of [1104], which follows
from the construction of Hefty, Horn, King, and Pfender [HHKP25], gives
$$h_3(k) \leq (2+o(1))k^2\log k.$$
The site states $(1+o(1))k^2\log k$, but the bounds recorded in [1104] give only $2+o(1)$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1013.variants.upper :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      (h3 k : ℝ) ≤ (2 + ε) * k ^ 2 * Real.log k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1033 — erdos laskar
problems.statement:
Erdős and Laskar [ErLa85] gave a construction showing that $h(n) \leq 2(\sqrt{3}-1)n+O(1)$:
for all large $n$ there is a graph on $n$ vertices with $>n^2/4$ edges in which every triangle
has degree sum at most $2(\sqrt{3}-1)n+O(1)$. The construction is made explicit in [Fa88].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1033.variants.erdos_laskar :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), n ^ 2 < 4 * #G.edgeFinset ∧
      ∀ t, G.IsNClique 3 t → ∑ v ∈ t, (G.degree v : ℝ) ≤ 2 * (Real.sqrt 3 - 1) * n + C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1033 — fan
problems.statement:
Fan [Fa88] proved that $h(n) \geq \frac{21}{16}n$: every graph on $n$ vertices with $>n^2/4$
edges contains a triangle whose degrees sum to at least $\frac{21}{16}n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1033.variants.fan (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : n ^ 2 < 4 * #G.edgeFinset) :
    ∃ t, G.IsNClique 3 t ∧ 21 * n ≤ 16 * ∑ v ∈ t, G.degree v

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1033 — three halves
problems.statement:
In [Er82e] it is asked whether $h(n)\geq \frac{3}{2}n$. The answer is no, since the construction
of Erdős and Laskar [ErLa85] gives $h(n) \leq 2(\sqrt{3}-1)n+O(1)$ and
$2(\sqrt{3}-1) < \frac{3}{2}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1033.variants.three_halves :
    ¬ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj], n ^ 2 < 4 * #G.edgeFinset →
      ∃ t, G.IsNClique 3 t ∧ 3 * n ≤ 2 * ∑ v ∈ t, G.degree v

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1034 — k4 free
problems.statement:
Erdős suggested that the answer is different if $G$ has no $K_4$. In the comments Ma and Tang
sketch a proof that the conjecture remains false even if we assume that $G$ contains no $K_4$,
constructing a graph with $n$ vertices, $>n^2/4$ edges, and no $K_4$, in which every triangle has
at most $(2\sqrt{3}-3+o(1))n$ vertices adjacent to at least two of its vertices (note that
$2\sqrt{3}-3\approx 0.464$).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1034.variants.k4_free (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ∧
        ∀ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T → ∀ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y → (Y.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 * Real.sqrt 3 - 3 + ε) * (n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1034 — lower bound
problems.statement:
Erdős and Faudree asked about the threshold $h(n)$ such that every graph with $n$ vertices and
$>n^2/4$ edges contained a triangle and $h(n)$ other vertices which are connected to at least two
vertices of the triangle. The fact that every graph with $>n^2/4$ edges contains a book of size
$n/6$ shows that
$$(1/6-o(1))n \leq h(n).$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1034.variants.lower_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) →
        ∃ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T ∧ ∃ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y ∧ (1 / 6 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ≤ (Y.card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1034 — upper bound
problems.statement:
The construction of Ma and Tang [MaTa25] of a graph with $n$ vertices and $>n^2/4$ edges in which
every triangle has at most $(2-(5/2)^{1/2}+o(1))n$ vertices adjacent to at least two of its
vertices shows that, for the threshold $h(n)$ of `erdos_1034.variants.lower_bound`,
$$h(n) \leq (2-(5/2)^{1/2}+o(1))n.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1034.variants.upper_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 4 < (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ∧
        ∀ T : Finset (Fin n), G.IsNClique 3 T → ∀ Y : Finset (Fin n),
          JoinedToTwo G T Y → (Y.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 - Real.sqrt (5 / 2) + ε) * (n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1044 — fixed degree of le two
problems.statement:
Tang also suggests that, if the degree $n$ is fixed, then the infimum over all such $f$ of
degree $n$ is attained by $f_n(z)=z^n-1$ (and proves this for $n=1$ and $n=2$).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1047 — goodman

Goodman [Go66] proved that one of the three components of
$$\{ z: \lvert (z^2+1)(z-2)^2\rvert < 5^{3/2}/4\}$$
is not convex.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1047 — pommerenke
problems.statement:
The answer is no, as shown by Pommerenke [Po61], who showed that, if $k$ is sufficiently large,
and $f(z)=z^k(z-a)$ where $a$ is sufficiently close to $(1+\frac{1}{k})k^{\frac{1}{k+1}}$, then
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ has two components, and the component which contains $0$ is
not convex.

          ¬ Convex ℝ (connectedComponentIn (sublevelSet (X ^ k * (X - C (a : ℂ))) 1) 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1062 — lebensold bounds

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1099 — ratio sum
problems.statement:
Erdős remarks that this problem occurred to him when considering $\sum_i \frac{d_{i+1}}{d_i}$.
It is easy to see that $\sum_{i} \frac{d_{i+1}}{d_i}> \tau(n)+\log n$, and Erdős asked whether
$$\liminf \left(\sum_{i} \frac{d_{i+1}}{d_i}-\tau(n)-\log n\right)<\infty,$$
which follows from the affirmative answer to the main question.

    ∑ i : Fin (n.divisors.card - 1), ((Nat.nth (· ∣ n) (i + 1) : ℝ) / Nat.nth (· ∣ n) i) -

problems.title: Erdős Problem 11 — granville soundararajan

Suppose that every odd $n > 1$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2. Then the set of
primes $p$ such that $2^p \not\equiv 2 \pmod{p^2}$ (the non-Wieferich primes) is infinite.
This follows from Theorem 1 in [GrSo98].
[GrSo98] Granville, A. and Soundararajan, K., A Binary Additive Problem of Erdős and the Order of $2$ mod $p^2$. The Ramanujan Journal (1998), 283-298.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1121 — higher dimension

The proof of Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] also generalises to higher dimensions: if
$B_1,\ldots,B_n$ are balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no hyperplane
disjoint from all the balls divides them into two non-empty sets then the balls can be covered by
a ball of radius $r=\sum r_i$.

problems.title: Mertens' third theorem

**Mertens' third theorem** [Me1874], in the weakened form the linked proof assumes: the product
over the primes up to $n$ of $1 - 1/p$ is at least $1/(3\log n)$.

the theorem and is what the deduction needs.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 12 — baier
problems.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of natural numbers with the property that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such
that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. If all elements in $A$ are pairwise coprime then
$$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \ll N^{2/3}/\log N$$
for infinitely many $N$.

    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),

Given any function $f(x)\to \infty$ as $x\to \infty$ there exists a set $A$ with the property
that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$, such that there are
infinitely many $N$ such that $$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert > \frac{N}{f(N)}.

    ∃ A, IsGood A ∧ {N : ℕ | (N : ℝ) / f N < (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard}.Infinite

property `P₁`. Sattler [Sa82] credits this observation to Erdős, who presumably found this after
[ErGr80]. The element `0` is not counted, since `P₁` ignores it, and the infinitude hypothesis
excludes degenerate sets such as `{2}`, on which `P₁` holds vacuously.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 321 — upper
problems.statement:
Let $R(N)$ be the maximal such size. Results of Bleicher and Erdős from [BlEr75] and [BlEr76b] imply that
$$
R(N) \le \frac{1}{\log 2} \log_r N \left( \frac{N}{\log N} \prod_{i=3}^{r} \log_i N \right),
$$
valid for any $k \ge 4$ with $\log_k N \ge k$ and any $r \ge 1$ with $\log_{2r} N \ge 1$. (In these bounds $\log_i n$ denotes the $i$-fold iterated logarithm.)

Since `Real.log` is defined on all of $\mathbb{R}$, the condition $\log_{2r} N \ge 1$ is
formalised as $\log_i N \ge 1$ for all $i \le 2r$, which is equivalent to it for the
genuine iterated logarithm and ensures that every intermediate iterate is positive.

[BlEr75] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., _The number of distinct subsums of $\sum_{1}^{N}\,1/i$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 29-42.
[BlEr76b] Bleicher, Michael N. and Erdős, Paul, _Denominators of Egyptian fractions. II_. Illinois J. Math. (1976), 598-613.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_321.variants.upper (N r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrN : ∀ i ≤ 2 * r, 1 ≤ log^[i] N) :
    R N ≤ 1 / log 2 * log^[r] N * N / log N * ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 3 r, (log^[i] N)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 326 — eq
problems.statement:
Erdős originally asked this for any basis (not necessarily minimal); such a basis was constructed
by Cassels [Ca57].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_326.variants.eq :
    ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ) (_ : StrictMono a) (_ : Set.range a |>.IsAddBasisOfOrder 2) (x : ℝ) (_ : 0 < x),
      Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a n : ℝ) / n ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 x)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 331 — ruzsa
problems.statement:
Ruzsa suggests that a non-trivial variant of this problem arises if one imposes the stronger
condition that $|A \cap \{1,\dots,N\}| \sim c_A N^{1/2}$ for some constant $c_A>0$, and similarly
for $B$.

The answer is yes. Write $A(N) = |A \cap \{1,\dots,N\}|$ and $B(N) = |B \cap \{1,\dots,N\}|$.
Erdős and Freud [ErFr84, Theorem 4] proved that if $a_1 - a_2 = b_1 - b_2$ has only trivial
solutions and $\liminf_N \min(A(N), B(N)) / N^{1/2} > 0$, then neither $A(N) / N^{1/2}$ nor
$B(N) / N^{1/2}$ tends to a limit. If there were only finitely many non-trivial solutions, removing
the finitely many elements of $A$ that occur in them would give sets with the same asymptotics and
no non-trivial solution.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_331.variants.ruzsa :
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ,
    (∃ c_A > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count (· ∈ A) n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ c_A * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))) →
    (∃ c_B > 0, (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (count (· ∈ B) n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ c_B * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))) →
    { s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | let ⟨a₁, a₂, b₁, b₂⟩ := s
      a₁ ∈ A ∧ a₂ ∈ A ∧ b₁ ∈ B ∧ b₂ ∈ B ∧
      a₁ ≠ a₂ ∧ a₁ + b₂ = a₂ + b₁ }.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 346 — example
problems.statement:
Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] also say that it is not hard to construct very irregular sequences
satisfying the aforementioned properties: there is a strictly increasing sequence `A` that is
strongly complete and not complete whenever infinitely many terms are removed from it, but with
$\liminf_n A(n+1)/A(n) = 1$ and $\limsup_n A(n+1)/A(n) = \infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_346.variants.example : ∃ A : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono A ∧ IsAddStronglyCompleteNatSeq A ∧
    (∀ B : Set ℕ, B ⊆ range A → B.Infinite → ¬ IsAddComplete (range A \ B)) ∧
    liminf (fun n => A (n + 1) / (A n : ℝ)) atTop = 1 ∧
    limsup (fun n => A (n + 1) / (A n : ENNReal)) atTop = ⊤

problems.title: Erdős Problem 357 — hegyvari
problems.statement:
Let $g(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1, \dotsc, a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. Hegyvári [He86] proved
that
$$\left(\frac 1 3 + o(1) \right)n \leq g(n) \leq \left(\frac 2 3 + o(1) \right)n.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_357.variants.hegyvari : ∃ (o o' : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    o' =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (g n : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc ((1 / 3 + o n) * n) ((2 / 3 + o' n)*n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 357 — infinite set lower density
problems.statement:
Suppose $A$ is an infinite set such that all finite sums of consecutive terms of $A$ are distinct.
Then $A$ has lower density 0.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_357.variants.infinite_set_lower_density (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : StrictMono A)
    (hA : HasDistinctSums A) : (Set.range A).lowerDensity = 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 387 — guy
problems.statement:
Is it true for any $c < 1$ and all $n$ sufficiently large, for all $1 \leq k < n$,
$\binom{n}{k}$ has a divisor in $(cn, n]$?

This variant appears in [Gu04]. Bui, Naprienko, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BNPZ26] answered it
negatively.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_387.variants.guy : ¬ ∀ c : ℝ, c < 1 → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k →
    k < n → ∃ d : ℕ, (d : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ioc (c * n) n ∧ d ∣ n.choose k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 400 — upper bound
problems.statement:
Erdős and Graham write that it is easy to show that $g_k(n) \ll_k \log n$ always, but the best
possible constant is unknown.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_400.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2) :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (g k n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 477 — degree two dvd condition b ne zero
problems.statement:
There is no such $A$ for any polynomial $f(x) = aX^2 + bX + c$, if $a | b$
with $a \ne 0$ and $b \ne 0$.
This was found be AlphaProof for the specific instance $X^2 - X + 1$ and then generalised.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_477.variants.degree_two_dvd_condition_b_ne_zero {a b c : ℤ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0)
    (hab : a ∣ b) :
    let f := a • X ^ 2 + b • X + C c
    ∀ A : Set ℤ, ∃ z, ¬ ∃! a ∈ A ×ˢ (Set.range f.eval), z = a.1 + a.2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 482 — stoll explicit
problems.statement:
The explicit base-$g$ construction in Stoll [St05, Theorem 1.3]. For a normalized
$t \in [1,g)$, take $a = g/((g-1)(t+g))$ and $b = (g-1)(t+g)$. Every parameter
$-1/g \le \varepsilon < (g+1)(g-2)/g$ gives the same significant digits of $t$.

The sequence is indexed from zero, so the difference at $2n+2$ and $2n$ gives digit $n$,
including the leading digit at $n=0$. The floor difference uses the terminating expansion
when $t$ has two base-$g$ expansions.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_482.variants.stoll_explicit (g : ℕ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (t : ℝ)
    (ht : 1 ≤ t) (htg : t < g) (ε : ℝ)
    (hεlo : -1 / (g : ℝ) ≤ ε)
    (hεhi : ε < ((g : ℝ) + 1) * ((g : ℝ) - 2) / g) :
    let a := (g : ℝ) / (((g : ℝ) - 1) * (t + g))
    let b := ((g : ℝ) - 1) * (t + g)
    ∀ n : ℕ,
      generalRecurrence g a b ε (2 * n + 2) -
          (g : ℤ) * generalRecurrence g a b ε (2 * n) =
        ⌊t * (g : ℝ) ^ n⌋ - (g : ℤ) * ⌊t * (g : ℝ) ^ n / g⌋

problems.title: Gladysz (1962) [Gl62]: independent set of size 2 in the closed case.
problems.statement:
**Gladysz (1962) [Gl62]: independent set of size 2 in the closed case.**

If all the sets `A x` are closed with Lebesgue measure `< 1`, then there exist two
distinct reals `x y` such that `x ∉ A y` and `y ∉ A x`.

This is a weaker result proved by Gladysz before the full Newelski–Pawlikowski–
Seredyński theorem [NPS87].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_501.variants.gladysz_size2 :
    ∀ (A : ℝ → Set ℝ),
      (∀ x, IsClosed (A x)) →
      (∀ x, volume (A x) < 1) →
      ∃ X : Set ℝ, 2 ≤ X.ncard ∧ X.Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 501 — hechler CH
problems.statement:
**Hechler (1972) [He72]: the answer to the main question is NO, assuming the continuum
hypothesis.**

Assuming CH (`ℵ₁ = 𝔠`), there exists a family `A : ℝ → Set ℝ` of bounded sets with
Lebesgue outer measure `< 1` for which no infinite independent set exists.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_501.variants.hechler_CH :
    (ℵ₁ = 𝔠) →
    ∃ (A : ℝ → Set ℝ),
      (∀ x, Bornology.IsBounded (A x)) ∧
      (∀ x, volume.toOuterMeasure (A x) < 1) ∧
      ¬ ∃ X : Set ℝ, X.Infinite ∧ X.Pairwise (fun x y => x ∉ A y)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 503 — R2
problems.statement:
When $n = 2$, the answer is 6 (due to Kelly [ErKe47] - an alternative proof is given by Kovács [Ko24c]).

[ErKe47] Erdős, Paul and Kelly, L. M., Elementary Problems and Solutions: Solutions: E735. Amer. Math. Monthly (1947), 227-229.
[Ko24c] Z. Kovács, A note on Erdős's mysterious remark. arXiv:2412.05190 (2024).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_503.variants.R2 :
    IsGreatest {(A.ncard) | (A : Set ℝ²) (hA : A.IsIsosceles)} 6

problems.title: Erdős Problem 503 — R3
problems.statement:
When $n = 3$, the answer is 8 (due to Croft [Cr62]).

[Cr62] Croft, H. T., $9$-point and $7$-point configurations in $3$-space. Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1962), 400-424.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_503.variants.R3 :
    IsGreatest {(A.ncard) | (A : Set ℝ³) (hA : A.IsIsosceles)} 8

problems.title: Erdős Problem 503 — lower bound
problems.statement:
Alweiss has observed a lower bound of $\binom{n + 1}{2}$ follows from considering the subset of
$\mathbb{R}^{n + 1}$ formed of all vectors $e_i + e_j$ where $e_i$, $e_j$ are distinct coordinate
vectors. This set can be viewed as a subset of some $\mathbb{R}^n$, and is easily checked to have
the required property.

The bound is stated as the existence of such a set and not as a bound on the `sSup` of the sizes:
in `ℕ` the `sSup` of an unbounded set is `0`, so the latter would also assert that the sizes are
bounded, which is the content of `erdos_503.variants.upper_bound`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_503.variants.lower_bound (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ m ∈ {(A.ncard) | (A : Set (ℝ^n)) (hA : A.IsIsosceles)}, (n + 1).choose 2 ≤ m

problems.title: Erdős Problem 503 — upper bound
problems.statement:
The best upper bound known in general is due to Blokhius [Bl84] who showed that
$$
|A| \leq \binom{n + 2}{2}
$$

[Bl84] Blokhuis, A., Few-distance sets. (1984), iv+70.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_503.variants.upper_bound (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ m ∈ {(A.ncard) | (A : Set (ℝ^n)) (hA : A.IsIsosceles)}, m ≤ (n + 2).choose 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 — delta four eq zero
problems.statement:
The contrasting positive result $\delta_3(4) = 0$ of Erdős, Hajnal, Simonovits, Sós, and
Szemerédi [EHSSS94]: the $K_4$ analogue of `erdos_533` is **true**. For every $\delta > 0$
there is a $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_4$-free graph $G$ on
$n$ vertices with at least $\delta n^2$ edges contains a triangle-free vertex set of size at
least $c n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_533.variants.delta_four_eq_zero :
    ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 →
        δ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
          ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), c * n ≤ (S.card : ℝ) ∧
            G.CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 — delta seven ge quarter
problems.statement:
The observation $\delta_3(7) \geq 1/4$ of Erdős, Hajnal, Simonovits, Sós, and Szemerédi
[EHSSS94], via a construction of Erdős and Rogers [ErRo62]: for every $\epsilon, \delta > 0$
and all sufficiently large $n$ there is a $K_7$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which every
triangle-free vertex set has at most $\delta n$ vertices, yet which has at least
$(1/4 - \epsilon)n^2$ edges.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_533.variants.delta_seven_ge_quarter (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 7 ∧
        (∀ S : Finset (Fin n),
            G.CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3 → (S.card : ℝ) ≤ δ * n) ∧
        (1 / 4 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 — ehsss upper
problems.statement:
The upper bound $\delta_3(5) \leq 1/12$ of Erdős, Hajnal, Simonovits, Sós, and Szemerédi
[EHSSS94]: for every $\epsilon > 0$ there is a $\delta > 0$ such that for all sufficiently
large $n$, every $K_5$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which every triangle-free vertex
set has at most $\delta n$ vertices has at most $(1/12 + \epsilon)n^2$ edges.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_533.variants.ehsss_upper (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 5 →
        (∀ S : Finset (Fin n),
            G.CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3 → (S.card : ℝ) ≤ δ * n) →
          (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 / 12 + ε) * n ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 533 — lrss lower
problems.statement:
The matching lower bound $\delta_3(5) \geq 1/12$, from the construction of Liu, Reiher,
Sharifzadeh, and Staden [LRSS21] (improving the earlier $\delta_3(5) > 0$ of Balogh and Lenz
[BaLe13]): for every $\epsilon, \delta > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$ there is a
$K_5$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in which every triangle-free vertex set has at most
$\delta n$ vertices, yet which has at least $(1/12 - \epsilon)n^2$ edges. In particular this
refutes `erdos_533`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_533.variants.lrss_lower (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 5 ∧
        (∀ S : Finset (Fin n),
            G.CliqueFreeOn (S : Set (Fin n)) 3 → (S.card : ℝ) ≤ δ * n) ∧
        (1 / 12 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 — sunflower erdos rado
problems.statement:
For the stronger $Ω(n)=k$ variant above, the Erdős–Rado method gives the weaker
bound $c_r^k \cdot k!$; see Erdős [Er73].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_535.variants.sunflower_erdos_rado {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) :
    ∃ c_r > (0 : ℝ),
      ∀ k : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℕ,
        AllBigOmega k A →
        NoConstantPairwiseGcdCoprimeSubsets r A →
        (A.card : ℝ) ≤ c_r ^ k * (Nat.factorial k)

problems.title: Menger's theorem for infinite graphs
problems.statement:
**Menger's theorem for infinite graphs** (Aharoni–Berger [AhBe09]).

The theorem actually proved by Aharoni and Berger holds for arbitrary vertex sets $A$
and $B$: in any (possibly infinite) graph $G$ there is a family $P$ of pairwise
vertex-disjoint $A$--$B$ paths together with an $A$--$B$ separator $S$ consisting of the
choice of exactly one vertex from each path in $P$. The disjointness and independence
hypotheses of `erdos_599` are not needed.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_599.variants.aharoni_berger :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V) (A B : Set V),
      ∃ (ι : Type) (a b : ι → V) (p : ∀ i, G.Walk (a i) (b i)) (S : Set V),
        (∀ i, a i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, b i ∈ B) ∧ (∀ i, (p i).IsPath) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint {v | v ∈ (p i).support} {v | v ∈ (p j).support}) ∧
        S ⊆ {v | ∃ i, v ∈ (p i).support} ∧
        (∀ i, ∃! v, v ∈ S ∧ v ∈ (p i).support) ∧
        (∀ a' ∈ A, ∀ b' ∈ B, ∀ q : G.Walk a' b', q.IsPath → ∃ v ∈ q.support, v ∈ S)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 670 — dim one
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er97f] proved the claim when $d = 1$: if $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a set of $n$ points
such that all pairwise distances differ by at least $1$, then the diameter of $A$ is at least
$(1+o(1))n^2$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_670.variants.dim_one :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)), A.card = n → HasSeparatedDistances A →
        (1 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ Metric.diam (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 670 — uniform in dim
problems.statement:
The version of the problem where the $o(1)$ term must be uniform in the dimension $d$ has a
negative answer. This follows from `Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.ho` (Ho [Ho26]).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_670.variants.uniform_in_dim :
    ¬ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ d : ℕ,
      ∀ A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), A.card = n → HasSeparatedDistances A →
        (1 - ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ Metric.diam (A : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 675 — brun
problems.statement:
Let $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a set of pairwise coprime integers with
$$\sum_{b \in B,\ b < x} \frac{1}{b} = o(\log \log x).$$
Then $A = \{n : b \nmid n \text{ for all } b \in B\}$ has the translation property.
As remarked on erdosproblems.com, this follows from Brun's sieve, and Erdős did not know what
happens if the condition on the sum is weakened or dropped.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_675.variants.brun (B : Set ℕ) (hB : B.Pairwise Nat.Coprime)
    (hsum : (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ b ∈ Finset.range x with b ∈ B, (1 : ℝ) / (b : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      fun x : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ))) :
    HasTranslationProperty {n : ℕ | ∀ b ∈ B, ¬ b ∣ n}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 690 — large k
problems.statement:
Is $d_k(p)$ unimodular for any $k\geq 21$?

The answer is no: $d_k(p)$ is not unimodal for any $k \geq 4$ [WC26] (arXiv preprint).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_690.variants.large_k :
    ¬ ∃ k ≥ 21, ∀ d : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ p, p.Prime → (kthPrimeFactorSet k p).HasDensity (d p)) → IsUnimodalOnPrimes d

problems.title: Erdős Problem 694 — inf unique
problems.statement:
Erdős has proved that if there exists an integer $n$ for which $\phi(m) = n$ has
exactly one solution, then there must be infinitely many such $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_694.variants.inf_unique (h : ∃ n > 0, ∃! m, Nat.totient m = n) :
    { n | ∃! m, Nat.totient m = n }.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 731 — egrs75
problems.statement:
A problem of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75], who say it is 'not hard to show that',
for almost all $n$, the minimal such $m$ satisfies
$$m=\exp((\log n)^{1/2+o(1)}).$$

[EGRS75, (8), p. 91] states this as: for every $\varepsilon>0$, for all $n$ outside a set of
density $0$, $\exp((\log n)^{1/2-\varepsilon}) < m < \exp((\log n)^{1/2+\varepsilon})$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_731.variants.egrs75 : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ),
    {n : ℕ | Real.exp (Real.log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - ε)) < (leastNonDivisor n : ℝ) ∧
      (leastNonDivisor n : ℝ) < Real.exp (Real.log n ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 + ε))}.HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 — chen fang
problems.statement:
Chen and Fang [ChFa15, Theorem 0.2] proved that for any $M > 1$,
$$A(x)B(x) - x \ge \min(A(x), B(x))^M$$
for all sufficiently large $x$. In particular $A(x)B(x)-x\ll A(x)^c$ cannot hold for any constant
$c>0$ when $A$ is the sparser of the two sets.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 < M) :
    ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
      (min (counting A x) (counting B x) : ℝ) ^ M ≤
        (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 — chen fang limsup
problems.statement:
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsAdditiveComplement A B)
    (hlim : limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
      < ((3 - Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : EReal)) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 — chen fang sharp
problems.statement:
This is sharp, as Chen and Fang [ChFa11] also proved that there exist such $A$ and $B$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{3}{2}$$
for which $A(x)B(x)-x=1$ for infinitely many $x$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          = ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 — ruzsa lower bound
problems.statement:
Ruzsa [Ru17, Theorem 1.2] proves that, if $a^*(x)=\max A \cap [1,x]$, $A$ and $B$ satisfy the
conditions in the problem, and $A$ is the sparser set with $A(2x)/A(x) \to 1$ (which holds after
possibly swapping the roles of $A$ and $B$ by Narkiewicz's theorem), then
$$A(x)B(x)-x > (1-o(1))\frac{a^*(x)}{A(x)}.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (hA₀ : 0 ∉ A) (hB₀ : 0 ∉ B) (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B)

[ChFa15, Theorem 0.2] (for instance, taking $M = 2$).

problems.title: Jaeger's reformulation: normal `5`-edge-colourings.
problems.statement:
**Jaeger's reformulation: normal `5`-edge-colourings.**

A proper `5`-edge-colouring of a cubic graph is *normal* if every edge, together with its four
neighbouring edges, sees either exactly `3` or exactly `5` colours. Jaeger showed that a cubic
graph has a Petersen colouring iff it has a normal `5`-edge-colouring.

*Reference:* [Ja88].
problems.lean:
theorem petersen_coloring_conjecture.variants.normal_five_edge_coloring
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hcubic : ∀ v, G.degree v = 3) :
    (∃ φ : Sym2 V → Sym2 PetersenVertex, IsPetersenColoring G φ) ↔
    ∃ c : Sym2 V → Fin 5,
      (∀ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, ∀ f ∈ G.edgeFinset, e ≠ f → (∃ v, v ∈ e ∧ v ∈ f) → c e ≠ c f) ∧
      ∀ e ∈ G.edgeFinset,
        ((G.edgeFinset.filter fun f => ∃ v, v ∈ e ∧ v ∈ f).image c).card = 3 ∨
        ((G.edgeFinset.filter fun f => ∃ v, v ∈ e ∧ v ∈ f).image c).card = 5

problems.statement:
**The even case (Bryant–Horsley–Pettersson 2014).**

For even $n$, the complete graph minus a perfect matching, $K_n - I$, decomposes into cycles of
lengths $m_1, \dots, m_t$ whenever $3 \le m_i \le n$ and $\sum m_i = \binom{n}{2} - n/2$.
Since Mathlib has no canonical perfect matching of $K_n$, we state this for any perfect
matching `I`.

*Reference:* [BHP14].

    (m : Multiset ℕ) (hm : ∀ x ∈ m, 3 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ n) (hsum : m.sum = n.choose 2 - n / 2) :
    ∃ C : Multiset (Cycle (completeGraph (Fin n) \ I.spanningCoe)),
      IsCycleDecomposition (completeGraph (Fin n) \ I.spanningCoe) C ∧ lengths C = m

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Simultaneously Small Entropies — temur
problems.statement:
Temur [Tem26], Theorem 1. There is an irrational $\xi \in (0, 1)$ all of whose partial quotients
are $1$ or $2$, such that
$$\lVert b^k \xi \rVert > 154^{-2^b} \quad (b \ge 2,\ k \ge 0),$$
where $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ denotes the distance to the nearest integer. The bound on the partial
quotients gives $E(\xi) \le (\log 2) / 4$, and the displayed inequality forces the base $b$
expansion of $\xi$ to omit a block of zeros, which gives $E(\xi, b) < \log b$ for every
$b \ge 2$. Temur's $\xi$ is moreover computable.

    ∃ ξ : ℝ, Irrational ξ ∧ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, partQuot ξ n = 1 ∨ partQuot ξ n = 2) ∧
      (∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → ∀ k : ℕ,
        (154 : ℝ) ^ (-(2 ^ b) : ℤ) < distToNearestInt ((b : ℝ) ^ k * ξ)) ∧
      cfEntropy ξ ≤ ((Real.log 2 / 4 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → baseEntropy b ξ < (Real.log b : EReal)

arbitrarily small for sufficiently large $H$ and $N$. Because `∀ᶠ H, ∀ᶠ N` lets the threshold for

problems.statement:
Kesten [Ke60] proved that if $f(\alpha,\beta,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{\beta+\alpha k\})$ then $f(\alpha,\beta,n)$ has asymptotic distribution function
$g(c)=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\rho c}\frac{1}{1+t^2}\mathrm{d}t$, where $\rho>0$ is an explicit
constant.

    ∃ ρ > 0,
      let g := fun (c : ℝ) ↦ (1 / π) * ∫ t in Iic (ρ * c), 1 / (1 + t^2)
      ∀ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun (n : ℕ) ↦
        (volume { p : ℝ × ℝ | let ⟨α, β⟩ := p; α ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ β ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧
          (1 / log n) * ∑ k ∈ Icc (1 : ℕ) n, (1 / 2 - Int.fract (β + α * k)) ≤ c }).toReal)
        atTop (𝓝 (g c))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1003 — eps87
problems.statement:
Erdős, Pomerance, and Sárközy [EPS87] proved that for all large $x$, the number
of $n \leq x$ with $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$ is at most $$\frac{x}{\exp((\log x)^{1/3})}$$.

[EPS87] Erd\H os, Paul and Pomerance, Carl and S\'ark\"ozy, Andr\'as, _On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions_. {II}. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1003.variants.eps87 :  ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
    {(n : ℕ) | (n ≤ x) ∧ φ n = φ (n + 1)}.ncard ≤
      x / Real.exp ((x.log) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1004 — le of isDistinctTotientRun
problems.statement:
Erdős, Pomerance, and Sárközy [EPS87] proved that if φ(n+k) are all distinct for 1 ≤ k ≤ K then
K ≤ n / exp(c (log n)^{1/3}) for some constant c > 0.
Here we state the existence of such a constant c.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1004.variants.le_of_isDistinctTotientRun :
    ∃ (c : ℝ) (hc : c > 0),
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ (K : ℕ), IsDistinctTotientRun n K →
        (K : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) / Real.exp (c * (Real.log n) ^ (1/3 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1008 — lower bound
problems.statement: In [Er71] Erdős revises the conjecture to $m^{2/3}$, and notes $\gg m^{1/2}$ is trivial.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1008 — three quarters
problems.statement:
Originally asked by Bollobás and Erdős in 'a colloquium on graph theory at Tihany' with $m^{2/3}$
replaced by $m^{3/4}$. Folkman showed this is false with the counterexample $K_{n,n^2}$, which has
$n^3$ edges, and yet every subgraph with $>n^2+\binom{n}{2}$ edges contains a $C_4$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1008.variants.three_quarters :
    ¬ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1009 — sauer
problems.statement:
Sauer gave an example of a graph on $n$ vertices with $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+2n-6$ many edges
which contains only $2n-7$ many edge disjoint triangles: if $n=2r+4$ then $G$ is the complete
tripartite graph on $[r]\times [r]\times [4]$, with a $K_4$ on the $[4]$ vertices also.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1009.variants.sauer : ∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * r + 4)),
    G.edgeSet.ncard = (2 * r + 4) ^ 2 / 4 + 2 * (2 * r + 4) - 6 ∧
      ∀ T : Finset (Finset (Fin (2 * r + 4))), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) →
        (T : Set (Finset (Fin (2 * r + 4)))).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) →
          T.card ≤ 2 * (2 * r + 4) - 7

problems.statement:

Erdős originally conjectured, in this language, that $c_2=1$, which he reports in [Er71] was

This is false, and $c_t<2$ for all $t$: a counterexample is provided by Wood [Wo13b], who
constructs, for any $r\geq 2$, a triangle-free $2$-degenerate $r$-uniform hypergraph with

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1023 — erdos kleitman
problems.statement:
Erdős and Kleitman proved in unpublished work that
$$F(n)\asymp \frac{2^n}{n^{1/2}}.$$
([Er71] has an exponent of $3/2$, but this is presumably a typo.)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1032 — simonovits toft
problems.statement:
Simonovits [Si72] and Toft [To72] independently constructed $4$-chromatic critical graphs with
minimum degree $\gg n^{1/3}$.

We state this as in [Ma15, Problem 5.1]: there are $4$-critical graphs on $n$ vertices with minimum
degree at least $c n^{1/3}$ for infinitely many $n$, for a fixed constant $c > 0$.

    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1036 — alon hajnal
problems.statement:
Alon and Hajnal [AlHa91] proved that $G$ must contain at least
$$\exp\left(n(\log n)^{-O(\log\log n)}\right)$$
many non-isomorphic induced subgraphs.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1036 — erdos hajnal
problems.statement:
Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa89b] proved that if neither $G$ nor its complement contains a balanced
complete bipartite graph $K_{k,k}$ on more than $c\log n$ vertices (as a not necessarily induced
subgraph) then $G$ contains at least $2^{\Omega_c(n)}$ many non-isomorphic induced subgraphs.

      NoLargeBiclique G (c * Real.log (n : ℝ)) →

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1042 — chebyshev segment
problems.statement:
Ghosh and Ramachandran [GhRa24, Example 2.7] note that for $F=[-2,2]\subset\mathbb{C}$ (a closed
set of transfinite diameter $1$ which is not contained in any closed disc of radius $1$) the
monic Chebyshev polynomial $f_n(z)=2T_n(z/2)$ has all its roots in $F$ and all its $n-1$ critical
values equal to $\pm 2$, so $\{\lvert f_n\rvert<1\}$ has exactly $n$ components, for every
$n\ge 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1042.variants.chebyshev_segment (F : Set ℂ)
    (hF : F = Complex.ofReal '' Set.Icc (-2 : ℝ) 2) :
    IsClosed F ∧ transfiniteDiameter F = 1 ∧ (∀ c : ℂ, ¬ F ⊆ Metric.closedBall c 1) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ f : ℂ[X], MonicWithRootsIn F n f ∧ numComponents f = n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1042 — connected le quarter
problems.statement:
If $d\leq 1/4$ and $F$ is connected then the set has only one connected component.

This is [GhRa24, Theorem 2.1(c)]: if the logarithmic capacity of the compact connected set $K$ is
at most $1/4$ then $\{\lvert f\rvert<1\}$ is connected for every monic $f$ with all roots in $K$.
We take the degree $n\ge 1$ (for $n=0$ the set is empty) and, as in [GhRa24], positive capacity.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1042.variants.connected_le_quarter (F : Set ℂ) (hF : IsClosed F)
    (hconn : IsConnected F) (h₀ : 0 < transfiniteDiameter F) (hd : transfiniteDiameter F ≤ 1 / 4)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (f : ℂ[X]) (hf : MonicWithRootsIn F n f) :
    numComponents f = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1043 — weak

Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain an infinitely edge-connected subgraph

A theorem of de Bruijn and Erdős [dBEr51] implies that, if $G$ has infinite chromatic number,

problems.statement:
Lambie-Hanson's quantitative theorem [La20, Theorem A], of which `erdos_110` is a consequence:
for every $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ there is a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such
that, for every $k \geq 3$, every finite subgraph with fewer than $f(k)$ vertices has chromatic
number less than $k$. (The graph constructed in [La20] has $2^{\aleph_1}$ vertices.)

There is equality $\tau_\perp(n)=\omega(n)$ for infinitely many $n$: Erdős and Hall [ErHa78, p. 480]

exist for every $k$, which we state.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1100 — erdos hall

Erdős and Hall [ErHa78, Theorem 1, p. 480] prove, for all $\epsilon>0$ and sufficiently large $x$,
$$\max_{n<x} \tau_\perp(n) > \exp((\log\log x)^{2-\epsilon}).$$
We write the maximum as: some $n<x$ has $\tau_\perp(n)$ above the bound.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.erdos_hall : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
    ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) < x ∧ Real.exp (Real.log (Real.log x) ^ (2 - ε)) < (tauPerp n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1100 — erdos simonovits
problems.statement:
Erdős and Simonovits (see [Er81h, p. 173]) proved
$$(2^{1/2}+o(1))^k < g(k) < (2-c)^k$$
for some constant $c>0$. We write the lower bound as: every fixed $0\leq r<\sqrt2$ satisfies
$r^k<g(k)$ for all large $k$, and the upper bound for all large $k$.

[Er81h] announces this without proof, and [ErTe89, p. 291] calls the argument of Erdős and
Simonovits for squarefree $n$, which it uses for the upper bound, unpublished. The upper bound also
follows from `erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_g`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.erdos_simonovits :
    (∀ r : ℝ, 0 ≤ r → r < Real.sqrt 2 → ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, r ^ k < (g k : ℝ)) ∧
      ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, (g k : ℝ) < (2 - c) ^ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1100 — erdos tenenbaum g
problems.statement:
For squarefree $n$ with $\omega(n)=k$ the bound $f(n)\leq 3\tau(n)B_1^{\omega_1(n)}$ of
[ErTe89, Theorem 1, (1.3), p. 287], with $B_1=3\cdot 2^{-5/3}$, gives
$$g(k)\leq 3\left(3\cdot 2^{-2/3}\right)^k,$$
and $3\cdot 2^{-2/3}=1.88988\ldots<2$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_g (k : ℕ) :
    (g k : ℝ) ≤ 3 * (3 / (2 : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)) ^ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1100 — erdos tenenbaum max
problems.statement:
Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe89, Theorem 4, p. 289] improved this considerably: for $x\geq 3$,
$$\max_{n\leq x}\tau_\perp(n)\geq \exp\Bigl(\bigl((\log 2)^2+o(1)\bigr)
\frac{\log x}{(\log\log x)^2}\Bigr).$$
We write $o(1)$ as an arbitrarily small $\delta>0$ and the maximum as: some $n\leq x$ has
$\tau_\perp(n)$ above the bound.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.erdos_tenenbaum_max : ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
    ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) ≤ x ∧
      Real.exp (((Real.log 2) ^ 2 - δ) * Real.log x / (Real.log (Real.log x)) ^ 2) ≤
        (tauPerp n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1100 — normal order
problems.statement:
Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe89, Corollary 2, p. 288] proved that for almost all $n$ (that is, on a set
of density $1$)
$$(\log n)^{\log 3-1+o(1)}\leq \tau_\perp(n)\leq (\log n)^{\log 2-1/2+o(1)}.$$
The paper credits the upper bound to an earlier work of the same authors (Bull. Soc. Math. France
111 (1983)). We write $o(1)$ as: for every $\epsilon>0$ the set of $n$ with
both bounds, with exponents shifted by $\mp\epsilon$, has density $1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1100.variants.normal_order : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    {n : ℕ | Real.log n ^ (Real.log 3 - 1 - ε) ≤ (tauPerp n : ℝ) ∧
      (tauPerp n : ℝ) ≤ Real.log n ^ (Real.log 2 - 1 / 2 + ε)}.HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1111 — el zahar erdos
problems.statement: El-Zahar and Erdős [ElEr85] proved the case $c = 3$: $d(t,3)$ exists for every $t$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1111.variants.el_zahar_erdos :
    ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧
      ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        (d : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → G.CliqueFree t →
          ∃ A B : Set V, Anticomplete G A B ∧
            3 ≤ (G.induce A).chromaticNumber ∧ 3 ≤ (G.induce B).chromaticNumber

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1111 — nguyen scott seymour
problems.statement:
Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [NSS24] prove that if $t,c\geq 1$ then there exists $d\geq 1$ such
that if $\chi(G)\geq d$ and $\omega(G)<t$ then there are anticomplete sets $A,B$ with
$\chi(B)\geq c$ and such that the minimum degree of the induced graph on $A$ is at least $c$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1111.variants.nguyen_scott_seymour :
    ∀ t c : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → 1 ≤ c → ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧
      ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        (d : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → G.CliqueFree t →
          ∃ A B : Set V, Anticomplete G A B ∧
            A.Nonempty ∧ (∀ v ∈ A, c ≤ (A ∩ G.neighborSet v).ncard) ∧
            (c : ℕ∞) ≤ (G.induce B).chromaticNumber

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1111 — three three
problems.statement: El-Zahar and Erdős [ElEr85] proved $d(3,3)\leq 8$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1111.variants.three_three :
    ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      8 ≤ G.chromaticNumber → G.CliqueFree 3 →
        ∃ A B : Set V, Anticomplete G A B ∧
          3 ≤ (G.induce A).chromaticNumber ∧ 3 ≤ (G.induce B).chromaticNumber

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1129 — four nodes
problems.statement:
For $n=4$ the canonical minimiser is $-1,-t,t,1$, where $t>0$ is the (unique positive) root of
$25t^6+17t^4+2t^2-1$, so $t\approx 0.4178$, and
$\Lambda=\frac{1+t^2}{1-t^2}\approx 1.4229$ [RaVa15, Section 3, (3.4)-(3.9)].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1129.variants.four_nodes (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (hroot : 25 * t ^ 6 + 17 * t ^ 4 + 2 * t ^ 2 - 1 = 0) :
    {x : Fin 4 → ℝ | IsCanonical x ∧ IsMinimiser x} =
        ({![(-1 : ℝ), -t, t, 1]} : Set (Fin 4 → ℝ)) ∧
      lebesgueConstant (![(-1 : ℝ), -t, t, 1] : Fin 4 → ℝ) = (1 + t ^ 2) / (1 - t ^ 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1130 — canonical
problems.statement:
The theorem of Kilgore [Ki77], [Ki78] and de Boor and Pinkus [dBPi78] in the form of
[Ib16, Section 3.7]: among canonical node sets ($x_1=-1$, $x_n=1$), the ones at which the smallest
of the $n-1$ local maxima between consecutive nodes is largest are exactly the canonical node sets
whose local maxima between consecutive nodes are all equal, that is, the canonical minimisers of
$\Lambda$ (`Erdos1129.erdos_1129.variants.canonical`). For canonical nodes the two outer gaps are
single points and the literal $\Upsilon$ is $1$, which is why $\Upsilon$ is replaced by
`minInteriorGapMax` here.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1130.variants.canonical (n : ℕ) :
    {x : Fin n → ℝ | IsCanonical x ∧
      ∀ y : Fin n → ℝ, IsCanonical y → minInteriorGapMax y ≤ minInteriorGapMax x} =
        {x | IsCanonical x ∧ Equioscillates x}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1130 — erdos inequality
problems.statement:
The inequality conjectured by Erdős and proved by Kilgore [Ki77], [Ki78] and by de Boor and
Pinkus [dBPi78] (stated in
[Ib16, Section 3.7] as $m_n(X)\le \Lambda_n(X^*)$ for every node set $X$): the smallest local
maximum of the Lebesgue function of any node set is at most the minimal Lebesgue constant. Here
$y$ is a minimiser of $\Lambda$. For nodes that contain neither $-1$ nor $1$, $\Upsilon$ is this
smallest local maximum [Ib16, Section 2.1 (b), (c)]; otherwise $\Upsilon=1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1130.variants.erdos_inequality (n : ℕ) (x y : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hx : IsNodeSet x) (hy : IsMinimiser y) :
    upsilon x ≤ lebesgueConstant y

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1130 — erdos inequality canonical
problems.statement:
The same inequality for a canonical node set `x`, in the form of [Ib16, Section 3.7]: the smallest
of the local maxima between consecutive nodes is at most the minimal Lebesgue constant.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1130.variants.erdos_inequality_canonical (n : ℕ) (x y : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hx : IsCanonical x) (hy : IsMinimiser y) :
    minInteriorGapMax x ≤ lebesgueConstant y

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1132 — erdos max
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er61c, Theorem 1] proved that, for any fixed $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in [-1,1]$,
$$\max_{x\in [-1,1]}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\lvert l_k(x)\rvert>\frac{2}{\pi}\log n-O(1).$$
Here $O(1)$ is an absolute constant $C$, and the maximum exceeds a bound if and only if some point
does, so we write the statement with `∃ t`. The nodes are required to be distinct.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1132.variants.erdos_max :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ x : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k < n, x k ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) →
      Set.InjOn x (Set.Iio n) →
        ∃ t ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, 2 / Real.pi * Real.log n - C < lebesgueFunction n x t

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1132 — tao
problems.statement:
Tao [Ta26b, Corollary 1.11] has proved that for any function $\omega(n)$ which tends to infinity
with $n$ there exists a dense set of $x\in (-1,1)$ such that
$$L_n(x)\geq \frac{2}{\pi}\log n-\omega(n)$$
for infinitely many $n$.

Tao proves this for an arbitrary triangular array of distinct nodes in $[-1,1]$, so in particular
for the first $n$ terms of a sequence. We state the array version: `x n k` is the $k$-th node
(counted from $0$) of the $n$-th row, and the set is dense in $(-1,1)$ if every point of
$(-1,1)$ is in its closure.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1132.variants.tao :
    ∀ x : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ, (∀ n, ∀ k < n, x n k ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) →
      (∀ n, Set.InjOn (x n) (Set.Iio n)) →
      ∀ ω : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto ω atTop atTop →
        Set.Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1 ⊆ closure {t ∈ Set.Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1 |
          ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 2 / Real.pi * Real.log n - ω n ≤ lebesgueFunction n (x n) t}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1133 — weaker
problems.statement:
Erdős proved that, for any $C>0$, there exists $\epsilon>0$ such that if $n$ is sufficiently
large and $m=\lfloor (1+\epsilon)n\rfloor$ then for any $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in [-1,1]$ there is a
polynomial $P$ of degree $n$ such that $\lvert P(x_i)\rvert\leq 1$ for $1\leq i\leq m$ and
$\max_{x\in [-1,1]}\lvert P(x)\rvert>C$. The robust interpolation statement above also implies
this result. Erdős in [Er67] could not prove the robust statement even for $m=n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1133.variants.weaker :
    ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      let m := ⌊(1 + ε) * (n : ℝ)⌋₊;
      ∀ x : Fin m → Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1,
        ∃ P : Polynomial ℝ,
          P.natDegree = n ∧
          (∀ i : Fin m, |P.eval (x i : ℝ)| ≤ 1) ∧
          ∃ z ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, |P.eval z| > C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1142 — mientka weitzenkamp
problems.statement:
Mientka and Weitzenkamp [MiWe69] proved that the only $n \leq 2^{44}$ such that $n > 2$ and
$n - 2^k$ is prime for all $k \geq 1$ with $2^k < n$ are $4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1142.variants.mientka_weitzenkamp :
    { n : ℕ | n ≤ 2 ^ 44 ∧ Erdos1142Prop n } = {4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 116 — log
problems.statement:
The lower bound $\lvert\{ z: \lvert p(z)\rvert <1\}\rvert \gg (\log n)^{-1}$ was proved by
Krishnapur, Lundberg, and Ramachandran [KLR25]; in particular the answer to the $(\log n)^{-O(1)}$
form of the question is also yes.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 116 — polya
problems.statement: Pólya [Po28]: $\lvert\{ z: \lvert p(z)\rvert <1\}\rvert \leq \pi$ always holds.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_116.variants.polya (n : ℕ) (z : Fin n → ℂ) :
    volume {w : ℂ | ‖∏ i, (w - z i)‖ < 1} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal Real.pi

problems.title: Erdős Problem 116 — upper
problems.statement:
Krishnapur, Lundberg, and Ramachandran [KLR25] proved that there are polynomials with
$\lvert\{ z: \lvert p(z)\rvert <1\}\rvert \ll (\log\log n)^{-1}$, improving a result of Wagner
[Wa88].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_116.variants.upper : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n →
    ∃ z : Fin n → ℂ, (∀ i, ‖z i‖ ≤ 1) ∧
      volume {w : ℂ | ‖∏ i, (w - z i)‖ < 1} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C / Real.log (Real.log n))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1164 — dembo peres rosen zeitouni
problems.statement:
Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni [DPRZ04, Theorem 1.4] proved a conjecture of Kesten and Révész:
if $T_n$ is the time it takes the simple random walk in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ to cover the disc of
radius $n$, then
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left(\log T_n\leq t(\log n)^2\right)=e^{-4/t}$$
for every $t>0$.

The disc is $D_n=D(0,n)\cap\mathbb{Z}^2$ (`openDisc`). Since $T_n$ is an integer,
$\log T_n\leq t(\log n)^2$ holds if and only if $T_n\leq\lfloor e^{t(\log n)^2}\rfloor$, that is,
if the disc is covered by that time.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1164.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω]
    [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ}
    (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦
      (ℙ {ω | Covers X ⌊Real.exp (t * Real.log n ^ 2)⌋₊ ω (openDisc n)}).toReal)
      atTop (𝓝 (Real.exp (-4 / t)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1165 — hao li okada zheng
problems.statement:
Hao, Li, Okada and Zheng [HLOZ24, Theorem 1.1] proved that, for the simple random walk on
$\mathbb{Z}^2$, almost surely
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty} \#K^{(2)}(n) = 3,$$
where $K^{(2)}(n)$ is the set of favourite sites at time $n$. The cardinalities are natural
numbers, so almost surely there are eventually at most three favourite sites, and exactly three
infinitely often. Tóth [To01] proved the corresponding bound for the one-dimensional walk, see
[HLOZ24, Section 1].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1165.variants.hao_li_okada_zheng {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω]
    [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ} (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∀ᵐ ω, limsup (fun n ↦ (favouriteSites X n ω).encard) atTop = 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1166 — dembo peres rosen zeitouni
problems.statement:
Dembo, Peres, Rosen and Zeitouni [DPRZ01, Theorem 1.1] proved the conjecture of Erdős and Taylor:
for the simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, if $T_n^*$ is the maximal number of visits to a
point in the first $n$ steps, then almost surely
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{T_n^*}{(\log n)^2}=\frac{1}{\pi}.$$

`maxLocalTime` counts the visit at time $0$. Whether this visit is counted changes $T_n^*$ by at
most one, so the limit is the same.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1166.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω]
    [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ}
    (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∀ᵐ ω, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (maxLocalTime X n ω : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 (1 / π))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1166 — erdos taylor
problems.statement:
Erdős and Taylor [ErTa60, p. 162] proved that, for the simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, if
$T_n$ is the maximal number of visits to a point in the first $n$ steps, then almost surely
$$\frac{1}{4\pi}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{T_n}{(\log n)^2}
  \leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{T_n}{(\log n)^2}\leq\frac{1}{\pi}.$$
They conjectured that the limit exists and equals $1/\pi$, see
`erdos_1166.variants.dembo_peres_rosen_zeitouni`.

We use `maxLocalTime`, which also counts the visit at time $0$. This changes $T_n$ by at most one.
The bounds are stated with $\varepsilon$ to avoid the junk values of `liminf` and `limsup`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1166.variants.erdos_taylor {Ω : Type*} [MeasureSpace Ω]
    [IsProbabilityMeasure (ℙ : Measure Ω)] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℤ × ℤ}
    (hX : IsSimpleRandomWalkSteps X) :
    ∀ᵐ ω, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, 1 / (4 * π) - ε ≤ (maxLocalTime X n ω : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2) ∧
      (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (maxLocalTime X n ω : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 2 ≤ 1 / π + ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1182 — small values
problems.statement:
The first few values of $F(n)$ and $f(n)$ (beginning with $n=2$) are $1,2,5,7,8$ and $1,2,5,8,12$
respectively, as reported in [BEFRS80, Table I]. Brandt, Brinkmann and Harmuth [BBH98, Table 2]
extended these (by computer) to all $n\le 12$:
$$F(n):\ 1,2,5,7,8,11,11,16,18,23,23,\qquad f(n):\ 1,2,5,8,12,16,20,27,33,41,49$$
for $n=2,\ldots,12$. (The value for $n=2$ is from [BEFRS80]; [BBH98] start at $n=3$.)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1189 — bbmst
problems.statement:
Let $I(k)$ count the number of irreducible covering sets of size $k$. Balister, Bollobás, Morris,
Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba [BBMST24] proved that
$$I(k) \leq \exp\left((c+o(1))\frac{k^{3/2}}{(\log k)^{1/2}}\right)$$
by proving that the right-hand side is an asymptotic for the number of minimal covering systems
on $k$ moduli.

Here $c = 4\sqrt{\tau}/3$ [BBMST24, Theorem 1.1]. The bound for $I(k)$ follows because each
irreducible covering set is the set of moduli of a minimal covering system. The $o(1)$ is stated
with an arbitrary $\varepsilon > 0$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1189.variants.bbmst (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop, (irreducibleCount k : ℝ) ≤
      Real.exp ((4 * Real.sqrt bbmstTau / 3 + ε) *
        ((k : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) / Real.sqrt (Real.log k)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1189 — simpson
problems.statement:
Simpson [Si85] proved $n_k\leq 2^{k-1}$.

Here $n_k$ is the largest element of an irreducible covering set of size $k$. The bound follows
from Simpson's theorem [Si85] (see [BBMST24, Theorem 2.4]), as stated in [BBMST24, Section 1].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1189.variants.simpson (M : Finset ℕ) (hM : IsIrreducibleCoveringSet M) :
    ∀ n ∈ M, n ≤ 2 ^ (M.card - 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1189 — sun
problems.statement:
The divisors of $12$ (which are $>1$) are an example of an irreducible covering set. Sun [Su07]
proved more generally that, for any odd prime $p$, the divisors (which are $>1$) of $2^{p-1}p$
form an irreducible covering set, settling the final question.

That $n=12$ is an example is already noted in [Er80, p. 95].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1189.variants.sun (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hodd : Odd p) :
    IsIrreducibleCoveringSet ((2 ^ (p - 1) * p).divisors.filter (1 < ·))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1190 — lt one
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er80] seems to credit Mirsky and Newman with the result that $\epsilon_m<1$, but gives no
reference.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1190.variants.lt_one (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (S : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hS : ∀ n ∈ S, m < n)
    (hdisj : ∀ n ∈ S, ∀ n' ∈ S, n ≠ n' → ¬ ∃ x : ℤ, x ≡ a n [ZMOD n] ∧ x ≡ a n' [ZMOD n']) :
    (∑ n ∈ S, (n : ℝ)⁻¹) < 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1192 — renyi
problems.statement:
Erdős and Rényi proved by the probabilistic method that there exists a set $A$ such that
$$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$ and $$\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert\gg x^{1/r}$$ for all $x$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1192.variants.renyi :
    ∀ r ≥ 2, ∃ A : Set ℕ,
      ((fun (x : ℕ) ↦ ∑ n ∈ range (x + 1), (f_r A r n : ℝ) ^ 2) =O[atTop]
        (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ))) ∧
      ((fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / (r : ℝ))) =O[atTop]
        (fun (x : ℕ) ↦ (count (· ∈ A) x : ℝ)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1194 — limsup eq top
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er80, p. 100] wrote it is 'easy to see' that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{a_n}{n}=\infty.$$
Indeed, since $A$ must be a Sidon set, if $a_n \leq f(n)n$ for all $n$, then all differences in
$[1,x/f(x)]$ can be realised by differences from $A\cap [1,x]$, and hence
$\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert^2 \gg x/f(x)$. Erdős (see for example [HaRo66]) proved that for
infinitely many $x$, $\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert \ll (x/\log x)^{1/2}$, which is a contradiction for
a suitable choice of $f$.

Formally: for every perfect difference set $A$ and every $C$, $a_n \geq Cn$ for infinitely many
$n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1194.variants.limsup_eq_top :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, IsPerfectDifferenceSetInt A → ∀ C : ℝ, HasLargeElement A (fun n ↦ C * n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1195 — exists set
problems.statement:
Schmidt [Sc69] asked whether such a set exists. Haight [Ha70] constructed a measurable set
$E\subset(0,\infty)$ of infinite Lebesgue measure such that $x_1/x_2$ is never an integer for
distinct $x_1,x_2\in E$, and Szemerédi [Sz71] independently constructed such a set.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1195.variants.exists_set :
    ∃ S : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet S ∧ S ⊆ Set.Ioi 0 ∧ volume S = ⊤ ∧ IntegerRatioFree S

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1198 — hindman
problems.statement:
The case where every $S_j$ is a singleton (Hindman's theorem [Hi74]): for every $2$-colouring of
$\mathbb{N}$ there is an infinite set all of whose finite sums of distinct elements have the same
colour.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1198.variants.hindman :

problems.title: Erdős Problem 291 — steinerberger generalization
problems.statement:
More generally, if the leading digit of $n$ in base $p$ is $p-1$ then $p\mid (a_n,L_n)$. There is
in fact a necessary and sufficient condition: a prime $p\leq n$ divides $(a_n,L_n)$ if and only if
$p$ divides the numerator of $1+\cdots+\frac{1}{k}$, where $k$ is the leading digit of $n$ in base
$p$. This can be seen by writing $a_n = \frac{L_n}{1}+\cdots+\frac{L_n}{n}$ and observing that the
right-hand side is congruent to $1+\cdots+1/k$ modulo $p$. (The previous claim about $p-1$ follows
immediately from Wolstenholme's theorem.)

\right\rfloor + 1 \leq f(N)$$
and
$$f(N)\leq \left\lfloor\sum_{n\leq N}\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{2}(1+o(1))
\frac{(\log\log N)^2}{\log N}\right\rfloor + 1.$$

        f N ≤ ⌊(harmonic N : ℝ) - 1 / 2 * (1 + o₂ N) * (log (log N)) ^ 2 / log N⌋₊ + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 319 — isTheta
problems.statement:
Let $c(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, \dots, N\}$ such that there is a function
$\delta : A \to \{-1, 1\}$ such that
$$
  \sum_{n\in A} \frac{\delta n}{n} = 0
$$
and
$$
  \sum_{n\in A'}\frac{\delta n}{n} \neq 0
$$
for all non-empty $A'\subsetneq A$. What is $\Theta(c(N))$?

Trivially $c(N) \leq N$, and `erdos_319.variants.lb` gives $c(N) \geq (1 - \frac{1}{e} + o(1))N$,
so $c(N) = \Theta(N)$.

    (h : ∀ N, IsGreatest
    { (#A : ℝ) | (A) (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N)
      (_ : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℤˣ, ∑ n ∈ A, (δ n : ℚ) / n = 0 ∧
        ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', (δ n : ℚ) / n ≠ 0) } (c N)) :
    c =Θ[atTop] erdos_319.variants.isTheta.answer

$$

$$

        ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', (δ n : ℚ) / n ≠ 0) }

problems.title: Erdős Problem 321 — lower
problems.statement:
Let $R(N)$ be the maximal such size. Results of Bleicher and Erdős from [BlEr75] and [BlEr76b] imply that
$$
\frac{N}{\log N} \prod_{i=3}^{k} \log_i N \le R(N),
$$
valid for any $k \ge 4$ with $\log_k N \ge k$ and any $r \ge 1$ with $\log_{2r} N \ge 1$. (In these bounds $\log_i n$ denotes the $i$-fold iterated logarithm.)

[BlEr75] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., _The number of distinct subsums of $\sum_{1}^{N}\,1/i$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 29-42.
[BlEr76b] Bleicher, Michael N. and Erdős, Paul, _Denominators of Egyptian fractions. II_. Illinois J. Math. (1976), 598-613.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 393 — berend osgood
problems.statement:
Let $F_m(N)$ count the number of $n \leq N$ such that $f(n) = m$. A theorem of Berend and
Osgood [BeOs92] implies that, for each fixed $m$, $F_m(N) = o(N)$, that is,
$\{n : f(n) = m\}$ has natural density $0$.

They proved that, for every $P \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree at least $2$, the set of $n$ such
that $P(x) = n!$ has an integer solution has density $0$. For $m \geq 1$ this applies because
$f(n) = m$ gives $n! = P(a_1)$ for one of the finitely many polynomials
$P(x) = \prod_{j \in S} (x + j)$ with $\{0, m\} \subseteq S \subseteq \{0, \ldots, m\}$. For
$m = 0$ the set is $\{0, 1\}$ (the junk values), so the statement is trivial.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_393.variants.berend_osgood (m : ℕ) :
    {n : ℕ | f n = m}.HasDensity 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 393 — bui pratt zaharescu
problems.statement:
A theorem of Bui, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BPZ23] implies that, for each fixed $m$,
$$F_m(N) \ll_m N^{33/34},$$
where $F_m(N)$ is the number of $n \leq N$ such that $f(n) = m$.

They proved that, for every $P \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree at least $2$, the number of
$N \leq n < 2N$ such that $P(x) = n!$ has an integer solution is $\ll_P N^{33/34}$. Summing over
the finitely many polynomials in `Erdos393.erdos_393.variants.berend_osgood` and over the dyadic
ranges $[2^i, 2^{i+1})$ gives the bound for $n \leq N$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_393.variants.bui_pratt_zaharescu (m : ℕ) :
    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (({n : ℕ | f n = m} ∩ Set.Iic N).ncard : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (33 / 34 : ℝ))

A conjecture of Graham [Gr70], who also conjectured that (assuming $A$ itself
has no common divisor) the only cases where equality is achieved are when
$A = \{1, \dots, n\}$ or $A = \{L/1, \dots, L/n\}$ (where $L = \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dots, n)$) or
$A = \{2, 3, 4, 6\}$.
Note: The source [BaSo96] mentioned on the Erdős page makes it clear what
quantifiers to use for "where equality is achieved". See Theorem 1.1 there.

an iff statement.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 402 — szegedy zaharescu weak
problems.statement:
Proved for all sufficiently large sets (including the sharper version which
characterises the case of equality) independently by Szegedy [Sz86] and
Zaharescu [Za87]. The following is taken from [Sz86].

There exists an effectively computable $n_0$ with the following properties:
(i) if $n \ge n_0$ and $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ are distinct natural numbers then
$\max_{i, j} \frac{a_i}{(a_i, a_j)} \ge n$.
(ii) If equality holds then the system $\{a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n\}$ is either of the
type $\{k, 2k, \dots, nk\}$ or of the type
$\left\{\frac{k}{1}, \frac{k}{2}, \dots, \frac{k}{n}\right\}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_402.variants.szegedy_zaharescu_weak : ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), A.card = n → 0 ∉ A →
      (n ≤ (A ×ˢ A).sup (fun x => x.1 / x.1.gcd x.2)) ∧
      (n = (A ×ˢ A).sup (fun x => x.1 / x.1.gcd x.2) ↔
        ∃ k > 0, A = (Finset.Icc 1 n).image (k * ·) ∨
          A = (Finset.Icc 1 n).image (k * (Finset.Icc 1 n).lcm id / ·))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 442 — tao
problems.statement:
Tao resolved erdos_442 in the negative in Theorem 1 of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04226.
The following is a formalisation of that theorem with $C_0 = 1$.

Let $\operatorname{Log} x := \max\{\log x, 1\}$,
$\operatorname{Log}_2x = \operatorname{Log} (\operatorname{Log} x)$, and
$\operatorname{Log}_3x = \operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log}(\operatorname{Log} x)).$
There exists a set $A$ of natural numbers such that
$$
\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n} =
  \exp\left(\left(\left(\frac{1}{2} + o(1)\right)\operatorname{Log}_2^{1/2}x \operatorname{Log}_3x\right)\right)
$$
and
$$
\sum_{n, m\in A: n, m\leq x} \frac{1}{\operatorname{lcm}(n, m)}\ll\left(\sum_{n\in A: n\leq x} \frac{1}{n}\right)^2
$$

    ∃ (A : Set ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (C: ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) (hf : f =o[atTop] (1 : ℝ → ℝ)),
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop,
        ∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n =
          Real.exp ((1 / 2 + f x) * √x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne * x.maxLogOne.maxLogOne.maxLogOne) ∧
        |∑ nm ∈ ((A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊) ×ˢ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊)).toFinset, (1 : ℝ) / nm.1.lcm nm.2| ≤
          C * (∑ n ∈ (A ∩ Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊ : Set ℕ), (1 : ℝ) / n) ^ 2
