problems.statement:
Abbott and Hanson [AbHa70] improved Erdős's upper bound to $f_r(N) \leq N^{1/2+o(1)}$
for all $r \geq 3$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_535.variants.abbott_hanson {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop,
      (f r N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2 + ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 — erdos upper bound
problems.statement: Erdős [Er64] proved that $f_r(N) \leq N^{3/4+o(1)}$ for all $r \geq 3$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_535.variants.erdos_upper_bound {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop,
      (f r N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 4 + ε)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 535 — lower bound
problems.statement: Erdős [Er64] proved that $f_3(N) > N^{c/\log\log N}$ for some constant $c > 0$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_535.variants.lower_bound : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ),
    ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in atTop,
      (N : ℝ) ^ (c / log (log (N : ℝ))) ≤ (f 3 N : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 — isBigO sq cube root
problems.statement: Granville and Roesler [GR99] showed that $$h(n)\ll n^{2/3}$$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_539.variants.isBigO_sq_cube_root :
    (fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / 3)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 539 — sq isBigO
problems.statement: Erdős and Szemerédi proved that$$n^{1/2} \ll h(n)$$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_539.variants.sq_isBigO :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ √n) =O[atTop] fun n ↦ (cofactorThreshold n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 541 — general moduli
problems.statement: Gao, Hamidoune, and Wang [GHW10] solved this for all moduli `p` (not necessarily prime).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_541.variants.general_moduli (p : ℕ) (a : Fin p → ZMod p)
    (ha₀ : ∃ r, ∀ (S : Finset (Fin p)), S ≠ ∅ → ∑ i ∈ S, a i = 0 → S.card = r) :
      (Set.range a).ncard ≤ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 541 — large primes
problems.statement: This was proved by Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz76] for p sufficiently large.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_541.variants.large_primes : ∀ᶠ p in atTop, p.Prime → ∀ a : Fin p → ZMod p,
    (∃ r, ∀ (S : Finset (Fin p)), S ≠ ∅ → ∑ i ∈ S, a i = 0 → S.card = r) →
      (Set.range a).ncard ≤ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 547 — sufficiently large
problems.statement:
For sufficiently large $n$, every tree $T$ on $n$ vertices satisfies $R(T)\leq 2n-2$.
Proved by Zhao [Zh11].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_547.variants.sufficiently_large :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ T : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      T.IsTree → SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey T ≤ 2 * n - 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 554 — acjmr
problems.statement:
Axenovich, Cames van Batenburg, Janzer, Michel and Rundström [ACJMR26, Theorem 1.1] proved that
$$R_k(C_{2n+1}) \leq (4n-2)^k k^{k/n}+1$$
for all $n, k \geq 1$. For $n \geq 2$ this improves the upper bound in
`Erdos554.erdos_554.variants.upper_bound`, since $k^{k/n}$ grows much more slowly than $(k+2)!$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_554.variants.acjmr :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k →
      (multicolourGraphRamsey k (cycleGraph (2 * n + 1)) : ℝ) ≤
        (4 * n - 2 : ℝ) ^ k * (k : ℝ) ^ ((k : ℝ) / n) + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 554 — day johnson
problems.statement:
Day and Johnson [DaJo17] proved that for every $n \geq 1$ there is a constant $c_n > 0$ such that
$$R_k(C_{2n+1}) > 2n(2+c_n)^{k-1}$$
for all sufficiently large $k$. So the lower bound in `Erdos554.erdos_554.variants.lower_bound`
is not sharp for fixed $n$ and large $k$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_554.variants.day_johnson :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 * n : ℝ) * (2 + c) ^ (k - 1) <
        (multicolourGraphRamsey k (cycleGraph (2 * n + 1)) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 554 — jenssen skokan
problems.statement:
Jenssen and Skokan [JeSk21] proved that the lower bound in
`Erdos554.erdos_554.variants.lower_bound` is sharp for fixed $k$ and large $n$: for every
$k \geq 2$,
$$R_k(C_{2n+1}) = n2^k+1$$
for all sufficiently large $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_554.variants.jenssen_skokan :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      multicolourGraphRamsey k (cycleGraph (2 * n + 1)) = n * 2 ^ k + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 554 — lower bound
problems.statement:
Bondy and Erdős [BoEr73] and Erdős and Graham [ErGr75] proved the lower bound
$$n2^k+1\leq R_k(C_{2n+1})$$
for all $n, k \geq 1$. The condition $k \geq 1$ excludes the junk value $R_0(G) = 2$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_554.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k →
      n * 2 ^ k + 1 ≤ multicolourGraphRamsey k (cycleGraph (2 * n + 1))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 554 — upper bound
problems.statement:
Erdős and Graham [ErGr75] (see also [BoEr73]) proved the upper bound
$$R_k(C_{2n+1})\leq 2n(k+2)!$$
for all $n, k \geq 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_554.variants.upper_bound :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k →
      multicolourGraphRamsey k (cycleGraph (2 * n + 1)) ≤ 2 * n * (k + 2).factorial

problems.title: Erdős Problem 559 — draganic petrova
problems.statement:
The best known upper bound for graphs of maximum degree $3$ is $\hat{R}(G)\leq n^{3/2+o(1)}$,
due to Draganić and Petrova [DrPe22].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_559.variants.draganic_petrova (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      G.maxDegree ≤ 3 → (sizeRamsey G G : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 + ε : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 60 — he ma yang
problems.statement:
He, Ma, and Yang [HeMaYa21] proved the conjecture when $n = q^2 + q + 1$ for some $q = 2^k$: they
showed that for large even $q$ every graph on $q^2 + q + 1$ vertices with
$\frac{1}{2}q(q+1)^2 + 1$ edges contains at least $q - 1$ copies of $C_4$, and
$\mathrm{ex}(q^2 + q + 1; C_4) = \frac{1}{2}q(q+1)^2$ when $q = 2^k$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_60.variants.he_ma_yang :
    ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧
      ∀ (q : ℕ) (_hq : q.isPowerOfTwo),
        ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (q^2 + q + 1))) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          (extremalNumber (q^2 + q + 1) (cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card) →
          (c * Real.sqrt ((q^2 + q + 1) : ℝ) ≤ ({ H' : G.Subgraph | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g cycleGraph 4) }.ncard : ℝ))

problems.title: Countable index set case.
problems.statement:
**Countable index set case.**

If the index set is countable, the answer is yes, and the intersection
condition is unnecessary. This is Bernstein's Lemma:
every countable system of infinite sets has Property B.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_602.variants.countable_index :
    ∀ {α : Type*} (A : ℕ → Set α),
      (∀ i, (A i).Countable ∧ (A i).Infinite) →
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).Finite) →
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Set.ncard (A i ∩ A j) ≠ 1) →
      HasPropertyB ℕ A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture — bnss23
problems.statement:
Bucić, Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [BNSS23] improved this to
$f(n) = \exp(c_H \sqrt{\log n \log \log n})$ for some constant $c_H > 0$ depending on $H$.

[BNSS23] Bucić, M. and Nguyen, T. and Scott, A. and Seymour, P., A loglog step towards Erdos-Hajnal
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_61.variants.bnss23 :
    ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α),
      ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H (fun n : ℕ => exp (c * sqrt (log n * log (log n))))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture — c5
problems.statement:
Chudnovsky, Scott, Seymour, and Spirkl [CSSS23] proved the conjecture for $H = C_5$, the
cycle on five vertices: every graph with no induced five-cycle has a clique or independent
set of polynomial size.

[CSSS23] Chudnovsky, M., Scott, A., Seymour, P. and Spirkl, S., Erdős–Hajnal for graphs with
no 5-hole. Proc. Lond. Math. Soc. (3) 126 (2023), 997–1014.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_61.variants.c5 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound (cycleGraph 5) (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture — erha89
problems.statement:
Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa89] proved that we can take $f(n) = \exp(c_H \sqrt{\log n})$
for some constant $c_H > 0$ depending on $H$.

[ErHa89] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., Ramsey-type theorems. Discrete Appl. Math. (1989), 37-52.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_61.variants.erha89 :
    ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (H : SimpleGraph α),
      ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound H (fun n : ℕ => exp (c * sqrt (log n)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 61 -- Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture — p5
problems.statement:
Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [NSS23] proved the conjecture for $H = P_5$, the path on five
vertices: every $P_5$-free graph on $n$ vertices has a clique or independent set of
polynomial size.

[NSS23] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., Induced subgraph density. VII. The
five-vertex path. [arXiv:2312.15333](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.15333)
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_61.variants.p5 :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), IsErdosHajnalLowerBound (pathGraph 5) (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 615 — fox loh zhao
problems.statement:
The result of Fox, Loh, and Zhao [FLZ15] disproving the problem: if $f(n) \geq 0$ satisfies
$f(n) = o(\sqrt{\log n/\log\log n})$, then for every $\epsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently
large $n$ there is a $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with independence number at most
$ne^{-f(n)}$ and at least $(1/8 - \epsilon)n^2$ edges; that is,
$\mathrm{rt}(n; 4, ne^{-f(n)}) \geq (1/8 - o(1))n^2$. Applied with
$f(n) = \log\log n$, this disproves the headline problem, since
$ne^{-f(n)} = n/\log n = o(n)$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_615.variants.fox_loh_zhao (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ n, 0 ≤ f n)
    (hfo : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => f n / Real.sqrt (Real.log n / Real.log (Real.log n)))
      atTop (nhds 0)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ n * Real.exp (-f n) ∧
        (1 / 8 - ε) * n ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 615 — sudakov
problems.statement:
The complementary result of Sudakov [Su03]: if $f(n)/\sqrt{\log n} \to \infty$ then
$\mathrm{rt}(n; 4, ne^{-f(n)}) = o(n^2)$; that is, for every $\epsilon > 0$ and all
sufficiently large $n$, every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with independence number at
most $ne^{-f(n)}$ has at most $\epsilon n^2$ edges.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_615.variants.sudakov (f : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => f n / Real.sqrt (Real.log n)) atTop atTop)
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 →
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ n * Real.exp (-f n) →
        (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ≤ ε * n ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 — add edges diam three
problems.statement:
Erdős, Gyárfás and Ruszinkó [EGR98]: every connected triangle-free graph on a finite
vertex set can be extended, by adding edges, to a triangle-free graph of diameter at
most $3$. This shows that the infimum defining `minNewEdges r G` ranges over a nonempty
set for every `3 ≤ r`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_619.variants.add_edges_diam_three {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.Connected) (hG' : G.CliqueFree 3) :
    ∃ H : SimpleGraph V, G ≤ H ∧ H.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.ediam ≤ 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 — h five le
problems.statement:
Erdős, Gyárfás and Ruszinkó [EGR98]: $h_5(G) \leq \frac{n-1}{2}$ for every connected
triangle-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_619.variants.h_five_le {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.Connected) (hG' : G.CliqueFree 3) :
    (minNewEdges 5 G : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card V - 1) / 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 — h three le
problems.statement:
Erdős, Gyárfás and Ruszinkó [EGR98]: $h_3(G) \leq n$ for every connected triangle-free
graph $G$ on $n$ vertices.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_619.variants.h_three_le {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.Connected) (hG' : G.CliqueFree 3) :
    minNewEdges 3 G ≤ Fintype.card V

problems.title: Erdős Problem 619 — h three lower
problems.statement:
Erdős, Gyárfás and Ruszinkó [EGR98]: there is a constant $c > 0$ such that for every
$n$ there exist connected triangle-free graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices with
$h_3(G) \geq n - c$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_619.variants.h_three_lower :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (G : SimpleGraph V),
        Fintype.card V = n ∧ G.Connected ∧ G.CliqueFree 3 ∧
        (n : ℝ) - c ≤ minNewEdges 3 G

problems.title: Erdős Problem 627 — conditional
problems.statement:
Araujo, Filipe, and Miyazaki [AFM25, Theorem 1.2]: suppose that $R(s,t) \leq R(k)$ for all
$s, t, k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $st \leq k^2$ (their Conjecture 1.1), and that
$\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{\log_2 R(k)}{k}$ exists and equals $\ell$. Then
$$f(n) = (\ell^2 + o(1)) \frac{n}{(\log_2 n)^2},$$
so the limit in `Erdos627.erdos_627` exists and equals $\ell^2$. Here $R(s,t)$ is the
two-colour Ramsey number and $R(k) = R(k,k)$ (see [77]). [AFM25] is an arXiv preprint.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_627.variants.conditional (ℓ : ℝ)
    (hR : ∀ s t k : ℕ, s * t ≤ k ^ 2 → classicalRamsey s t ≤ diagonalRamsey k)
    (hlim : Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ Real.logb 2 (diagonalRamsey k : ℝ) / (k : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 ℓ)) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ maxChromaticCliqueRatio n / ((n : ℝ) / Real.logb 2 n ^ 2))
      atTop (𝓝 (ℓ ^ 2))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 629 — property b
problems.statement:
They also prove that if $m(k)$ is the size of the smallest family of $k$-sets without property B
(i.e. the smallest number of $k$-sets in a graph with chromatic number $3$) then
$m(k)\leq n(k)\leq m(k+1)$.

[ERT80, p. 129] prints the upper bound as $2m(k)$; we state that form. Here $m(k)$ is
`Hypergraph.minChromaticEdges k 3`, as in Erdős Problem 901. We assume $k \geq 2$: for $k = 1$
this is `⊤`, since singleton edges admit no proper colouring, whereas $m(1) = 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_629.variants.property_b (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    (Hypergraph.minChromaticEdges k 3).toNat ≤ n k ∧
      n k ≤ 2 * (Hypergraph.minChromaticEdges k 3).toNat

problems.title: Erdős Problem 636 — erdos faudree sos
problems.statement:
Erdős, Faudree, and Sós proved that there exist $\gg n^{3/2}$ many such subgraphs, as stated on
erdosproblems.com. Section 2 of [KwSu21] describes two short proofs of this weaker bound.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_636.variants.erdos_faudree_sos :
    ∀ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ γ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (G.cliqueNum : ℝ) < C * Real.log n → (G.indepNum : ℝ) < C * Real.log n →
        HasManyDistinctInducedSubgraphs G (γ * (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 643 — exact t ge four
problems.statement:
Huang, Ma, and Yang [HMY26, Theorem 1.2] determine the maximum size of an avoiding family
for each fixed $t\geq4$ and all sufficiently large $n$:
$$\binom{n-1}{t-1}+\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{t}\right\rfloor.$$
The forcing threshold is one larger.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_643.variants.exact_t_ge_four :
    ∀ t : ℕ, 4 ≤ t → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      Hypergraph.extremalNumber n t (fun H ↦ ¬ H.HasRepeatedDisjointUnion) =
        (n - 1).choose (t - 1) + (n - 1) / t

problems.title: Erdős Problem 65 — liu montgomery
problems.statement:
Liu and Montgomery [LiMo20, Corollary 1.2] have proved the asymptotically sharp lower bound of
$\geq (\tfrac{1}{2}-o(1))\log k$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_65.variants.liu_montgomery :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k : ℝ in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        0 < n →
        Fintype.card V = n →
        (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) = k * n →
        (∑ᶠ a ∈ G.cycleLengths, (1 : ℝ) / a) ≥ (1 / 2 - ε) * Real.log k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 652 — first
problems.statement:
It is trivial that $R(x_1)=1$ is possible.
We require $n\geq 2$ because a singleton determines no distances to other points.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_652.variants.first (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ points : Finset ℝ², points.card = n ∧
      ∃ point ∈ points, distinctDistancesFrom points point = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 652 — kth lower bound
problems.statement:
Mathialagan's bound immediately implies $R(x_k)\gg (kn)^{1/2}$ for
$2\leq k\leq n^{1/3}$: fewer than $k$ points have distance count below the bound.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_652.variants.kth_lower_bound :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ points : Finset ℝ², ∀ k : ℕ,
      2 ≤ k → k ^ 3 ≤ points.card →
        (points.filter fun point => (distinctDistancesFrom points point : ℝ) <
          c * Real.sqrt ((k : ℝ) * points.card)).card < k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 652 — mathialagan
problems.statement:
Mathialagan [Ma21, Theorem 14] proved that given a set $P$ of $k$ points and a set $Q$
of $n$ points, with $2\leq k\leq n^{1/3}$, there exists a point in $P$ which determines
$\gg (kn)^{1/2}$ distances to points in $Q$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_652.variants.mathialagan :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ P Q : Finset ℝ²,
      2 ≤ P.card → P.card ^ 3 ≤ Q.card →
        ∃ p ∈ P, c * Real.sqrt ((P.card : ℝ) * Q.card) ≤
          (Q.image fun q => dist p q).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 652 — order sqrt
problems.statement:
Elekes' construction and Mathialagan's lower bound give
$\alpha_k=\Theta(\sqrt k)$, as noted by Zach Hunter in the discussion.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_652.variants.order_sqrt :
    ∃ c C : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      c * Real.sqrt k ≤ alpha k ∧ alpha k ≤ C * Real.sqrt k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 652 — product
problems.statement:
We always have $R(x_1)R(x_2)\gg n$.
Equivalently, the same bound holds for any two distinct points of the set.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_652.variants.product :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ points : Finset ℝ²,
      ∀ p ∈ points, ∀ q ∈ points, p ≠ q →
        c * points.card ≤
          (distinctDistancesFrom points p : ℝ) * distinctDistancesFrom points q

problems.title: Erdős Problem 657 — dim one
problems.statement:
The question on the real line, which Erdős [Er73] said was open, has a positive answer: there is
a function $f$ with $f(n)\to \infty$ such that every set of $n$ real numbers with no three-term
arithmetic progression determines at least $f(n)n$ distinct distances. This follows from the
lower bound of Dumitrescu [Du08].

On the line, a set has no isosceles triangle exactly when it has no three-term arithmetic
progression.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_657.variants.dim_one :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℝ, A.card = n → (A : Set ℝ).IsIsoscelesFree →
        f n * (n : ℝ) ≤ (distinctDistances A : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 657 — dim one lower
problems.statement:
Dumitrescu [Du08] proved that there is a constant $c > 0$ such that, for all large $n$, every set
of $n$ real numbers with no three-term arithmetic progression determines at least
$n(\log n)^c$ distinct distances.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_657.variants.dim_one_lower :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ A : Finset ℝ, A.card = n → (A : Set ℝ).IsIsoscelesFree →
        (n : ℝ) * (Real.log n) ^ c ≤ (distinctDistances A : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 657 — dim one upper
problems.statement:
As noted in [Du08], Behrend's construction of large sets without three-term arithmetic
progressions shows that there is a constant $C > 0$ such that, for all large $n$, some set
of $n$ real numbers with no three-term arithmetic progression determines at most
$n 2^{C\sqrt{\log n}}$ distinct distances.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_657.variants.dim_one_upper :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ A : Finset ℝ, A.card = n ∧ (A : Set ℝ).IsIsoscelesFree ∧
        (distinctDistances A : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) * (2 : ℝ) ^ (C * √(Real.log n))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 660 — altman planar
problems.statement:
For the similar problem in $\mathbb{R}^2$ there are always at least $n/2$ distances, as proved by
Altman [Al63].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_660.variants.altman_planar (n : ℕ) (P : Finset ℝ²)
    (hcard : P.card = n) (hconv : ConvexIndependent ℝ ((↑) : ↥(P : Set ℝ²) → ℝ²))
    (haff : affineSpan ℝ (P : Set ℝ²) = ⊤) :
    n / 2 ≤ distinctDistances P

problems.title: Erdős Problem 668 — four points
problems.statement:
For $n=4$ there is, up to congruence, exactly one set of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which maximises
the number of unit distances: two unit equilateral triangles $abc$ and $bcd$ joined by the edge
$bc$, with $a\neq d$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_668.variants.four_points :
    ∃ a b c d : ℝ², dist a b = 1 ∧ dist a c = 1 ∧ dist b c = 1 ∧ dist b d = 1 ∧ dist c d = 1 ∧
      ({a, b, c, d} : Finset ℝ²).card = 4 ∧
      ∀ B : Finset ℝ², B.card = 4 →
        (unitDistNum B = maxUnitDistances 4 ↔ ∃ f : ℝ² ≃ᵢ ℝ², f '' {a, b, c, d} = B)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 675 — squarefree
problems.statement:
Elementary sieve theory implies that the set of squarefree numbers has the translation property
(as remarked on erdosproblems.com).
problems.lean: theorem erdos_675.variants.squarefree : HasTranslationProperty {m : ℕ | Squarefree m}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 683 — erdos log
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er55d] improved this to $P(n, k) \gg \min(n - k + 1, k \log k)$ for $k \le n/2$. The
minimum cannot be dropped: at $n = 2k$ one has $P(n, k) \le 2k$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_683.variant.erdos_log :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 →
      (P n k : ℝ) ≥ min (↑(n - k + 1) : ℝ) (c * k * Real.log k)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 704 — davies lower
problems.statement:
Davies [Da26, Theorem 1.4] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \geq (2 + o(1))^n,$$
improving the bound of Raigorodskii (see `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.raigorodskii`): for every
$0 < c < 2$ we have $\chi(G_n) \geq c^n$ for all large $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_704.variants.davies_lower :
    ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 2, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → c ^ n ≤ (k : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 704 — davies upper
problems.statement:
Davies [Da26, Theorem 1.5] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \leq (3\sqrt{3}/2 + o(1))^n,$$
improving the bound of Larman and Rogers (see `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.larman_rogers`).
(The abstract of [Da26] prints $3\sqrt{3}/4$; Theorem 1.5 has $3\sqrt{3}/2 \approx 2.598$.)
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_704.variants.davies_upper :
    ∀ C > 3 * Real.sqrt 3 / 2, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ C ^ n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 704 — frankl wilson
problems.statement:
Frankl and Wilson [FrWi81] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \geq (1 + o(1)) 1.2^n.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_704.variants.frankl_wilson :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → (1 - ε) * 1.2 ^ n ≤ (k : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 704 — larman rogers
problems.statement:
Larman and Rogers [LaRo72] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \leq (3 + o(1))^n.$$
Prosanov [Pr20] has given an alternative proof of this bound.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_704.variants.larman_rogers :
    ∀ C > (3 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∃ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k ∧ (k : ℝ) ≤ C ^ n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 704 — larman rogers conjecture
problems.statement:
Larman and Rogers [LaRo72] conjecture that the truth may be
$$\chi(G_n) = (2^{3/2} + o(1))^n,$$
that is, $\chi(G_n)^{1/n} \to 2^{3/2}$.

This is false: by `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.davies_upper` [Da26] we have
$\limsup \chi(G_n)^{1/n} \leq 3\sqrt{3}/2 < 2^{3/2}$. Whether the limit exists remains open
(`Erdos704.erdos_704.parts.ii`).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_704.variants.larman_rogers_conjecture :
    ¬ Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((unitDistanceGraph n).chromaticNumber.toNat : ℝ) ^ (1 / (n : ℝ)))
      atTop (𝓝 ((2 : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 704 — raigorodskii
problems.statement:
Raigorodskii [Ra00] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \geq (1.239\cdots + o(1))^n.$$
We state the weaker bound with the truncated constant $1.239$: for every $0 < c < 1.239$ we
have $\chi(G_n) \geq c^n$ for all large $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_704.variants.raigorodskii :
    ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1.239, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ k : ℕ, (unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → c ^ n ≤ (k : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 710 — lower bound
problems.statement:
Erdős and Pomerance [ErPo80] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{e}}+o(1)\right)n\left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}
\leq f(n) \leq (1.7398\cdots+o(1))n(\log n)^{1/2}.$$

This is the lower bound [ErPo80, Theorem 2].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_710.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 / Real.sqrt (Real.exp 1) - ε) * n *
        Real.sqrt (Real.log n / Real.log (Real.log n)) ≤ (f n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 710 — upper bound
problems.statement:
Erdős and Pomerance [ErPo80] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{e}}+o(1)\right)n\left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}
\leq f(n) \leq (1.7398\cdots+o(1))n(\log n)^{1/2}.$$

This is the upper bound. Here $1.7398\cdots = \sqrt{r}/(1-r)$, where $r$ is the solution of
$e^{-r} = r$ [ErPo80, (11), p. 154].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_710.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ r : ℝ, Real.exp (-r) = r ∧ ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (f n : ℝ) ≤ (Real.sqrt r / (1 - r) + ε) * n * Real.sqrt (Real.log n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 717 — erdos fajtlowicz
problems.statement:
Erdős and Fajtlowicz [ErFa81, Theorem 3] showed that for almost all graphs on $n$ vertices
$$\chi(G) \gg \frac{n^{1/2}}{\log n}\sigma(G).$$
As in [ErFa81, p. 141], "almost all" means all but $o(2^{\binom{n}{2}})$ labelled graphs on $n$
vertices.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_717.variants.erdos_fajtlowicz :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
        (Nat.card {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n) //
          ¬ (C * (Real.sqrt n / Real.log n) * (cliqueSubdivisionNumber G : ℝ) <
            (G.chromaticNumber.toNat : ℝ))} : ℝ) / 2 ^ n.choose 2) atTop (𝓝 0)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 725 — erdos kaplansky
problems.statement:
Erdős and Kaplansky [ErKa46] proved the count is
$$\sim e^{-\binom{k}{2}}(n!)^k$$
when $k=o((\log n)^{3/2-\epsilon})$.

Here $\epsilon>0$ is fixed.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_725.variants.erdos_kaplansky (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hk : (fun n ↦ (k n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun n ↦ Real.log n ^ (3 / 2 - ε)) :
    (fun n ↦ (L (k n) n : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      fun n ↦ Real.exp (-((k n).choose 2 : ℝ)) * (n.factorial : ℝ) ^ k n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 725 — yamamoto
problems.statement:
Yamamoto [Ya51] extended this to $k\leq n^{1/3-o(1)}$.

As in [Ya51, p. 113], we assume $k<n^{1/3-\delta}$ with $n^{-\delta}\to 0$, where $\delta$
may be a positive constant or a function of $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_725.variants.yamamoto (δ : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hδ : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (-δ n)) atTop (nhds 0)) (k : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hk : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (k n : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 - δ n)) :
    (fun n ↦ (L (k n) n : ℝ)) ~[atTop]
      fun n ↦ Real.exp (-((k n).choose 2 : ℝ)) * (n.factorial : ℝ) ^ k n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 727 — k 1
problems.statement:
Balakran proved this holds for $k = 1$.

Let $k = 1$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ for infinitely many $n$?

problems.title: Erdős Problem 727 — k 1 2
problems.statement:
Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus observe that the method of Balakran can be further used to prove
that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $(n+k)!(n+1)!∣(2n)!$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 739 — aleph zero
problems.statement:
Every graph with chromatic number $\mathfrak{m}>\aleph_0$ has a subgraph with chromatic number
$\aleph_0$. This is the case $\mathfrak{n}=\aleph_0$ of the question and follows from the
de Bruijn–Erdős theorem [dBE51]. The source credits Galvin [Ga73] with the case
$\mathfrak{m}=\aleph_0$, which has no infinite $\mathfrak{n}<\mathfrak{m}$; it is read here as
$\mathfrak{n}=\aleph_0$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_739.variants.aleph_zero :
    ∀ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), ℵ₀ < G.chromaticCardinal →
      ∃ H : G.Subgraph, H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀

problems.title: Erdős Problem 739 — induced
problems.statement:
Galvin [Ga73] proved that the stronger version of `erdos_739`, in which the subgraph is induced,
implies $2^{\mathfrak{k}}<2^{\mathfrak{n}}$ for all cardinals $\mathfrak{k}<\mathfrak{n}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_739.variants.induced :
    (∀ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : Cardinal.{u}),
      ℵ₀ ≤ n → n < G.chromaticCardinal →
        ∃ s : Set V, (G.induce s).chromaticCardinal = n) →
    ∀ κ μ : Cardinal.{u}, κ < μ → (2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ κ < 2 ^ μ

problems.title: Erdős Problem 751 — bondy vince
problems.statement:
Bondy and Vince [BoVi98] proved that every graph with minimum degree at least $3$ has two cycles
whose lengths differ by at most $2$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_751.variants.bondy_vince {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : 3 ≤ G.minDegree) :
    ∃ m ∈ G.cycleLengths, ∃ m' ∈ G.cycleLengths, m < m' ∧ m' ≤ m + 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 753 — alon
problems.statement:
Alon [Al92] proved that, for every $n$, there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that
$$\chi_L(G)+\chi_L(G^c)\ll (n\log n)^{1/2},$$
where the implied constant is absolute.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_753.variants.alon :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (listChromaticNumber G : ℝ) + (listChromaticNumber Gᶜ : ℝ) ≤
        C * ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ)) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 757 — lowerBound
problems.statement: The supremum is strictly larger than `1 / 2`, which is proved in [GyLe95].
problems.lean: theorem erdos_757.variants.lowerBound {A : Set ℝ} : 1 / (2 : ℝ) < sSup {c | IsAdmissible c}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 757 — upperBound
problems.statement: In [GyLe95], the authors also prove that the supremum is smaller than `3 / 5`.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_757.variants.upperBound {A : Set ℝ} : sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} < 3 / (5 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 760 — erdos gimbel
problems.statement:
A problem of Erdős and Gimbel, who proved that there must exist a subgraph $H$ with
$$
\zeta(H) \gg \left(\frac{m}{\log m}\right)^{1/2}.
$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_760.variants.erdos_gimbel :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type*) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (m : ℕ),
      G.chromaticNumber = (m : ℕ∞) →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, ∃ k : ℕ, ((k : ℕ∞) ≤ H.coe.cochromaticNumber) ∧
          (c * Real.sqrt ((m : ℝ) / Real.log (m : ℝ)) ≤ (k : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 761 — parts ii imp i
problems.statement:
A positive answer to the second question implies a positive answer to the first via the bound
mentioned in [760].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_761.variants.parts_ii_imp_i :
    (∀ k : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type u) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (m : ℕ∞) ≤ G.cochromaticNumber →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, (k : ℕ∞) ≤ dichromaticNumber H.coe) →
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type u) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (m : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber → (k : ℕ∞) ≤ dichromaticNumber G

problems.title: Erdős Problem 762 — bounded clique number
problems.statement:
A conjecture of Erdős, Gimbel, and Straight [EGS90], who proved that for every $n>2$ there exists
some $f(n)$ such that if $G$ contains no clique on $n$ vertices then $\chi(G)\leq \zeta(G)+f(n)$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_762.variants.bounded_clique_number (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 < n) :
    ∃ f : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.CliqueFree n → G.chromaticNumber ≤ G.cochromaticNumber + f

problems.title: Erdős Problem 765 — second term
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er93] conjectured that $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) = \frac{n^{3/2}}{2} + \frac n4 + O(n^{1/2})$ for all
$n$, having proved the upper bound $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) \le \frac{n^{3/2}}{2} + \frac n4 + O(n^{1/2})$
in [Er75]. This is false: Ma and Yang [MaYa23] proved that, for some absolute constant $c > 0$ and
a positive density set of $n$, $\mathrm{ex}(n; C_4) \le \frac{n^{3/2}}{2} + (\frac14 - c) n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_765.variants.second_term :
    ¬ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4) : ℝ) -
      (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) / 2 - (n : ℝ) / 4) =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 775 — gao
problems.statement:
The answer is no, as proved by Gao [Ga25]: more generally, for any $k\geq 3$, every $k$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains at most $n-f_k(n)$ different sizes of cliques, where
$f_k(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_775.variants.gao :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ H : UniformHypergraph (Fin n) 3,
        (UniformHypergraph.cliqueSizes H).ncard + f n ≤ n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 782 — dietmann elsholtz
problems.statement:
Dietmann and Elsholtz [DiEl12, Theorem 1] proved that, for all sufficiently large $N$, if
$a_0\geq 0$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ are distinct positive integers such that the Hilbert cube
$a_0+\{0,b_1\}+\cdots+\{0,b_d\}$ consists of squares in $[1,N]$, then $d\leq 7\log\log N$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_782.variants.dietmann_elsholtz :
    ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N ≥ N₀, ∀ (d : ℕ) (a₀ : ℤ) (b : Fin d → ℤ),
      0 ≤ a₀ → Function.Injective b → (∀ i, 0 < b i) →
      hilbertCube a₀ b ⊆ {n : ℤ | IsSquare n ∧ 1 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ N} →
        (d : ℝ) ≤ 7 * Real.log (Real.log N)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 — danzer
problems.statement:
Danzer [Da64] proved that exact additive complements exist (Hanani had earlier conjectured they
do not exist, as reported in [Er57] and [Er61]).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_785.variants.danzer :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B

problems.title: Erdős Problem 785 — ruzsa upper bound
problems.statement:
Ruzsa [Ru17] has constructed, for any function $w(x)\to \infty$, such a pair of sets with
$$A(x)B(x)-x<w(x)$$
for infinitely many $x$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : Tendsto w atTop atTop) :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ 0 ∉ B ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) < w x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 787 — beker
problems.statement:
Beker [Be25] has proved
$$(\log n)^{1+\tfrac{1}{68}+o(1)} \ll g(n).$$

Here this means that $g(n) \geq (\log n)^{1+c}$ for every $c < 1/68$ and all large $n$
[Be25, Theorem 1.2].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_787.variants.beker :
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → c < 1 / 68 → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Real.log n ^ (1 + c) ≤ (g ℝ n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 787 — ruzsa
problems.statement:
The current best bounds known are
$$(\log n)^{1+c} \ll g(n) \ll \exp(\sqrt{\log n})$$
for some constant $c>0$, the lower bound due to Sanders [Sa21] and the upper bound due to
Ruzsa [Ru05].

This is the upper bound. [Ru05] proves it in the form $\exp(O(\sqrt{\log n}))$, which is the form
stated here.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_787.variants.ruzsa :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (g ℝ n : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp (C * Real.sqrt (Real.log n))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 794 — frankl furedi
problems.statement:
This problem is then now asking how many edges a $3$-uniform hypergraph can have before it
contains $K_4$ minus an edge, and whether the critical edge density is $2/9$. In fact there is a
construction of Frankl and Füredi [FrFu84] showing it must be at least $2/7$, which is the
conjectured truth (although Turán conjectured before [Er69] that the edge density was $1/4$, and
so likely there is simply a typo in this problem's statement).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_794.variants.frankl_furedi (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ H : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), H.IsUniform 3 ∧
      ¬ H.ContainsSubgraph 4 3 ∧ (2 / 7 - ε) * (n.choose 3 : ℝ) ≤ (H.card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 802 — shearer
problems.statement:
Shearer [Sh95] proved that any $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $t$ contains
an independent set on
$$\gg_r \frac{\log t}{\log\log(t+1)t}n$$
many vertices.

We assume $t \geq 2$. For $t + 1$ slightly larger than $e$ the factor $\log\log(t+1)$ is close
to $0$, so the bound blows up and the statement is false without such a restriction.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_802.variants.shearer : ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    G.CliqueFree r → 2 ≤ G.averageDegree →
      c * (log G.averageDegree / (log (log (G.averageDegree + 1)) * G.averageDegree)) * n ≤
        G.indepNum

problems.title: Erdős Problem 803 — alon
problems.statement:
Alon [Al08] proved that for every $D>1$ and large $n$ there is a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices
and $\geq n\log n$ edges such that if $H$ is a $D$-balanced subgraph on $m$ vertices then $H$ has
$\ll m\sqrt{\log m}+\log D$ many edges.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_803.variants.alon :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ D : ℝ, 1 < D → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) * log n ≤ G.edgeSet.ncard ∧
      ∀ H : G.Subgraph, IsBalanced H.coe D →
        (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ≤ C * (H.verts.ncard * √(log H.verts.ncard) + log D)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 803 — janzer sudakov
problems.statement:
Janzer and Sudakov [JaSu23] have proved that, for any $k$, if $n$ is sufficiently large then
any graph on $n$ vertices with at least $n\log n$ edges contains a $O(1)$-balanced subgraph on
$m\geq k$ vertices with $\gg_k \frac{\sqrt{\log m}}{(\log\log m)^{3/2}}m$ many edges.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_803.variants.janzer_sudakov :
    ∃ D : ℝ, ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) * log n ≤ G.edgeSet.ncard →
        ∃ H : G.Subgraph, k ≤ H.verts.ncard ∧ IsBalanced H.coe D ∧
          c * (√(log H.verts.ncard) / (log (log H.verts.ncard)) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) *
            H.verts.ncard ≤ H.edgeSet.ncard

problems.title: Erdős Problem 806 — erdos newman
problems.statement:
Erdős and Newman [ErNe77] proved that there exist $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert\asymp n^{1/2}$ such that if $A\subseteq B+B$ then
$\lvert B\rvert \gg \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_806.variants.erdos_newman : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n ∧ c * √n ≤ A.card ∧ (A.card : ℝ) ≤ √n ∧
      ∀ B : Finset ℤ, A.map Nat.castEmbedding ⊆ B + B →
        c * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n * √n ≤ B.card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 808 — positive
problems.statement:
The conjecture already fails for positive integers: the set of integers constructed in
[ARS20, Theorem 3] consists of positive integers. This is `erdos_808` with the extra hypothesis
`∀ v, 0 < a v`, so it implies `erdos_808`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_808.variants.positive :
    ¬ ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (a : V ↪ ℕ), (∀ v, 0 < a v) →
        ∀ (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          n₀ ≤ Fintype.card V →
          (Fintype.card V : ℝ) ^ (1 + c) ≤ (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) →
          (Fintype.card V : ℝ) ^ (1 + c - ε) ≤
            max ((edgeSums a G).card : ℝ) ((edgeProducts a G).card : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 81 — split
problems.statement:
Chen, Erdős, and Ordman [CEO94] have shown that any split graph can be partitioned
into $\frac{3}{16}n^2+O(n)$ many cliques.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_81.variants.split :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.IsSplitGraph →
      ∃ P : Finset (Finset (Fin n)), G.IsCliqueEdgePartition P ∧
        (P.card : ℝ) ≤ 3 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / 16 + C * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 814 — sauermann
problems.statement: Sauermann [Sa19] proved this with $c_k \gg 1/k^3$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_814.variants.sauermann :
    ∃ C > 0, ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ n ≥ k - 1, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (k - 1) * (n + 2 - k) + (k - 2).choose 2 + 1 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
        ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), S.Nonempty ∧ (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 - C / k ^ 3) * n ∧
          k ≤ (G.induce (S : Set (Fin n))).minDegree

problems.title: Erdős Problem 817 — bdd power
problems.statement:
A problem of Erdős and Sárközy who proved
$$
  g_3(n) \gg \frac{3^n}{n^{O(1)}}.
$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_817.variants.bdd_power : ∃ O > (0 : ℝ),
    (fun (n : ℕ) => (3 ^ n : ℝ) / n ^ O) =O[atTop] fun n => (g 3 n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 827 — martinez roldan pensado
problems.statement:
In [Er78c] Erdős gave an argument for $n_k \leq k+2\binom{k-1}{2}\binom{k-1}{3}$, but this
argument is incorrect, as explained by Martínez and Roldán-Pensado [MaRo15], who give a corrected
argument that proves $n_k\ll k^9$.

[MaRo15, Theorem 1.1] assumes only that no four points lie on a line or a circle. That class
contains the sets in general position, so the bound holds for $n_k$ as defined here.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_827.variants.martinez_roldan_pensado :
    (fun k : ℕ ↦ (n k : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun k : ℕ ↦ (k : ℝ) ^ 9

problems.title: Erdős Problem 831 — szekeres
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er75h, p. 2] attributes to E. Szekeres the observation that for three points
$x_1,x_2,x_3$ of the plane, not on a line, there is a unique point $x_4$ such that
$x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ are not on a circle and the four circles determined by the four triples of these
points have the same radius; one can take $x_4$ to be the orthocentre of the triangle
$x_1x_2x_3$.

Read literally this fails for a right-angled triangle, whose orthocentre is a vertex, so we assume
that the triangle has no right angle. We also require the four points to be in general position,
so that the four circles exist.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_831.variants.szekeres (x₁ x₂ x₃ : ℝ²)
    (hcol : ¬ Collinear ℝ ({x₁, x₂, x₃} : Set ℝ²)) (hright : ¬ IsRightAngled x₁ x₂ x₃) :
    ∃! x₄ : ℝ², x₄ ∉ ({x₁, x₂, x₃} : Set ℝ²) ∧
      InGeneralPosition ({x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄} : Set ℝ²) ∧
      (circleRadii ({x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄} : Set ℝ²)).ncard = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 852 — tendsto atTop
problems.statement:
Brun's sieve implies $h(x) \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$ (remark on
[erdosproblems.com/852](https://www.erdosproblems.com/852)).

That is, for every $H$ and all large $x$ there is some $n < x$ such that $d_n, \ldots, d_{n+H-1}$
are all distinct. Since more values of $n$ are allowed as $x$ grows, this holds exactly when, for
every $H$, some $n$ has $d_n, \ldots, d_{n+H-1}$ all distinct.

This also follows from `Erdos6.erdos_6.variants.increasing`, because strictly increasing prime
gaps are distinct.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_852.variants.tendsto_atTop :
    ∀ H : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, ∃ n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) < x ∧ DistinctGapRun n H

problems.title: Erdős Problem 865 — upper bound
problems.statement:
Choi, Erdős, and Szemerédi [CES75] have proved that, for all $k\geq 3$, there exists $\epsilon_k>0$
such that (for large enough $N$) $f_k(N)\leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\epsilon_k\right)N$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_865.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, (f N k : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 - ε) * N

problems.title: Erdős Problem 867 — coppersmith phillips upper bound
problems.statement:
The current best bounds are due to Coppersmith and Phillips [CoPh96], who prove that the
maximal size of such an $A$ satisfies
$$\lvert A\rvert \leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{512}\right)N+\log N.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_upper_bound :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (2 / 3 - 1 / 512) * (N : ℝ) + Real.log (N : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 875 — deshouillers freiman
problems.statement:
Deshouillers and Freiman [DeFr99, Theorem 1] proved a conjecture of Erdős on the finite version
([874](https://www.erdosproblems.com/874)): for all sufficiently large $N$, every admissible set
$A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfies
$$\lvert A\rvert\leq 2\sqrt{N+\tfrac14}-1.$$
This is sharp: by Straus, the set of $k$ consecutive integers ending at $N$ is admissible if and
only if $k\leq 2\sqrt{N+\frac14}-1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_875.variants.deshouillers_freiman :
    ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → ∀ A : Finset ℕ, (A : Set ℕ) ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N →
      IsAdmissible (A : Set ℕ) → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt ((N : ℝ) + 1 / 4) - 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 875 — erdos nicolas sarkozy
problems.statement:
Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy [ENS91, Theorem 2] constructed an infinite admissible set $A$ with
$$A(x)=\lvert\{a\in A: a\leq x\}\rvert \gg x^{5-2\sqrt6}.$$
The implied constant is positive and the inequality is required for all large $x$. This improves
a result of Erdős [Er62c], who obtained $A(x)\gg x^{c}$ for some unspecified $c>0$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_875.variants.erdos_nicolas_sarkozy :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsAdmissible A ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
      ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, c * (x : ℝ) ^ (5 - 2 * Real.sqrt 6) ≤ (countingFunction A x : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 875 — polynomial gaps
problems.statement:
Since $5-2\sqrt6=(5+2\sqrt6)^{-1}$, the result of [ENS91, Theorem 2] gives
$a_n\ll n^{5+2\sqrt6}$, hence $a_{n+1}-a_n\leq a_{n+1}\ll n^{5+2\sqrt6}$. So every
$c>5+2\sqrt6$ is possible in the main question.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_875.variants.polynomial_gaps (c : ℝ) (hc : 5 + 2 * Real.sqrt 6 < c) :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsAdmissible A ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (gap A n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ c

problems.title: Erdős Problem 878 — H div self liminf finite
problems.statement: Erdős [Er84e] showed that $\liminf_{x\to\infty}H(x)/x<\infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_878.variants.H_div_self_liminf_finite :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, H x / (x : ℝ) ≤ C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 878 — H div self limsup infinite
problems.statement: Erdős [Er84e] showed that $\limsup_{x\to\infty}H(x)/x=\infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_878.variants.H_div_self_limsup_infinite :
    ∀ C : ℝ, ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, C ≤ H x / (x : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 878 — H upper triple log
problems.statement: Erdős [Er84e] proved that $H(x)\ll x\log\log\log x$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_878.variants.H_upper_triple_log :
    H =O[atTop] fun x : ℕ ↦
      (x : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 890 — liminf lower bound
problems.statement:
A question of Erdős and Selfridge [ErSe67], who observe that
$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\geq k+\pi(k)-1$ for every $k$. This follows from
Pólya's theorem that the set of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded gaps - indeed,
$n(n+1)\cdots (n+k-1)$ is divisible by all primes $\leq k$ and, provided $n$ is large, all but at
most one of $n,n+1,\ldots,n+k-1$ has a prime factor $>k$ by Pólya's theorem.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_890.variants.liminf_lower_bound (k : ℕ) :
    liminf (fun n ↦ (∑ i ∈ range k, (ω (n + i) : EReal))) atTop ≥ k + π k - 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 890 — omega limsup
problems.statement: It is a classical fact that $\limsup_{n\to \infty}\omega(n)\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1.$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_890.variants.omega_limsup :
    limsup (fun n ↦ (ω n : EReal) * (log (log n) / log n)) atTop = 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 891 — weisenberg
problems.statement:
Weisenberg has observed that Dickson's conjecture implies the answer is no if we replace
$p_1\cdots p_k$ with $p_1\cdots p_k-1$. Indeed, let $L_k$ be the lowest common multiple of all
integers at most $p_1\cdots p_k$. By Dickson's conjecture [Wikipedia], there are infinitely many
$n'$ such that $\frac{L_k}{m}n'+1$ is prime for all $1\leq m < p_1\cdots p_k$. It follows that,
if $n=L_kn'+1$, then all integers in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k-1)$ have at most $k$ prime factors.

The statement is conditional on Dickson's conjecture, formalised as
`Dickson.dickson_conjecture`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_891.variants.weisenberg (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2)
    (hdickson : type_of% Dickson.dickson_conjecture) :
    ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
      ∀ m ∈ Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ range k, i.nth Nat.Prime) - 1),
      ω m ≤ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 914 — equitable colouring
problems.statement:
Equivalently, every graph with $rm$ vertices and maximum degree at most $m-1$ has a proper vertex
colouring with $m$ colours in which every colour class has exactly $r$ vertices (an equitable
colouring).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_914.variants.equitable_colouring {r m : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) (hm : 1 ≤ m) {V : Type*}
    [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hV : Fintype.card V = r * m)
    (hdeg : G.maxDegree ≤ m - 1) :
    ∃ C : G.Coloring (Fin m), ∀ i, (C.colorClass i).ncard = r

problems.title: Erdős Problem 933 — mahler
problems.statement: Mahler proved (a more general result that implies in particular) that $2^k3^l<n^{1+o(1)}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_933.variants.mahler :
    ∃ c : ℕ → ℝ, (c =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ)) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ((2 ^ k n * 3 ^ l n : ℕ) : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ (1 + c n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 934 — ccjk conjecture false
problems.statement:
The inequality $h_3(d) \leq d^3-d^2+d+2$ conjectured in [CCJK22] is false [KMP26, Conjecture 1.9
and Lemma 3.1]. Here the inequality is stated as `h 3 d + d ^ 2 ≤ d ^ 3 + d + 2`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_934.variants.ccjk_conjecture_false :
    ¬ ∀ d : ℕ, h 3 d + d ^ 2 ≤ d ^ 3 + d + 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 934 — h two
problems.statement:
Erdős and Nešetřil and Bermond, Bond, Paoli, and Peyrat [BBPP83] independently conjectured that
$h_2(d) \leq \tfrac{5}{4}d^2+1$, with equality for even $d$. This was proved by Chung, Gyárfás,
Tuza, and Trotter [CGTT90].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_934.variants.h_two :
    (∀ d : ℕ, 4 * h 2 d ≤ 5 * d ^ 2 + 4) ∧
      ∀ d : ℕ, Even d → 4 * h 2 d = 5 * d ^ 2 + 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 934 — kmp liminf
problems.statement:
Kumar, Mohar and Pragada [KMP26, Theorem 1.11] proved
$$\liminf_{d\to\infty}\frac{h_3(d)}{d^3}\geq \frac{253}{225}.$$
In particular the conjecture of [CCJK22] that $h_t(d)\leq (1+o(1))d^t$ is false for $t=3$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_934.variants.kmp_liminf :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop, (253 / 225 - ε) * (d : ℝ) ^ 3 ≤ (h 3 d : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 934 — lower large t
problems.statement:
The same authors prove that, if $t$ is large, then there are infinitely many $d$ such that
$h_t(d) \geq 0.629^td^t$. See [CCJK22, Proposition 5].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_934.variants.lower_large_t :
    ∃ t₀ : ℕ, ∀ t : ℕ, t₀ ≤ t →
      ∃ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop, ((629 : ℝ) / 1000) ^ t * (d : ℝ) ^ t ≤ (h t d : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 934 — lower liminf
problems.statement:
For every fixed $t\geq 2$, $\liminf_{d\to\infty} h_t(d)/d^t \geq 1$ [CvBK26, Corollary 1.2]. This
confirms, in a strong form, the conjecture of [CCJK22] that $h_t(d)\geq (1-o(1))d^t$ for
infinitely many $d$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_934.variants.lower_liminf :
    ∀ t : ℕ, 2 ≤ t → ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop,
      (1 - ε) * (d : ℝ) ^ t ≤ (h t d : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 — eight
problems.statement:
Cambie has also found solutions when $r=8$.

The source adds that the $r=8$ solution works "even with the sum of $5$ $8$-powerful numbers".
That is a stronger result than this statement, which asks for the $r - 2 = 6$ summands of
`Erdos939Sums`.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_939.variants.eight : (Erdos939Sums 8).Nonempty

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 — finite
problems.statement:
If $r≥4$, are there at most finitely many sums of $r-2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers
that are themselves $r$-powerful?

The answer is no: for every $r \ge 6$ there are infinitely many such sums, see
`erdos_939.variants.infinite_of_six_le`. (For $r = 4$ and $r = 5$ the question is open; for
$r = 4$ no example is known at all, see `erdos_939`.)
A construction in the site's comments, from GPT-5.5 Pro prompted by Price, gives infinitely
many for every $r \ge 6$. This statement quantifies over every $r \ge 4$, so it stays open at
$r = 4$ and $r = 5$. The category is unchanged because the construction is recorded in the
comments and not in the literature.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_939.variants.finite : ¬ ∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939Sums r).Finite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 — infinite of six le
problems.statement:
For every $r \ge 6$ there are infinitely many sums of $r - 2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers that
are themselves $r$-powerful.

A construction, found by GPT-5.5 Pro prompted by Liam Price and recorded in the comments on
[erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/939), expands
$(X+Y)^r = (X-Y)^r + \sum_{j \text{ odd}} 2\binom{r}{j} X^{r-j} Y^j$, splits the $j = 3$ term into
$\lfloor r/2 \rfloor - 2$ distinct pieces to obtain exactly $r - 2$ summands, and takes
$X = q^r$, $Y = B^r$ with $B$ divisible by all primes in the coefficients and $q > B$ a prime not
dividing $B$; varying $q$ gives infinitely many solutions.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_939.variants.infinite_of_six_le : ∀ r ≥ 6, (Erdos939Sums r).Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 — seven
problems.statement: Cambie has also found solutions when $r=7$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_939.variants.seven : (Erdos939Sums 7).Nonempty

problems.title: Erdős Problem 939 — triples
problems.statement:
Are there infinitely many triples of coprime $3$-powerful numbers $a, b, c$ such that $a + b = c$?

The answer is yes. Nitaj [Ni95] proved it, with $2^3\cdot 3^5\cdot 73^3 + 271^3 = 919^3$ as an
example. In Nitaj's construction at least two of $a, b, c$ are perfect cubes. Cohn [Co98]
constructed infinitely many triples of which none is a perfect cube, and Walsh [Wa24] gave a
further construction.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_939.variants.triples :
    {(a,b,c) | ({a, b, c} : Finset ℕ).Coprime ∧
      0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧
      (3).Full a ∧ (3).Full b ∧ (3).Full c ∧
      a + b = c}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 940 — three powerful
problems.statement:
Heath-Brown [He88] has proved that all large numbers are the sum of at most three
$2$-powerful numbers.

This is the case $r = 2$ of `Erdos1107.erdos_1107`, which asks the same question with $r + 1$
summands, and it is stated there as `Erdos1107.erdos_1107.variants.two`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_940.variants.three_powerful :
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, (2).Full s) ∧ x = S.sum

problems.title: Erdős Problem 940 — two
problems.statement:
The set of integers which are the sum of at most two $2$-powerful numbers has density $0$.

Erdős called this 'easy'. Baker and Brüdern [BaBr94] gave the first proof in the literature.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_940.variants.two :
    {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ),
      S.card ≤ 2 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, (2).Full s) ∧ n = S.sum}.HasDensity 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 944 — k sub one not prime
problems.statement:
Lattanzio [La02] proved there exist $k$-critical graphs without critical edges for all $k$ such that
$k - 1$ is not prime.

[La02] Lattanzio, John J., A note on a conjecture of {D}irac. Discrete Math. (2002), 323--330
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_944.variants.dirac_conjecture.k_sub_one_not_prime (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k)
    (h : ¬ (k - 1).Prime) : ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.IsErdos944 k 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950 — debruijn erdos turan
problems.statement:
This function was considered by de Bruijn, Erdős, and Turán, who showed that
$\sum_{n<x}f(n)\sim \sum_{n<x}f(n)^2\sim x$. They gave no proofs, but a proof of the (harder) second
claim is given by Gorodetsky here [mathoverflow/508491].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_950.variants.debruijn_erdos_turan :
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.range x, f n) ~[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ)) ∧
    (fun x : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.range x, (f n) ^ 2) ~[atTop] (fun x : ℕ ↦ (x : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 950 — weaker pi implies f
problems.statement:
He notes that if $\pi(x)< \pi(y)+O\left(\frac{x-y}{\log x}\right)$ for all $y<x-(\log x)^C$ for
some constant $C>0$ then $f(n)\ll \log\log\log n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_950.variants.weaker_pi_implies_f
    (h : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∃ K > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, ∀ y : ℕ,
      (y : ℝ) < x - (Real.log x) ^ C →
      (π x : ℝ) < (π y : ℝ) + K * ((x - y : ℝ) / Real.log x)) :
    f =O[atTop] fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 955 — pollack pomerance thompson bound
problems.statement:
Pollack, Pomerance, and Thompson [PPT18] prove that if $\epsilon(x)=o(1)$ and $A\subset \mathbb{N}$
has size at most $x^{1/2+\epsilon(x)}$ then $\#\{ n\leq x: s(n)\in A\} =o(x)$ as $x\to \infty$. It
follows that (using $s(n)\ll n\log\log n$) if $A$ grows like
$\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert\leq x^{1/2+o(1)}$ then $s^{-1}(A)$ has density $0$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_955.variants.pollack_pomerance_thompson_bound :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (ε : ℕ → ℝ),
      Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) →
      (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (count (· ∈ A) n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 / 2 : ℝ) + ε n)) →
      { x | s x ∈ A }.HasDensity 0

problems.title: Erdős Problem 962 — tang lower bound
problems.statement:
Tang's lower bound [Tang]:

$\log k(n) \ge (1/\sqrt{2} - o(1)) * \sqrt{\log n * \log \log n}$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_962.variants.tang_lower_bound :
    ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
          (1 / sqrt 2 - ε n) *
              sqrt (log n * log (log n))
            ≤ log (k n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 962 — tao upper bound
problems.statement:
Tao's upper bound [Tao]:

$k(n) \le (1 + o(1)) * n^{1/2}$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_962.variants.tao_upper_bound :
    ∃ ε : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, |ε n| < δ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
          (k n : ℝ) ≤ (1 + ε n) * sqrt n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 971 — infinite sequence
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er49c] proved that the statement in `erdos_971` holds for infinitely many values of `d`.

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_971.variants.infinite_sequence :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ),
      {d : ℕ | C * (d.totient : ℝ) ≤
        #{a < d | a.Coprime d ∧ (leastCongruentPrime a d : ℝ) > (1 + c) * d.totient * log d}}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 971 — many small
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er49c] proved that for any `ε > 0` we have `p(a, d) < ε * φ(d) * log d` for `≫_ε φ(d)` many
values of `a` (for all large `d`).

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_971.variants.many_small :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ d in atTop,
      C * (d.totient : ℝ) ≤
        #{a < d | a.Coprime d ∧ (leastCongruentPrime a d : ℝ) < ε * d.totient * log d}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 973 — le one
problems.statement:
Erdős proved (as described on p.35 of [Tu84b]) that such a sequence does exist with
$\lvert z_i\rvert\leq 1$. Indeed, Erdős' construction gives a value of $C\approx 1.32$.

    ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,

problems.title: Erdős Problem 973 — tang
problems.statement:
Tang notes in the comments that Theorem 6.1 of [Tu84b] implies that, if $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$
for all $i$, then
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert \geq (2e)^{-(1+o(1))n}$.

    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ z : ℕ → ℂ,
      (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) →
      ∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1),

        (2 * Real.exp 1) ^ (-(1 + f n) * (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 976 — erdos
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er52c] improved the bound of Nagell and Ricci to
$$F_f(n) \gg n(\log n)^{\log\log\log n}.$$
More precisely, [Er52c] gives $F_f(n) > n(\log n)^{c\log\log\log n}$ for some constant
$c = c(f) > 0$; the site omits $c$.

never published it. A proof was provided by Tenenbaum [Te90].

problems.statement:
Erdős could not even prove $h(n)\geq n$. Pach has shown $h(n) < n^{\log_2 3}$.
Erdős, Füredi, and Pach [EFPR93] have improved this to
$h(n) < n\exp(c\sqrt{\log n})$ for some constant $c>0$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 981 — first time
problems.statement:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ and $f_\epsilon(p)$ be the smallest integer $m$ such that $\sum_{n\leq m} \left(\frac{n}{p}\right)<\epsilon m$. Prove that
$$\sum_{p<x}f_\epsilon(p)\sim c_\epsilon \frac{x}{\log x}$$
for some $c_\epsilon > 0$.

$$f(\pi(n)+1,n)=2\pi(n^{1/2})+o_A\left(\frac{n^{1/2}}{(\log n)^A}\right)$$
for any $A>0$.

$$
\left\lvert (\# \theta_i \in I) - \frac{\lvert I\rvert}{2\pi}d\right\rvert \leq n-1,
$$
and noted this is essentially sharp since $f(x)=(x^{p}-1)^{n-1}$ has $n$ non-zero coefficients and
has $1$ as a positive real zero of multiplicity $n-1$ (although for this $f$ the parameter $M$
becomes very large).

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 29 — variant
problems.statement:
The known result [Br13, Theorem 6.5; CrSi10; Sa10]: for each $K$ there is $c(K) > 0$
such that every $K$-approximate group $A$ has a set $S$ (not necessarily contained in $A$) with
$|S| \ge c(K)|A|$ and $S^8 \subseteq A^4$. The open problem asks whether $c(K)$ can be bounded
below by $C K^{-c}$ for absolute constants $C, c > 0$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_29.variant :
    ∀ K : ℝ, 1 ≤ K →
      ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ -- Allow c to depend on K.
        ∀ {G : Type*} [Group G] [DecidableEq G] (A : Finset G),
          IsApproximateSubgroup K (A : Set G) →
            ∃ S : Finset G, -- No S ⊆ A requirement in this variant.
              c * (A.card : ℝ) ≤ (S.card : ℝ) ∧
              S ^ 8 ⊆ A ^ 4

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 44 — less than sqrt
problems.statement: The answer is affirmative if the primes are all less than $N^{1/2}$, by the large sieve. [Gr24]
problems.lean:
theorem green_44.variants.less_than_sqrt :
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (p : Fin 1000 → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin 1000) → Finset (ZMod (p i))),
      let remaining := (Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun x => ∀ i, (x : ZMod (p i)) ∉ A i)
      (∀ i, (p i).Prime) →
      StrictMono p →
      (p 999) ^ 2 < N →
      (∀ i, (A i).card = (p i) / 2) →
      10 * remaining.card ≤ N

problems.title: Voloch's theorem.
problems.statement:
**Voloch's theorem.** If $p$ is an odd prime and $A \subset \mathbb{F}_p^2$ is a set meeting every
line in at most 2 points, with $|A| > \frac{44}{45} p + \frac{8}{9}$, then $A$ lies on a conic
[BaLa19, Theorem 52], due to Voloch [Vo90]. This is the affine form of the theorem for planar arcs
in $\mathrm{PG}(2, p)$: a set of affine points is an arc in $\mathrm{PG}(2, p)$ if and only if it
meets every affine line in at most 2 points, and the affine equation $Q(x, y, 1) = 0$ of a conic
$Q = 0$ through $A$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $2$ vanishing on $A$. We assume $p$
odd, as in [BaLa19, Section 15.3].
problems.lean:
theorem green_68.variants.voloch :
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], p ≠ 2 →
      ∀ A : Finset (Fin 2 → ZMod p), MeetsLinesInAtMost 2 A →
        (44 : ℝ) / 45 * p + 8 / 9 < A.card →
          ∃ F : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) (ZMod p),
            F ≠ 0 ∧ F.totalDegree ≤ 2 ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, MvPolynomial.eval a F = 0

problems.title: Babai (1979): long cycles in vertex-transitive graphs.
problems.statement:
**Babai (1979): long cycles in vertex-transitive graphs.**

Every finite connected vertex-transitive graph on $n \ge 3$ vertices contains a cycle of length
at least $\sqrt{3n}$.

*Reference:* [Ba79].

problems.title: Christofides–Hladký–Máthé (2014): Hamiltonian-path corollary of the dense case.
problems.statement:
**Christofides–Hladký–Máthé (2014): Hamiltonian-path corollary of the dense case.**

For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $n_0$ such that every connected vertex-transitive graph on
$n \ge n_0$ vertices with minimum degree at least $\varepsilon n$ has a Hamiltonian path.
This is a corollary of the Hamiltonian-cycle result in [CHM14, Theorem 2].

*Reference:* [CHM14].
problems.lean:
theorem lovasz_conjecture.variants.dense :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj], n₀ ≤ Fintype.card V →
      G.Connected → IsVertexTransitive G → ε * Fintype.card V ≤ G.minDegree →
      HasHamiltonianPath G

Every $r$-regular Hamiltonian graph with $r \ge 300$ has a second Hamiltonian cycle.

*Reference:* [Th98].

problems.title: Optimal monotone families for the discrete isoperimetric inequality — weak kahn kalai
problems.statement:
Weaker version proven by Kahn–Kalai (2006): for every fixed $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a constant
$C = C_\varepsilon$ such that for every monotone increasing family $F$ with critical probability
$t$, i.e. $\mu_t(F) = 1/2$, there is some $p \in [n^{-\varepsilon} t, t]$ for which $F$ is
$(C \log(1/p), p)$-optimal.
problems.lean:
theorem mathoverflow_10799.variants.weak_kahn_kalai :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ) (_ : 2 ≤ n)
    (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (_ : IsMonotoneIncreasing F)
    (t : ℝ) (_ : 0 < t) (_ : t < 1) (_ : μFamily t F = 1 / 2),
    ∃ p, (n : ℝ) ^ (-ε) * t ≤ p ∧ p ≤ t ∧ IsOptimalWith C p F

problems.title: Scott–Sudakov (2011): the best known general bound.
problems.statement:
**Scott–Sudakov (2011): the best known general bound.**

Every connected graph on `n` vertices has cop number at most `n / 2^((1 - o(1)) √(log₂ n))`.
This (together with the same bound obtained independently by Lu–Peng and by Frieze, Krivelevich
and Loh) is the best known bound towards Meyniel's conjecture.

*Reference:* [SS11].

      ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.Connected →
        (copNumber G : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card V : ℝ) /
          2 ^ ((1 - f (Fintype.card V)) * Real.sqrt (Real.logb 2 (Fintype.card V)))

Sidorenko's inequality holds when `H = K_{s,t}` is a complete bipartite graph. This is one

problems.title: The bound $2n - 2$ would be sharp.
problems.statement:
**The bound $2n - 2$ would be sharp.**

For every $n \ge 2$ there is an oriented tree on $n$ vertices — the out-star, with arcs from a
centre to the $n - 1$ other vertices — that embeds in no regular tournament on $2n - 3$ vertices:
every vertex of such a tournament has out-degree $n - 2 < n - 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem sumner_conjecture.variants.sharp (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ (W : Type) (_ : Fintype W) (_ : DecidableEq W) (D : Digraph W) (_ : DecidableRel D.Adj),
      Fintype.card W = n ∧ IsOrientedTree D ∧
      ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (_ : DecidableEq V) (G : Digraph V) (_ : DecidableRel G.Adj),
        Fintype.card V = 2 * n - 3 ∧ G.IsTournament ∧ ¬ Embeds D G

problems.title: The Suen–Tarr inequality (2012).
problems.statement:
**The Suen–Tarr inequality (2012).**

For all finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$,
$\gamma(G \,\square\, H) \ge \tfrac12\,\gamma(G)\,\gamma(H) +
\tfrac12\min\{\gamma(G), \gamma(H)\}$, improving the Clark–Suen bound.

*Reference:* [SuTa12].
problems.lean:
theorem vizing_conjecture.variants.suen_tarr
    {α β : Type} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β) :
    G.dominationNumber * H.dominationNumber + min G.dominationNumber H.dominationNumber ≤
      2 * (G □ H).dominationNumber

problems.title: Agoh-Giuga conjecture — isStrongGiuga growth
problems.statement:
Let `G(X)` denote the number of exceptions `n ≤ X` to Giuga’s conjecture.
Then for `X` larger than an absolute constant which can be made
explicit, `G(X) ≪ X^{1/2} log X`.
Ref: Vicentiu Tipu, _A Note on Giuga’s Conjecture_
problems.lean:
theorem agoh_giuga.variants.isStrongGiuga_growth
    (G : ℕ → ℕ) (hG : G = fun x => Finset.Icc 1 x |>.filter IsStrongGiuga |>.card) :
    ∃ N O, ∀ n ≥ N, G n ≤ O * (n : ℝ).sqrt * (n : ℝ).log

problems.title: The Graham–Pollak theorem (1971).
problems.statement:
**The Graham–Pollak theorem (1971).**

The edge set of $K_n$ cannot be partitioned into fewer than $n - 1$ complete bipartite
subgraphs, and $n - 1$ suffice: $\operatorname{bp}(K_n) = n - 1$.

*Reference:* [GP71].
problems.lean:
theorem alon_saks_seymour_conjecture.variants.graham_pollak (n : ℕ) :
    bicliquePartitionNumber (completeGraph (Fin n)) = n - 1

problems.title: The Dixmier Conjecture — poisson implication
problems.statement:
If the Poisson conjecture in dimension `n` holds over every field of characteristic zero,
then so does the Dixmier conjecture in dimension `n`. This is $CPC(n, 0) \Longrightarrow
CDC(n, 0)$ in [AvdE07], Theorem 7, where both statements quantify over all fields of
characteristic zero (Notations 5 and 7). The proof reduces to prime characteristic and
uses the Azumaya property of Weyl algebras in characteristic `p`.
problems.lean:
theorem dixmier_conjecture.variants.poisson_implication (n : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ (L : Type) [Field L] [CharZero L], PoissonConjectureFor L n)
    (L : Type) [Field L] [CharZero L] : DixmierConjectureFor L n

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Simultaneously Small Entropies — all bases
problems.statement:
Problem 10.53, in the stronger form that asks for every base at once: there is an irrational
real number $\xi$ such that $E(\xi) < \log 2$ and $E(\xi, b) < \log b$ for every integer
$b \ge 2$. Answered by Temur [Tem26].
problems.lean:
theorem problem_10_53.variants.all_bases :
    ∃ ξ : ℝ, Irrational ξ ∧ cfEntropy ξ < (Real.log 2 : EReal) ∧
      ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → baseEntropy b ξ < (Real.log b : EReal)

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Simultaneously Small Entropies — uncountable
problems.statement:
There are uncountably many numbers as in Problem 10.53. This follows from a result of Broderick,
Bugeaud, Fishman, Kleinbock and Weiss [BBFKW10] applied to the Gauss-Cantor set
$\{[0; 1, a_1, 1, a_2, \ldots] : a_j \in \{1, 2\}\}$, as observed in [Tem26].
problems.lean:
theorem problem_10_53.variants.uncountable :
    ¬ {ξ : ℝ | Irrational ξ ∧ cfEntropy ξ < (Real.log 2 : EReal) ∧
      ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → baseEntropy b ξ < (Real.log b : EReal)}.Countable

problems.title: Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Pisot orbits on the Cantor set — almost every
problems.statement:
The hypothesis $\xi \in C(\alpha)$ cannot be dropped: by Koksma's metric theorem [Kok35],
for a fixed $\alpha > 1$ the sequence $(\xi \alpha^n)_{n \ge 1}$ is uniformly distributed
modulo one for Lebesgue-almost every $\xi$. Problem 10.61 asks a null set of starting
points to defeat an almost-everywhere law.
problems.lean:
theorem problem_10_61.variants.almost_every (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) :
    ∀ᵐ ξ ∂(MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ),
      IsEquidistributedModuloOne fun n : ℕ => ξ * α ^ (n + 1)

problems.title: Norin–Turcotte (2024): the burning number conjecture holds asymptotically.
problems.statement:
**Norin–Turcotte (2024): the burning number conjecture holds asymptotically.**

For every `ε > 0`, every sufficiently large connected graph on `n` vertices can be burned in
at most `(1 + ε) √n` rounds.

*Reference:* [NT24].
problems.lean:
theorem burning_number_conjecture.variants.norin_turcotte (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.Connected →
      n₀ ≤ Fintype.card V →
        (burningNumber G : ℝ) ≤ (1 + ε) * Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V)

problems.title: Paths attain the conjectured bound
problems.statement:
**Paths attain the conjectured bound** (Bonato–Janssen–Roshanbin [BJR16]).

The burning number of the path on `n ≥ 1` vertices is exactly `⌈√n⌉`, so the bound in the
burning number conjecture cannot be improved.
problems.lean:
theorem burning_number_conjecture.variants.path (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    burningNumber (SimpleGraph.pathGraph n) = ⌈Real.sqrt n⌉₊

problems.title: Stark–Heegner theorem
problems.statement:
**Stark–Heegner theorem** : For any squarefree integer `d < 0`, the class number of the imaginary
quadratic field Q(√d) is one if and only if `d ∈ {-1, -2, -3, -7, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163}`.

The pair `(SAT, ¬SAT)` is then a disjoint NP pair, and every disjoint NP pair `(A, B)` reduces

problems.title: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture — bombieri vinogradov
problems.statement:

$\theta < 1/2$. This result may be regarded as an averaged form of the generalized
Riemann hypothesis.

problems.title: Goldfeld's conjecture — two le
problems.statement:
**Goldfeld's conjecture** ([Goldfeld1979], Conjecture B), in the form stated in the
introduction of [Smith2025], in the case $2 \leq r$: a density $0$ of the quadratic twists $E^d$
of an elliptic curve $E$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ have rank $r$.

For the Mordell–Weil rank used here this is an unconditional theorem: by Theorem 1.1 of
[Smith2025], $100\%$ of the twists $E^d$ have $2^\infty$-Selmer corank $0$ or $1$, and the
Mordell–Weil rank is at most the $2^\infty$-Selmer corank (equation (1.1) there), so the twists
of rank at least $2$ have density $0$. The corresponding statement for the analytic rank is
open.
problems.lean:
theorem goldfeld_conjecture.variants.two_le (E : RatEllipticCurve) (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) :
    atTop.Tendsto
      (fun H ↦ ({d ∈ twistIndexLE H | E.twistRank d = r}.ncard / (twistIndexLE H).ncard : ℝ))
      (𝓝 0)

Dirac gave an example of a $6$-chromatic critical graph with minimum degree $>n/2$.

Dirac's graphs join two disjoint odd cycles of length $n/2$ [Di52], [Ma15]. Here we state that
there are such graphs for infinitely many $n$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1046 — diameter
problems.statement:
Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58] conjecture that if $\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ is
connected then its diameter is at least $2$.

The answer is yes, and connectedness is not needed. For monic $f$ of degree $n \geq 1$ the set
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ has logarithmic capacity $1$ [Ra95, Theorem 5.2.5], and Pólya
[Po28] proved $\mathrm{cap}(E) \leq \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{diam}(E)$ for every compact
$E \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, see [BPS02, (1.2)]. Hence the diameter is at least $2$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1046.variants.diameter : ∀ f : ℂ[X], f.Monic →
    IsConnected (closedLemniscate f) → 2 ≤ Metric.ediam (closedLemniscate f)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1048 — diam ge two is best
problems.statement:
If $0\leq r\leq 1/2$ then the component which contains $0$ must have diameter $\geq 2$, which
$f(z)=z^n$ shows is best possible.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1048.variants.diam_ge_two_is_best (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet ((X : ℂ[X]) ^ n)) 0) = 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1066 — pach toth
problems.statement:
Erdős initially thought that $g(n)=n/3$, but Chung and Graham, and independently Pach, gave a
construction that shows $g(n)\leq \frac{6}{19}n$. Pach and Tóth [PaTo96] improved this to
$g(n)\leq \frac{5}{16}n$.

Since $g(1) = 1$, the bound cannot hold for all $n$, so it is stated for infinitely many $n$,
with $5/16$ replaced by $5/16+\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (g n : ℝ) ≤ (5 / 16 + ε) * n

where $\alpha=1-2^{-1/3}\approx 0.206299$: for some $C$ and all large $x$, $A(x)$ lies between
$(\log\log x)^{-C}$ and $(\log\log x)^{C}$ times $x/(\log x)^{\alpha}$.

        (A x : ℝ) ≤ x / Real.log x ^ alpha * Real.log (Real.log x) ^ C

problems.title: Linear lower bound (ZFC, [EHS82])
problems.statement:
**Linear lower bound (ZFC, [EHS82])**: Every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ has
$h_G(n) \geq c \cdot n$ for some positive constant $c > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$
(i.e., the *linear* lower bound $h_G(n) \gg n$ is known).

This follows from the fact that every graph with uncountable chromatic number contains
$\aleph_1$ vertex-disjoint odd cycles of some fixed odd length $\ell$: any induced subgraph
on $n$ vertices containing $\gg n / \ell$ such cycles requires removing $\gg n$ edges to
become bipartite.

This is a *strictly weaker* statement than the headline `erdos_111`, which asks for
$h_G(n)/n \to \infty$ (i.e., $h_G(n)$ grows *super-linearly* — the constant `c` could be
taken arbitrarily large for a fixed graph $G$). Whether the linear lower bound can be
improved to super-linear remains the open question.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_111.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 →
      ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
        ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, c * n ≤ hG G n

problems.title: Upper bound existence (Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi [EHS82])
problems.statement:
**Upper bound existence (Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi [EHS82])**: There exists a graph $G$ with
chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that $h_G(n) \ll n^{3/2}$, i.e., there is a constant $C > 0$
with $h_G(n) \leq C \cdot n^{3/2}$ for all $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_111.variants.upper_bound_existence :
    ∃ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1 ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (hG G n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1119 — erdos wetzel
problems.statement:
Erdős's theorem [Er64g], answering a question of Wetzel: if $\mathfrak{c} > \aleph_1$,
then every family of entire functions taking only countably many distinct values at each
point $z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$ is itself countable.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1119.variants.erdos_wetzel (h : ℵ_ 1 < 𝔠) (F : Set (ℂ → ℂ))
    (hF : ∀ f ∈ F, Differentiable ℂ f)
    (hval : ∀ z₀ : ℂ, {y : ℂ | ∃ f ∈ F, f z₀ = y}.Countable) :
    F.Countable

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1119 — erdos wetzel ch
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er64g] also showed that the previous statement fails under the continuum
hypothesis: if $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$, then there is an **uncountable** family of
entire functions taking only countably many distinct values at each point
$z_0 \in \mathbb{C}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1119.variants.erdos_wetzel_ch (h : 𝔠 = ℵ_ 1) :
    ∃ F : Set (ℂ → ℂ), (∀ f ∈ F, Differentiable ℂ f) ∧
      (∀ z₀ : ℂ, {y : ℂ | ∃ f ∈ F, f z₀ = y}.Countable) ∧
      ¬ F.Countable

Erdős [Er46] proved that $f(n)=c\log n$ for some $c\in\mathbb{R}$ if $A$ is empty, that is, if

theorem erdos_1122.variants.monotone (f : ℕ → ℝ)

    ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ n > 0, f n = c * Real.log n
