problems.title: Erdős Problem 1129 — canonical
problems.statement:
The theorem of Kilgore [Ki77], [Ki78] and de Boor and Pinkus [dBPi78] for canonical node sets
($x_1=-1$, $x_n=1$), as in [Ib16, Section 3.7] and [RaVa15, Definition 2.7 and Proposition 2.8]:
the canonical node sets that minimise $\Lambda$ among all node sets are exactly the canonical node
sets whose local maxima $\lambda_i=\max_{[x_i,x_{i+1}]}\sum_k\lvert l_k\rvert$ between consecutive
nodes are all equal. The two outer gaps $[-1,x_1]$ and $[x_n,1]$ are single points for canonical
nodes and are not used.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1129.variants.canonical (n : ℕ) :
    {x : Fin n → ℝ | IsCanonical x ∧ IsMinimiser x} = {x | IsCanonical x ∧ Equioscillates x}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1129 — chebyshev upper bound
problems.statement:
This is best possible: for the zeros of the Chebyshev polynomial $T_n$ there is an absolute
constant $c_2$ with $\max_{x\in[-1,1]}\sum_k\lvert l_k(x)\rvert<\frac{2}{\pi}\log n+c_2$
([Er61c, p. 236], [Er67, p. 66]). [Ib16, Section 3.2] gives the precise asymptotics.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1129.variants.chebyshev_upper_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ), 1 ≤ n → IsChebyshevNodes x →
      lebesgueConstant x < 2 / Real.pi * Real.log n + C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1129 — erdos lower bound
problems.statement:
Faber [Fa14] proved $\Lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\gg \log n$ for all choices of $x_i$, and Bernstein
[Be31] announced $\Lambda>(\frac{2}{\pi}-o(1))\log n$ (see [Er61c, p. 235]). Erdős [Er61c,
Theorem 1] improved this: there is an absolute constant $c_1$ such that for all
$-1\le x_1<\cdots<x_n\le 1$
$$\max_{x\in[-1,1]}\sum_k\lvert l_k(x)\rvert>\frac{2}{\pi}\log n-c_1.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1129.variants.erdos_lower_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ), 1 ≤ n → IsNodeSet x →
      2 / Real.pi * Real.log n - C < lebesgueConstant x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1129 — free nodes not unique
problems.statement:
Without the canonical hypothesis the minimiser of $\Lambda$ is not unique. For every $n\ge 3$
there are uncountably many node sets $x_1<\dots<x_n$ in $[-1,1]$ with the minimal Lebesgue
constant [RaVa15, Theorem 2.5]. The reason is affine invariance. Rescaling a node set to a
canonical one keeps its local maxima between consecutive nodes and does not increase $\Lambda$
([Ib16, Section 2.1 (e)]), so the minimal Lebesgue constant $\Lambda^*$ is attained by the
canonical minimiser $x^*$. The shrunk node set $x^*/\tau$ with $\tau\ge 1$ has
$\Lambda(x^*/\tau)=\max_{\lvert u\rvert\le\tau}L_{x^*}(u)$. Since $L_{x^*}(\pm 1)=1<\Lambda^*$ for
$n\ge 3$, this is still $\Lambda^*$ for all $\tau\ge 1$ close to $1$ (see the proof of
[RaVa15, Theorem 2.5]). For $n=4$ the node sets
$\pm 1/\tau,\pm t/\tau$ with $1\le\tau\le b$ for a constant $b\approx 1.0433$, where $t$ is as
in `erdos_1129.variants.four_nodes`, are all optimal [RaVa15, Theorem 4.2].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1129.variants.free_nodes_not_unique (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    ¬ {x : Fin n → ℝ | IsMinimiser x}.Countable

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1129 — three nodes
problems.statement:
For $n=3$ the canonical minimiser is $-1,0,1$, with $\Lambda=\frac54$ (Bernstein [Be31], see
[RaVa15, Section 2]).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1129.variants.three_nodes :
    {x : Fin 3 → ℝ | IsCanonical x ∧ IsMinimiser x} = ({![(-1 : ℝ), 0, 1]} : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) ∧
      lebesgueConstant (![(-1 : ℝ), 0, 1] : Fin 3 → ℝ) = 5 / 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1129 — unique
problems.statement:
Kilgore [Ki78] and de Boor and Pinkus [dBPi78] proved that for $n\ge 2$ there is at most one
canonical node set whose local maxima $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{n-1}$ are all equal, and that it
is symmetric about $0$ ([Ib16, Section 3.7], [RaVa15, Proposition 2.8]). A canonical minimiser
exists ([RaVa15, Section 2]) and must equioscillate ([Ki77], [Ib16, Section 3.7]), so there is
exactly one such node set, and hence a unique canonical minimiser of $\Lambda$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1129.variants.unique (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃! x : Fin n → ℝ, IsCanonical x ∧ Equioscillates x

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1130 — erdos sqrt
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er47, Theorem 2, pp. 1171-1172] proved that for nodes $x_1\le\cdots\le x_n$ in $[-1,1]$
there is an $i$ with $\max_{x\in[x_i,x_{i+1}]}\sum_k\lvert l_k(x)\rvert<\sqrt n$, that is,
$\Upsilon(x_1,\ldots,x_n)<\sqrt n$. The paper allows coinciding nodes (then it calls the claim
obvious); here the nodes are distinct. We take $n\ge 2$: for $n=1$ the sum is identically $1$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1130.variants.erdos_sqrt (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (x : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hx : IsNodeSet x) :
    upsilon x < Real.sqrt n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1130 — log bound

It follows from `erdos_1130.variants.erdos_inequality` and the bound for Chebyshev nodes in
[Er61c, p. 236] that
$$\Upsilon(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\le\frac{2}{\pi}\log n+O(1).$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_1130.variants.log_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ), 1 ≤ n → IsNodeSet x →
      upsilon x ≤ 2 / Real.pi * Real.log n + C

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1140 — at most one exception
problems.statement:
The known such $n$ are $2,5,7,13,31,61,181,199$. It is known that these are, with at most one
exception, all such $n$. An even such $n$ must be prime (take $x = 0$), so $n = 2$. Theorem 4.1
of Epure and Gica [EpGi10] implies that the only such

other exception.

$F(n)\geq n-1$ ([BEFRS80, p. 193]).

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1182 — befrs lower
problems.statement:
Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp [BEFRS80, Theorem 1(a)] proved
$$\frac{17n+1}{15}\leq F(n),$$
the lower bound for all $n\geq 4$.

We state the integer-part version $n+\lfloor (2n+1)/15\rfloor\le F(n)$, which is what the proof
gives (the number $k$ of extra edges there is an integer with $0\le k\le (2n+1)/15$) and which
follows from the printed bound because $n+\lfloor (2n+1)/15\rfloor\leq(17n+1)/15$.

    n + (2 * n + 1) / 15 ≤ F n

degree are not $3$-good. In [BBH98, p. 6], of which Brandt is a coauthor, it is stated without

$$2^{c^{\frac{k}{\log k}}}\leq F(k) \leq c_0^{(\frac{1}{5}+o(1))2^k},$$
where $c>0$ is some absolute constant and $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$ is the square of the 'Vardi
constant' $1.26408\cdots$. The lower bound is due to Konyagin [Ko14] and the upper bound to
Elsholtz and Planitzer [ElPl21]. (erdosproblems.com gives $c_0=1.26408\cdots$;
[ElPl21, Remark 3] gives $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$.)

[Ko14, Theorem 1] states the lower bound in the explicit form
$$F(k) \geq \exp\left(\exp\left(\left(\frac{(\log 2)(\log 3)}{3}+o(1)\right)
\frac{k}{\log k}\right)\right) \quad (k \to \infty),$$
which is the statement formalised here.

    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧ ∀ᶠ k : ℕ in atTop,
      exp (exp ((log 2 * log 3 / 3 + o k) * ((k : ℝ) / log k))) ≤ F k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 148 — upper bound
problems.statement:
The current best bounds known are
$$2^{c^{\frac{k}{\log k}}}\leq F(k) \leq c_0^{(\frac{1}{5}+o(1))2^k},$$
where $c>0$ is some absolute constant and $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$ is the square of the 'Vardi
constant' $1.26408\cdots$. The lower bound is due to Konyagin [Ko14] and the upper bound to
Elsholtz and Planitzer [ElPl21]. (erdosproblems.com gives $c_0=1.26408\cdots$;
[ElPl21, Remark 3] gives $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$.)

[ElPl21, Corollary 3(2)] shows that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all $k \geq k(\varepsilon)$,
the number $f_k(1,1) \geq F(k)$ of solutions with $n_1 \leq \cdots \leq n_k$ is less than

problems.title: Erdős Problem 22 — bollobas erdos lower
problems.statement:
The construction of Bollobás and Erdős [BoEr76]: for every $\epsilon > 0$ and $\delta > 0$,
for all sufficiently large $n$ there is a $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices with independence
number at most $\delta n$ and at least $(1/8 - \epsilon)n^2$ edges. Together with
`erdos_22.variants.szemeredi_upper` this shows that the Ramsey–Turán density of $K_4$ is $1/8$.

    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ δ * n ∧ (1 / 8 - ε) * n ^ 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card

problems.statement:

independence number is sublinear in $n$ has at most $(1/8 + o(1))n^2$ edges. That is, for every
$\epsilon > 0$ there is a $\delta > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, every
$K_4$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\alpha(G) \leq \delta n$ has at most
$(1/8 + \epsilon)n^2$ edges.
problems.lean:

    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), G.CliqueFree 4 →
        (G.indepNum : ℝ) ≤ δ * n →
        (G.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ≤ (1 / 8 + ε) * n ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 377 — ae
problems.statement:
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
$$
  \gamma_0 = \sum_{k = 2}^{\infty} \frac{\log k}{2^k}
$$
then for almost all integers $f(m) = \gamma_0 + o(1)$, i.e. for every $\varepsilon > 0$ the set of
$n$ with $|f(n) - \gamma_0| < \varepsilon$ has natural density one.

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_377.variants.ae (γ₀ : ℝ) (hγ₀ : γ₀ = ∑' (k : ℕ), (k + 2 : ℝ).log / 2 ^ (k + 2)) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), {n : ℕ | |sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n - γ₀| < ε}.HasDensity 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 377 — i
problems.statement:
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
$$
  \gamma_0 = \sum_{k = 2}^{\infty} \frac{\log k}{2^k}
$$
then
$$
  \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{1}{x}\sum_{n\leq x} f(n) = \gamma_0
$$

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.

      atTop (𝓝 γ₀)

Erdős and Obláth observed that the Bertrand-style fact (first proved by Breusch [Br32]) that, if

2! + 5^2 = 3^3\\
4! + 1^4 = 5^2
$$

    { x : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ | let (a, k, p) := x; p.Prime ∧ Odd p ∧

    {(1, 1, 3), (5, 3, 3), (1, 2, 5)}

problems.title: Erdős Problem 408 — ford konyagin luca
problems.statement:
The third question asks what can be said about the largest prime factor $P^+(\phi_k(n))$ when,
say, $k = \log\log n$; it is open-ended and is not formalised. The site remarks that it is likely
true that, if $k \to \infty$ however slowly with $n$, then $P^+(\phi_k(n)) \leq n^{o(1)}$ for
almost all $n$.

Ford, Konyagin and Luca [FKL10, Theorem 5] proved that for every $\epsilon > 0$ and $\delta > 0$
there is an integer $k$ such that, for all large $x$, at least $(1 - \epsilon)x$ integers
$n \leq x$ satisfy $P^+(\phi_k(n)) \leq x^{\delta}$. Since $P^+(\phi(m)) \leq P^+(m)$, this gives
the remark above for every $k = k(n) \to \infty$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_408.variants.ford_konyagin_luca (ε δ : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, (1 - ε) * x ≤
      ((Finset.Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊).filter fun n ↦
        ((Nat.totient^[k] n).maxPrimeFac : ℝ) ≤ x ^ δ).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 408 — pillai
problems.statement:
Pillai [Pi29] proved that, for all $n \geq 2$,
$$\left\lfloor \frac{\log n - \log 2}{\log 3} \right\rfloor + 1 \leq f(n) \leq
  \left\lfloor \frac{\log n}{\log 2} \right\rfloor + 1.$$
These are Theorems I and III of [Pi29]; Pillai's function $R(n)$ is the least $r$ with
$\phi_r(n) = 1$, which is $f(n)$. The lower bound is attained at $n = 2 \cdot 3^k$, and
$f(2^k) = k$ (`Erdos408.f_two_pow`), so the upper bound cannot be replaced by $f(n) < \log_2 n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_408.variants.pillai (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ⌊(Real.log n - Real.log 2) / Real.log 3⌋₊ + 1 ≤ f n ∧
      f n ≤ ⌊Real.log n / Real.log 2⌋₊ + 1

Erdős proved that the barrier set for `expProd` is infinite and even has positive density.

`HasPosDensity` is the right reading rather than positive lower density. In [Er79d] this is
Theorem 1, "the density of integers satisfying (2) is positive", where `d₀(n) = ∏ αᵢ` is
`expProd`. The averaging argument there bounds the density below, but Erdős states the existence
separately on the last page: "With a little more trouble, I can prove that the density of
integers `n` for which `n` is a barrier for `d₀(n)` exists." He goes further, that if `αᵢ` is the
density of `n` with `max_{m<n} (m + d₀(m)) = n + i`, then every `αᵢ` exists and they sum to `1`.

[Er79d] Erdős, P., *Some unconventional problems in number theory*.
Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 420 — rankin frequently lt two
problems.statement:
Erdős, Graham, Ivić and Pomerance proved [EGIP96, Corollary 2] that for infinitely many $n$,
$$K(n) > \frac{\log n \cdot \log\log n \cdot \log\log\log\log n}{9(\log\log\log n)^3},$$
with $K(n)$ as in the module docstring. Equivalently,
$F(f,n) < 2$ for infinitely many $n$, where $f(n)$ is the right-hand side.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_420.variants.rankin_frequently_lt_two :
    ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, F (fun m ↦ Real.log m * Real.log (Real.log m) *
      Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (Real.log m))) /
        (9 * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log m)) ^ 3)) n < 2

problems.title: Shiu's theorem
problems.statement:
**Shiu's theorem**: for any $k \geq 1$ and $(a, q) = 1$ there exist infinitely many $k$-tuples of consecutive primes
$p_m, \dots, p_{m + k - 1}$ all of which are congruent to $a$ modulo $q$.

This is stated ahead of `erdos_427` because the formal proof linked there assumes it, and the
`assuming` clause must name a declaration that already exists.

[Sh00] Shiu, D. K. L., _Strings of congruent primes_. J. London Math. Soc. (2) (2000), 359-373.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_427.variants.shiu : ShiuTheorem

problems.title: Erdős Problem 437 — tao
problems.statement:
Tao [Ta24] shows that, if $u(x)=(\log x\log\log x)^{1/2}$, then
$$x\exp(-(2^{1/2}+o(1))u(x)) \leq L(x) \leq x\exp(-(2^{-1/2}+o(1))u(x)).$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_437.variants.tao :
    ∃ o₁ o₂ : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto o₁ atTop (nhds 0) ∧ Tendsto o₂ atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        x * exp (-(√2 + o₁ x) * √(log x * log (log x))) ≤ L x ∧
        L x ≤ x * exp (-((√2)⁻¹ + o₂ x) * √(log x * log (log x)))

theorem erdos_441.variants.chen :

problems.title: Erdős Problem 441 — chen dai infinitely often
problems.statement:
Chen and Dai [ChDa07] proved that, infinitely often, Erdős' construction is not optimal: for
infinitely many $N$, $g(N) \geq \lvert B\rvert+t-2$, where $B$ is the construction and $t\geq 0$
is such that the $t$-fold iterated logarithm of $N$ is in $[0,1)$. (erdosproblems.com omits the
$-2$; [ChDa07] proves the bound with it.)
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_441.variants.chen_dai_infinitely_often :
    ∃ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, (erdosConstruction N).card + Real.iteratedLog N ≤ g N + 2

    (fun N : ℕ ↦ (g N : ℝ) - √(9 / 8 * N)) =O[atTop]

problems.title: Erdős Problem 448 — erdos tenenbaum
problems.statement:
Quantitative form of the (negative) answer to `erdos_448`. Erdős and Tenenbaum [ErTe81] showed that
the upper density of $\{n : \tau^+(n) < \epsilon \cdot \tau(n)\}$ is in fact
$\asymp \epsilon^{1 - o(1)}$, where the $o(1)$ in the exponent tends to $0$ as $\epsilon \to 0$.
Equivalently, $\log(\text{upper density}) / \log \epsilon \to 1$ as $\epsilon \to 0^+$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_448.variants.erdos_tenenbaum :
    Tendsto
      (fun ε : ℝ =>
        Real.log ({n : ℕ | (tauPlus n : ℝ) < ε * (n.divisors.card : ℝ)}.upperDensity) / Real.log ε)
      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (1 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 448 — hall tenenbaum distribution
problems.statement:
Hall and Tenenbaum [HaTe88] further prove that $\tau^+(n)/\tau(n)$ has a distribution function:
there is a distribution function `F` (non-decreasing, with $F(-\infty) = 0$ and $F(+\infty) = 1$)
such that, for every continuity point $z$ of `F`, the set $\{n : \tau^+(n)/\tau(n) \le z\}$ has
density `F z`. Tenenbaum [Te13] proved that `F` is continuous at $z = 1$ and asked to determine
its discontinuity points, if any.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_448.variants.hall_tenenbaum_distribution :
    ∃ F : ℝ → ℝ, Monotone F ∧ Tendsto F atBot (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto F atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      ∀ z : ℝ, ContinuousAt F z →
        {n : ℕ | (tauPlus n : ℝ) / (n.divisors.card : ℝ) ≤ z}.HasDensity (F z)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 448 — hall tenenbaum upper bound
problems.statement:
A more precise result of Hall and Tenenbaum [HaTe88, §4.6]: the upper density of
$\{n : \tau^+(n) < \epsilon \cdot \tau(n)\}$ is $\ll \epsilon \cdot \log(2/\epsilon)$ as
$\epsilon \to 0^+$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_448.variants.hall_tenenbaum_upper_bound :
    (fun ε : ℝ => ({n : ℕ | (tauPlus n : ℝ) < ε * (n.divisors.card : ℝ)}).upperDensity)
      =O[𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)] (fun ε : ℝ => ε * Real.log (2 / ε))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 455 — liminf
problems.statement:
Let `q : ℕ → ℕ` be a strictly increasing sequence of primes such that
`q (n + 2) - q (n + 1) ≥ q (n + 1) - q n`. Then `liminf q n / (n ^ 2) > 0.352`, and this is proved in
[Ri76].
problems.lean:

    (∀ n, (q n).Prime ∧ q (n + 2) - q (n + 1) ≥ q (n + 1) - q n) →
    liminf (fun n : ℕ => (q n : ℝ≥0∞) / n ^ 2) atTop > 0.352

problems.title: Erdős Problem 499 — one le
problems.statement:
A weaker version of Erdős' problem 499, which asks whether for every doubly stochastic matrix, there
exists a permutation $σ \in S_n$ with $M_{i, σ(i)} ≠ 0$ and such that
$$
\sum_{1 \leq i \leq n} M_{i, σ(i)} \geq 1
$$
Proved by Marcus and Ree [MaRe59].

[MaRe59] Marcus, M. and Ree, R., Diagonals of doubly stochastic matrices. Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (2) (1959), 296-302.
problems.lean:
lemma erdos_499.variants.one_le :
    ∀ n > 0, ∀ M ∈ doublyStochastic ℝ (Fin n), ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      (∀ i, M i (σ i) ≠ 0) ∧ 1 ≤ ∑ i, M i (σ i)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 — banks freiberg maynard
problems.statement:
Banks, Freiberg, and Maynard [BFM16] showed that at least $12.5\%$ of $[0,\infty)$ belongs
to $S$.

This is [BFM16, Theorem 1.1]: for any nine nonnegative reals
$\beta_1\leq\beta_2\leq\cdots\leq\beta_9$, at least one of the differences $\beta_j-\beta_i$
with $i<j$ belongs to $S$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard (β : Fin 9 → ℝ) (hβ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ β i)
    (hβmono : Monotone β) : ∃ i j, i < j ∧ β j - β i ∈ limitPointSet

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 — banks freiberg maynard measure
problems.statement:
The $12.5\%$ claim itself, as deduced in [BFM16, Corollary 1.2]:
$\lambda([0,T]\cap S)\geq (1-o(1))T/8$ as $T\to\infty$.

Note that the constant $1/8$ is only attained asymptotically and ineffectively; the bound
[BFM16] obtain for *all* $T>0$ is the weaker $\lambda([0,T]\cap S)>T/22$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_5.variants.banks_freiberg_maynard_measure : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ T : ℝ in atTop,
    ENNReal.ofReal ((1 - ε) * T / 8) ≤ volume (limitPointSet ∩ Icc 0 T)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 — merikoski
problems.statement:
Merikoski [Me20] showed that at least $1/3$ of $[0,\infty)$ belongs to $S$.

This is [Me20, Theorem 1]: for any reals $\beta_1\leq\beta_2\leq\beta_3\leq\beta_4$, at least
one of the differences $\beta_j-\beta_i$ with $i<j$ belongs to $S$. Note that, in contrast with

problems.lean:
theorem erdos_5.variants.merikoski (β : Fin 4 → ℝ) (hβmono : Monotone β) :

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 — merikoski bounded gaps
problems.statement:
Merikoski [Me20] showed that $S$ has bounded gaps.

This is [Me20, Corollary 3]: there is a (ineffective) constant $C\geq 0$ such that
$S\cap[T,T+C]\neq\emptyset$ for all $T\geq 0$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_5.variants.merikoski_bounded_gaps :
    ∃ C ≥ (0 : ℝ), ∀ T ≥ (0 : ℝ), (limitPointSet ∩ Icc T (T + C)).Nonempty

problems.title: Erdős Problem 5 — merikoski measure
problems.statement:
The $1/3$ claim itself [Me20, Corollary 2]: $\lambda([0,T]\cap S)\geq T/3$ for all $T>0$.

Unlike the $1/8$ of [BFM16], this bound holds uniformly in $T$ with no error term.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_5.variants.merikoski_measure : ∀ T > (0 : ℝ),
    ENNReal.ofReal (T / 3) ≤ volume (limitPointSet ∩ Icc 0 T)

problems.title: Erdős–Szekeres (1960). — endpoint
problems.statement:
**Erdős–Szekeres (1960).** For $n \ge 3$, also
$\alpha_{2^n - 1} = \pi\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_504.variants.endpoint {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    minimaxAngle (2 ^ n - 1) = (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) * π

problems.title: Sendov (1995).
problems.statement:
**Sendov (1995).** The complete determination: for $n \ge 3$,
$\alpha_N = \pi(1 - 1/n)$ whenever $2^{n-1} + 2^{n-3} < N \le 2^n$, and
$\alpha_N = \pi\left(1 - \frac{2}{2n - 1}\right)$ whenever
$2^{n-1} < N \le 2^{n-1} + 2^{n-3}$.

This is the statement of [Se95] (as given in Zbl 0853.52009) with $n$ shifted by one.
For $n = 3$ the second branch gives $\alpha_5 = 3\pi/5$, the value computed in [ErSz60],
and $\alpha_N$ is nondecreasing in $N$ across the two branches.
The problem page [erdosproblems.com/504](https://www.erdosproblems.com/504) prints the
second branch as $\pi(1 - \frac{1}{2n-1})$, which would give $\alpha_5 = 4\pi/5 > \alpha_6$;
that appears to be a typo.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_504.variants.sendov {n N : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (h1 : 2 ^ (n - 1) < N) (h2 : N ≤ 2 ^ n) :
    minimaxAngle N =
      if 2 ^ (n - 1) + 2 ^ (n - 3) < N then (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) * π
      else (1 - 2 / (2 * (n : ℝ) - 1)) * π

problems.title: Erdős Problem 509 — Cartan bound
problems.statement:
Let $f(z) ∈ ℂ[z]$ be a monic non-constant polynomial. Can the set
$\{z ∈ ℂ : |f(z)| ≤ 1\}$
be covered by a set of closed discs the sum of whose radii is $≤ 2e$?
Solution: True. This is due to Cartan.
See *Sur les systèmes de fonctions holomorphes à variétés linéaires
lacunaires et leurs applications*, Henri Cartan,
http://www.numdam.org/article/ASENS_1928_3_45__255_0.pdf
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_509.variants.Cartan_bound : ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.natDegree ≠ 0 →
    ∃ (ι : Type), Nonempty (BoundedDiscCover {z | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ 1} (2*rexp 1) ι)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 509 — Pommerenke connected
problems.statement:
Let $f(z) ∈ ℂ[z]$ be a monic non-constant polynomial.
If it is connected, can the set $\{z ∈ ℂ : |f(z)| ≤ 1\}$
be covered by a set of circles the sum of whose radii is $≤ 2$?
Solution: True. This is due to Pommerenke.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_509.variants.Pommerenke_connected : ∀ (f : ℂ[X]), f.Monic → f.natDegree ≠ 0 →
    IsConnected {z | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ 1} →
    ∃ (ι : Type), Nonempty (BoundedDiscCover {z | ‖f.eval z‖ ≤ 1} 2 ι)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 513 — lower bound
problems.statement:
`maxTermConstant > 1 / 2`: there is a transcendental entire `f` with
`liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop > 1 / 2`. This was observed by Kövári (unpublished), and
[ClHa64] proves the stronger bound `> 4 / 7`. It does not hold for every `f`: for `f = exp` the

        ¬ HasManyDistinctInducedSubgraphs G (K * (n : ℝ) ^ (5 / 2 : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 639 — exact
problems.statement:
The exact maximum number of uncovered edges is $\binom{n}{2}$ for $n\leq 5$, $10$ for
$n=6$, and $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ for $n\geq 7$ [KeSu04, Theorem 1.1].
`IsGreatest` states both the upper bound and its attainment by a colouring.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_639.variants.exact :
    ∀ n : ℕ, IsGreatest
      (Set.range fun C : Sym2 (Fin n) → Fin 2 => (uncoveredEdges C).ncard)
      (if n ≤ 5 then n.choose 2 else if n = 6 then 10 else n ^ 2 / 4)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 651 — antitone
problems.statement:
The function $f_k(n)$ does not increase with the dimension: $f_{k+1}(n) \leq f_k(n)$ for
$k \geq 2$. Given a set in general position in $\mathbb{R}^{k+1}$ with at least $f_k(n)$ points,
project it to a generic hyperplane, find $n$ points in convex position in the projection, and
lift them back. This projection argument is due to Valtr [Va96]; see [PoZa22, Section 1, (1)].

The site states that $f_2(n) > f_3(n) > \cdots$. [PoZa22] gives only the non-strict inequality, so
we state that. The strict inequalities fail for small $n$: for example $f_2(3) = f_3(3) = 3$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_651.variants.antitone {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (n : ℕ) : f (k + 1) n ≤ f k n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 651 — planar
problems.statement:
For $k = 2$ the lower bound of the question holds: $f_2(n) > (1+c)^n$ for some $c > 0$ and all
large $n$. Erdős and Szekeres [ErSz60] proved that
$2^{n-2} + 1 \leq f_2(n)$, see [PoZa22, abstract and Section 1], and $(3/2)^n < 2^{n-2} + 1$ for
all $n \geq 5$. The Erdős-Klein-Szekeres conjecture (Erdős Problem 107) states that
$f_2(n) = 2^{n-2} + 1$ for $n \geq 3$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_651.variants.planar :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (1 + c) ^ n < (f 2 n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 651 — pohoata zakharov
problems.statement:
Pohoata and Zakharov [PoZa22, Theorem 1.1] proved that $ES_3(n) = 2^{o(n)}$, where $ES_k(n)$ is
the function $f_k(n)$ above: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large $n$, any set of at least
$2^{\varepsilon n}$ points in general position in $\mathbb{R}^3$ contains $n$ points in convex
position. By the projection argument of Valtr [Va96] (see `erdos_651.variants.antitone`) the same
holds in every dimension $k \geq 3$ [PoZa22, abstract and Section 1].

The theorem gives $f_k(n) \leq \lceil 2^{\varepsilon n} \rceil$. The form below follows by
applying it with $\varepsilon / 2$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_651.variants.pohoata_zakharov {k : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (f k n : ℝ) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (ε * (n : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 651 — subexponential
problems.statement:
For every dimension $k \geq 3$ and every $c > 0$ one has $f_k(n) \leq (1+c)^n$ for all large
$n$. This is `erdos_651.variants.pohoata_zakharov` with $\varepsilon = \log_2(1 + c)$. In
particular, for every $c > 0$ the lower bound $f_k(n) > (1+c)^n$ fails not only for infinitely
many $n$ but for all large $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_651.variants.subexponential {k : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    ∀ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (f k n : ℝ) ≤ (1 + c) ^ n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 667 — ramsey bounds
problems.statement:
The case $q = 1$ is the classical Ramsey problem, giving the bounds
$\tfrac{1}{p-1} \leq c(p, 1) \leq \tfrac{2}{p+1}$ for $p \geq 3$. (For $p = 2$ the condition
forces $G$ to be complete, so $c(2, 1) = 1$ and the upper bound fails.)

theorem erdos_667.variants.ramsey_bounds (p : ℕ) (hp : 3 ≤ p) :
    1 / ((p : ℝ) - 1) ≤ c p 1 ∧ c p 1 ≤ 2 / ((p : ℝ) + 1)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 669 — burr grunbaum sloane atLeast

The problem with $k=3$ is the classical 'Orchard problem' of Sylvester. Burr, Grünbaum, and Sloane
[BGS74] have proved that

and
$$F_3(n)=\frac{n^2}{6}-O(n).$$

This is the statement for $F_3$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 669 — limit le
problems.statement:
There is a trivial upper bound of $F_k(n) \leq \binom{n}{2}/\binom{k}{2}$, and hence
$$\lim F_k(n)/n^2 \leq \frac{1}{k(k-1)}.$$
See also [101](https://www.erdosproblems.com/101).

Here the limit is assumed to exist and is called `L`.

    (hL : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (maxLinesAtLeast k n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) ^ 2) atTop (𝓝 L)) :
    L ≤ 1 / ((k : ℝ) * ((k : ℝ) - 1))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 682 — exceptional count
problems.statement:
Gafni and Tao [GaTa25, Theorem 1.1] proved that the number of exceptional gaps

$$\ll \frac{X}{(\log X)^2}.$$

        ∀ m ∈ Set.Ioo (p n) (p (n + 1)), m.minFac < p (n + 1) - p n}.ncard : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      fun X : ℕ ↦ (X : ℝ) / Real.log X ^ 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 692 — cambie local maxima
problems.statement:
Cambie [Ca25] has shown that, for fixed $n$, the sequence $\delta_1(n,m)$ has superpolynomially

problems.statement:

      Tendsto (fun m : ℕ ↦ (f (2 * m + 1) : ℝ) / 2 ^ ((2 * m + 1 : ℝ) / 2)) atTop
        (nhds c₁)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 772 — upper bound
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er84d] proved that $H_k(n) \ll n^{2/3}$, where the implied constant is absolute.

Since $1_A\ast 1_A$ counts ordered pairs, the bound needs $k\geq 4$: the construction of
Erdős has at most two unordered representations of each sum, hence at most four ordered ones,
while $k\leq 2$ forces $A$ itself to be Sidon and so $H_k(n)=n$. For $k=3$ the only collisions
are $a+b=2c$, so the Sidon subsets of $A$ are its $3$-term-progression-free subsets, which have
size $n^{1-o(1)}$, and the bound fails there too.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_772.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ k ≥ 4, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (H k n : ℝ) ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ)

$$(\log n)^{1+c} \ll g(n) \ll \exp(\sqrt{\log n})$$
for some constant $c>0$, the lower bound due to Sanders [Sa21] and the upper bound due to
Ruzsa [Ru05].

This is the lower bound.

    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Real.log n ^ (1 + c) ≤ (g ℝ n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 802 — aeks
problems.statement:
Ajtai, Erdős, Komlós, and Szemerédi [AEKS81] proved that any $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices
with average degree $t$ contains an independent set on
$$\gg_r \frac{\log\log(t+1)}{t}n$$
many vertices.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_802.variants.aeks : ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    G.CliqueFree r →
      c * (log (log (G.averageDegree + 1)) / G.averageDegree) * n ≤ G.indepNum

problems.title: Erdős Problem 802 — alon
problems.statement:
Alon [Al96b] proved the conjectured bound under the stronger assumption that the induced graph
on every vertex neighbourhood has chromatic number $\leq r - 2$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_802.variants.alon : ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    (∀ v, (G.induce (G.neighborSet v)).Colorable (r - 2)) →
      c * (log G.averageDegree / G.averageDegree) * n ≤ G.indepNum

problems.title: Erdős Problem 802 — r eq three
problems.statement:
Ajtai, Komlós, and Szemerédi [AKS80] proved the conjectured bound when $r = 3$: any
triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $t$ contains an independent set on
$$\gg \frac{\log t}{t}n$$
many vertices.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_802.variants.r_eq_three : ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    G.CliqueFree 3 →
      c * (log G.averageDegree / G.averageDegree) * n ≤ G.indepNum

problems.title: Erdős Problem 805 — alon bucic sudakov
problems.statement:
Alon, Bucić, and Sudakov [ABS21] construct such a graph with
$$g(n)\leq 2^{2^{(\log\log n)^{1/2+o(1)}}}.$$

Here all logarithms are to base $2$, as in [ABS21], so the cliques and independent sets have at
least $\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ vertices; this implies the natural-logarithm version of the problem.
The $o(1)$ is expressed as: for every $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and all large $n$ there is such a graph
with $g(n)=\lceil 2^{2^{(\log_2\log_2 n)^{1/2+\varepsilon}}}\rceil$. This form, with the rounding,
follows from [ABS21, Theorem 2].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_805.variants.alon_bucic_sudakov :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 / 2 → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      IsLocallyRamsey G
        ⌈(2 : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) ^ (Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 n) ^ (1 / 2 + ε)))⌉₊
        ⌈Real.logb 2 n⌉₊

problems.title: Erdős Problem 805 — alon sudakov
problems.statement:
Alon and Sudakov [AlSu07] proved that there is no such graph with
$$g(n)=\frac{c}{\log\log n}(\log n)^3$$
for some constant $c>0$.

Here `log` is the natural logarithm, as in [AlSu07], and the statement is for all large `n`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_805.variants.alon_sudakov :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ¬ ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      IsLocallyRamsey G ⌊c * Real.log n ^ 3 / Real.log (Real.log n)⌋₊ ⌈Real.log n⌉₊

problems.title: Erdős Problem 806 — alon bukh sudakov
problems.statement:
Alon, Bukh, and Sudakov [ABS09] proved that for any $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert \leq n^{1/2}$ there exists some $B$ such that $A\subseteq B+B$ and
$\lvert B\rvert \ll \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n^{1/2}$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_806.variants.alon_bukh_sudakov : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n → (A.card : ℝ) ≤ √n →
      ∃ B : Finset ℤ, A.map Nat.castEmbedding ⊆ B + B ∧
        (B.card : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n * √n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 812 — lower bound

problems.title: Erdős Problem 816 — chen ma
problems.statement:
Chen and Ma [ChMa25] proved that, provided $n\geq 600$, all graphs with $2n+1$ vertices and at
least $n^2+n$ edges contain two vertices of the same degree joined by a path of length $3$, except
$K_{n,n+1}$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 818 — solymosi

$\geq \frac{x}{(\log x)^{O(1)}}$ many primes $p\leq x$ such that all prime factors of $p-1$ are

Harman [BaHa98]).

problems.statement:
Mordell proved $\limsup_{n \to \infty} (1_A \ast 1_A)(n) = \infty$, where $A$ is the set of

problems.title: Erdős Problem 830 — pomerance
problems.statement:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\log x)^{1/3})$.

problems.title: Erdős Problem 862 — lower bound
problems.statement:
This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that
the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least $2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each
Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each maximal Sidon set contains at most
$2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_862.variants.lower_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ (((0.16 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) ≤ (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 864 — lower bound
problems.statement:
Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] [Er92c] prove that
$$\lvert A\rvert \geq (1+o(1))\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}N^{1/2}.$$
This is shown by taking a genuine Sidon set $B\subset [1,N/3]$ of size $\sim N^{1/2}/\sqrt{3}$
and taking the union with $\{N-b : b\in B\}$.

That is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large $N$ there is a set $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$
with the property of `Erdos864.erdos_864` and $|A| \geq (1-\varepsilon)\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}N^{1/2}$.
So the constant $2/\sqrt{3}$ there cannot be replaced by a smaller one.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_864.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      HasAtMostOneRepeatedSum A ∧
        (1 - ε) * (2 / Real.sqrt 3) * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) ≤ #A

problems.title: Erdős Problem 867 — coppersmith phillips lower bound

theorem erdos_867.variants.coppersmith_phillips_lower_bound :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, ConsecutiveSumFree A ∧
      ((13 / 24 : ℝ) * (N : ℝ) - C ≤ (A.card : ℝ))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 876 — dem polynomial
problems.statement:
Deshouillers, Erdős and Melfi [DEM99, Theorem 4] proved that for every $\delta>0$ there is an
infinite sum-free set with $a_n\sim n^{3+\delta}$; we state the consequence $a_n\ll n^{3+\delta}$.
The site writes $a_n\sim n^{3+o(1)}$.

Let $R$ be the supremum of $\sum_j 1/n_j$ over sum-free sequences $\{n_j\}$. Levine and O'Sullivan
[LeOS77] proved $R<4$ (and $R>2.035$), and Abbott [Ab87] improved the lower bound to $R>2.064$,

infinite sum-free set $A$; see also [Er75b, p. 302] and [DEM99, p. 49]. The later paper

$$2^{n+1}-1 \leq f(n) \ll n^22^n.$$

problems.title: Erdős Problem 910 — rudin CH
problems.statement:
Assume the continuum hypothesis. Rudin [Ru58, p. 15] constructed a connected subset $M$ of the
plane, with more than one point, such that $M\setminus N$ is at most countable for every connected
subset $N\subseteq M$ with more than one point.

This disproves a conjecture of Erdős [Er44, p. 443] that every connected set $C$ contains a
connected subset $C'$ such that $C\setminus C'$ has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Erdős [Er82e,
p. 77] reports that Rudin's examples answer both questions of this problem in the negative; see
the docstrings of `erdos_910.parts.i` and `erdos_910.parts.ii`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_910.variants.rudin_CH :
    (ℵ₁ = 𝔠) → ∃ M : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), IsConnected M ∧ M.Nontrivial ∧
      ∀ N ⊆ M, IsConnected N → N.Nontrivial → (M \ N).Countable

problems.title: Erdős Problem 917 — dirac
problems.statement:
In fact Dirac [Di52] proved
$$f_6(4n+2) \geq 4n^2+8n+3,$$
as witnessed by taking two disjoint copies of $C_{2n+1}$ and adding all edges between them.

We take $n \geq 1$, so that $C_{2n+1}$ is a cycle.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_917.variants.dirac (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    4 * n ^ 2 + 8 * n + 3 ≤ f 6 (4 * n + 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 917 — erdos three dvd
problems.statement:
Erdős [Er69b] observed that Dirac's construction generalises to show that, if $3\mid k$, there are
infinitely many values of $n$ (those of the shape $mk/3$ where $m$ is odd) such that
$$f_k(n) \geq \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{k/3}\right)n^2 + n.$$

We take $m \geq 3$, so that the cycle $C_m$ exists.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_917.variants.erdos_three_dvd (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (h3 : 3 ∣ k) (m : ℕ)
    (hm : Odd m) (hm3 : 3 ≤ m) :
    conjecturedValue k (m * (k / 3)) + ((m * (k / 3) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (f k (m * (k / 3)) : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 917 — lower construction
problems.statement:
Constructions of Stiebitz [St87] show that, for $k\geq 6$, there exist infinitely many values of
$n$ such that
$$f_k(n) \geq \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\lfloor k/3\rfloor+\delta_k}\right)n^2$$
where $\delta_k=0$ if $k\equiv 0\pmod{3}$, $\delta_k=1/7$ if $k\equiv 1\pmod{3}$, and
$\delta_k = 24/69$ if $k\equiv 2\pmod{3}$.

[LMY23] state the same bound in the form $(\frac12-\frac{3}{2k-\delta_k'})n^2$ with
$\delta_k'=0,8/7,44/23$, and credit the constructions to Toft [To70].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_917.variants.lower_construction (k : ℕ) (hk : 6 ≤ k) :
    ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      1 / 2 * (1 - 1 / (((k / 3 : ℕ) : ℝ) + delta k)) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ (f k n : ℝ)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 917 — luo ma yang
problems.statement:
Luo, Ma, and Yang [LMY23] have improved this upper bound to
$$f_k(n) \leq \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{k-2}-\frac{1}{36(k-1)^2}+o(1)\right)n^2.$$

[LMY23, Theorem 1.1] proves the stronger bound
$f_k(n) \leq \mathrm{ex}(n;K_{k-1}) - \frac{n^2}{36(k-1)^2}$ for $k \geq 4$ and all large $n$, where
$\mathrm{ex}(n;K_{k-1})$ is the number of edges of the Turán graph $T_{k-2}(n)$. We state this form.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_917.variants.luo_ma_yang (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (f k n : ℝ) ≤
      (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin (k - 1))) : ℝ) -
        (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / (36 * ((k : ℝ) - 1) ^ 2)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 917 — not asymptotic
problems.statement:
The constructions in `erdos_917.variants.lower_construction` disprove Erdős' conjectured asymptotic
$f_k(n) \sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\lfloor k/3\rfloor}\right)n^2$ for $k\not\equiv 0\pmod{3}$,
$k \geq 6$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_917.variants.not_asymptotic (k : ℕ) (hk : 6 ≤ k) (h3 : ¬ 3 ∣ k) :
    ¬ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (f k n : ℝ)) ~[atTop] conjecturedValue k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 917 — stiebitz upper
problems.statement:
Stiebitz also proved the general upper bound
$$f_k(n) < \mathrm{ex}(n;K_{k-1})\sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{k-2}\right)n^2$$
for large $n$.

Here $k \geq 4$, as in [LMY23].
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_917.variants.stiebitz_upper (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      f k n < SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin (k - 1)))

problems.title: Erdős Problem 920 — k eq 3

A positive answer to this question for all $k\geq 5$, i.e.

theorem erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_ge_5 (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 5) :

    (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)) / (log n) ^ c)

Graver and Yackel [GrYa68] proved that

problems.statement:
Alon, Krivelevich, and Sudakov [AKS03] proved $\mathrm{ex}(n;H_k) \ll kn^{3/2}$ with an

problems.statement:
It follows from Rosser's sieve that $S(k)> k^{1/2-o(1)}$.

Erdős [Er76d, p. 26] states this for the index $\ell$ with $p_\ell = S(k)$. Since
$S(k) = p_\ell \geq \ell$, the bound transfers to $S(k)$. The $o(1)$ is stated with an arbitrary

problems.title: Erdős Problem 930 — consecutive integers
problems.statement:
Erdos and Selfridge [ErSe75] proved that the product of
consecutive integers is never a power (establishing the case $r=1$).

Theorem 1 from [ErSe75].

It is implied from `erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong`.

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.

theorem erdos_930.variants.consecutive_integers :

problems.title: Erdős Problem 930 — consecutive strong
problems.statement:
Let $k$, $l$, $n$ be integers such that $k \ge 3$, $l \ge 2$ and $n + k \ge p^{(k)}$,
where $p^{(k)}$ is the least prime satisfying $p^{(k)} \ge k$.
Then there is a prime $p \ge k$ for which $l$ does not divide
the multiplicity of the prime factor $p$ in $(n + 1) \ldots (n + k)$.

Theorem 2 from [ErSe75].

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong :
    ∀ k l n, 3 ≤ k → 2 ≤ l → nextPrime k ≤ n + k →
      ∃ p, k ≤ p ∧ p.Prime ∧
        ¬ (l ∣ Nat.factorization (∏ m ∈ Icc (n + 1) (n + k), m) p)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 934 — h one
problems.statement:
It is easy to see that $h_t(d)\leq 2d^t$ always and $h_1(d)=d+1$.

The site (and [CCJK22, p. 1]) states $h_1(d)=d+1$ without restriction; it fails for $d=2$ (the
triangle has three pairwise intersecting edges, so $h_1(2)=4$), hence we assume $d\neq 2$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_934.variants.h_one : ∀ d : ℕ, d ≠ 2 → h 1 d = d + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 934 — h three three
problems.statement: Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, de Joannis de Verclos, and Kang [CCJK22, Theorem 2] proved that $h_3(3)=23$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_934.variants.h_three_three : h 3 3 = 23

problems.title: Erdős Problem 934 — kmp h three four
problems.statement:
Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, de Joannis de Verclos, and Kang [CCJK22] conjectured that
$h_3(d) \leq d^3-d^2+d+2$ (with equality if $d-1$ is a prime power; the site writes "if and only
if", while [CCJK22, Conjecture 1] says "if"). Kumar, Mohar and Pragada [KMP26, Lemma 3.1]
refute the inequality: the odd graph $KG(7,3)$ has $35$ vertices, is $4$-regular, has $70$ edges
and any two of its edges are at distance less than $3$, so $h_3(4)\geq 71 > 54$.
problems.lean: theorem erdos_934.variants.kmp_h_three_four : 71 ≤ h 3 4

problems.title: Erdős Problem 968 — infinite decreasingTriples
problems.statement:
Erdős asked whether there are infinitely many solutions to `uₙ > uₙ₊₁ > uₙ₊₂`.

The answer is yes. Since `uₙ > uₙ₊₁` is equivalent to `pₙ₊₁ - pₙ < pₙ / n`, it suffices to have
infinitely many `n` with `pₙ₊₂ - pₙ` bounded, because `pₙ / n → ∞`. Maynard [Ma15] proved that
`liminf (pₙ₊₂ - pₙ) < ∞`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_968.variants.infinite_decreasingTriples :
    {n : ℕ | u n > u (n + 1) ∧ u (n + 1) > u (n + 2)}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 968 — infinite increasingTriples
problems.statement:
Erdős asked whether there are infinitely many solutions to `uₙ < uₙ₊₁ < uₙ₊₂`.

The answer is yes. Since `uₙ < uₙ₊₁` is equivalent to `pₙ₊₁ - pₙ > pₙ / n`, it suffices to have
infinitely many `n` with two consecutive prime gaps larger than `pₙ / n ∼ log n`. Ford, Maynard,
and Tao [FMT18] proved that for every fixed `k` there are infinitely many `n` with `k` consecutive
prime gaps all of size `≫ log pₙ · log log pₙ · log log log log pₙ / log log log pₙ`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_968.variants.infinite_increasingTriples :
    {n : ℕ | u n < u (n + 1) ∧ u (n + 1) < u (n + 2)}.Infinite

problems.title: Helfgott and Juschenko.
problems.statement:
**Helfgott and Juschenko.** If the Higman group is sofic, then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there
is $N$ such that for every odd $n \ge N$ there is a bijection $f : \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to
\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with $f(x + 1) = 2 f(x)$ for at least $(1 - \varepsilon) n$ values of $x$
and $f(f(f(f(x)))) = x$ for all $x$ [HJ19, Theorem 2, case $m = 2$]. The last condition already
makes $f$ a bijection. [HJ19] presents the Higman group with the order of the generators
reversed, which gives an isomorphic group.
problems.lean:
theorem green_100.variants.helfgott_juschenko :
    IsSofic HigmanGroup → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → n.Coprime 2 →
      ∃ f : ZMod n → ZMod n, (1 - ε) * n ≤ Set.ncard {x | f (x + 1) = 2 * f x} ∧
        ∀ x, f (f (f (f x))) = x

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 100 — operator norm
problems.statement:
Suppose that $G$ is a group. Is the following true? For every finite set $A \subset G$ containing
the identity $e_G$ and for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there is some unitary group $U(n)$ and a map
$\phi : A \to U(n)$ such that $\phi(e_G) = I_n$, such that $\phi$ is an 'approximate
homomorphism' in the sense that $\|\phi(a_1 a_2) - \phi(a_1)\phi(a_2)\| < \varepsilon$ for all
$a_1, a_2 \in A$ such that $a_1 a_2 \in A$, whilst $\phi$ is 'nontrivial' in the sense that
$\|\phi(a) - I_n\| \ge 1$ for all $a \in A$, $a \ne e_G$. (Here $\|-\|$ is the
$\ell^2$-to-$\ell^2$ operator norm.)

[Gr24] gives this as a precise statement of `green_100.parts.ii`. In [Pe08], hyperlinearity uses
the normalised Hilbert–Schmidt norm, and approximation in the operator norm defines a class of
groups whose relation to hyperlinear groups was open there [Pe08, Remark 8.6 and Question 8.7];
these are now usually called MF groups. We state the question as written, with the operator
norm, for every group.

[Gr24] lists this as open. The answer is no. Exhausting a countable group by finite sets
containing the identity, with errors tending to zero, the maps $\phi$ give a homomorphism into the
unitary group of $\prod_k M_{n_k}(\mathbb{C}) / \bigoplus_k M_{n_k}(\mathbb{C})$, which is
injective by the bound $\|\phi(a) - I_n\| \ge 1$. So every countable group with this property is
MF in the sense of [Ec26, Definition 4.1]. Eckhardt [Ec26, Theorem 4.3 and Examples 3.2 and 4.5]
gives a countable group that is not MF, built from a property (T) group such as
$\mathbb{Z}^3 \rtimes \mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$. This is a 2026 preprint.
problems.lean:
theorem green_100.variants.operator_norm :
    ¬ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], OperatorNormApprox G

problems.title: Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer.
problems.statement:
**Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer.** There are constants $c, C > 0$ such that every set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_3^n$ of density at least $C (\log \log \log n)^{-c}$ contains a 3-term
progression with nonzero common difference in $\{0, 1\}^n$.

This is [BKLM24, Theorem 3] for $\Sigma = \mathbb{F}_3$ and
$S = \{(x, x + a, x + 2a) : x \in \mathbb{F}_3, a \in \{0, 1\}\}$, as in [BKLM24, Section 1.2.1]:
three points of $A$, not all equal, with $(x_i, y_i, z_i) \in S$ for all $i$ form such a
progression. We state it for large $n$, where $\log \log \log n > 0$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_17.variants.bklm :
    ∃ c C : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ A : Finset (𝔽₃ n),
      C / Real.log (Real.log (Real.log n)) ^ c * 3 ^ n ≤ (A.card : ℝ) → HasRestrictedAP A

problems.title: Hązła
problems.statement:
**Hązła.** For every $\mu > 0$ there is $\delta > 0$ such that every symmetric set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_3^n$ of density at least $\mu$ contains at least $\delta 6^n$
progressions $x, x + d, x + 2d$ with $d \in \{0, 1\}^n$ [Hą20, abstract and Theorem 2, case
$q = 3$].

[Hą20] counts all pairs $(x, d)$ with $d \in \{0, 1\}^n$, including the $|A|$ pairs with
$d = 0$; this is why `A.card` is added to `numRestrictedAPs A`. For large $n$ the $d = 0$ pairs
are negligible, so `green_17.parts.ii` holds for symmetric sets. [Hą20, abstract] states the
result for sets of density exactly $\mu$. The form with density at least $\mu$ follows from the
removal statement [Hą20, Theorem 2] with $\mu/2$ in place of $\mu$: it removes a single symmetric
set of density at most $\mu/2$ and leaves a set with no progressions, but the remaining set is
nonempty and contains the progressions with $d = 0$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_17.variants.symmetric :
    ∀ μ : ℝ, 0 < μ → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset (𝔽₃ n), IsSymmetric A →
      μ * 3 ^ n ≤ (A.card : ℝ) → δ * 6 ^ n ≤ (numRestrictedAPs A + A.card : ℝ)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 32 — finite field
problems.statement:
Tom Sanders' finite field variant [Gr24].
If $N = 2^n$ and $A$ is a subset of size $\lfloor \sqrt{N} \rfloor$, then $A^c$ contains a coset of
size at least $100\sqrt{N}$ for sufficiently large $n$.

      ∀ A : Finset (𝔽₂ n), A.card = ⌊Real.sqrt (2^n : ℝ)⌋₊ →
      HasCosetHole A ⌊100 * Real.sqrt (2^n : ℝ)⌋₊

[Sh20] has used the polynomial method to show that this is true with 100 replaced by 2 [Gr24].

Note: More precisely [Sh20, Theorem 1] implies a gap of at least $\lfloor 2p/|A| - 2 \rfloor$.
For a set $A$ of size $\lfloor \sqrt{p} \rfloor$, this guarantees a gap of at least
$\lfloor 2\sqrt{p} \rfloor - 2$.

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 38 — best lower

The lower bound $(C_1 - o(1))^n \leqslant |A|$ where $C_1 = 367^{1/5} \approx 3.2578$, from a
valid set of size $367$ in $\mathbb{F}_7^5$ [Po20, Section 9.1]. This was the best known bound

$C_2 = \frac{7 \cos(\pi/7)}{1 + \cos(\pi/7)} \approx 3.3177$ [La79, Corollary 5].

Itty, Rosin, Carstensen and Reichman [IRCR26] found a valid set of size $134753$ in

[Gr24, Comments to Problem 43] For exponents `α < 1/2` the lower bound `N^{1-o(1)}` is

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 5 — gowers sl two
problems.statement:
For the largest product-free subsets of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ of order $n$, the
best-known upper bound is $O(n^{8/9})$, due to Gowers [Go08].

theorem green_5.variants.gowers_sl_two :
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime], ∀ S : Finset (SL₂ p),

      (S.card : ℝ) ≤ C * (Fintype.card (SL₂ p) : ℝ) ^ ((8 : ℝ) / 9)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 5 — kedlaya
problems.statement:
Kedlaya [Ke97] observed, refining some work of Babai and Sós [BaSo85], that it follows from the
classification of finite simple groups that every finite group $G$ of order $n$ has a
product-free subset of size $\gg n^{11/14}$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_5.variants.kedlaya :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Fintype G], Nontrivial G →
      ∃ S : Finset G, IsProductFree (S : Set G) ∧
        c * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ^ ((11 : ℝ) / 14) ≤ (S.card : ℝ)

problems.title: Balog's theorem.
problems.statement:
**Balog's theorem.** For every $\varepsilon > 0$, every sufficiently large integer $N$ is
$n_1 + n_2$ with positive integers $n_1, n_2$ whose prime factors are all at most
$N^{4/(9\sqrt{e}) + \varepsilon}$, where $4/(9\sqrt{e}) \approx 0.2695$.

This is due to Balog [Ba89]. We take it from [NS08, Section 6.6], which states it with exponent
$4/(9\sqrt{e})$, and [DVA21, Theorem 4], which states it with exponent
$4/(9\sqrt{e}) + \varepsilon$, as here. Applied to each large $n \le N$ (and with
$n = 1 + (n - 1)$ for small $n$), it gives `green_59` with $\varepsilon$ replaced by any number
greater than $4/(9\sqrt{e})$; [Gr24] says this is still the record.
problems.lean:
theorem green_59.variants.balog :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∃ a b : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ 0 < b ∧ a + b = N ∧
      IsSmooth ((N : ℝ) ^ (4 / (9 * Real.sqrt (Real.exp 1)) + ε)) a ∧
      IsSmooth ((N : ℝ) ^ (4 / (9 * Real.sqrt (Real.exp 1)) + ε)) b

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 70 — empty pentagon
problems.statement:
Generalised empty pentagon theorem [ABBCDHKLPW11, Theorem 3]: for every integer $k \geq 2$,
every sufficiently large finite set of points in the plane contains $k$ collinear points or an
empty pentagon. By `HasEmptyPentagon.hasMutuallyVisible`, this implies
`green_70.variants.five_visible`, which is [ABBCDHKLPW11, Theorem 5].
problems.lean:
theorem green_70.variants.empty_pentagon :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ),
      n₀ ≤ #P → HasCollinear k P ∨ HasEmptyPentagon P

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 70 — five visible
problems.statement:
The answer to `green_70` is yes for $\ell \leq 5$ [Gr24]: for every $k$, every sufficiently large
planar set contains $k$ collinear points or $5$ mutually visible points. The case $\ell = 5$ is
[ABBCDHKLPW11, Theorem 5], and it implies the cases $\ell \leq 4$ (see
`HasMutuallyVisible.mono`). According to [ABBCDHKLPW11, Section 1.4], the case $\ell = 4$ was
proved in [KPW05]. In [ABBCDHKLPW11] and [PoWo10] the letters $k$ and $\ell$ are interchanged.
problems.lean:
theorem green_70.variants.five_visible :
    ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ),
      n₀ ≤ #P → HasCollinear k P ∨ HasMutuallyVisible 5 P

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 75 — alon
problems.statement:
Kupitz conjectured that one can take the difference to be at most $1$ [CL25, Section 1]. Alon
showed that this is false: there are finite point sets for which, for every line through two of
its points, the numbers of points on the two sides differ by at least $2$ [CL25, Section 1].
[Gr24] phrases this as: the answer to `green_75` is no if $100$ is replaced by $2$. Since the
sets in [CL25] have differences of at least $2$, they show that $100$ cannot be replaced by $1$.
We state the form given in [CL25].
problems.lean:
theorem green_75.variants.alon :
    ∃ X : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), 2 ≤ #X ∧ ∀ p ∈ X, ∀ q ∈ X, p ≠ q → 2 ≤ imbalance X p q

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 75 — pinchasi
problems.statement:
Pinchasi [Pi03] proved that the answer to `green_75` is yes if $100$ is replaced by
$C \log \log n$ for an absolute constant $C$, where $n = |X|$ [Gr24]. This is the best known bound.
[CL25, Theorem 1.1] states Pinchasi's theorem for generalised configurations (points with
pseudolines); sets of points with lines are a special case. The hypothesis $n \geq 3$ ensures
that $\log \log n > 0$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_75.variants.pinchasi :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ X : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), 3 ≤ #X → ∃ p ∈ X, ∃ q ∈ X, p ≠ q ∧
      (imbalance X p q : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.log (Real.log #X)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 76 — subset
problems.statement:
If $A'$ is required to be a subset of $A$, then the answer to `green_76` is no, even with $1000$
replaced by any constant. [Gr24] attributes this remark to Alon. It follows from
[PT13, Lemma 4.1], which [Gr24] cites as Lemma 3.1, its number in the arXiv version.
problems.lean:
theorem green_76.variants.subset :
    ¬ ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), ∃ A' ⊆ A, #A' ≤ #A / 2 ∧ HitsRichRectangles k A A'

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 76 — subset log log
problems.statement:
The answer to `green_76` is yes if $1000$ is replaced by $C \log \log n$ [Gr24]. This follows
from [AES10, Theorem 2.2], which gives $\varepsilon$-nets of size
$O(\varepsilon^{-1} \log \log \varepsilon^{-1})$ for axis-parallel rectangles. These nets are
subsets of $A$. The hypothesis $n \ge 3$ ensures that $\log \log n > 0$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_76.variants.subset_log_log :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ A : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), 3 ≤ #A → ∃ A' ⊆ A,
      #A' ≤ #A / 2 ∧ HitsRichRectangles ⌈C * Real.log (Real.log #A)⌉₊ A A'

problems.title: Flat Littlewood polynomials exist.
problems.statement:
**Flat Littlewood polynomials exist.** There are constants $\Delta > \delta > 0$ such that, for
all $n \ge 2$, there is a polynomial $P(z) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \varepsilon_k z^k$ with
$\varepsilon_k \in \{-1, 1\}$ such that $\delta\sqrt{n} \le |P(z)| \le \Delta\sqrt{n}$ for all
$z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| = 1$ [BBMST20, Theorem 1.1].

With $N = n + 1$ and $f(m) = \varepsilon_{m-1}$, one has $|\hat f(\theta)| = |P(e(\theta))|$, so
this answers `green_84` for all $N \ge 3$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_84.variants.bbmst :
    ∃ δ Δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ δ < Δ ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ ε : Fin (n + 1) → ℤ,
      (∀ k, ε k = 1 ∨ ε k = -1) ∧
        ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ = 1 → δ * √n ≤ ‖signPoly ε z‖ ∧ ‖signPoly ε z‖ ≤ Δ * √n

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 84 — golay
problems.statement:
The merit factor problem of Golay: "it is conjectured ... that
$\int_0^1 |P(z)|^4 \, dz \geq (1 + c)N^2$ for some universal $c > 0$" [Gr24], for every
polynomial $P(z) = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} \varepsilon_i z^i$ with $\pm 1$ coefficients, where
$z = e(\theta)$. Since $|P(e(\theta))| = |\hat f(\theta)|$ for $f(n) = \varepsilon_{n-1}$, we
integrate $|\hat f|^4$.

We require $N \ge 2$, since for $N = 1$ the integral equals $1 = N^2$. The integral is
$N^2(1 + 1/F)$, where $F$ is the merit factor of the coefficient sequence [JKS13], so the
conjecture says that the merit factor of binary sequences is bounded.

[Gr24] lists this as open. The conjecture is false: the largest merit factor of a binary sequence
of length $N$ tends to infinity as $N \to \infty$ [OAI26a, Corollary 8.1], a consequence of
[OAI26a, Theorem 1.1], which answers `Erdos1150.erdos_1150`. [OAI26a] is a 2026 preprint.
problems.lean:
theorem green_84.variants.golay :
    ¬ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, 2 ≤ N → ∀ f : ℕ → ℤ, IsSignOn N f →
      (1 + c) * (N : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖fourierSum N f θ‖ ^ 4

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 87 — exists tendsto
problems.statement:
For every $k$, $i(n, k)$ converges as $n \to \infty$ [BW15, Section 2]; the limit is
$p(k)$ in Green's notation. It is the probability that the random multiset with
$\mathrm{Pois}(1/j)$ parts of size $j$ ($1 \le j \le k$, independent) has a sub-multiset
of total size $k$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_87.variants.exists_tendsto (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n ↦ i n k) atTop (𝓝 L)

problems.title: Green's Open Problem 87 — order
problems.statement:
$p(k)$ is bounded above and below by constant multiples of $k^{-\delta} (\log k)^{-3/2}$.
[EFG16, Theorem 1.1] proves this for $i(n, k)$ uniformly in $1 \le k \le n/2$ (with
$(1 + \log k)^{-3/2}$); letting $n \to \infty$ gives the statement for $p$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_87.variants.order :
    ∀ p : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, Tendsto (fun n ↦ i n k) atTop (𝓝 (p k))) →
      p =Θ[atTop] fun k : ℕ ↦ (k : ℝ) ^ (-δ) * (Real.log k) ^ (-(3 / 2 : ℝ))

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 91 — all friendly
problems.statement:
Is there almost surely a bipartition of $G(n, \frac{1}{2})$ into two sets of $n/2$ vertices with
the property that all vertices have more neighbours on their own side than on the other?

[Gr24] reports that the authors of [FKNSS22] believe this may be true. Minzer, Sah and Sawhney
[MSS24, Theorem 1.3] prove it, conditional on a numerical hypothesis [MSS24, Assumption 1.5] that
they check by computer, partly with interval arithmetic and partly in floating point only. Under
the same hypothesis they find the critical margin: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, with high
probability there is a bisection in which every vertex has at least
$(\gamma - \varepsilon)\sqrt{n}$ more neighbours in its own part than in the other, but none with
$(\gamma + \varepsilon)\sqrt{n}$. Here $\gamma = \gamma_{\mathrm{crit}} / \sqrt{2} \approx 0.17566$,
and $\gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is defined by an optimisation problem for Gaussian tail
probabilities [MSS24, Definition 1.2].
problems.lean:
theorem green_91.variants.all_friendly :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ prob n fun G ↦
      ∃ s : Finset (Fin n), s.card = n / 2 ∧ ∀ v, 0 < friendliness G s v)
      atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Ferber, Kwan, Narayanan, Sah and Sawhney.
problems.statement:
**Ferber, Kwan, Narayanan, Sah and Sawhney.** With high probability, $G(n, \frac{1}{2})$ admits a
bisection in which $n - o(n)$ vertices are friendly [FKNSS22, Theorem 1.1]. A vertex is friendly
if it has more neighbours in its own part than across, and a bisection is a partition into two
parts whose sizes differ by at most one. This implies `green_91`.
problems.lean:
theorem green_91.variants.fknss :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ prob n fun G ↦
        ∃ s : Finset (Fin n), s.card = n / 2 ∧ (n : ℝ) - f n ≤ numFriendly G s)
        atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Chase's lower bound.
problems.statement:
**Chase's lower bound.** For every deletion probability $q \in (0, 1)$ and every
$\delta \in (0, 1)$ there is $c > 0$ such that at least $c n^{3/2} / \log^7 n$ traces are required
to distinguish between $x_n = (01)^k 1 (01)^{k+1}$ and $y_n = (01)^{k+1} 1 (01)^k$ with
probability at least $1 - \delta$, where $n = 4k + 3$ [Ch21, Theorem 1]. A decoder that recovers
every string distinguishes these two. We state it for $q = 1/2$ and $\delta = 1/10$, for large
$n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$. [Gr24] quotes the bound $n^{3/2} (\log n)^{-16}$ of the first arXiv
version of [Ch21]; the published version has $(\log n)^{-7}$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_92.variants.chase_lower :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, n % 4 = 3 →
      c * (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) / Real.log n ^ 7 ≤ numTraces n

problems.title: Chase's upper bound.
problems.statement:
**Chase's upper bound.** For every deletion probability $q \in (0, 1)$ and every $\delta > 0$
there is $C > 0$ such that every $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ can be reconstructed with probability at least
$1 - \delta$ from $\exp(C n^{1/5} \log^5 n)$ independent traces of $x$ [Ch20, Theorem 1]. We
state it for $q = 1/2$ and $\delta = 1/10$, with the number of traces rounded up, for large $n$.
It improves the bound $\exp(C n^{1/3})$ of [NP17] and [DOS19].
problems.lean:
theorem green_92.variants.chase_upper :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      numTraces n ≤ ⌈Real.exp (C * (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 5 : ℝ) * Real.log n ^ 5)⌉₊

problems.title: Breuillard and Varjú.
problems.statement:
**Breuillard and Varjú.** Assume the Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta functions of all
number fields $\mathbb{Q}(a)$ with $a$ a root of a polynomial with coefficients in $\{0, 1\}$
(`ZeroOneRootFieldsRH`). Then $p_n \to 1$ [BrVa19, Theorem 1].
problems.lean:
theorem green_93.variants.breuillard_varju :
    ZeroOneRootFieldsRH → Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ irreducibleProb 1 n) atTop (𝓝 1)

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 93 — bskk large
problems.statement:
Bary-Soroker, Koukoulopoulos and Kozma [BSKK23, Theorem 1(a)] proved that a random monic
polynomial of degree $n$ whose coefficients are uniform on $N \ge 35$ consecutive integers in
$[-H, H]$, with nonzero constant term, is irreducible with probability at least $1 - n^{-c}$.
Here $c > 0$ is an absolute constant, and $n$ must be at least an absolute constant and at least
$(\log H)^3$. We state it for the integers
$\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ with $M \ge 34$, so $N = M + 1 \ge 35$ and $H = M$. In particular
`irreducibleProb M n` $\to 1$ for each such $M$, which is the analogue of `green_93` for
coefficients in $\{0, \dots, M\}$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_93.variants.bskk_large :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ M n : ℕ, 34 ≤ M → n₀ ≤ n → (Real.log (M : ℝ)) ^ 3 ≤ n →
      1 - (n : ℝ) ^ (-c) ≤ irreducibleProb M n

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 93 — bskk small
problems.statement:
Bary-Soroker, Koukoulopoulos and Kozma [BSKK23, Theorem 1(b)] proved that a random monic
polynomial of degree $n$ whose coefficients are uniform on $N$ consecutive integers in $[-H, H]$
with $2 \le N \le 34$, and with nonzero constant term, is irreducible with probability at least
$\delta$. Here $\delta > 0$ is an absolute constant, and $n$ must be at least an absolute constant
and at least $(\log H)^3$. We state it for the integers $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ with
$1 \le M \le 33$, so $N = M + 1$ and $H = M$. The condition on $(\log H)^3$ is absorbed into
$n_0$, because $M$ is bounded. The case $M = 1$ gives $p_n \ge \delta$ for large $n$ for the
polynomial of `green_93`.
problems.lean:
theorem green_93.variants.bskk_small :
    ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ M n : ℕ, 1 ≤ M → M ≤ 33 → n₀ ≤ n →
      δ ≤ irreducibleProb M n

problems.title: Ben Green's Open Problem 93 — konyagin
problems.statement:
Konyagin [Ko99] proved that $p_n \ge c / \log n$ for an absolute constant $c > 0$, as stated in
[BrVa19, Section 1]. We state it for all large $n$. It is superseded by
`green_93.variants.bskk_small`.
problems.lean:
theorem green_93.variants.konyagin :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c / Real.log (n : ℝ) ≤ irreducibleProb 1 n

problems.title: Cilleruelo, Luca and Baxter. — lower bound
problems.statement:
**Cilleruelo, Luca and Baxter.** Let $g \ge 2$. There is a constant $c_1 > 0$ such that, for all
real $x \ge 2$, the number of $n \le x$ which are a sum of two base-$g$ palindromes is at least
$x^{1 - c_1 / \sqrt{\log x}} = x e^{-c_1 \sqrt{\log x}}$ [CLB18, Theorem 1.3]. We count positive
$n$ only.
problems.lean:
theorem green_95.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ g : ℕ, 2 ≤ g → ∃ c₁ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ ∀ x : ℝ, 2 ≤ x →
      x ^ (1 - c₁ / Real.sqrt (Real.log x)) ≤
        ({n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ x ∧ n ∈ sumsOfTwo g}.ncard : ℝ)

problems.title: Cilleruelo, Luca and Baxter. — three palindromes
problems.statement:
**Cilleruelo, Luca and Baxter.** Let $g \ge 5$. Then every positive integer is a sum of three
base-$g$ palindromes [CLB18, Theorem 1.2]. Here $0$ counts as a palindrome, as in [CLB18], so
this says that every positive integer is a sum of at most three positive palindromes.
problems.lean:
theorem green_95.variants.three_palindromes :
    ∀ g : ℕ, 5 ≤ g → ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      ∃ p q r, IsPalindrome g p ∧ IsPalindrome g q ∧ IsPalindrome g r ∧ p + q + r = n

problems.title: Zakharov's theorem.
problems.statement:
**Zakharov's theorem.** For every integer $g \ge 2$ there is a constant $c > 0$ such that, for all
large $X$, the number of $n < X$ which are a sum of two positive base-$g$ palindromes is at most
$X / \log^c X$ [Za24, Theorem 1]. We state it for integer $X$. This answers the question of
[CLB18], who had proved an upper bound $c X$ with $c < 1$ for $g \ge 3$ [CLB18, Theorem 1.4].
problems.lean:
theorem green_95.variants.zakharov :
    ∀ g : ℕ, 2 ≤ g → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ X : ℕ in atTop,
      ((sumsOfTwoPositive g ∩ Set.Iio X).ncard : ℝ) ≤ (X : ℝ) / Real.log X ^ c

problems.title: Bowtell and Keevash.
problems.statement:
**Bowtell and Keevash.** For $n \equiv 1, 5 \pmod 6$ the number of toroidal $n$-queens
configurations satisfies $T(n) = ((1+o(1))\, n e^{-3})^n$ [BoKe21, Theorem 1.2]. The filter
`toroidalDegrees` restricts to these $n$, because $T(n) = 0$ for all other $n \ge 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_97.variants.bowtell_keevash :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numToroidalQueens n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / n) / n) toroidalDegrees
      (𝓝 (Real.exp (-3)))

problems.title: Eberhard, Manners and Mrazović.
problems.statement:
**Eberhard, Manners and Mrazović.** For odd $n$, the number $s_n$ of pairs $(\pi_1, \pi_2)$ of
bijections $\{1, \dots, n\} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with $\pi_1 + \pi_2$ also a bijection is
$$s_n = (e^{-1/2} + o(1))\, \frac{(n!)^3}{n^{n-1}}$$
[EMM19, Theorem 1.2]. [Gr24] refers to this paper for the variant of the toroidal question where
only $\pi_1$, $\pi_2$ and $\pi_1 - \pi_2$ are required to be bijections. Replacing $\pi_2$ by
$-\pi_2$ shows that this variant has the same count $s_n$. For even $n$, $s_n = 0$
[EMM19, Section 1], so the theorem is stated for odd $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_97.variants.eberhard_manners_mrazovic :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numAdditiveTriples n : ℝ)) ~[atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {n : ℕ | Odd n}]
      fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.exp (-(1 / 2)) * ((n ! : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 3 / (n : ℝ) ^ (n - 1)

problems.title: Simkin's theorem.
problems.statement:
**Simkin's theorem.** There is a constant $1.94 < \alpha < 1.9449$ such that
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{Q(n)^{1/n}}{n} = e^{-\alpha},$$
that is, $Q(n) = ((1+o(1))\, n e^{-\alpha})^n$ [Si23, Theorem 1.1]. The constant $\alpha$ is
defined in [Si23] as the solution of a convex optimisation problem over Borel probability measures
on the square $[-1/2, 1/2]^2$. The limit determines $\alpha$ uniquely. Nobel, Agrawal and Boyd
[NAB23] combined Simkin's formulation with a sharper bound of Knuth, solved the resulting convex
problems numerically, and report the tighter range
$\alpha \in [1.944000752, 1.944001082]$.
problems.lean:
theorem green_97.variants.simkin :
    ∃ α : ℝ, 1.94 < α ∧ α < 1.9449 ∧
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ ↦ (numQueens n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / n) / n) atTop
        (𝓝 (Real.exp (-α)))

problems.title: Paths (Gyárfás 1987).
problems.statement:
**Paths (Gyárfás 1987).**

For every $n$, the class of $P_n$-free graphs is $\chi$-bounded. For $n \ge 2$ and
nonempty $G$, Gyárfás's argument gives $\chi(G) \le (n-1)^{\omega(G) - 1}$.

*Reference:* [Gy87].
problems.lean:
theorem gyarfas_sumner_conjecture.variants.path (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, IsChiBoundedBy (pathGraph n) f

problems.title: Trees of radius two (Kierstead–Penrice 1994).
problems.statement:
**Trees of radius two (Kierstead–Penrice 1994).**

Every tree of radius at most $2$ (i.e. with a vertex within distance $2$ of every other vertex)
specifies a $\chi$-bounded class.

*Reference:* [KP94].
problems.lean:
theorem gyarfas_sumner_conjecture.variants.radius_two
    {W : Type} [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] (T : SimpleGraph W) [DecidableRel T.Adj]
    (hT : T.IsTree) (hrad : ∃ c : W, ∀ w : W, T.dist c w ≤ 2) :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, IsChiBoundedBy T f

problems.title: Catlin (1979): counterexamples for every $k \ge 7$.
problems.statement:
**Catlin (1979): counterexamples for every $k \ge 7$.**

*Reference:* [Ca79].
problems.lean:
theorem hajos_conjecture.variants.catlin (k : ℕ) (hk : 7 ≤ k) :
    ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      (k : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber ∧ ¬ ContainsSubdivision (completeGraph (Fin k)) G

problems.title: The cases $k \le 4$ (Dirac 1952).
problems.statement:
**The cases $k \le 4$ (Dirac 1952).**

Every graph with chromatic number at least $4$ contains a subdivision of $K_4$; the cases
$k \le 3$ are elementary.

*Reference:* [Di52].
problems.lean:
theorem hajos_conjecture.variants.le_four
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ 4)
    (h : (k : ℕ∞) ≤ G.chromaticNumber) : ContainsSubdivision (completeGraph (Fin k)) G

problems.title: The Hall ratio is a lower bound for the fractional chromatic number.
problems.statement:
**The Hall ratio is a lower bound for the fractional chromatic number.**

For every graph, $\rho(G) \le \chi_f(G)$ (see [SU97]); the conjecture asked for an inequality in
the other direction up to a constant.
problems.lean:
theorem hall_ratio_conjecture.variants.hallRatio_le_fractionalChromaticNumber
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    hallRatio G ≤ G.fractionalChromaticNumber

problems.title: Unbounded ratio (Dvořák–Ossona de Mendez–Wu 2020; Blumenthal et al. 2022).
problems.statement:
**Unbounded ratio (Dvořák–Ossona de Mendez–Wu 2020; Blumenthal et al. 2022).**

For every $C$ there is a graph with $\chi_f(G) > C\,\rho(G)$.

*References:* [DOW20], [BLMNPV22].
problems.lean:
theorem hall_ratio_conjecture.variants.unbounded (C : ℝ) :
    ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (_ : DecidableEq V) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      C * hallRatio G < G.fractionalChromaticNumber

problems.title: El-Zahar–Sauer (1985): the conjecture holds when `min {χ(G), χ(H)} ≤ 4`.
problems.statement:
**El-Zahar–Sauer (1985): the conjecture holds when `min {χ(G), χ(H)} ≤ 4`.**

If both $G$ and $H$ are $4$-chromatic then so is $G \times H$; together with the easy cases
$\min\{\chi(G), \chi(H)\} \le 3$, this gives Hedetniemi's equality whenever
$\min\{\chi(G), \chi(H)\} \le 4$.

*Reference:* [ES85].
problems.lean:
theorem hedetniemi_conjecture.variants.el_zahar_sauer
    {α β : Type} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β)
    (h : min G.chromaticNumber H.chromaticNumber ≤ 4) :
    (tensorProd G H).chromaticNumber = min G.chromaticNumber H.chromaticNumber

problems.title: Shitov (2019): the conjecture fails.
problems.statement:
**Shitov (2019): the conjecture fails.**

There exist finite graphs $G$, $H$ with $\chi(G \times H) < \min\{\chi(G), \chi(H)\}$.
Tardif [Ta22] later gave counterexamples with $\min\{\chi(G),\chi(H)\} = 14$ and
$\chi(G \times H) = 13$, and Zhu [Zh21] considerably smaller ones.

*References:* [Sh19], [Ta22], [Zh21].
problems.lean:
theorem hedetniemi_conjecture.variants.shitov :
    ∃ (α β : Type) (_ : Fintype α) (_ : Fintype β) (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β),
      (tensorProd G H).chromaticNumber < min G.chromaticNumber H.chromaticNumber

Every finite group is realisable over the field of rational functions

problems.title: Kaplansky's Conjectures — char two
problems.statement:
The counterexample of [OAI26c], as stated in OpenAI's Lean proof: a finite field $K$ of
characteristic two, a finitely generated group $G$ and $a, b \in K[G]$ with $ab = 1$ and
$ba \neq 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem direct_finiteness_conjecture.variants.char_two :
    ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Field K) (_ : Fintype K) (_ : CharP K 2),
      ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Group.FG G),
        ∃ a b : MonoidAlgebra K G, a * b = 1 ∧ b * a ≠ 1

problems.title: Kaplansky's Conjectures — char zero
problems.statement: Kaplansky proved the conjecture for fields of characteristic zero [Ka69].
problems.lean:
theorem direct_finiteness_conjecture.variants.char_zero (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K]
    (G : Type*) [Group G] : IsDedekindFiniteMonoid (MonoidAlgebra K G)

problems.title: Merkurjev's theorem
problems.statement:
**Merkurjev's theorem** [Merkurjev1991], see also [EKM2008, Theorem 38.4]: every positive even
integer is a $u$-invariant. The case $6$, the first counterexample to Kaplansky's conjecture, is
[Merkurjev1989].
problems.lean:
theorem u_invariant_values.variants.even (n : ℕ) (hn : Even n) (hn₀ : n ≠ 0) :
    IsUInvariant n

problems.title: Kaplansky's conjecture
problems.statement:
**Kaplansky's conjecture** [Kaplansky1953, p. 202]: the $u$-invariant of a field is a power of
$2$ whenever it is finite. Disproved by Merkurjev, who constructed a field of $u$-invariant $6$
[Merkurjev1989] (`u_invariant_values.variants.even`).
problems.lean:
theorem u_invariant_values.variants.kaplansky_conjecture :
    ¬ ∀ n, IsUInvariant n → ∃ k, n = 2 ^ k

problems.title: Karpenko's theorem
problems.statement:
**Karpenko's theorem** [Karpenko2026, Theorem 1.1]: if neither $n + 1$ nor $n + 3$ is a power
of $2$, then there is a field of $u$-invariant $n$. This covers every positive integer except
$1$, $3$, $5$, $7$ and the integers $2^r - 1$, $2^r - 3$ with $r \ge 4$. As of September 2026
the result is a preprint and not yet peer-reviewed.
problems.lean:
theorem u_invariant_values.variants.karpenko (n : ℕ) (h₁ : ∀ r, 2 ^ r ≠ n + 1)
    (h₃ : ∀ r, 2 ^ r ≠ n + 3) : IsUInvariant n

problems.title: Vishik's theorem
problems.statement:
**Vishik's theorem** [Vishik2009, Corollary 5.2]: for every $r \ge 3$ there is a field of
$u$-invariant $2^r + 1$.
problems.lean:
theorem u_invariant_values.variants.two_pow_add_one (r : ℕ) (hr : 3 ≤ r) :
    IsUInvariant (2 ^ r + 1)

problems.title: Conjecture 1.74 (Minimal topological groups) — tarski monster
problems.statement:
There exists a Tarski monster group that admits a non-discrete Hausdorff group
topology. This follows from Theorem 1.4 of Klyachko, Olshanskii and Osin, which
gives a topologizable Tarski monster of every sufficiently large odd exponent $n$;
taking $n$ to be a prime $p$ makes every non-trivial proper subgroup cyclic of
order $p$. Any such group is a minimal topological group.
problems.lean:
theorem kourovka_1_74.variants.tarski_monster :
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : TopologicalSpace G),
      IsTarskiMonster G ∧ IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ T2Space G ∧
      ¬ DiscreteTopology G

problems.title: Lam--Litt conjecture — eisenstein
problems.statement:
Eisenstein's theorem (1852): an algebraic power series over $\mathbb{Q}[z]$ has bounded
denominators, i.e., there exists $N$ such that all coefficients lie in $\mathbb{Z}[1/N]$.
problems.lean:
theorem lam_litt.variants.eisenstein (f : PowerSeries ℚ) (hAlg : IsAlgebraic (Polynomial ℚ) f) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, IsCoeffIntegralAdjointInvNat f N

problems.title: Lehmer's Mahler measure problem — not reciprocal
problems.statement: If $f$ is irreducible and not reciprocal and $M(f) > 1$ then $M(f) \ge M(X^3 - X - 1)$.
problems.lean:
theorem lehmer_mahler_measure_problem.variants.not_reciprocal (f : ℤ[X]) (hi : Irreducible f)
    (hf : mahlerMeasureZ f > 1) (hf' : f.reverse ≠ f) :
    mahlerMeasureZ f ≥ mahlerMeasureZ (X^3 - X - 1)

problems.title: Lehmer's Mahler measure problem — odd
problems.statement:
If $f$ is not reciprocal, all the coefficients of $f$ are odd and $M(f) > 1$, then
$M(f) \ge M(X^2 - X - 1)$.

A polynomial $f$ of degree $d$ is *reciprocal* when $X^d f(1/X) = \pm f$, so nonreciprocity
rules out both signs. The negative sign has to be excluded as well: the polynomial
$X^7 - X^6 - X^5 - X^4 + X^3 + X^2 + X - 1$ has all coefficients odd and satisfies
$X^7 f(1/X) = -f$, but $1 < M(f) = 1.5823\dots < M(X^2 - X - 1)$.
problems.lean:
theorem lehmer_mahler_measure_problem.variants.odd (f : ℤ[X])
    (hf : mahlerMeasureZ f > 1) (hf' : f.reverse ≠ f) (hf'' : f.reverse ≠ -f)
    (hodd : f.HasOddCoeffs) :
    mahlerMeasureZ f ≥ mahlerMeasureZ (X^2 - X - 1)

problems.title: Alon (1988): the linear arboricity conjecture holds asymptotically.
problems.statement:
**Alon (1988): the linear arboricity conjecture holds asymptotically.**

For every `ε > 0` there is a `Δ₀` such that every graph of maximum degree `Δ ≥ Δ₀` has linear
arboricity at most `(1 / 2 + ε) Δ`.

*Reference:* [Al88].
problems.lean:
theorem linear_arboricity_conjecture.variants.alon (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ Δ₀ : ℕ, ∀ Δ : ℕ, Δ₀ ≤ Δ → ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∀ [DecidableRel G.Adj], G.maxDegree ≤ Δ →
        (linearArboricity G : ℝ) ≤ (1 / 2 + ε) * Δ

problems.title: Cubic graphs have linear arboricity two
problems.statement:
**Cubic graphs have linear arboricity two** (Akiyama–Exoo–Harary [AEH81]).

The edges of every nonempty `3`-regular graph can be partitioned into two linear forests, and one
linear forest is not enough.
problems.lean:
theorem linear_arboricity_conjecture.variants.cubic {V : Type} [Fintype V] [Nonempty V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hreg : ∀ v, G.degree v = 3) :
    linearArboricity G = 2

problems.title: Theorem 1.3 (Tao, 2017; arXiv:1701.02048).
problems.statement:
**Theorem 1.3 (Tao, 2017; arXiv:1701.02048).**
There exists an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$,
the gap of loneliness satisfies
$\delta_n \ge \frac{1}{2n} + \frac{c \log n}{n^2 (\log \log n)^2}$.
problems.lean:
theorem lonely_runner_conjecture.variants.tao_2017 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
      (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
        deltaGap n ≥
          ((1 : ℝ) / (2 * (n : ℝ))
            + c * Real.log (n : ℝ) /
                ((n : ℝ) ^ 2 * (Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ))) ^ 2)))

problems.title: Mahler's 3/2 Problem — flatto lagarias pollington
problems.statement:
Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington proved that for all rational `p/q > 1` in lowest terms with
`q ≥ 2`, we have `Ω(p/q) ≥ 1/p`: for every `θ > 0`, the limit points of `{θ (p/q)^n}` are not
contained in any interval of length less than `1/p`.
problems.lean:
theorem mahler_conjecture.variants.flatto_lagarias_pollington (p q : ℕ) (hq : 1 < q)
    (hpq : p.Coprime q) (hpq' : q < p) : 1 / p ≤ Ω (p / q)

problems.title: The Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture (1988) — pokrovskiy
problems.statement:

problems.title: Trees are cop-win (Nowakowski–Winkler 1983).

**Trees are cop-win (Nowakowski–Winkler 1983).**

Every nonempty tree has cop number `1`: a single cop, always moving towards the robber, catches

problems.statement:
**Complete multipartite graphs with parts of size at most $2$ (Erdős–Rubin–Taylor 1979).**

The complete multipartite graph $K_{2,2,\dots,2}$ with $k$ parts has $2k$ vertices

problems.title: Pfister's problem on the Pythagoras number of $\mathbb{R}(X_1, \dots, X_n)$ — lower bound
problems.statement:
The lower bound $n + 2 \le p(\mathbb{R}(X_1, \dots, X_n))$ for $n \ge 2$ [Pfister1995, p. 97],
a consequence of the Cassels–Ellison–Pfister theorem [CEP1971]. The hypothesis $n \ge 2$ is
needed: $p(\mathbb{R}(X)) = 2 < 3$.
