problems.title: Sendov's conjecture — eventually true
problems.statement:
**Sendov's conjecture** states that for a polynomial
$$f(z)=(z-r_{1})\cdots (z-r_{n}),\qquad (n\geq 2)$$
with all roots $r_1, ..., r_n$ inside the closed unit disk $|z| ≤ 1$, each of the $n$ roots is at a
distance no more than $1$ from at least one critical point.

It has been shown that Sendov's conjecture holds for polynomials of sufficiently large degree.
problems.lean:
theorem sendov_conjecture.variants.eventually_true :
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, n.SatisfiesSendovConjecture

distance no more than $1$ from at least one critical point.

It has been shown that Sendov's conjecture holds when the degree $n$ is at most $8$.

minimal prime $P$ with $\dim R/P = \dim R$.

problems.title: Matzri's theorem
problems.statement:
**Matzri's theorem** [Matzri2016, Theorem 8.2] for $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m)$, which is a
$C_m$ field by Tsen–Lang [Lang1952]: for $m \ge 1$, every class in
$K^M_2(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p^t$ is a sum of at most $t(p^{m-1} - 1)$ symbols.
problems.lean:
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_two (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (p t : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) :
    t * (p ^ (m - 1) - 1) ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) (p ^ t) 2

problems.title: The symbol length of $K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$ — degree two ge
problems.statement:
The matching lower bound in degree $2$ [BecherHoffmann2004, Proposition 4.5], by an argument going
back to Nakayama: for distinct monic irreducibles $f_1, \dots, f_{m-1}$ in $\mathbb{C}[x_1]$ the
tensor product of the symbol algebras $(f_i, x_{i+1})_p$ is a division algebra over
$\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m)$, so no $k < m - 1$ bounds the symbol length of
$K^M_2(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$.
problems.lean:
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.degree_two_ge (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (p : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) :
    ∀ k ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p 2, m - 1 ≤ k

problems.title: The symbol length of $K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p$ — zero mem of lt
problems.statement:
$K^M_n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m))/p = 0$ for $n > m$: the field has cohomological dimension $m$
[Serre1997, Ch. II, §4.2], so $H^n(\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_m), \mu_p^{\otimes n}) = 0$, and
$K^M_n/p \cong H^n(-, \mu_p^{\otimes n})$ by the norm residue isomorphism theorem [Voevodsky2011].
problems.lean:
theorem symbol_length_problem.variants.zero_mem_of_lt (m n p : ℕ) (hmn : m < n) (hp : p.Prime) :
    0 ∈ symbolLengthBounds (MvRatFunc (Fin m) ℂ) p n

Roberts and Simpson [Ro10] showed that the union-closed sets conjecture holds for set families of
size at most 46.
Their method, however, combined with the result of [Vu17], further shows that it holds for `#A ≤ 50`
as well.
[Ro10] Roberts, Ian; Simpson, Jamie (2010). "A note on the union-closed sets conjecture" (PDF). Australas. J. Combin. 47: 265–267.
[Vu17] Vuckovic, Bojan; Zivkovic, Miodrag (2017). "The 12-Element Case of Frankl's Conjecture" (PDF). IPSI BGD Transactions on Internet Research. 13 (1): 65.

    (h_union_closed : IsUnionClosed A)
    (hA : #A ≤ 50) :
    ∃ i : n, (1 / 2 : ℚ) * #A ≤ #{x ∈ A | i ∈ x}

problems.title: The Clark–Suen inequality (2000).
problems.statement:
**The Clark–Suen inequality (2000).**

For all finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$,
$\gamma(G \,\square\, H) \ge \tfrac12\,\gamma(G)\,\gamma(H)$; that is, Vizing's conjecture holds
up to a factor of $2$.

*Reference:* [ClSu00].

    {α β : Type} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β) :
    G.dominationNumber * H.dominationNumber ≤ 2 * (G □ H).dominationNumber

theorem erdos_137.variants.perfect_power (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2) (n : ℕ) (x l : ℕ) (hl : 2 ≤ l) :
    (∏ x ∈ Finset.Ioc n (n + k), x) ≠ x ^ l

problems.title: Erdős Problem 23 — n5
problems.statement:
Every triangle-free graph on $25$ vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most $25$
edges.

This is the $n = 5$ case of Erdős Problem 23.  It follows from the high-density range of
Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky together with McKay's complete catalogue of the 23-vertex extremal
graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_23.variants.n5 :
    ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)),
        H ≤ G ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 25

problems.title: Erdős Problem 23 — n5 tight
problems.statement:
There exists a triangle-free graph on $25$ vertices such that at least $25$ edges must be
removed to make it bipartite.  The balanced blow-up of $C_5$ with five parts of size $5$
witnesses this.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_23.variants.n5_tight :
    ∃ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 ∧ ∀ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)),
        H ≤ G → H.IsBipartite → 25 ≤ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card

problems.title: Erdős Problem 375 — bounded gap
problems.statement:
If `Erdos375Prop` is true, then `(n + 1).nth Prime - n.nth Prime < (n.nth Prime) ^ (1 / 2 - c)`
for some `c > 0`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_375.variants.bounded_gap : Erdos375Prop →
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (n + 1).nth Nat.Prime - n.nth Nat.Prime
    < (n.nth Nat.Prime : ℝ) ^ (1 / (2 : ℝ) - c)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 375 — log
problems.statement:
There exists a constant `c > 0` such that for all `n`, if
`k < c * (log n / (log (log n))) ^ 3 → (∀ i < k, ¬ (n + i + 1).Prime)`, then
there are distinct primes `p₁, ... pₖ` such that `pᵢ ∣ n + i` for all `1 ≤ i ≤ k`. This is proved
in [RST75]. There is no need to only consider sufficiently large `n` because one can always take
`c` small enough so that `k < c * (log n / (log (log n))) ^ 3` implies that `k = 0` until `n` is
large.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_375.variants.log : ∃ c > 0, ∀ n k : ℕ,
    k < c * (Real.log n / (Real.log (Real.log n))) ^ 3 → (∀ i < k, ¬ (n + i + 1).Prime) →
    ∃ p : Fin k → ℕ, p.Injective ∧ ∀ i, (p i).Prime ∧ p i ∣ n + i + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 506 — large n
problems.statement:
For $n > 393$ the answer is $\binom{n-1}{2} + 1 - \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor$
(Elliott [El67], with the correction of Purdy and Smith [PuSm], also reported in [BaBa94]): this is
both a lower bound for every such configuration and is attained, e.g. by a circle with $n - 1$
points together with a single point off the circle.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_506.variants.large_n (n : ℕ) (hn : 393 < n) :
    IsLeast { k : ℕ | ∃ P : Finset ℝ²,
        P.card = n ∧ ¬ Collinear ℝ (P : Set ℝ²) ∧ ¬ Cospherical (P : Set ℝ²) ∧
        numCircles (P : Set ℝ²) = k }
      (erdos_506.variants.large_n.answer n)

problems.title: Erdős Problem 506 — segre n eq eight
problems.statement:
Segre's observation: the lower bound $\binom{n-1}{2}$ (without the correction of [PuSm]) is
already false for $n = 8$, as witnessed by the projection of a cube onto a plane. Hence the minimum
number of circles determined by $8$ such points is strictly less than $\binom{7}{2} = 21$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_506.variants.segre_n_eq_eight :
    ∃ P : Finset ℝ²,
      P.card = 8 ∧ ¬ Collinear ℝ (P : Set ℝ²) ∧ ¬ Cospherical (P : Set ℝ²) ∧
      numCircles (P : Set ℝ²) < (8 - 1).choose 2

problems.title: Erdős Problem 617 — r2
problems.statement:
Erdős and Gyárfás [ErGy99] showed this property fails for infinitely many $r$ if we replace $r^2+1$
by $r^2$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_617.variants.r2 :
    {r : ℕ | ∃ (V : Type) (_ : Fintype V) (_ : DecidableEq V), Fintype.card V = r^2 ∧
      ∃ (coloring : Sym2 V → Fin r),
        ∀ (S : Finset V), S.card = r + 1 →
          ∀ (k : Fin r), ∃ u ∈ S, ∃ v ∈ S, u ≠ v ∧ coloring s(u, v) = k}.Infinite

problems.title: Erdős Problem 617 — r eq 3
problems.statement: Erdős and Gyárfás [ErGy99] proved the conjecture for $r=3$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_617.variants.r_eq_3 (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≥ 3) {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (hV : Fintype.card V = 3^2 + 1) (coloring : Sym2 V → Fin 3) :
    ∃ (S : Finset V) (k : Fin 3),
      S.card = 3 + 1 ∧
      ∀ u ∈ S, ∀ v ∈ S, u ≠ v → coloring s(u, v) ≠ k

problems.title: Erdős Problem 617 — r eq 4
problems.statement: Erdős and Gyárfás [ErGy99] proved the conjecture for $r=4$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_617.variants.r_eq_4 (r : ℕ) (hr : r ≥ 3) {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

problems.statement: Erdős [Er68b] originally asked about $a=b=3$ which was proved by Brown and Jung [BrJu69] (who in fact prove that $G$ must contain two vertex disjoint odd cycles)..

problems.title: Erdős Problem 743 — all but two stars
problems.statement:
Gyárfás and Lehel [GyLe78] proved that this holds if all but at most $2$ of the trees are stars,
or if all the trees are stars or paths. This variant is the first case.

Here a star on `Fin k` is `starGraph c` for a centre `c`. The two trees that may fail to be
stars are $T_a$ and $T_b$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_743.variants.all_but_two_stars (n : ℕ) (T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k))
    (hT : ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, (T k).IsTree)
    (hstar : ∃ a b : ℕ, ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, k ≠ a → k ≠ b → ∃ c : Fin k, T k = starGraph c) :
    IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 743 — almost linear degree
problems.statement:
Allen, Böttcher, Clemens, Hladký, Piguet, and Taraz [ABCHPT21] proved that this conjecture holds
when all the trees have maximum degree $\leq c\frac{n}{\log n}$ for some constant $c>0$. That is,
there is $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$ the following holds. If $T_k$ is a tree
with $k$ vertices and maximum degree at most $cn/\log n$ for $2 \leq k \leq n$, then $K_n$
decomposes into $T_2, \ldots, T_n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_743.variants.almost_linear_degree :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k),
      (∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n,
        (T k).IsTree ∧ ((T k).maxDegree : ℝ) ≤ c * (n : ℝ) / Real.log (n : ℝ)) →
        IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 743 — bollobas
problems.statement:
Bollobás [Bo83] proved that the smallest $\lfloor n/\sqrt{2}\rfloor$ many trees can always be
packed greedily into $K_n$.

The smallest trees are $T_1, \ldots, T_m$ with $m = \lfloor n/\sqrt{2} \rfloor$. The tree $T_1$ is
a single vertex, so we only pack $T_2, \ldots, T_m$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_743.variants.bollobas (n : ℕ) (T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k))
    (hT : ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 ⌊(n : ℝ) / Real.sqrt 2⌋₊, (T k).IsTree) :
    IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 ⌊(n : ℝ) / Real.sqrt 2⌋₊) T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 743 — bounded degree
problems.statement:
Joos, Kim, Kühn, and Osthus [JKKO19] proved that this conjecture holds when the trees have
bounded maximum degree. That is, for every $d$ there is $N$ such that for all $n \geq N$ the
following holds. If $T_k$ is a tree with $k$ vertices and maximum degree at most $d$ for
$2 \leq k \leq n$, then $K_n$ decomposes into $T_2, \ldots, T_n$.

They even allow the first $o(n)$ trees to have arbitrary maximum degree.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_743.variants.bounded_degree (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → ∀ T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k),
      (∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, (T k).IsTree ∧ (T k).maxDegree ≤ d) →
        IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 743 — fishburn
problems.statement: Fishburn [Fi83b] proved this for $n\leq 9$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_743.variants.fishburn (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 9) (T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k))
    (hT : ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, (T k).IsTree) :
    IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 743 — largest trees
problems.statement:
Janzer and Montgomery [JaMo24] have proved that there exists some $c>0$ such that the largest $cn$
trees can be packed into $K_n$.

We state this for all sufficiently large $n$. The trees are $T_k$ with $n - cn < k \leq n$, and
we also require $2 \leq k$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_743.variants.largest_trees :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k),
      (∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k ≤ n → (n : ℝ) - c * n < k → (T k).IsTree) →
        IsPacking n {k : ℕ | 2 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ n ∧ (n : ℝ) - c * n < k} T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 743 — stars or paths
problems.statement:
Gyárfás and Lehel [GyLe78] proved that this holds if all but at most $2$ of the trees are stars,
or if all the trees are stars or paths. This variant is the second case: each tree is a star or a
path.

Here a star on `Fin k` is `starGraph c` for a centre `c`, and a path is a graph isomorphic to
`pathGraph k`.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_743.variants.stars_or_paths (n : ℕ) (T : (k : ℕ) → SimpleGraph (Fin k))
    (hT : ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 2 n, (T k).IsTree ∧
      ((∃ c : Fin k, T k = starGraph c) ∨ Nonempty (T k ≃g pathGraph k))) :
    IsPacking n (Set.Icc 2 n) T

problems.title: Erdős Problem 151 — cliqueFree three
problems.statement:
If $G$ is triangle-free, then $\tau(G)\leq n-H(n)$: the complement of an independent set meets
every edge.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_151.variants.cliqueFree_three (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (hG : G.CliqueFree 3) : cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - H n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 151 — sqrt bound
problems.statement:
It is easy to see that $\tau(G)\leq n-\sqrt{n}$. We state this with $\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor$:
with the real square root the bound fails for a single edge ($n = 2$, $\tau = 1$).
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_151.variants.sqrt_bound (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) :
    cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - Nat.sqrt n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 551 — sufficiently large
problems.statement:
For sufficiently large $n$ and every $k\geq n$, $R(C_k,K_n)=(k-1)(n-1)+1$.

Keevash, Long, and Skokan [KLS21] have proved this identity when
$k\geq C\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}$ for some constant $C$, thus establishing the conjecture
for sufficiently large $n$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_551.variants.sufficiently_large :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ, n ≤ k →
      SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph k)
        (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) = (k - 1) * (n - 1) + 1

problems.title: Erdős Problem 556 — benevides skokan large even
problems.statement:
Benevides and Skokan [BeSk09] settled the even case for large $n$: for all sufficiently large
even $n$,
$$R(C_n; 3) = 2n.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_556.variants.benevides_skokan_large_even :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Even n → multicolourRamsey (cycleGraph n) 3 = 2 * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 556 — kss large odd
problems.statement:
Kohayakawa, Simonovits and Skokan [KSS05] settled the conjecture for large odd $n$: for all
sufficiently large odd $n$,
$$R(C_n; 3) = 4n - 3.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_556.variants.kss_large_odd :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Odd n → multicolourRamsey (cycleGraph n) 3 = 4 * n - 3

problems.title: Erdős Problem 556 — luczak asymptotic
problems.statement:
Łuczak's asymptotic bound [Lu99]: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, for all sufficiently large $n$,
$$R(C_n; 3) \le (4 + \varepsilon)n.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_556.variants.luczak_asymptotic :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (multicolourRamsey (cycleGraph n) 3 : ℝ) ≤ (4 + ε) * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 556 — luczak asymptotic even
problems.statement:
Łuczak's asymptotic bound for even $n$ [Lu99]: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, for all sufficiently
large even $n$,
$$R(C_n; 3) \le (3 + \varepsilon)n.$$
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_556.variants.luczak_asymptotic_even :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, Even n →
      (multicolourRamsey (cycleGraph n) 3 : ℝ) ≤ (3 + ε) * n

problems.title: Erdős Problem 556 — odd lower bound
problems.statement:
For odd $n$ the bound $4n - 3$ is best possible: the $3$-colour Ramsey number is at least
$4n - 3$, so equality holds whenever the conjectured upper bound does.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_556.variants.odd_lower_bound (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hodd : Odd n) :
    4 * n - 3 ≤ multicolourRamsey (cycleGraph n) 3

problems.title: Resolution of singularities fails over imperfect fields.
problems.statement:
**Resolution of singularities fails over imperfect fields.**
If the field $k$ is not perfect, then there is an integral scheme $X$ of dimension zero that is
separated and of finite type over $k$ and has no resolution of singularities: no integral scheme
smooth over $k$ admits a proper birational morphism to $X$.

A witness: $k$ has characteristic $p > 0$ and there is some $a \in k \setminus k^p$. Take
$X = \operatorname{Spec} k(a^{1/p})$. Every integral scheme birational to $X$ has function field
$k(a^{1/p})$, which is not separable over $k$, whereas the function field of an integral scheme
smooth over $k$ is separable over $k$.

So the hypothesis `PerfectField k` cannot be dropped from `resolution_of_singularities` or from
`resolution_of_singularities_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_three`.
problems.lean:
theorem exists_not_hasResolution_of_not_perfectField (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (hk : ¬ PerfectField k) :
    ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)), IsIntegral X ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType sX ∧
      QuasiCompact sX ∧ IsSeparated sX ∧ topologicalKrullDim X = 0 ∧
      ¬ Scheme.HasResolution sX

problems.statement:
The greedy construction gives a Sidon set `A ⊆ {1, ..., N}` of size at least $N^{1/3}$,

problems.title: Optimal monotone families for the discrete isoperimetric inequality
problems.statement:
Now a famous isoperimetric relation asserts that
(IR) $I^p(F) \ge \frac{1}{p} \mu_p(F) \log_p \mu_p(F)$
This relation holds for monotone increasing families $F$ and $0 < p < 1$.
It is especially famous and simple when
$p=1/2$ and $\mu_p(F)=1/2$. In this case, it says that given a set of half the vertices of the
discrete cube $2^X$, the number of edges between $F$ and its complement is at least $2^{n-1}$.

*Note on translation:* We use `Real.logb p m` to represent the logarithm base $p$ directly.
The factor of $p$ in the denominator (equivalent to $1/p$ in front) is consistent with the
definition of `IsOptimal` used in the counterexample proof.
problems.lean:

    (F : Finset (Finset (Fin n))) (hF : IsMonotoneIncreasing F) :
    let m := μFamily p F
    edgeBoundary n p F ≥ m * Real.logb p m / p

problems.title: Erdős Problem 1114 — rolle
problems.statement:
All the zeros of $f'(x)$ are all distinct real numbers in $(a_0,a_n)$ by Rolle's theorem.

Precisely, for $f$ as in `erdos_1114` (degree $N+1$, roots $a+jd$ for $0\le j\le N$), each
interval $(a+kd,a+(k+1)d)$ with $k<N$ contains exactly one zero of $f'$, and every zero of $f'$
lies in one of these intervals.

    (hdegree : f.natDegree = N + 1)
    (hroots : ∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ N → f.eval (a + d * j) = 0) :
    (∀ k : ℕ, k < N →
      ∃! x : ℝ, x ∈ Set.Ioo (a + d * k) (a + d * (k + 1)) ∧ f.derivative.eval x = 0) ∧
    (∀ x : ℝ, f.derivative.eval x = 0 →
      ∃ k : ℕ, k < N ∧ x ∈ Set.Ioo (a + d * k) (a + d * (k + 1)))

problems.statement:
Suppose monotone sequence $A$ satisfies the following: `A 0 = 1` and for all `j`, `A (j + 1)` is the
smallest natural number that cannot be written as a sum of consecutive terms of `A 0, ..., A j`.
Then the first few terms of $A$ are $1,2,4,5,8,10,14,15,...$.
problems.lean:
theorem erdos_359.variants.isGoodFor_1_low_values (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : IsGoodFor A 1) :
    A '' (Set.Iic 7) = {1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 15}
